With a hierarchical attention mechanism for efficient feature extraction, the Swin Transformer achieves a top 1 accuracy of 85.6%, and a top 5 accuracy of 96.2%. Utilizing its encoder-decoder attention technique, Detection Transformer (DETR) effectively detects diseases by employing an encoder to forecast bounding boxes and class labels for affected areas. Segmentation performance is enhanced with SAM2-UNet, achieving a pixel-level segmentation with a Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC) of 94.7%, cleanly delineating disease-affected areas. Finally, disease impact is quantified in the final severity prediction stage to allow for targeted interventions based on disease intensity. The framework has been extensively validated through experiments, and it performs significantly better on all the evaluation metrics: Average ROC AUC of 99.97%, Average Precision-Recall AUC of 98.47%, and F1-score of 94.46%. The suggested system improves precision agriculture by making disease detection and management reliable, scalable, and efficient. This work applies cutting-edge deep learning to sustainable agriculture to reduce crop losses, optimise resource use, and provide farmers with proactive disease management knowledge.

title: An Innovative Smart Irrigation Using Embedded and Regression-Based Machine Learning Technologies for Improving Water Security and Sustainability
abstract: Global agriculture is facing major challenges such as food security, sustainable water management, and the preservation of natural resources. Water scarcity, exacerbated by climate change, requires adopting more efficient agricultural practices. Traditional irrigation systems, often imprecise, contribute to water wastage. The use of embedded systems and machine learning offers a solution for optimizing irrigation according to local conditions and actual crop needs while contributing to food security and environmental sustainability. This study proposes an innovative approach to irrigation management, integrating real-time data and predictive models to improve irrigation efficiency. This study proposes an irrigation system based on embedded systems, using sensors and algorithms to collect and analyze data in order to optimize water management. The system adjusts irrigation levels according to specific crop needs, thus contributing to more sustainable water management. Using ML algorithms like linear regression algorithms to model the relationships between environmental factors and crop water requirements, enabling accurate prediction of required irrigation levels based on data collected by sensors. The use of embedded systems such as the ESP32, combined with temperature, humidity, and water level sensors, has enabled the development of an autonomous and efficient system for collecting data in real-time and processing it for decision-making. The proposed model has an MAE of 0.8434, an RMSE of 0.8434, and a coefficient (R2Score) of 0.4044, offering soil moisture prediction accuracy. Furthermore, the training time of our model is 0.00253 seconds, while the prediction time is 0.00117 seconds. These results show not only the performance of the proposed model in terms of accuracy but also its computational efficiency, outperforming some of the studies mentioned. The results of the study show a significant reduction in water consumption, with a marked improvement in water resource management. Discussions reveal that the integration of embedded systems with machine learning algorithms can not only improve irrigation efficiency but also contribute to the sustainability of agriculture by enabling more accurate and adaptive management of water resources. This paper represents an important step towards improving food security and sustainable water management, particularly in regions facing increasing climatic challenges.

title: An Improved IoT Based Hybrid Predictive Load Forecasting Model for a Greenhouse Integrated With Demand Side Management
abstract: Greenhouse farming enhances agricultural productivity but remains highly energy-intensive, requiring advanced energy management strategies to ensure sustainability. Traditional load forecasting and demand-side management (DSM) methods often fall short in adapting to the dynamic and highly variable environmental conditions within greenhouses. This study hypothesizes that combining hybrid machine learning models with IoT-based DSM can optimize energy consumption while maintaining critical microclimatic conditions for crop growth. A hybrid predictive model integrating Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) for static feature learning and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) for sequential pattern recognition is proposed, coupled with a priority-based DSM framework deployed on a Raspberry Pi IoT platform. The model was trained and tested using one year of real-world greenhouse data, achieving a Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) of 5.3%, reducing grid energy dependency by 7.1%, and lowering the average electricity cost by 17.3%. These results demonstrate that the proposed system offers a scalable, economically viable, and sustainable solution for intelligent energy management in greenhouse environments, significantly advancing the integration of AI and DSM technologies in controlled agriculture. A laboratory-scale prototype was developed for physical verification using an EcoSense 500W solar microgrid, Raspberry Pi 3B+, relay modules, current sensors (SCT-013, ADS1115 ADC), and load simulators. Furthermore, this work contributes directly to Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) 2, 7, and 12 by promoting food security, increasing renewable energy utilization, and enhancing responsible resource consumption in greenhouse farming.

title: AI-Driven Smart Agriculture: An Integrated Approach for Soil Analysis, Irrigation, and Crop-Fertilizer Recommendations
abstract: Modern agriculture faces critical challenges, including climate change induced water shortage, inefficient resource utilization, and reducing soil health which reduce sustainability and reduce crop yields. Traditional farming methods, dependent on manual observation and generalized practices, often lack the precision needed to address these growing issues. To meet these demands, this study presents an artificial intelligence (AI) powered smart agriculture system that integrates deep learning (DL), Internet of Things (IoT), and explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) to enable intelligent, data-driven farming. This study addresses key challenges such as ineffective soil management, poor irrigation practices, and the absence of personalized crop and fertilizer recommendations. IoT-based sensors provide real-time soil analysis, measuring critical parameters such as nutrient levels, moisture, and temperature. Advanced DL models were employed for various tasks in the AI-Driven Smart Agriculture System. The Transformer-based Tabular Learning (TTL) model for irrigation advice gives an accuracy of 99.13%. For soil analysis, the TabNet regressor achieved a root mean square error (RMSE) of 1.51 and an R² score of 98.7%, while XAI techniques were used to explain and interpret its predictions. The Sparse Weighted Fusion Transformer (SwiFT) model for crop recommendation gives an accuracy of 98.75%. For fertilizer recommendation, the TabNet classifier achieved an accuracy of 99.3%, with XAI techniques applied to explain the reasoning behind its predictions. These results demonstrate that the system delivers precise and actionable insights. A weather Application Programming Interface (API) is integrated to support timely irrigation decisions through accurate forecasting. A chatbot interface is also added which enhances system usability, accessibility and user-friendliness for farmers. The proposed model improves crop productivity, optimizes resource use, and supports adaptation to environmental changes. By leveraging AI and IoT technologies, the proposed model gives a solution which helps in sustainable agriculture, environmental resilience, and global food security, thus benefiting stakeholders ranging from individual farmers to large-scale agricultural business. Future work will explore real-time adaptive control mechanisms and expand model generalization across diverse geographical region.

title: A Price Risk Early Warning Model for Agricultural Products Based on the Integration of Deep Learning and Knowledge Graphs
abstract: Agricultural price volatility poses significant challenges for food security, market regulation, and rural economic stability. To address these issues, this study proposes an integrated early warning model that combines the representational capabilities of deep learning with the interpretability of symbolic knowledge. The framework features two primary components: AgroFormer, a Transformer-based architecture specifically designed to capture hierarchical spatio-temporal dependencies across crops, regions, environmental factors, and time; and AgroScope, a strategic reasoning module that converts predictive insights into operational decisions through knowledge-aware constraints and risk-sensitive optimization. The model is evaluated on four benchmark datasets—Agmarknet, AGRIS, WorldCereal, and GAEZ—spanning structured tabular records, multilingual textual documents, and high-resolution remote sensing data. Experimental results show that the proposed approach achieves superior performance across all datasets, outperforming state-of-the-art baselines with an average improvement of 12.3% in prediction accuracy and a 12.1% reduction in RMSE. Ablation studies further validate the unique contributions of symbolic attribute alignment, differentiable scheduling graphs, and knowledge-aware constraints. Beyond technical contributions, the proposed system offers tangible value to agricultural practitioners. It enables proactive decision-making by delivering early warnings for price fluctuations, optimizing crop rotation schedules under policy and environmental constraints, and supporting adaptive planning in response to real-time market signals. The framework’s modular design facilitates deployment in diverse agro-ecological contexts, making it suitable for applications ranging from farm-level management to national food security planning. These results highlight the potential of combining deep learning with domain knowledge to create interpretable, scalable, and actionable tools for intelligent agricultural risk management.

title: Forecasting the Global Price of Corn Using Neural Network and Hybrid Approach
abstract: The global price of corn is critical in agricultural markets, food security, and trade policies, making accurate forecasting essential for policymakers and stakeholders. Traditional econometric forecasting models have been widely used but often fail to capture market volatility, nonlinear trends, and external shocks, necessitating advanced machine-learning techniques. This study explored forecasting models, including traditional and advanced machine learning and hybrid approaches, to determine the most effective method for predicting corn prices. Using monthly corn price data from 2014 to 2024, the study evaluated model performance based on different evaluation metrics. The results indicated that the Neural Network Auto Regressive (NNETAR) model outperformed traditional econometric models, effectively capturing complex temporal structures and adapting to sudden market fluctuations. Additionally, hybrid models integrating NNETAR and Seasonal and Trend decomposition using LOESS Model (STLM) demonstrated further improvements in forecasting accuracy, suggesting that combining statistical and machine learning methods enhances predictive reliability. These findings underscore the potential of machine learning in agricultural price forecasting, providing valuable insights for policymakers to implement market stabilization strategies, adjust trade policies, and enhance risk management in the U.S. corn sector.

title: AI-Based Assessment of Food Security and Climate Change: Multi-Scenario Analysis for Africa
abstract: Food security is tightly linked to climate change, with conflicts, pandemics, and extreme events compounding risk. Sub-Saharan Africa is especially affected by this situation. This study develops an AI-based framework to quantify how climate variability and market dynamics shape food security in Africa and to translate these relations into forward-looking indicators. A compile multi-source panel have for African countries that integrates climate variables, undernourishment, production, yield, and price data. After cleaning, normalization, and context-aware imputation, we construct a Food Security Vulnerability Index (FSVI) that synthesizes availability, access, and stability through principal components and an autoencoder. Panel models approach combines machine learning algorithms, clustering, scenario experiments, and attribute imputation to capture structural drivers and short-term shocks. The findings indicate that warming exerts the strongest negative pressure on maize yields, while wheat is more sensitive to rainfall anomalies. Moderate CO₂ fertilization cannot offset heat stress in some regions. High import dependence on wheat and rice increases access risks during price increases. Vulnerability clusters concentrate in parts of the Sahel, the Horn of Africa, and Southern Africa, where climate exposure coincides with limited input use, storage constraints, and inland transport frictions. Projections indicate that yield growth will lag behind demand in many subregions, unless targeted interventions are implemented. Validation demonstrates strong agreement with observations (Pearson r ≈ 0.81) and meaningful concordance with outcome-based indices, supporting the early warning utility. In scenario analyses, yield changes for maize/teff clusters range from −1.5% to −5.0% under Dry/Hot conditions and +1.5% to +5.0% across six crops under Wet/Warm conditions, with an FSVI increase of roughly +0.3 to +0.6 in Dry/Hot regimes. Overall, the framework provides a practical and interpretable tool for prioritizing interventions and tracking vulnerability as data ecosystems evolve.

title: Multi-Temporal UAV Imagery Feature Fusion for Paddy Yield Prediction in Tropical Smallholder Farms: Integrating RGB Color, Texture, and NDVI Indicators Across Growth Stages
abstract: Accurate paddy (Oryza sativa) yield prediction is essential for food security planning and precision agriculture. While most existing approaches rely on single-phase observations near harvest, they fail to capture the cumulative growth dynamics that determine final productivity. This study presents a multi-temporal framework for predicting paddy yield using UAV-derived RGB and multispectral (NDVI) imagery across three critical growth stages—Vegetative, Reproductive, and Ripening—spanning 514 experimental plots in Kedungwaras, Lamongan, East Java. The field was cultivated with a locally adapted early-maturing (genjah) rice variety. Hand-crafted features including color moments, GLCM texture descriptors, and NDVI statistics were extracted and fused temporally. An extensive comparison was conducted between traditional Machine Learning models (Support Vector Regression, Random Forest, XGBoost) and Deep Learning baselines (Multi-Layer Perceptrons). Our results demonstrate that SVR using the fusion of Reproductive and Ripening phases achieves the best predictive performance among tested configurations (R² = 0.2083, MAE = 0.1277 kg/m²), representing a 24.7% relative improvement over single-phase ripening prediction. Notably, traditional ML models significantly outperformed tabular MLP architectures on this dataset scale. SVR feature importance rankings were explored using Kernel SHAP and compared with Random Forest Tree SHAP (Spearman rank correlation rho = 0.217, p = 0.1151). Leave-One-Petak-Out spatial block cross-validation was implemented, revealing a drop in R² (best RF R² = 0.0642) due to spatial autocorrelation and localized microclimates. These findings highlight the value of temporal feature fusion for identifying critical monitoring windows in tropical smallholder agriculture, while underscoring the challenges of spatial generalizability.

title: Explainable Spatiotemporal Ensemble Modeling Using Knowledge Distillation to Forecast Food Security
abstract: Accurate prediction of food security is crucial for managing climate-induced agricultural hazards, but current approaches struggle to include spatiotemporal complexity while producing interpretable and understandable results. This study fills this gap by conducting a thorough examination of machine learning paradigms for rainfall-driven food security forecasting in Uganda, including the use of baseline models, ensemble approaches, and spatiotemporal graph neural networks. A unifying framework was established, incorporating 15 various models, including linear regressors (Ridge and Lasso), tree-based ensembles (XGBoost and Gradient Boost), and a unique Spatial Graph Attention Network (GAT) with multi-head temporal attention. Temporal-GNN was implemented to model spatiotemporal trends in rainfall-food security interactions by combining graph convolutional networks (GCNs) and gated recurrent units (GRUs). To bridge the transparency gap in AI-driven predictions, SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) and LIME (Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations) are systematically applied across all models, quantifying the influence of climatic drivers such as immediate rainfall intensity (r1h), seasonal fluctuations, and pressure gradients (rfq). Key advancements in this study include: XGBoost achieving state-of-the-art performance ( $\mathrm{R}^{2}=0.9949$ , MAE = 1.4067), surpassing baseline models by 14.3% in predictive accuracy; The Spatial GAT model demonstrating robust temporal dependency capture (MSE = 0.2092, MAE = 0.337), offering granular spatiotemporal insights despite a lower R2 (0.7801) and model-agnostic explainability revealing divergent feature importance. Linear models prioritise temperature, whereas ensembles emphasise atmospheric pressure dynamics. Recognising the practical challenges of deploying complex models, this work successfully implemented Knowledge Distillation (KD) to create a lightweight, efficient model from the best-performing XGBoost. The distilled student model achieved a compression ratio of 37.5% (reducing from 80 to 50 estimators) while maintaining 98.7% of the teacher model’s R2 score (0.9866 vs 0.9949). Despite a moderate increase in error metrics (MAE increased from 1.4067 to 2.3001, MSE from 3.8404 to 10.0075), the student model preserved the same feature importance hierarchy, with r1h and r1h_avg remaining the most influential predictors post-distillation. A reproducible pipeline incorporating spatial cross-validation, CUDA-accelerated training, and interactive XAI visualisation is introduced to enhance methodological rigour. Policymakers benefit from actionable trade-offs: the Voting Regressor (MAE = 2.2880) balances interpretability and performance, while the Spatial GAT enables localised, climate-resilient planning. This work advances scalable food security analytics by unifying statistical robustness with temporal dependency modelling, setting the stage for hybrid ensemble-GAT architectures in future research.

title: Potato Leaf Disease Prediction Using Machine Learning for Sustainable Agriculture
abstract: Diseases in crop plants pose a great threat to our global food supply, causing important losses in agricultural yields. The manual identification of these diseases is laborintensive and requires much expertise, which makes it difficult to predict early and quite accurately. Traditional plant disease identification methods are time-consuming and involve much specialization. Evidently, an automatic, and accurate approach is much needed to reduce crop plant loss and contribute to securing food supplies. The paper presents a new approach in plant disease detection by integrating image processing and machine learning methods. Some of the machine learning models implemented for the identification and classification of affected potato leaves' images are K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Support Vector Machines (SVM), Decision Tree (DT), and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs). The architecture of the ensemble is designed to achieve the highest levels of accuracy and robustness during the classification tasks. Extensive datasets that contain pictures of potato leaves both infected and uninfected will train the model. The system classifies the leaves precisely into categories such as healthy, early blight, and late blight. Since the model identifies the detailed characteristics of leaves, including different colors and appearances, the diagnosis of potential states of diseases in leaves is effective. This work provides the essential developments to the designing an automated systems that detect diseases. This technology brings together simple manual techniques and advanced techniques to provide a very favorable system for the early detection of diseases in the processes of protection and diagnosis. This method enhances agricultural production rates which creates better global food security. CNN model is better than the other models in the proposed work.

title: M3-DP: Measured Metrics Mapped Data Preparation for Gain Crop Yield Prediction
abstract: The agricultural industry not only powers the economies of many countries, but it also contributes significantly to their food security. This paper proposes a novel structural mathematical modeling method for creating datasets essential for forecasting grain crop yield. To ensure accurate modeling of the desired datasets, the methodology has been tested with wheat ear images that have been processed using a pre-trained Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) for essential feature extraction. To improve relevance, further phases imply thorough preprocessing and focused feature selection. A complete dataset that captures contextual insights and fine-grained information is produced by combining manual measurements with precision derived by machines. The changing nature of agricultural landscapes in terms of crop density and diversity is accommodated by iterative procedures to guarantee adaptability. Using a threshold, the dataset is refined so that only high-quality data is kept. The result is a final dataset that has been thoroughly created and is ready to be fed to a model to forecast grain crop yield. By combining manual measurements, machine learning, and precision agriculture, this method represents a major advancement in the field.

title: Carbon Dioxide Emission Forecasting using Machine Learning and Time Series Statistical Models
abstract: Climate change is considered a global disaster that has wreaked havoc worldwide. Climate change conditions are primarily driven due to emission of carbon dioxide and other greenhouse gases. Around the globe, several countries are facing serious challenges related to global warming and climate change. The adverse effects of global warming and climate change are recently observed in the form heat waves, floods, extreme rainfall events and drought conditions. The escalating CO2 emission level causes threats of food security and water scarcity. To overcome this, timely and accurate CO2 emissions forecasting is essential for developing effective mitigation strategies in such a manner that CO2 emission impacts can be reduced. The aim of this study is to forecast the total CO2 emissions of upcoming years using various statistical, machine learning models such as ARIMA (Auto-Regressive Integrated Moving Average), SARIMA (Seasonal ARIMA), Linear Regression, and Decision tree regressor. We had forecasted CO2 emission on the basis of influencing factors, which highly contributes in CO2 emission. The performance of the models is validated using multiple evaluation metrics such as MAE, MSE RMSE,MAPE and R2 square. The results show that CO2 emission is highly affected by fossil fuel consumption. In particular, Linear regression performs better among all applied models, with R2 value 0.93 and MAE, RMSE and MAPE values 5.52, 6.47 and 0.03, respectively. Our research delineates the results and insights that will assist concerned authorities, policymakers and environmental agencies. The present study also aim to inform authorities, helping them to better understand the future of CO2 emission trajectories and make timely efforts and interventions to tackle the climate change and global warming challenges.

title: AgriFusionNet: A Hybrid Deep Learning and IoT Framework for Unified Crop Yield Forecasting and Disease Detection
abstract: Global food security is largely dependent on agriculture, and modern farming systems depend on precise crop yield forecasting and plant disease detection to be durable, lucrative, and environmentally friendly. Precision agriculture has been transformed by the quick developments in machine learning (ML), deep learning (DL), the Internet of Things (IoT), and remote sensing (RS). These developments allow farmers and policymakers to make well-informed, data-driven decisions. In order to maximize output, minimize losses, and lessen environmental effects, this review summarizes state-of-the-art research that combines sensing technologies, spectral imaging, and intelligent algorithms. Neural networks, ensemble models, and hybrid frameworks like MARS-ANN and MARS-SVR consistently outperform conventional statistical methods in yield forecasting, according to studies conducted in a variety of regions, including Kazakhstan, Nigeria, and multi-country evaluations. More advanced methods, like MHRA-MS-3D-ResNet-BiLSTM and LSTM-based models, use data fusion from various sources and model explainability to find spatio temporal dependencies, identify crop-specific traits, and show important growth stages. In the same way, deep learning and computer vision models like ResNet-50, Multi-ViT, and MaizeNet are significantly more precise than classical ML algorithms when it comes to detecting plant diseases. They get 98–99% of the time right. Furthermore, the combination of AI-IoT systems and multimodal data from UAVs, satellites, and ground sensors shows a lot of opportunities for automated, scalable, and real-time uses in agriculture. Even with these successes, there are still problems to solve, such as the lack of large, high-quality labeled datasets, the reality that models fail to perform well across different crop types and regions, and the need for better interpretability to encourage real-world farming. The findings collectively underscore the transformative impact of AI-driven frameworks in precision agriculture, providing robust decision-support systems that can enhance yield prediction, facilitate early and reliable disease detection, improve crop management, and promote sustainable farming practices worldwide. The findings together underscore the transformative impact of AI-driven frameworks in precision agriculture, providing robust decision-support systems that can enhance yield prediction, facilitate early and accurate disease detection, optimize crop management, and advocate for sustainable farming practices worldwide.

title: Deep Learning technique for predicting tomato leaf disease
abstract: The increased focus on smart agriculture in recent years can be attributed to various factors, including the adverse effects of climate change, extreme weather events, population growth, the need for food security, and the scarcity of natural resources. The Moroccan government has undertaken proactive measures to address plant diseases, particularly in relation to tomatoes, which are globally recognized as one of the most significant vegetable crops and are susceptible to numerous diseases resulting in substantial yield reduction. The identification of tomato leaf diseases has increasingly shifted towards the utilization of deep learning techniques. In this study, we have conducted a comparative analysis of various deep learning techniques, specifically focusing on CNN models. Our objective was to determine the most suitable, efficient, and accurate method for detecting diseases that affect tomato leaves by merging two publicly available datasets, namely PlantVillage and PlantDoc. This research examines the potential of utilizing cutting-edge deep learning techniques that are focused on YOLO models. We have selected four models, namely YOLOv5, YOLOX, YOLOv7, and YOLOv8, which fall under the category of "One-stage detectors." These models are renowned for their fast inference speed and exceptional accuracy. Based on the experimental findings, YOLOv5 demonstrates the highest level of accuracy, achieving a mAP of 93.1% after fine-tuning the hyperparameters. The ultimate model is implemented as a mobile application to enhance usability.

title: Greensense: IoT-Enabled Smart Monitoring And Early Detection System For Optimal Plant Health In Greenhouse
abstract: The emergence of Agriculture 4.0 signifies a transformative shift in traditional farming practices, integrating cutting-edge technologies like IoT, machine learning, and robotics to support productivity and sustainability. This era leverages real-time data and automation for precision farming, predictive analytics, and resource optimization, crucial for addressing global food security challenges while minimizing environmental impact. GreenSense represents progress within Agriculture 4.0. It seeks to revolutionize greenhouse management by integrating IoT and advanced machine learning algorithms. Through sensors, actuators, and a Raspberry Pi 4 board, this system offers a comprehensive solution for monitoring and optimizing plant health in controlled environments. The motivation behind this system stems from the imperative to enhance agricultural practices sustainably in the face of population growth. By enabling real-time monitoring and swift anomaly detection through application, this paper empowers proactive intervention to mitigate risks and optimize growing conditions. Integration of the YOLOv5 algorithm with 97% accuracy enhances precision in leaf disease and pest detection using OpenCV, reducing crop losses effectively. Beyond greenhouse management, this paper contributes to advancing sustainable agriculture. Its scalable and adaptable nature promotes resource-efficient practices and environmental care. Finally, a user-friendly interface is tailored to facilitate efficient data collection from sensors, enabling comprehensive monitoring of crop conditions, including pest and disease detection.

title: Design Science Research Methodology (DSRM) for IoT-Enabled Predictive Maintenance Towards Sustainability
abstract: The importance for sustainable and resilient food production systems has positioned smart agriculture as a key enabler of food security in both rural and urban contexts. Within the Industry 5.0 framework that emphasizes sustainability, resilience, and human-technology collaboration, predictive maintenance has emerged as a crucial component for ensuring reliable and efficient operation of IoT-enabled agricultural systems. However, conventional cloud-based machine learning (ML) approaches face limitations due to their dependence on high-bandwidth connectivity, centralized processing, and continuous data transmission-leading to latency, energy inefficiency, and data privacy concerns.

title: COMPARATIVE STUDY OF MACHINE-LEARNING-BASED CLASSIFIERS FOR SOIL SALINIZATION PREDICTION USING SENTINEL-1 SAR AND SENTINEL-2 MSI DATA
abstract: Under arid and semi-arid climatic conditions, salinization, naturally induced by parental materials weathering or artificially caused by anthropogenic actions, depicts a severe land degradation form, which significantly impacts crop yield in arable lands affecting food security on local and regional scales. At the same time, its adverse effects on urban infrastructures extend to land subsidence, erosion, and groundwater quality deterioration. Hence, soil salinity and sodicity monitoring using remote sensing and GIS tools has been an attractive field of research for soil scientists and experts worldwide, mainly for promoting sustainable agriculture. In this context, using Sentinel-l SAR and Sentinel-2 MSI data acquired in September-October 2019 and soil salinity data provided by the Research Institute of Soil Sciences and Agricultural Chemistry (RISSAC), four machine learning classifiers, namely, random forest (RF), maximum likelihood (ML), minimum distance (MD), and nearest neighbors (KNN) were applied and compared in terms of classification accuracy. The results revealed that RF had outperformed other classifiers, with the highest overall accuracy of 97 % and a mean percentage error (MPE) of 0.028, followed by KNN (= 96 %, 0.041), ML (= 94.5 %, 0.054), and MD (= 86.5 %, 0.135). The importance score report based on the RF classifier showed that the VV backscatter coefficient, SWIRl, SWIR2, and VH backscatter coefficient are the most important features retrieved from remotely sensed data to estimate salinization risks. Despite its strong dependence on training data, random forest depicts the most suitable algorithm for salinization detection using radar and optical data. This study can provide a timeless reference for selecting efficient machine learning algorithms in future studies to predict salinization using data retrieved from multiple sensors.

title: Rice Modeling Using Long Time Series of High Temporal Resolution Vegetation Indices in Nepal
abstract: Quick prediction and forecasting of crop yield during the growing season and before harvest are of important value in supporting decision makers in agriculture and food security at large. Indices derived from remote sensing have been approved rapid approach of monitoring and detecting crop growth conditions. The correlation between vegetation indices and crop yield has been well recognized and applied in many yield estimation study. High temporal resolution time series of vegetation index maps are generated up to daily coverage using multiple source remote sensing data at different spatial resolution. The result index maps are up-scaled to match the rice statistic at district level. The condition profiles represented in crop condition indices are smoothed using Best Index Slope Extraction (BISE) and double sigmoid model. Regression models have been trained over different periods of data since 2000. The condition profiles for the year under study is estimated during stages and used to estimate the yield. Validation of different machine learning models has been tested with different periods. The results showed that the profile series of recent years yield better estimation than using all the years since 2000. This may be caused by the yield increase over the years due to other factors such as rice farming technology development.

title: Precision Agriculture and Machine Learning
abstract: Agriculture production is one of the most important sectors in any country’s growth. It has an influence not only on the economics of the country but also on global food grain statistics. Food security is a major challenge due to the rapidly increasing global people as well as the reducing trend in yields of crops. Obtaining sustainable crop production is always a problem for agriculturists. Due to ever-changing climatic circumstances, achieving optimal agricultural output has always been a problem for farmers. Land types, resource availability, and fluctuating climate patterns are the main causes of agricultural production uncertainty. Thus, researchers are developing tools that can predict crop production correctly and effectively in advance, allowing farmers worldwide to act accordingly in strategies to respond to obstacles. Agronomic strategies used by farmers at various phases of crop production and meteorological elements have a significant impact on crop production output [5]. The supply of nutrients directly impacts crops and the production of crops. Crops require a variety of nutrients, which are branched into two groups based on their requirements: macroeconomic nutrients and essential micronutrients. Phosphorous (P), Nitrogen (N), Calcium (Ca), Zinc (Zn), Potassium (K), Boron (B), Iron (Fe),Magnesium (Mg), Sulphur (S), and other nutrients are among them. Many micronutrients in the crops regulate biochemical processes, give resistance to diseases, and ultimately degrade crop quality. As a result, regulated nutrient management is critical for increasing crop production and achieving the essential rise in output. Furthermore, minerals have an important function in soil fertility, making it more productive for crop development. The following review article is going to address the most current facts regarding nutrients along with their usage in agricultural production for crop development.

title: Climate Change and Agriculture Land Suitability Insights from Interpretable Machine Learning
abstract: This research uses the transparent inferential machine learning models that can be used to outline the non-trivial nature of the correlations between the climate change, agronomic opportunity and the food security. The scenario would suppose that to investigate the threats of sustainability of the land and what sustainability of the land will imply to the future of the local food system, climate, information of the soil and the land-use in each of the different sceneries of the carbon emissions would be assumed. Certain construction of a machine learning model which has been chosen to predict the suitability of the land to the changes that influence the climate offered the following goal in particular, it offered the definite degree of interpretation of the definite model that was wanted to make the stakeholders learn what comprises a specific prediction. The accuracy of the model in the entire accuracy of 86 percent and the general accuracy of 72 percent of the multi-class of land suitability classification. The fact can be considered as the explanation of the correctness and reliability of the model in terms of a friendly environment of data analysis. The spatial level also allowed determining the key direction the changes in the suitability of the land to the changing climate conditions were going to take. The novelty in the presentation of the studies according to the argument of the research was explained by the fact that the outcome of this paper has been interpreted through interpretable AI techniques to make open data analytics less complex in agricultural planning setting by achieving climatic and spatial data. The conclusion is very timely concerning the local development, the food security programs and the environmental policy in the terms that now the course of changes in the adaptation to the climate and use of the land sustainably can be singled out.

title: Role of Artificial Intelligence in the Management of Food Waste
abstract: Food waste is caused by a complex collection of interconnected behavior at both the supplier and customer levels. Computational and mathematical models provide various methods for simulating, diagnosing, and predicting various aspects of the dynamic food waste generation and prevention system. This paper describes three modeling methods that have been used to analyze food waste in the past. Bayesian networks and machine learning algorithms are applied to help determine how much food is discarded at the household level. Agent-Based Simulation was used to gain insight into how innovation and adoption of a particular technology can help minimize retail food waste. The first BN-ABM integrated model assesses consumer food waste levels affected by particular features and aspects, resulting in the model reaching equilibrium. Proofing that there is a need for policy interventions, including training, economic incentives, and campaigns, to obtain the resulting model transformation. These interventions are ready to be assessed by the model, but further study is needed to understand the effects of enforcing these structures on the accuracy of the BN-ABM predictive model. The second ABM model aims to determine the factors that establish the adoption of food waste reduction technology at the retail level, which is influenced by particular but not limited to economic factors, including a strong network between retailers and consumer's awareness regarding food waste reduction technology. These findings can study the effects of policy intervention regarding food waste reduction at the retail and consumer level. The third ABM model employed a general food chain network model consisting of consumers, traders, and producers to simulate the dynamic change of product flow between agents and to be able to assess the effect of agent's behavioral contrast. Resilience is measured by the ability to deal with shocks, and efficiency is the share of total food manages to be dispatched to consumers. At first glance, the simulation results seem to show a system trade-off between efficiency and resilience. Network chain structures with higher efficiency displayed more sensitivity to shocks, while networks with less efficiency show more resilience. However, there seem to be modifications in the results when applying several trading interactions and shock types. Resiliency and efficiency are affected by social aspects (trust and preference) in trading interaction between agents. An essential aspect of resilience is the agent's ability to switch links (trading partners) which shows the capability of reorganization. Insights regarding the research can be applicable when considering real-life food chain and structural reorganization to increase resilience and efficiency in meeting national food security goals.

title: Precision Agriculture Advancements: A Comprehensive Integrated System for Disease Prediction And Crop Yield Estimation Using Image Analysis And Environmental Data
abstract: The primary problem facing agriculture, which is essential to ensuring the world’s food security, is maximizing crop productivity while reducing the effects of plant diseases. Advanced technologies have the potential to completely transform agricultural methods, particularly in the parts of computer vision and machine learning. This study uses meteorological datasets and fruit image analysis to create an integrated agricultural decision support system for crop yield estimation and disease prediction. By offering early plant disease detection and precise crop yield estimates, the system seeks to improve precision agriculture techniques. A variety of datasets with plant photos labelled with disease information are gathered for the study, and meteorological data is integrated to capture environmental variables. The technology includes advanced image processing techniques to extract relevant features from plant pictures. The suggested method analyses images using a convolutional neural network technique to forecast the disease in impacted fruits. Make recommendations for natural fertilizers based on the ailment being suffered. The Multilayer Perceptron algorithm is used to train the model using a large dataset that contains historical meteorological data, allowing it to identify patterns and connectionsbetween environmental conditions. Lastly, farmers receive an SMS notice with prediction specifics.

title: Predicting Potato Crop Yield With Latest Deep Learning Appraoches for Sustainable Agriculture
abstract: Accurate prediction of crops' yield is essential to develop farm management and food security. This paper presents the use of a hybrid deep model of Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) with ResNet-59 to enhance potato crop yield prediction for sustainable agriculture. Extracted high-resolution spatial features of crop health, soil, and disease from drone and satellite imagery are identified for essential factors to use in predictive modeling. On the other hand, RNN learns long-term dependencies and seasonality influencing potato yield by being trained on time-series data, such as past weather data, soil moisture level, and yield data. Through the integration of temporal and spatial data, the novel approach enhances the precision of forecasts and enables farmers to take optimal decisions. With a strong system of real-time yield estimation, efficient utilization of resources, and climate-resilient agricultural practices, the sequence processing capability of RNN and feature extraction capability of ResNet-59 are combined. With minimum wastage of resources and maximum output, the process is a part of precision agriculture. The study indicates that the hybrid deep learning model can be employed to enhance agricultural sustainability and is therefore a valuable tool for farmers, scientists, and policy makers who would like to produce potatoes sustainably and efficiently.

title: Boosting Agricultural Productivity in India through Machine Learning-Based Yield Predictions
abstract: Agricultural productivity stands as a cornerstone for India's sustenance and economic advancement, given the nation's vast array of climatic regions and agricultural practices. The accurate anticipation of crop yields emerges as a pivotal factor in optimizing agricultural outputs, guaranteeing food security, and effectively managing resource allocation. However, traditional predictive models often grapple with the intricate and nonlinear dynamics that influence crop yields. In response to this challenge, this study pioneers an innovative approach by leveraging a suite of machine learning models, encompassing Linear Regression, Random Forest Regression, CatBoost Regression, Gradient Boosting Regression, K-Nearest Neighbors Regression, and Bagging Regression, to refine the predictive accuracy of agricultural crop yields across diverse Indian states. Through the assembly of a comprehensive data set comprising climatic variables, fertilizer, pesticides, crop types, and historical yield data from various regions, this research aims to enhance the understanding of the intricate interplay between these factors. Our results illuminate a significant enhancement in predictive accuracy across all models examined, with the Random Forest Regression emerging as the most adept in forecasting crop yields accurately. This outcome not only augments precision in yield forecasts but also provides invaluable insights into the relative significance of distinct factors influencing crop productivity. This study underscores the pivotal role of advanced data preprocessing techniques, such as Power BI, in unleashing the full potential of machine learning for agricultural applications. By harnessing these methodologies, stakeholders can make more informed decisions, fostering improved agricultural productivity and sustain ability amidst the diverse agricultural landscape of India

title: Corn Pest Identification Based on Improved VGGNet Model
abstract: Corn as an important food crop in China, with good drought resistance, cold resistance, barrenness, by China's large-scale planting, its planting area and total output is second only to wheat and rice ranked third in the country. In addition to corn as people's food, but also food, health care, chemical industry and other indispensable raw materials, national food security is of great significance. In recent years, the frequent occurrence of corn diseases has had a great impact on corn yield, in response to this situation, this paper takes the common corn grey spot, corn rust and corn leaf spot, which are the three most common diseases of corn, as the object of research, and based on the classical serial convolutional neural network structure of VGG Net, we designed a variety of corn leaf disease-aware convolutional neural network suitable for embedded systems, using the data The model training results were optimised using data enhancement and the addition of a Dorpout layer. After experimental testing, the accuracy of the model in the test set reaches 95.93%, which reduces the model prediction time by nearly 5 times compared to the traditional VGGNet with similar recognition accuracy, and improves the recognition accuracy by 4.74% compared to AlexNet. On the embedded device Raspberry Pi 4b, the average predicted frame rate of video transmitted in real time for a single camera is up to 450 frames, which meets the requirement of real-time detection in agricultural production and can be deployed on precision application equipment in large fields. This study provides new ideas for deep learning network lightweight research and deployment of neural networks on embedded devices.

title: Implementation of Hybrid model for Enhanced Crop Yield Prediction using Explainable AI for Precision Agriculture
abstract: Crop yield prediction is important for global food security, sustainable farming, and efficient resource management in agriculture. Inaccuracy and inherent opacity are the main issue for accurate prediction. To solve the problems of deep learning models a hybrid model has been developed for better prediction. This research works to improve agricultural decision-making through advanced predictive modelling. In this research work SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) and Grad-CAM (Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping), have been employed. SHAP analysis helps us to understand the input feature impact of soil moisture at middle level growth and helps us to analyse the over fertilization that is no longer increasing the crop yield rather reducing it. This work shows integration of deep learning and explainable AI for data-driven decisions on irrigation process, usage of fertilizers, and strategies to improve the decision making of farmers and thus heading towards precision farming. A hybrid model that considers dynamic and static characteristics to forecast crop yields. The model employs Conv1D layers for finding short-term patterns and Bidirectional LSTM layers for long-term dependencies, along with dedicated dense layers for static features. The overall $\mathbf{R}^{\boldsymbol{\wedge}} \mathbf{2}$ is $\mathbf{0. 8 1}$ and $\mathbf{R}^{\boldsymbol{\wedge}} \mathbf{2}$ for specific crop types (wheat, soybean, corn, and rice) is always 0.91 and above, therefore outperforming models based on exclusive use of dynamic or static characteristics by a wide margin.

title: Machine Learning and Deep Learning-Based Framework for Crop Area and Yield Estimation in Agricultural Analytics
abstract: This study presents a machine learning and deep learning-based framework for accurate crop area and yield estimation, with a focus on smallholder farms in India. Using predictive analytics can help to improve agricultural planning, resource allocation, and decision-making mostly. Using a complete dataset consisting of 19,689 records with 19 agronomic characteristics-including rainfall, fertilizer use, pesticide application, and crop type- investigated The approach comprised preprocessing via imputation, encoding, and scaling, then model creation utilizing both traditional and innovative techniques. Key models consisted in CNN-LSTM, Deep Recurrent Q-Network (DRQN), Hybrid Random Forest + Gated Recurrent Unit (RF+GRU), and Linear Regression as baseline. Features relationships and distribution patterns were found by exploratory data analysis (ED A). Adaptive prediction features made possible by real-time data integration from IoT sensors and satellite systems Transparency and stakeholder confidence were guaranteed by means of SHAP (SHapley Additive Explanations) ensuring interpretability. With a Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) of 0.159 for yield and 0.049 for area, the RF+GRU model proved to be the greatest performance among experimental findings, much above conventional models. The results show how well spatial and temporal learning mix to enable precision farming. Strong potential exists for this robust, scalable architecture to support crop insurance programs, maximize resource allocation, and enhance food security in resource-limited agricultural environments.

title: Smart NFT based Hydroponic System for Precision Agriculture using IoT and AI
abstract: Precision agriculture (PA) presents numerous possibilities to address the growing challenges of sustainability and food security. To develop an effective PA system, it is essential to collect and analyze real-time data using Artificial Intelligence (AI) methodologies. This research integrates the Internet of Things (IoT) and AI within a Nutrient Film Technique (NFT) hydroponic system for the growth of the Holy basil plant. The aim is to create an ideal indoor environment through optimized resource management. This involves establishing an IoT-enabled framework for real-time data collection to monitor $\mathbf{p H}$, temperature, humidity, and dissolved substances, affecting both artificial conditions and plant growth rates. The AI processes these data to fine-tune the environment and perform the necessary automated adjustments within the PA system. In addition, AI-driven predictive models will anticipate plant growth patterns and ensure a robust crop management system with precise yield predictions. Addressing these areas is crucial for the successful application of IoT and AI in PA systems. The Random Forest machine learning (ML) model predicts the yield in cm with an accuracy of 97%, while XGBoost is used to predict the NPK dosing with an accuracy of 99%.

title: IoT Based Food and Grain Condition Traceability and Controlling System in Warehouses
abstract: India, a predominantly agrarian nation with 70% of its population engaged in farming, emphasizes the significance of grain storage and food security for national economic strength. Atmospheric factors such as temperature, humidity, and carbon dioxide concentration profoundly impact stored grain quality in warehouses. This paper presents a real-time grain storage monitoring system utilizing DHT22, MQ135, Peltier module, flame sensor, ultrasonic repellant, and PIR sensors, grounded in IoT principles. The project incorporates features like online detection, control mechanisms, and systematic updates. Temperature regulation through the Peltier module aids in pinpointing locations affected by food spoilage, enhancing farming practices. Machine learning techniques contribute to animal control, adjusting ultrasonic repeller frequencies based on detected animal presence. Predictive analysis through machine learning anticipates future readings, elevating the quality standard for stored grains. The primary goal is to minimize grain wastage, reduce manpower, and eliminate constant manual oversight.

title: Mapping the vegetative stage of rice cultivation using deep learning
abstract: Monitoring rice growth stages is important for maintaining food security, especially from flood and drought, which is more frequent due to climate change. The Sentine1-2 Rice Growth Stages (S-2 RGS) monitoring project from the Ministry of Agriculture is one of the ongoing monitoring systems (http://katam.litbang.pertanian.go.id/sc). However, S-2 RGS has difficulty providing a cloud-free project, especially in the wet season. Sentinel-1 (S-1) has recently been used to identify mapping rice area due to better spatial resolution than the MODIS dataset. This study focuses on mapping the vegetative stage using a multi-look of S-1 dataset with a deep learning method. Deep learning has been proven to be one of the classification methods on non-parametric approaches that give high accuracy, high computation speed, and less memory usage. The method of this study is as follows: First, the S-1 images downloaded from Google Earth Engine, which has been preprocessed accordingly. Secondly, the rice growth stages condition of Indramayu Regency was extracted from S-2 RGS using random sampling on 16 May 2020. Next step, both multi-look S-1 (Ascending, Descending). Third, the values of RGS was reclassified from four classes (Bare land, Vegetative, Reproductive, and Ripening) into two class (vegetative and Non-vegetative). Finally, the vegetative stage was modeled from four predictors (DESC-VH, DESC-VV, ASC-VH, ASC-VV) using deep learning using two layers with a training dataset (n=9,319). The accuracy of the model is 73.6% (n=3,994). This result shows that deep learning can predict a vegetative stage map with high accuracy where it can fill a cloudy area in the RGS-2 system to provide a cloud-free rice growth stages map in near real-time.

title: A Machine Learning Approach for Crop Yield Prediction Using Weather Condition
abstract: Efficient and sustainable farming is essential for human survival, particularly as global population growth and climate change place increasing demands on agricultural systems. Meteorological conditions, including temperature, humidity, and soil moisture, directly affect crop growth and yield. For varying conditions, this research aims to leverage real-time environmental data for predicting best-suited crops and informed decisions made with former and to optimize productivity and food security. Real-time data collection systems monitor key environmental parameters, and the data is stored in cloud-based systems for efficient management and accessibility. This enables scalable and reliable handling of large datasets, which is crucial in agriculture. The study uses two machine learning algorithm Decision Tree with Random Forest (DT-RF) to predict the optimal crop based on the environmental factors. For reducing overfitting and prediction accuracy improvement, the multiple decision trees aggregated with the Random Forest in which the data classified using Decision Tree algorithm. Temperature, humidity, and moisture content are the parameters that are used to gather real-time data and choose the best crop. To consider computational efficiency, accuracy and precision, both algorithms effectiveness assessed with the comparative analysis. Due to real-time meteorological data, the crop selection as the most reliable algorithm for the identification of results. The research provides recommendations on integrating these predictive systems into agricultural practices to improve crop selection, enhance productivity, and promote sustainable farming in the face of climate challenges.

title: Satellite-based Crop Yield Prediction using Machine Learning Algorithm
abstract: Agriculture is the backbone of India's economy as 70% of the population's household is dependent on agriculture. Crop yield prediction is a crucial step for food security, market planning, and yield mapping. Machine learning with remote sensing has shown magnificent results for crop yield prediction. In this research, the authors implemented machine learning techniques along with the remote sensing data to extract features. Support Vector Machine and K-Nearest Neighbor- techniques have shown outstanding results - are implemented to predict the crop yield using remote sensing data. Authors focused on distinguish parts of a satellite image based on the vegetation for a few months and then finding the relation between their Normalized Difference Vegetation Index values and vegetation similarly, and also found out that vegetation of the same crop field varies over the months and on further computations, we can predict the crop growth in that particular area. For this research, K-Nearest Neighbor outperformed Support Vector Machine.

title: Advancing Agricultural Sustainability: Machine Learning-Driven Insights for Optimized Crop Yield Forecasting
abstract: Sustainable agriculture is crucial for addressing global challenges related to food security, resource efficiency, and environmental preservation. This study examines the potential of machine learning (ML) in forecasting crop production to enhance decision-making and promote sustainable agricultural practices. The research investigates advanced machine learning techniques, including Multilayer Perceptron Artificial Neural Networks (MLP ANN), Decision Trees, Voting Classifiers, and YOLO models, for accurate agricultural yield prediction. These models employ several data sources, encompassing climatic conditions, soil properties, and agricultural practices. Among the assessed models, the MLP ANN achieved a notable accuracy of 91%, illustrating its efficacy in predicting agricultural production. The results demonstrate how these predictive models aid farmers and policymakers in optimizing resource allocation, reducing waste, and aligning agricultural inputs with expected outputs, thereby decreasing environmental impact and improving economic outcomes. Essential insights highlight the effectiveness of data-driven methods in reducing uncertainty and enhancing agricultural productivity. The paper finishes by identifying barriers to the widespread adoption of ML-based solutions and outlining opportunities for integrating these technologies into sustainable agricultural systems, so offering a framework for future implementation.

title: Intelligent Decision Support System for Sustainable Precision Agriculture: A Deep Learning Approach
abstract: The rising need for food security and sustainable agriculture worldwide has led to the development of precision agriculture as an important means of managing resources effectively. This study presents an Intelligent Decision Support System for precision farming that utilizes a state-of-the-art convolutional neural network based deep learning model trained on a comprehensive dataset of images of rice, maize, and wheat varieties, as well as associated disease conditions. This system consists of three main components: nutrient management for each crop, to determine optimal amounts of fertilizer to apply at any point in time; pest management that utilizes CNN-based models to identify and monitor pests early. The CNN-based disease prediction and ML-based yield forecasting modules operate independently but are connected through a crop-type mapping layer. The Xception CNN model has been shown to have substantial progress, as evidenced by high training and validation accuracies 96.56% and 91.84%, respectively. In addition, the decision tree-based model for predicting crop yield has lower mean squared error 0.2991 than the random forest model 0.3395 and a higher coefficient of determination 0.8883 for decision tree-based model and 0.8732 for random forest model, demonstrating superior predictive capability and ability to capture variable interactions. Contributions of this study can provide valuable guidelines for advancement in precision agriculture, which will yield more productive farming on a large-scale basis.

title: Machine Learning for Agricultural Price Prediction: A Case of Coffee Commodity in Vietnam Market
abstract: Predicting agricultural commodity prices is crucial for farmers, governments, and related stakeholders to make important decisions about crop planning and food security. This is especially important in economies that rely greatly on agriculture, such as Vietnam and other developing countries, where the instability and inadequate predictability of agricultural commodity prices may lead to overproduction, "good season - devaluation" phenomenon, and significant economic losses. Aiming to address this issue, this paper presents the use of machine learning models to predict the price of coffee, a major agricultural commodity in Vietnam. Various machine learning techniques, namely LSTM (Long Short-Term Memory), ARIMA (Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average), SARIMA (Seasonal ARIMA), GRU (Gated Recurrent Unit), SVM (Support Vector Machine), and RF (Random Forest), are trained and evaluated using different data, including historical prices and additional data, such as fuel prices and weather data. The results of numerical experiments demonstrated that using additional data can significantly improve prediction performance.

title: DPCformer: An Interpretable Deep Learning Model for Genomic Prediction in Crops
abstract: Addressing global food security demands more efficient crop breeding. While Genomic Selection (GS) accelerates breeding by predicting phenotypes from genomic data, its accuracy is limited by complex trait architectures and environmental dependencies. To overcome these challenges, we propose DPCformer, a deep learning model integrating convolutional neural networks with self-attention to capture nonlinear genotype-phenotype relationships. Evaluated on 13 traits across five crops (maize, cotton, tomato, rice, chickpea) using chromosomally-ordered SNP data processed with 8-dimensional encoding and PMF feature selection, DPCformer demonstrated superior performance. It achieved accuracy improvements of$0.74-2.92 \%$in maize, up to 8.37% in cotton, and remarkable PCC enhancements of 57.35% in tomato and 16.62% in chickpea compared to baselines. These results establish DPCformer as a robust framework for genomic prediction, excelling in accuracy, small-sample performance, and polyploid data processing.

title: A Generalized Multimodal Deep Learning Model for Early Crop Yield Prediction
abstract: Early crop yield prediction is crucial in agriculture for making administrative plans to ensure food security, post harvest management and distribution of a crop. Remote sensing data captured using various satellites provide reliable phenological information for a crop through surface reflectance bands. Other important factors, affecting crop yield include meteorological and soil. The data which we have used for crop yield prediction is multimodal. It consists of spatiotemporal meteorological (numeric) and surface reflectance bands (satellite image), and temporally static soil (satellite image) data. We effectively utilize this multimodal data to develop the proposed multimodal deep learning model, CropYieldNet. The objective of the paper is to accurately predict crop yield using high resolution data obtained from recently launched satellites such as Landsat8 and Sentinel-2. We used contrastive learning in a supervised setting and data augmentation techniques to overcome the limited historical data available for training deep learning models.We introduce a depth-level selection module for effectively modelling the depth-variant information of soil data. We have also modified our model to perform in-season (early) crop yield prediction which is as accurate as end-season prediction. We evaluate our model for two crops, corn and soybean, on counties in US and districts in India using data from MODIS, Landsat8, and Sentinel-2 satellites. Our extensive experimentation show that our model outperforms competing models. Our experiments also show that CropYieldNet generalizes well when applied on different crops and geographies.

title: Methodology for food prices forecasting
abstract: Fluctuations in food prices play a pivotal role in maintaining economic equilibrium and influencing the very fabric of our everyday lives. This paper presents a comprehensive framework for modeling and analyzing food price trends in 12 select European countries, spanning from January 2013 to January 2023, utilizing advanced state-of-the-art Machine Learning techniques. To achieve this objective, historical price data and technical indicators are incorporated into the proposed XGBoost model alongside a baseline model. The model results are assessed using various measures, and a benchmark is established. Notably, the average achieved $R^{2}$ for predicting food prices within the time frame from January 2020 to January 2022 is 0.85 and 0.64 from January 2021 to January 2023. The findings reveal the efficacy of the proposed model, providing valuable insights into food price forecasting model interpretability and laying the groundwork for further research, including exploration into areas such as food fraud, food sustainability, and other pertinent topics in food economics.

title: A study on phenotype prediction using an artificial intelligence-based data augmentation approach
abstract: Global food security is increasingly at risk due to factors like climate change and population growth, necessitating advancements in agricultural technology. Digital breeding, a method centered around genotype-phenotype selection using next-generation sequencing (NGS), offers a solution by enabling the identification of genetic mutations and predicting crop traits with greater speed and precision compared to traditional approaches. This automated breeding process efficiently gathers and analyzes genotype and phenotype data, improving key traits such as growth, yield, and tolerance while minimizing human intervention. Despite advancements in sequencing technologies, challenges remain due to the high cost and impracticality of acquiring extensive genomic datasets. To address these limitations, this study explores data augmentation strategies using deep learning techniques, focusing on their success in other fields like computer vision. Unlike conventional Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), which face stability issues, we present a novel approach using a stacked convolutional and LSTM architecture. This model leverages SNP position information to capture correlations within genomic regions and introduces a specialized metric to evaluate the quality of augmented data. The effectiveness of the proposed phenotype prediction model is demonstrated through real-world testing on a collection of 192 tomato varieties, highlighting its potential to revolutionize breeding processes and improve agricultural outcomes.

title: On Building Real Time Intelligent Agricultural Commodity Trading Models
abstract: The global population is expected to reach 9.7 billion in 2050, according to the UN News [1]. This suggests that food, agriculture, and global commodity trading are essential and critical to human beings. To stabilize food price and better understand and predict the market trend, people need a real-time efficient online platform as an intelligent trading tool to support dynamic agriculture commodity trading. However, current trading platforms lack Al-powered solutions to support traders and investors with dynamic commodity market analysis based on historical big data, accurate forecasts on market trends and trading price forecasts. This paper focuses on this demand by studying and comparing existing machine learning models for intelligent trading and price prediction. The paper presents three improved machine learning models based on LSTM, GRU, and SARIMA, and proposes an advanced deep learning LSTM model with time series and multi-variant features to forecast crop market trends with predicted prices. As a result, our proposed agriculture trading models for crops (corn, oats, soybean, and soybean oil) based the improved LSTM provide great accurate prediction results (>0.95%). Based on our comparative evaluation results, the proposed model outperforms other existing models. The research results show a great potential application for a future intelligent trading platform which provides traders with real-time data driven market analysis and accurate predictions on market trends and commodity trading prices.

title: Estimating Future Prices of Key Agricultural Commodities Using Machine Learning Models
abstract: Farmers, consumers, and policymakers face difficulties as a result of the price fluctuation of basic agricultural commodities like rice, tomatoes, onions, and dals. For better market stability and well-informed decision-making, accurate price forecasts are essential. In order to assess historical market data and forecast price patterns, this study proposes a machine learning-based method that makes use of regression and time-series forecasting models. The suggested models show superior accuracy than conventional statistical techniques by capturing the intricacies of price swings caused by seasonal demand and crop yields, promoting enhanced supply chain planning and efficiency in agriculture.

title: Weather Prediction Using Cross-Visual Data with Random Forest and LSTM Models
abstract: The climate crisis that has occurred in recent decades has led to significant environmental changes, including increasing temperatures, changing rainfall patterns, and increasingly frequent extreme weather events. These changes have a direct impact on various sectors, especially the agricultural sector, which is the main foundation for food provision. Big data analysis is emerging as an innovative solution to analyze and predict weather conditions by utilizing historical data such as temperature, humadity, cloud cover, sea level preasure, wind speed and rainfall. This analysis can provide important insights in making decisions on sustainable agricultural strategies, especially in determining the early planting period to minimize the risk of crop failure and ensure food security in the future. This study aims to implement the weather prediction system using machine learning methods, comparing random forests and short-term memory algorithms (LSTM). The system development process includes several stages, namely Data Collection, Preprocessing, Model Training, and Testing using 136,800 datasets from 38 provinces in Indonesia in the last 10 years from BMKG, BPS, and visual cross data website. The comparison results show that the LSTM method performs better, with a difference of 1.16% compared to the Random Forest method, with a Mean Absolute Error value of 0.0345. This prediction system will help farmers determine the optimal planting time according to dynamic climate conditions.

title: Forecasting Spring Frost Frequency Based on Time Series Decomposition Model and Machine Learning
abstract: Spring frost can significantly impact agriculture. Predicting the occurrence frequency of spring frosts is crucial for reducing agricultural economic losses and ensuring food security. To reduce noise interference and improve prediction accuracy, we propose a time series decomposition model to extract the trend features of spring frost frequencies in the Northern Hemisphere, the primary agriculture planting region in the world, from 1948 to 2016. Based on the extracted trend features, we utilized random forest and deep neural network models to forecast future occurrence frequencies of spring frost in the Northern Hemisphere. The results show that spring frost frequencies will continue to increase in some Northern Hemisphere regions in the future.

title: Prediction of Environment Temperature for Grain Warehouses Based on LightGBM and Transformer
abstract: With the increasing prominence of global climate change and food security issues, the monitoring and control of grain warehouse environments have become particularly important. The external environment temperature has a direct impact on the internal temperature of grain warehouses and the safety of stored grain. Therefore, accurately predicting the external environment temperature of grain warehouses is crucial for formulating reasonable warehouse management strategies. Existing research mainly focuses on traditional statistical methods and simple machine learning models, which have limited performance in handling complex time series data. This study employs advanced deep learning models and optimizes input features through feature engineering to improve the accuracy of temperature predictions. The study proposes a method to generate new feature variables through feature fusion and validates its effectiveness. By adding new time series feature variables to the dataset, the model's understanding of time series data is enhanced, effectively reducing experimental errors. A comparative analysis of the predictive performance of various models identifies the best model and feature combination.

title: Dynamic Crop Recommendation System Using Geospatial and Weather Data
abstract: The agricultural sector, as a vital pillar of global food security, is increasingly subjected to climate variability, resource constraints, and land degradation. Traditional crop selection approaches, based on historical heuristics, do not account for dynamic geospatial and environmental conditions, eventually resulting in inefficient use of resources and productivity. This paper introduces the Dynamic Crop Recommendation System (DCRS), a novel machine learning-based system that incorporates real-time information on soil health, weather, and geospatial features to recommend optimal crop options for a given location and seasonal duration. The system utilizes ensemble machine learning models, time-series forecasting, and geospatial analysis to provide actionable recommendations to farmers. It also includes sustainability measures and Internet of Things (IoT) interfaces to enable real-time monitoring and decision-making. Field trials show a 23% increase in yield and a 31% reduction in resource utilization, showcasing the potential of the DCRS to revolutionize modern agricultural practices.

title: Monitoring Agricultural Stress Using Multi-Sensor Satellite Data and Machine Learning Techniques
abstract: Agriculture in Maharashtra is increasingly threatened by climate variability and recurring droughts, which adversely affect crop yields and food security. To address this, the present study develops a robust, data-driven framework integrating remote sensing and machine learning for monitoring and predicting agricultural stress across$\mathbf{3 4}$districts of the state. Multi-source satellite data from Sentinel-2, MODIS, and Landsat-8 were used to derive key vegetation indices-such as NDVI, NDWI, VCI, TCI, VHI, MSI, CVI, EVI, and SAVIcapturing indicators of plant vigor, water availability, and thermal conditions. A dataset comprising 2,722 satellite observations from 2015 to 2023 underwent preprocessing steps including cleaning, normalization, and feature engineering to prepare high-quality inputs for model training. The performance of multiple algorithms, including Random Forest, LightGBM, XGBoost, Bagging Tree, and Decision Tree, was compared alongside a hybrid Deep Neural Network-Long Short-Term Memory (DNN-LSTM) model designed to learn intricate spatialtemporal patterns. The DNN-LSTM outperformed other models, achieving an$\mathbf{R}^{\mathbf{2}}$of 0.992 and an RMSE of 1.415. Feature importance analysis highlighted Sentinel-2-based indices, particularly CVI, MSI, and NDWI, as the most critical predictors. The findings demonstrate that combining satellitederived indices with advanced AI methods enables accurate, early detection of drought and climate-induced stress, providing valuable insights for irrigation scheduling, crop management, and resource distribution, thereby fostering climate-resilient and sustainable agriculture in drought-prone regions.

title: Prediction in Shopping Apps: A Study on 1D CNN, Random Forest, ANN, and Hybrid Ensemble Performance
abstract: With the dynamic world of e-commerce, accurate price prediction is the key to improved customer satisfaction and improved pricing strategy. Traditional statistical methods are unable to cope with quick changes in markets, demanding flexible, data-driven methods. While some machine learning models like Random Forest, ANN, and 1D CNN have been individually applied to predict prices, there are not many studies comparing their relative performances and the efficacy of applying them in a hybrid ensemble model. This study bridges this gap by comparing and evaluating these three models with a hybrid ensemble method that enhances their performance. Using historical food data from the year 2007 to 2024, all the models were tested and trained in a uniform setting.
