All the models were exceedingly predictive ($\mathbf{R}^{2} \lt 0.95$), with the Hybrid Ensemble being top in performance ($\mathbf{R}^{\mathbf{2}} \boldsymbol{=} \mathbf{0. 9 8 7 6}$), showing its capability to minimize errors and increase robustness.

title: Deep Learning techniques applied to predict the irrigation prescription for potato crops in Boyacá
abstract: Potato crops are one of the fundamental productive chains for the economic development of Boyacá region, due to its importance in family nutrition and food security. The objective of this work was to improve the management of the water resources in a potato crop by applying deep learning algorithms to predict the irrigation prescription. Three deep learning models, such as one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1-DCNN), long short-term memory (LSTM), and a hybrid convolutional LSTM were reviewed and evaluated. The climatic variables of the potato crop were collected daily for three years, such as temperature, rain, water content in soil, and evapotranspiration, among others. The measured variables were provided by two meteorological stations located in the USoChicamocha Irrigation District. Deep learning models were trained and validated using Python®, calculating performance metrics. The CNN-LSTM model predicted the potato crop irrigation prescription with better precision in the training and validation dataset with MSE values less than 0,067 and RMSE values less than 0,258. The achievement of the CNN-LSTM algorithm had the highest coefficient of determination, obtaining a score of R2= 0,96. The proven deep learning techniques made it possible to predict the precision irrigation prescription in the studied potato crop, significantly improving the management of water resources. Deep learning techniques have served as a support instrument to assist farmers in decision-making and efficient management of water resources in irrigation planning at the farm level according to the measurement of crop variables.

title: CNN-Based Crop Disease Prediction for Enhanced Productivity
abstract: For the purpose of maintaining economic stability and providing food security, agriculture is absolutely necessary. Agricultural diseases, on the other hand, constitute a substantial obstacle, as they result in decreased yields and economic losses. This study aims to predict agricultural diseases by using Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) and Deep Learning (DL) methods to identify them accurately and efficiently. For the purpose of disease detection, the system examines the visual patterns included in crop leaf images. We utilize an extensive collection of images that depict both healthy and damaged leaves for training purposes. This approach allows the model to accurately differentiate between the various diseases. The CNN model achieves outstanding classification accuracy while simultaneously optimizing feature extraction without the need for human involvement. Through the use of mobile or internet applications, it makes an effort to assist farmers and agriculture professionals by providing real-time disease detection. It is possible for the identification to be exact and at the appropriate time, which enables prompt action to be taken to reduce losses and promote sustainable agricultural practices.

title: Design and implementaion of the edge-enabled UAV assisted sensing and analytics framework for precision agriculture
abstract: The pressing need for revolutionary farming practices is highlighted by the growing challenges posed climate change and increasing need for food worldwide. The combination of IoT sensors, drones, machine learning, and cloud computing is reviving traditional farming techniques, which are becoming less and less effective. In order to maximize irrigation, fertilization, and pest control, this study suggests a centralized system that makes use of real-time data on crop health, soil conditions, and environmental factors. Critical field data and high-resolution imagery are captured by UAVs outfitted with IoT sensors and high-resolution cameras, while Convolutional neural networks and support vector machines are two examples of machine learning algorithms that use trend analysis to forecast yield potential, disease outbreaks, and nutrient deficiencies. The results demonstrate significant improvements in crop productivity, resource efficiency, and environmental sustainability. The complexity of data integration is one issue that edge computing solutions address, enabling localized data processing and speedier decision-making. The study replicates the value of intelligent systems, such as targeted drones for spraying and analytics powered by AI in cutting waste and increasing accuracy. By bridging the gap between technology and practical farming needs, this approach fosters resilient, scalable agricultural systems that can satisfy the demands of future food security. The findings demonstrate the importance of affordable innovations and legal backing in democratizing small-scale farmers' access and advancing sustainable practices around the world.

title: Agri Foresight: Amplifying Crop Yield Prediction employing Computational Models and Explainable AI Techniques
abstract: Crop production is the backbone of agronomy, which not only contributes significantly to a country’s GDP but also generates employment. The agricultural sector is also a pivotal industry in eliminating global hunger. Crop production not only motivates research and development in agronomy but also induces technological advancements such as improved irrigation methods and precision farming. Machine learning (ML) is a powerful tool for crop prediction, helping farmers decide which crops to grow and how to manage resources effectively. Agriculture planning plays an important role in the development of the economy and the food security of a specific country. Selecting a particular crop for cultivation depends on various set of parameters including rainfall, temperature, soil conditions, and other factors that maximize the yield of that crop. The proposed methods will guide farmers in sowing suitable crops under the supervision of algorithms. In conclusion, this research involves single classifiers, bagging and boosting algorithms, ensemble models, and explainable AI techniques encompassing 22 discrete crop species to predict production outcomes. In bagging, Random Forest Classifier achieved 99% accuracy outperforming other ML algorithm Ensemble learning and explainable AI provide insights to aid the decision-making ability of the model. This research contributes to advancements in agricultural science by demonstrating the improved efficiency of combining distinct ML methodologies to tackle real-world challenges in crop yield prediction.

title: Predictive Analytics for Agriculture: Enhancing Crop and Fertilizer Decisions with ML and DL Models
abstract: Most Indians live in rural areas where agriculture is their main source of income. This sector is vital to the economy and feeds the growing population. Agriculture's relevance in India's economic growth and food security is highlighted by the growing population's need for food. Indian crop outputs varied by area, crop type, weather, and farming practices. Recent Indian agricultural harvests have fluctuated. Farmers grow the same crops without expanding their crop variety. Without knowing nutrient deficits and quantities, they use fertilizers. Machine learning-based crop advice is crucial in modern agriculture. It revolutionizes farming by using data to select crops. Machine Learning optimizes crop selection using soil, climate, and historical data. Farmers can boost yield and reduce risk by cultivating recommended crops and using suggested fertilizers. The proposed approach, ‘ Crop and Fertilizer Recommendation System (CFRS)’, uses machine learning methods to predict crop suitability depending on soil conditions, rainfall, and pesticide use. Farmers can determine which crop is best for their land and environmental conditions. This article forecasts suitable crops to boost crop productivity and help agriculture. Increased productivity is another benefit. Accurate recommendations boost yields, enhancing farmers' income and food security.

title: Comparative Analysis: Machine Learning vs. Artificial Neural Networks for Animal Disease Prediction
abstract: Accurate animal disease prediction is essential for improving livestock health and mitigating the impact of disease outbreaks, thereby safeguarding food security andreducing agricultural losses. This study presents a comparative analysis of two prominent approaches: Machine Learning (ML) and Artificial Neural Networks (ANN), for predicting animal diseases using symptoms and temperature data. Our experiments revealed that while both methods offer valuable insights, the ANN model, implemented with TensorFlow and Keras, outperforms ML in predictive accuracy. The Support Vector Classifier (SVC) achieved an accuracy of 79.59%, whereas the ANN model demonstrated superior accuracy and robustness, making it a more reliable tool for early disease detection and livestock health management.

title: Improving Agricultural Yield Prediction: An Empirical Comparison with Advanced Feature Selection Methods
abstract: Proper prediction of crop yields is important for agricultural and economic strategy. It is helpful in enabling farmers and policymakers to make superior decisions about resource allocation, improving output, and minimizing losses. In this paper, we propose a machine learning-based technique for developing a prediction system by forecasting crop yield using major determinants of soil quality, weather trends, and previous yield data. Investigation of these variables can allow us to provide data-driven insights that further improve decision-making and increase agricultural productivity. We compare various machine learning algorithms to identify the best one performing well in yield prediction. Our model is trained and tested with real-world agriculture data, which ascertains functioning for various types of climates and regions. The increased accuracy of predictions is achieved using different preprocessing techniques along with feature selection methods such as LASSO, Boruta, and MRMR to identify those variables that strongly influence yield. The results revealed that machine learning-based yield prediction models significantly outperform traditional methods, which prove to be viable for modern agriculture. We also show that using feature selection reduces computational burdens while maintaining high prediction accuracy. This work demonstrates the potential of AIpowered analytics in precision farming and sustainable food security. This article highlights the increasing role of AI in sustainable agriculture, helping farmers and decision-makers to arrive at wiser, more effective decisions.

title: A Study on Application of Model-Agnostic Explainable AI Techniques for Crop Recommendation
abstract: Sustainable agricultural practices play a major role in meeting global food security amid the rising impacts of climate change. Intelligent crop recommendation systems have become essential to assist farmers to make informed decisions in crop selection. Although Machine Learning (ML) models offer strong predictive capabilities, their black-box nature poses challenges in gaining trust and ensuring accountability. To address this gap, this study proposes a crop recommendation framework that combines tree-based ML classifiers with model-agnostic Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) techniques to enhance transparency and interpretability. The system predicts suitable crops using key weather features such as temperature, rainfall, humidity, and soil nutrients (N, P, K, and pH). Among the models evaluated, Random Forest (RF) achieved the top accuracy of 99.55 percent and selected for interpretability and fairness analysis. Subsequently, the system adopts three model-agnostic XAI methods, SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), Local Interpretable Model-Agnostic Explanations (LIME), and Partial Dependence Plots (PDP) to provide both local and global explanations of model behavior, focusing on the ‘rice’ crop. The result analysis demonstrated that rainfall, nitrogen, and humidity are the most influential features globally, with temperature consistently contributing in local instances. Fairness evaluation through SHAP summaries, LIME comparisons and counterfactual analysis demonstrated stable and justifiable predictions. Therefore, the proposed system shows strong potential for application in real-world agricultural decision support systems.

title: The analysis and prediction system of non-staple food price trends
abstract: As an important part of people’s daily life, the price change of non-staple food directly affects consumers’ purchasing power and living standard. In order to better analyze and predict the price of non-staple food, a non-staple food price trend analysis and prediction system is designed. This system cleans, transforms and integrates the data of some non-staple food prices, and visualizes the integrated data to obtain a series of intuitive and clear visualization charts. Comparing the three regression algorithms of multiple linear regression, Ridge regression and Lasso regression, the model with the best fit was selected and the price trend of many kinds of non-staple food was predicted respectively. Through testing, the results show that the scores of the test set of predictive models meet the expected effect.

title: Data-Driven Approaches for Enhancing Groundnut Yield Prediction: Integrating Climate, Soil, and Machine Learning Insights
abstract: Groundnut is a key oilseed crop with diverse applications in food, cooking oil, and animal feed, playing a crucial role in global agriculture. Accurate yield forecasting is essential for agricultural planning, resource optimization, and food security, yet it remains challenging due to dependence on multiple climatic and agronomic variables. This study leverages data-driven methodologies and machine learning to analyze the complex relationships between groundnut yield and influencing factors such as soil characteristics, farming practices, and climate. A comparative evaluation of forecasting techniques is presented, highlighting their strengths, limitations, and areas for improvement. The paper also identifies research gaps and proposes enhancements to support sustainable agriculture and climate-resilient groundnut production.

title: Comparing the Suitability of Traditional, Weighted, Fuzzy, and Modified k-Nearest Neighbor Methods in Predicting Rice Grain Types
abstract: Presently, the changing climatic patterns are affecting the growth of crops and quality of food, thereby threatening food security. In this context, machine learning methods are popular in identifying not only plant disease but also the type of grain. Among these approaches, k-Nearest Neighbors and its variants, deploying weights and fuzzy logics, are used widely due to their simplicity, efficiency, and ease of implementation. Considering this, the study presents a comparative analysis of Traditional, Weighted, Fuzzy, and Modified k-Nearest Neighbor approaches for predicting rice types, specifically Cammeo and Osmanick. In this binary classification, meant for predicting the kind of Turkish rice, the highest performance measures are 92.25% accuracy, 92.27% F-score, and 0.922 Area Under the Curve measure by Traditional k-Nearest Neighbor at k equals 9. With the same value of k, the second highest is Distance Weighted k-Nearest Neighbor, having an Area Under the Curve score of 0.916, F-score of 91.73%, and accuracy of 91.73%. Thereafter, Fuzzy k-Nearest Neighbor gained an accuracy of 91.076%, F-score of 91.10%, and Area Under the Curve measure of 0.91. The Modified k-Nearest Neighbor reached gained accuracy, F-, and Area Under the Curve scores of 88.18%, 88.27%, and 0.881, respectively. The work further delineates the appropriateness, advantages, and limitations of each methodology based on various characteristics. Additionally, these methodologies can also be effectively employed to predict adverse weather conditions, pest infestations, and assess soil quality, thereby reducing the possibilities of crop failures and enhancing overall profitability.

title: Evaluating Machine Learning Models for Wheat Yield Prediction in Amritsar District
abstract: Agriculture is pivotal for global food security and economic stability, yet optimizing yields remains a formidable challenge amidst variable climatic conditions. Accurate and timely crop yield prediction (CYP) is crucial for strategic decision-making, particularly in countries like India, where agri-culture is a lifeline for a substantial segment of the population and the economy. The advent of modern technology, notably machine learning (ML), offers promising solutions to the complexities of CYP. ML techniques provide an advanced alternative to conventional statistical methods, revealing complex patterns within datasets, particularly in cases involving nonlinear relationships. This study harnesses meteorological data to forecast wheat yields in the Amritsar district of Punjab. Through the application and comparison of six ML models, we endeavor to ascertain the most efficacious method for CYP. Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Root Mean Square Error (RMSE), Coefficient of Determination (R 2), and Mean Average Percentage Error (MAPE) are employed for model validation. Our results indicate that ensemble ML models significantly surpass linear ML models, demonstrating the lowest error metrics. An exhaustive comparative analysis of all models is conducted, providing valuable insights to the readers. Consequently, this study underscores the potential of ML techniques to augment CYP accuracy. The integration of cutting-edge technologies into agricultural practices enables stakeholders to make enlightened decisions, thereby fostering sustainable agricultural production and bolstering food security in India and beyond.

title: Comparative Machine Learning Framework for Rainfall Forecasting and Agricultural Loss Estimation
abstract: Because of the growing unpredictability of the weather, which can affect food security and productivity, the consequences of climate change are no longer speculative; every farmer in South Asia is starting to suffer the ramifications in their fields. In the two most susceptible districts of Bangladesh, Rajshahi and Ishwardi, the comparative machine learning method presented in this study aims to predict rainfall and identify regions at risk of agricultural impacts due to climate change. We examine the performance of four models: the Prophet model, ARIMA, Random Forest, and XGBoost, using 48 years of historical rainfall data (1976–2024). With an R-squared value of 0.89, Random Forest displayed the best accuracy, exceeding both standard time series and boosting-based approaches while efficiently capturing non-seasonal trends. On the other hand, XGBoost performed poorly, possibly due to the difficulty in fitting noisy, small-scale meteorological data. To classify years as droughts or floods, we apply a conventional anomaly detection technique that utilizes z-scores (1.5 standard deviations) in conjunction with predictive modeling. It is feasible to identify problematic years and regions by using these characteristics, which are linked to historical periods of agricultural displacement. The findings are more accessible and helpful when simplified visual maps of climate-induced risk validate the relationship between the projected anomalies and previous crop failures. The suggested method would provide a scientifically informed tool for climate resilience planning, agricultural planning, and early warning systems. The objective of preserving vulnerable livelihoods during a climate transition is achieved by integrating the three aspects of this architecture, namely translating the long-term records of the meteorological system into risk information that agronomists, policymakers, and humanitarian actors can utilize.

title: Enhancing Potato Leaf Disease Classification Using a Modified CNN with XAI
abstract: Leaf diseases significantly impact potato cultivation and cause considerable harvest loss if not detected and treated promptly. Existing traditional diagnosis techniques are often imprecise and time-consuming, leading to delayed treatment. This research presents a robust deep learning-based system utilizing a custom CNN architecture, based on the modified EfficientNet-B7, for the precise identification of potato leaf disease, thereby addressing the shortcomings of established identification procedures. To enhance interpretability and foster trust in automated decisions, the model integrates explainable AI techniques, specifically Grad-CAM++ and LIME. This model was built using an EfficientNet B7-based CNN, which was refined and cross-validated on a dataset of 1,500 categorized images of three classes. Essential initial processing stages, such as scaling, normalization, and data augmentation, were implemented, and effectiveness was thoroughly tested using 5-fold cross-validation. The proposed model achieved a 97.33% test accuracy, along with a precision of 96.76%. These indicators demonstrate the model’s robust ability to recognize categories of potato leaf disease. The observation suggests this tool offers a significant, early direction aid for farmers. Its application is predicted to minimize yield damage, provide economic advantage to farmers, and eventually foster sustainable cultivation and global food security.

title: A Federated Learning Framework for Sustainable Boro Rice Yield Prediction Using Multi-Regional Agro-Climatic Data
abstract: Boro rice, the primary dry-season crop in Bangladesh, plays a critical role in national food security. Accurate prediction of yield is critical in the context of escalating climate uncertainty and mounting population pressure. This study will propose a federated machine learning model that leverages 25 years (2000-2024) of agro-climatic and production data across six major divisions of Bangladesh to predict Boro rice yield. A novel dataset was built from satellite-extracted environmental characteristics and ground-truth yield information from the Bangladesh Bureau of Statistics and NASA POWER. The local-level performance of ten regression models was compared, in which SGD regressor was the best performer(up to R2of 0.978). A Federated Averaging (FedAvg) approach was used for decentralized learning with linear SGD regressors while preserving privacy of the data and improving generalization. The global federated model had convergence with lesser validation MSE (0.0953) and higher R2(0.871) than any single-division model, outperforming local models. The addition of federated learning to rich agro-climatic data offers a scalable, privacy-protecting solution for crop yield estimation, with impactful agro-planning and climate resilience implications for Bangladesh.

title: Deep Learning-Based Classification of Banana Plant Leaf Diseases
abstract: Banana is among the most important food crops supporting the agricultural economy of tropical and subtropical regions. Nevertheless, several diseases are considered as threat to the productivity and quality of banana. The commonly used detection approaches based on manual detection is tedious, subjective, and not suitable for the large-scale agricultural disease detection. In this paper, we propose a deep learning model based automated classification system to classify different diseases of banana plants using image processing techniques. We use the CNNs to process the leaf images and to predict accurately the types of diseases. The approach consists of image preprocessing followed by feature extraction, then classification using proprietary and pretrained CNNs such as Custom CNN, InceptionV3, ResNet50 and EfficientNetB0. The developed system provides a scalable, precise, and fast resolution to detect diseases at an early stage, thereby facilitating in time intervention to reduce the crop damage. This research highlights the contribution of AI to improving agricultural diagnostics, with the aim of supporting food security.

title: Crop Yield Prediction Using Temporal Data
abstract: Agriculture is the backbone of many countries throughout the world and forecasting crop yield is critical for food security. Different types of data such as meteorological data and field data combined with temporal data are the methods of estimating the yield. One of the major challenges is to develop a multi-resource data-based estimating model using machine learning techniques. Throughout planting to harvest, several investigations have been undertaken. Researchers have not focused on the impact of time period and different agricultural seasons on yield prediction so far. The outcome of the current study reveals that estimating outcomes vary based on temporal training conditions and agricultural zones. Integrating machine learning and multi-source data have been suggested by the findings of this study. A strong tool for yield prediction could be developed. Here we have considered two crops namely rice and onion using Indian government website. The region Karnataka state is chosen. The outcome of this project can be used by agriculture department to decide crop yield. The neural network algorithm provides the best result showed of 0.3133 mean absolute error.

title: Deep Learning-Based Grapevine Leaf Classification Using a Fine-Tuned VGG19 Architecture
abstract: This study work traverses the classification of photographs of the grapevine leaf by means of deep learning algorithms applied under the fine-tuned VGG19 model. There are five well established classifications of grapevine leaves: Ak, Ala_Idris, Buzgulu, Dimnit and Nazli. The Kaggle open-source platform provides the comprehensive collection of tagged grapevine leaf photos. We used preprocessing techniques like downsizing, normalising, and picture augmentation to increase the model execution. With five convolutional layers and four max pool layers to efficiently address the complex leaf characteristics, the refined VGG19 model is built. The model was effectively generalised hence it validates with an 80:10:10 split of the data. It comprised the Adam optimiser and a loss function measuring the variations between the predicted and actual groups. Reaching an accuracy of $80 \%$, the model has demonstrated its ability to exactly classify the images of grapevine leaves. The detailed study through loss and accuracy graphs and the intricate confusion matrix emphasizes both the complete performance and the areas of prospective improvement. This work emphasizes the effectiveness of using deep learning models, including finely calibrated VGG19, for the automation of grapevine diagnosis, so allowing a consistent solution for exact grapevine leaf classifying. Resilient agricultural systems and sustainable development are supported by this effort in line with sustainable farming practices, innovation in food security, climate adaptation, resource economy, and environmental protection.

title: Regional Crop Yield Forecasting Using a Stacked Hybrid Model with Temporal Spatial Feature Fusion
abstract: Accurate and region-specific crop yield forecasting is vital for optimizing resources, guiding decisions, and reducing risks from climate variability. This paper proposes a stacked hybrid learning model that fuses temporal weather patterns and spatial satellite features using LSTM and CNN, alongside Linear Regression and Random Forest, with Gradient Boosting as the meta-learner. A region-specific dataset covering environmental, soil, crop management, and market factors across five seasons was used for evaluation. The model achieved an RMSE of $\mathbf{1 6. 9 2 ~ t} \boldsymbol{/} \mathbf{h a}$, an MAE of $\mathbf{1 3. 1 2 ~ t} \boldsymbol{/} \mathbf{h a}$, and an $\mathbf{R}^{\mathbf{2}}$ of 0.89, outperforming the baseline approaches as well as recent state-of-the-art methods. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of integrating deep learning with traditional machine-learning techniques in an ensemble framework, providing a scalable and adaptable solution for precision agriculture and long-term food security.

title: Winter Wheat Crop Yield Prediction on Multiple Heterogeneous Datasets using Machine Learning
abstract: Winter wheat is one of the most important crops in the United Kingdom, and crop yield prediction is essential for the nation's food security. Several studies have employed machine learning (ML) techniques to predict crop yield on a county or farm-based level. The main objective of this study is to predict winter wheat crop yield using ML models on multiple heterogeneous datasets, i.e., soil and weather on a zone-based level. Experimental results demonstrated their impact when used alone and in combination. In addition, we employ numerous ML algorithms to emphasize the significance of data quality in any machine-learning strategy.

title: Enhancing Crop Productivity: Integrated Solutions for Crop Yield, Crop Recommendation, and Crop Disease Management
abstract: The paper presents an integrated approach for crop disease prediction, crop recommendation, and crop yield prediction to address the challenges in modern agriculture. The research leverages diverse agricultural datasets, including historical crop disease records, soil composition data, climate variables, and past crop yield records. Machine learning algorithms, such as decision trees, support vector machines, and neural networks, are utilized to develop predictive models for each component. The integration of these models creates a unified platform that facilitates seamless information flow and decision-making for farmers and agronomists. The system's performance is assessed using various evaluation metrics, ensuring the accuracy and effectiveness of disease detection, personalized crop recommendations, and crop yield forecasts. The experimental outcomes contribute to advancing sustainable farming practices and enhancing agricultural productivity. The proposed integrated system holds great promise in revolutionizing modern agriculture and ensuring food security in a changing world.

title: Climate Change Impacts on Food Supply in India with Machine Learning Predictions
abstract: As a developing country, India is significantly impacted by climate change. Its agricultural production is disturbed with an immediate threat to food security. The rainfall pat-terns are being affected by the increase in temperatures, and changing climate variability affect crop productivity, thereby forcing urgent efforts of prediction and mitigation for these impacts. This paper proposes machine learning-based predictive modeling for agrarian output expectations reliant upon climatic conditions, historical climatic parameters fluctuations, crop yield and socioeconomic parameters within India[16]. The machine learning approaches will comprise Random Forest and Autore-gressive Distributed Lag(ARDL), based on Python, Scikit-Iearn, and Statsmodels. The basic metrics for evaluation of these models are MAE and Mean Squared Error. This dataset will be historical records set up by the government on temperature, rainfall, fertil-izer application, and crop yields, assuming historical consistency and fouling to regional adaptability. The paper undertakes three stages of data preprocessing and feature selection, model training and validation, and testing on unseen data. The most relevant climatic factors related to yield variations are those of an increasing temperature and the changed rainfall patterns, with different models performing better than others in forecasting those yield variations. Improvement of model accuracy, together with the remedy of data uncertainty, will enable better prediction and consequently agricultural planning and policymaking. The paper adds the ML paradigm into agriculture which aims at reducing climate peril, augmenting food security, and providing scalable solutions to redress data quality perceptions by considering the regional differences effectively. Climate change presented Indian agricultural productivity with the biggest challenge. This research discusses the effect of the change in climate trends on farm outputs and suggests a machine learning predictive model in terms of Random Forest and ARDL models. Historical yield and climatic data were preprocessed and modelled based on performance measures such as MAE and RMSE. Random Forest was more consistent and accurate compared to ARDL. These comments outline the precision of evidence-based models in facilitating agricultural planning and minimizing food security threats. Random Forest model outperforms the ARDL model.

title: An Investigation into Farming Suitability Prediction using Advanced ML Models
abstract: In recent years, there has been a surge of interest in utilizing machine learning (ML) techniques to tackle the challenge of predicting farming suitability. This research presents a novel approach to predicting farming suitability holistically, by employing a hybrid of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks. LSTMs excel at extracting temporal sequences from climatic and soil data, thus ensuring complete prediction insights. On the other hand, CNNs excel at extracting spatial characteristics from satellite and landscape imagery. Our unified model was trained on data from a variety of environmental types and weather records spanning several agricultural regions over the years. The findings reveal that the combined CNN-LSTM model out- performed the individual ML models in predicting agricultural suitability, with greater accuracy and fewer prediction errors. Furthermore, the model exhibited adaptability in low-historical-data regions. The synergistic effect of CNN and LSTM not only provides new avenues for research in agricultural ML applications, but also demonstrates the potential of hybrid models. Considering the growing emphasis on sustainable agriculture and efficient land use, such predictive models will play a crucial role in ensuring food security and sustainable agricultural practices in the coming decades.

title: Optimized Random Forest with Explainable AI for Accurate Boro Rice Yield Prediction and Real-Time Web App
abstract: A precise prediction of rice yield is vital when it comes to planning of food security and decisions making in agricultural fields. This paper involves an elaborate machine learning model to forecast the Boro rice yield by using a data set consisting of$\text{4, 4 8 0}$records and 43 agricultural, environmental, and soil characteristics. We compared five regression models: Linear Regression, Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, Support Vector Regression and K-Nearest Neighbors, optimizing hyperparameters using cross-validation grid search. The selection of feature was done using a mutual information analysis, and the most significant indicators are considered the inputs fertilizers (urea, muriate of potash, DAP), the characteristics of the soil (pH, texture, moisture) and the rainfall. The optimized Random Forests model performed better, with$\mathrm{R} \hat{\mathrm{2}}=\text{0. 9 9 9 9}$,$\text{R M S E}=\text{0. 0 0 0}$, and the computational time of 0.01 seconds. Explainable AI methods such as SHAP and Morris sensitivity analysis offered an insight into the model decision process, where it was found that yield estimates are strongly affected by soil category, cultivated area, and fertilizer usage data. A practical web application was designed to ease its use in the field, where farmers and agricultural planners can have real-time estimation of their yields. The presented model shows a great enhancement of the available methods, as it yields high scores in accuracy, as well as availability of interpretation on sustainable agricultural management.

title: Gross Paddy Yield Estimation Using a Lightweight Deep Learning Model
abstract: One of the important roles of a government is to ensure food security among its citizens, which is highlighted in the second Sustainable Development Goal - Zero Hunger. Therefore, the government needs to effectively monitor staple food production and distribution so that the supply always meets the demand of their citizen. In Asia, rice is the most important staple food that is produced by many countries but only a few of them managed to export the rice due to no surplus compared to the local consumption. In order to effectively monitor the paddy plantation, many government agencies have explored the usage of remote sensing imagery due to the main advantage of wide coverage areas with a low-cost repeated sample sensing platform. However, manually monitoring the paddy fields is a tedious process that needs to be automated, especially for the task of gross paddy yield estimation. Therefore, this paper proposed a novel lightweight deep regressor network to predict the gross paddy yield using Pleiades satellite imagery. In this study, a single day information of days after planting is used to model the yield prediction, which has been set at the age of 60 days. The ground truth has been manually annotated by the field officers, and organized in the MakGeoPadi system. The base of the regressor model is MobileNet V2, which has been enhanced by using optimal attention mechanism embedding. Five variants of the proposed model have been analyzed that differ in terms of the embedding placement and the set of convolutional filters used in the embedding. The best results with a mean accuracy of 0.715 is obtained when the embedding is placed at the second inverted residual block of the regressor model with a set of (32,64,128) convolutional filters used in the attention mechanism. The results show that the proposed model performance exceeds the other benchmarked models and is suitable to be implemented for predicting the paddy yield.

title: Paddy Land Abandonment Detection Using Time Series Sentinel-1 SAR and BiLSTM
abstract: Paddy land abandonment poses significant challenges to food security, agricultural sustainability, and land-use planning, particularly in regions experiencing socioeconomic and climatic stress. This study proposes a deep learning-based framework to detect abandoned paddy fields using time-series Sentinel-1 Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) data in the Udupi district of coastal Karnataka, India. VH-polarized backscatter coefficients from the primary cultivation period (June to December) across four years (2021–2024) were used as input to a Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) model. Ground truth data enabled the classification of paddy fields into active and two temporally distinct abandonment classes. The model achieved an overall accuracy of 96.81%, with high class-wise F1-scores and a Cohen’s Kappa value of 0.9516 indicating strong predictive performance and inter-class agreement. The proposed approach demonstrates the utility of SAR time-series and recurrent neural networks for monitoring agricultural land-use transitions in complex agro-ecological landscapes. The results highlight the potential for scalable, real-time abandonment detection systems to support targeted policy interventions and sustainable land management strategies.

title: Kolmogorov–Arnold Networks for Marine Aquaculture Site Suitability: A Case Study in the Southeastern Sea of Tamil Nadu
abstract: Aquaculture plays a pivotal role in ensuring food security and boosting coastal economies, yet its sustainable growth relies on precise site suitability assessments driven by complex marine dynamics. This study introduces a deep learning-based framework using Kolmogorov–Arnold Networks (KANs) to evaluate aquaculture zone suitability along the southeastern coast of Tamil Nadu, India. The model integrates remote sensing–derived oceanographic parameters—including Chlorophyll-a, Colored Dissolved Organic Matter (CDOM), Sea Surface Temperature (SST), Suspended Particulate Matter (SPM), and Dissolved Oxygen (DO)—sourced from NASA MODIS and VIIRS datasets. The KAN model dynamically captures nonlinear relationships and spatial variability across eight predefined coastal zones, from Nagapattinam to Pondicherry. Among the zones, Tharangambadi (Zone 3) emerged as the most suitable location, achieving the highest prediction accuracy of 83.2%, followed closely by Karaikal and Cuddalore. SST showed the best model performance, while CDOM and DO also demonstrate strong predictive accuracy above 80%. Compared to conventional GIS-MCDA techniques, KAN offers superior interpretability, adaptability, and performance in complex oceanographic environments. The results highlight the potential of KANs as a robust, scalable, and data-driven decision-support tool for marine aquaculture zoning and sustainable coastal resource management.

title: Advances in Machine Learning for Crop Yield Prediction: A Comprehensive Review of Techniques, Trends, and Challenges
abstract: Addressing food security amidst climate change and population growth requires precise crop yield prediction models that surpass the limitations of traditional approaches. In this field, machine learning has become a potent instrument, utilizing comprehensive data from soil metrics, climatic variables, and crop characteristics to enhance forecasting accuracy. This review examines the application of ML algorithms such as Artificial Neural Networks, Random Forests, and Gradient Boosting Decision Trees for predicting crop productivity. Out of 200 articles initially reviewed from major databases, 47 were rigorously selected based on relevance and methodological rigor. The findings provide an in-depth analysis of ML’s efficacy in predicting yields across diverse agricultural environments, identifying trends, key challenges, and limitations related to data heterogeneity, regional specificity, and interpretability. This paper aims to guide researchers in advancing ML-driven yield prediction, particularly in integrating IoT technologies and improving model generalizability, hence encouraging precision farming and sustainable agriculture.

title: Role of Machine Learning Techniques in Agriculture to Enhance Crop Production
abstract: Agriculture is the primary engine of any civilization. It provides food and fiber, serving food security and supporting economic growth. Since rising populations and extreme climatic conditions are straining traditional practices in farming, it threatens society through increased resource competition, rise in food prices and urban-rural migration. To encounter this issue, machine learning offers a wide range of alternatives, such as combining environmental data to boost yield forecasts, LSTMs and transformers synchronizing precise irrigation schedule with shifting weather, CNN/YOLO image models detect leaf diseases early, IoT based SVMs optimize water usage, GAN augmented hyperspectral data enhance soil-type and moistures mapping and RFID sensors to monitor livestock locomotion. Together these techniques promise to reduce wastage and boost resilience and better use of resources. Our motivation in writing this paper is to accelerate translating these technological innovations to daily practices in the field of agriculture.

title: Integrated Smart Agriculture and Solar Monitoring System Using IoT and Deep Learning Techniques
abstract: The intersection of renewable energy and datadriven agriculture has led to innovative solutions to tackle pressing challenges in energy optimization, food security, and climate adaptation. This study presents a comprehensive, integrated system that encompasses three major components: an IoT-enabled dual-axis solar tracking system, a machine learning- based crop and yield prediction module, and an automated solar panel defect detection model utilizing MobileNetV3. The goal is to improve solar energy efficiency, support farmers with predictive analytics, and ensure continuous operation of solar infrastructure by timely detection of panel defects. The system leverages Arduino IoT cloud integration, Random Forest and XGBoost algorithms for crop analytics, and a transfer-learning approach in CNNs for classification tasks, achieving high accuracy and reliability across all modules.

title: Carbon Price Prediction in the European Market using Deep Learning
abstract: Greenhouse gas emissions (GHG) generated by human activities have negative impacts such as climate change, global warming, threats to food security, natural disasters, and rising sea levels. Several countries have implemented measures to reduce GHG emissions, including reforestation, environmentally friendly industries, and providing incentives to initiatives that reduce GHG emissions. A carbon price prediction is provided to optimize carbon incentives for investors. Carbon price fluctuation on global market conditions requires methods to predict the prices accurately. The methods utilize carbon price data from European Energy Exchange (EEX) carbon market. The data employed in this research encompasses the closing prices of carbon. This research applies two algorithms, Deep Multilayer Perceptron (DMLP) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), to forecast carbon prices in time series predictions. These models use the closing price variable. The simulation results show that the Deep Multilayer Perceptron method is more accurate than the Long Short-Term Memory method. The method with higher performance will result in better risk measurement of carbon price.

title: Transfer learning on VGG16 for the Classification of Potato Leaves Infected by Blight Diseases
abstract: According to the FAO of the UN, availability, access, utilization, and stability are the four pillars of food security that largely depend on sufficient, safe, and nutritious food. Detecting plant disease in advance might be a measure of resilience to the future disruption or unavailability of food supply. Due to the notable performance through highly accurate mechanization, deep learning-based methods have been applied to automatically identify and diagnose plant disease that can improve efficiency and productivity. The work prioritizes Transfer Learning of VGG16 for predicting potato blight disease. The model’s weights are pretrained on ImageNet, which can be extracted from specific features of small datasets. The implemented approach presents a significant performance improvement on a self-prepared dataset. After completing the necessary training and testing process, 96.88% accuracy was achieved by the model. Experimental results are compared with well-established models, which concludes that the model performs better in classifying potato leaves blight diseases.

title: Artificial Intelligence-Driven Model for Evaluating the Economic Impact of Cross-Border Dam Water Release in Nigeria
abstract: The annual water release from the Lagdo Dam into the Benue River, which flows into Nigeria, is one of the causes of the potential flooding in several Nigerian states. Consequently, this has led to the annual displacement of a large number of people, the destruction of infrastructure, and a severe consequence on livelihoods and food security, all of which have a significant effect on Nigeria's economy. This study addresses these issues by developing and applying artificial intelligence (AI) models to assess the economic impacts of cross-border dam water release in Nigeria. The study designed a multi-task learning system capable of forecasting economic repercussions on Nigeria, utilizing hydrological, meteorological, and socioeconomic data. The study adopted a machine learning model to capture the interaction between the economic and environmental variables. The findings demonstrate the model's good predicted accuracy and consistent performance, emphasizing its effectiveness. This study recommends that artificial intelligence has great potential in disaster management, contributing to Nigeria's long-term growth and resistance to climate change-induced disasters.

title: Weather-Driven Machine Learning Decision Support for Rice Cultivation Suitability in Bangladesh
abstract: Rice (Oryza sativa) underpins food security in Bangladesh, yet its yields are highly vulnerable to daily weather fluctuations. This paper introduces a machine-learning decision-support framework that predicts daily rice-cultivation suitability using four key weather parameters: average daytime temperature (19–40°C), average nighttime temperature (16–23 °C), daily sunshine hours ( 0–12h ), and daily rainfall (0–50mm). We first generated a 10000 -sample synthetic dataset, labeled "suitable" or "unsuitable" according to agronomic thresholds for flowering (22–23°C ), grain filling ( 20–21°C ), and seasonal water requirements (80–180 cm ). Six classifiers—Logistic Regression, SVM, k-NN, Random Forest, XGBoost, and LightGBM—were trained and benchmarked via stratified 5-fold cross-validation, with ensemble methods achieving F1≥0.99 and AUC ≥0.99 on synthetic data. Without retraining, these models were then applied to ten years (2013–2022) of real-world weather records from Data.gov.bd, yielding F1≈0.95 and AUC ≈ 0.96, which confirms robust generalization. Finally, the framework integrates real-time forecasts from the OpenWeather API to deliver daily suitability assessments and tailored agronomic recommendations—such as optimized irrigation schedules and variety selection—thereby enabling scalable, climate-smart rice farming in data-scarce environments.

title: Monocot Crop Yield Prediction using Sentinal-2 Satellite Data
abstract: Agriculture is the life force of many countries throughout the world, and forecasting yields is critical to guaranteeing food security. Integrating remote sensing data in addition with field data and meteorological data is one method of estimating a production. For many years, the research has been conducted for agricultural areas all over the world. Different parameters such as rainfall, temperature, soil type and pH are taken into consideration. Recent research has shown that remote sensing is an effective way for estimating yields, and that machine learning, particularly deep learning, can predict a decent forecast by combining multisource datasets including such temperature data, Satellite data, soil data, and etc. Addition of remote sensing imagery has a direct impact on accuracy of the models. For many models, both ground truth data and MODIS NDVI pictures are obtained from several sources. Crop production prediction from planting through harvest has been the subject of numerous research. The impact of various time intervals on yield prediction has yet to be studied. The results of the current study show that estimating outcomes vary based on temporal training conditions and agricultural zones. With the use of the Normalized Difference Vegetative Index (NDVI), remote sensing has made identifying spatial patterns and vegetation much easier. This research presents a system for predicting Monocot Crop Yield utilizing the XGBoost algorithm to extract trends by analyzing various factors such as NDVI, EVI, SAVI, Temperature, Precipitation, and so on. The results of this study show that the Monocot Crop yield prediction utilizing the XGBoost algorithm has a coefficient of variance of RMSE 1.59.

title: Decoding Disease Intensity: Predicting Pythium Severity with CNN-SVM Hybrid Models
abstract: A precise and prompt evaluation is required to establish efficient disease control measures because Pythium disease poses a serious hazard to agricultural products. The severity levels of the Pythium disease in crops are divided into five classes in this study report, with 1-20%, 20-40%, 40-60%, 60-80%, and 80-100% being the most severe. To extract useful information from high-resolution photos of infected crop samples, the CNN model consists of three convolutional layers, three max-pooling layers, and one fully connected layer. Precision ranges from 95.22% to 98.31%, recall ranges from 95.49% to 96.79%, and F1-Score ranges from 95.74% to 97.48% are excellent results for each severity level class, according to their evaluation of the model's performance using these measures. The model's capacity for producing accurate predictions is further confirmed by its total accuracy of 96.99%. By allowing fast disease severity assessment and directing educated decision-making for efficient disease control, their CNN-based strategy has significant potential to revolutionize agricultural practices. Even though their work represents a substantial improvement in plant pathology, the model still has to be validated using a variety of datasets and real-world situations to determine its robustness and applicability. Advanced deep-learning methods for disease monitoring can help to improve global food security and enable sustainable agricultural production.

title: CropOptimizer: Intelligent Crop Forecasting and Decision Support System
abstract: CropOptimizer is an innovative crop forecasting and decision support system designed to revolutionize agricultural practices. Comprising five key modules—crop recommendation, fertilizer suggestion, disease detection, weather forecasting, and market price tracking—CropOptimizer combines modern technologies to help farmers make informed decisions. The crop recommendation module, leveraging XGBoost, uses soil, climate, and nutrient data to select suitable crops that maximize production potential. The fertilizer suggestion module provides specialized guidance based on specific crop and soil characteristics, ensuring effective nutrient management through XGBoost. The disease detection module employs deep learning with ResNet-9 for image processing to identify plant diseases from leaf images, followed by specific treatment recommendations, achieving high accuracy. Weather forecasting offers a 7-day forecast, including rainfall predictions, based on plant type, state, and city through an API. Market price tracking provides live market prices for various crops, enabling farmers to make informed selling decisions. By integrating these components, CropOptimizer increases crop yield and sustainability, fostering a more resilient agricultural ecosystem and improving food security and economic success.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Agricultural Transformation for Enhancing Food Security through Precision Farming
abstract: Growing worldwide consumption of food security has laid the foundation to make farming methods more effective and sustainable. Machine learning (ML), which falls under the broader AI framework, has become an innovative enabler for precision farming—we facilitate the continuous analysis of data, the use of this data for modelling Outlooks to support farming activity, and manage resources to improve farming yields. This paper discusses the Implication of AI in precision farming as a concept that enhances crop yield forecast, resource utilisation, and the mitigations of farming hurt on the environment. The proposed AI models also use IoT sensors, remote sensing, and machine learning to decide on the use of water, fertilizers, and pesticides. The simulations reveal quite encouraging gains to the precision of yield accuracies, optimization of resources, and reduction of costs. The investigated AI applications in farming demonstrate a significant capacity to cut the farming manifold and environmental emissions, thereby indicating an ability to support the longer-term health and growth of farming and food security for the globe. However, issues like data quality, the accuracy of models used and declaration or adoption have become issues yet to settle. The study indicates that there is hope for the modern agriculture as being revolutionized by AI and points to the ways of improving the use of AI further.

title: Revolutionizing Agriculture through Leaf Disease Prediction in Plants
abstract: India's agricultural strength is hindered by plant diseases due to limited understanding of disease markers and remedies. Deep learning, particularly Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), offers hope for enhanced disease detection in agriculture. Our proposal centers on CNNs for accurate plant disease identification, streamlining the process. Urgency arises from economic repercussions and global food security. Deep learning is employed in various sectors such as healthcare, finance, and agriculture. Its applications range from identifying diseases, classifying weeds and leaves, to predicting soil moisture levels. The survey tackles current trends and objections in deep learning for plant disease prediction, guiding aspiring researchers. Machine Learning (ML) and Deep Learning (DL) tools replace costly visual inspection. Our study deploys ML algorithms including K Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Logistic Regression, Random Forest(RF) algorithm, Naïve Bayes, Decision Trees, and Support Vector Machines(SVM) on a diverse crop image dataset. A CNN-based system, coupled with ML soil analysis, suggests fitting crops, enabling informed planting choices. Classifier comparison validates Support Vector Classifier's (SVC) superiority. Swift disease detection is critical for food demand and economic growth. This study proposes a modern evaluation system using ML and pre-trained models (VGG16, InceptionV3, ResNet152) on datasets to classify plant diseases. IoT further augments disease and yield prediction, vital for modern agriculture.

title: Predictive Model for Affordable Greenhouse Operations
abstract: Food insecurity is an increasing problem worldwide due to the effects of climate change and lack of access to water. Lower agricultural outputs lead to higher food prices, which only exacerbates food insecurity. Technology innovations that can help mitigate some of these issues, such as affordable greenhouses, are increasingly being used across Sub-Saharan Africa. Greenhouses help reduce water consumption and often produce higher crop yields. This article describes a predictive model that assesses the probability of success for different use cases for greenhouses. By utilizing inputs (water accessibility, level of agricultural expertise, soil quality, etc.) and by taking into account the modes of greenhouse operation (whether crops are grown to maturity and harvest, seedlings are transplanted to open-air fields, etc.), the model forecasts outputs (mainly net yield) to better predict the success of a given greenhouse. Each input is identified and discussed in terms of how it affects the greenhouse and the four modes of operation are outlined, including how they each affect outputs. The outputs are then described followed by several scenarios that can be used to better understand the model. This article is of interest to innovators and entrepreneurs engaged in greenhouse farming as well as nonprofits and agricultural ministries trying to support them. The real value of this article is not in predicting yields as much as understanding the relationships between the inputs, outputs, and environmental parameters for different modes of operation and use cases.

title: Mining Spectral Libraries with Machine Learning for Soil Sensing in Low Resource Settings
abstract: Smallholder farmers and extension workers in sub-Saharan Africa have limited access to the soil information needed to improve crop yields, and therefore boost incomes and improve food security. A promising approach to provide this information at farm level is a low-cost optical spectroscopy device and an accompanying decision support application. This paper describes our efforts to explore spectral libraries, both publicly accessible and acquired through our own efforts, to define the instrument specifications and data handling procedures for such an approach. Spectral ranges throughout the mid-infrared (MIR) and near-infrared (NIR) regions and spectral resolution pertinent to available hardware technologies were evaluated. Given the complex physical-chemical properties of soil samples, numerous preprocessing strategies were applied prior to regression with partial least squares, support vector machine, and multilayer perceptron neural network (MLPNN) models for predicting relevant soil properties. The experiments with existing spectral datasets demonstrated that the MLPNN approach outperformed other approaches most consistently for soil property prediction, and that the MIR region offers better performance than NIR, even with truncated spectral ranges and degraded spectral resolutions. At this time, however, there are hardware limitations for MIR systems that prevent a low cost device from collecting acceptable signals, thus making an NIR solution more appealing overall.

title: Integrating Sentinel-2 Imagery and Machine Learning for Crop Damage Evaluation in Thai Agriculture
abstract: This research enhances food security and sustainable agriculture by improving crop damage assessments, aligning with SDG 2: Zero Hunger and SDG 13: Climate Action. Accurate damage evaluations can promote growth in Thailand's agribusiness sector, where over 30% of the population works in agriculture, frequently affected by drought. The goal is to create a Crop Damage Assessment Index (CDAI) model for droughtaffected areas with the assumption underlying this research is that vegetation indices derived from satellite imagery can effectively monitor and predict crop damage. We are analyzing over 5 million damaged and non-damaged plots across nine provinces to train the model. Using 9 vegetation indices and the Random Forest machine learning technique, the model distinguished between damaged and undamaged plots with Sentinel-2 satellite imagery at 20 meters resolution. MNDWI stands out as the most influential index, especially for maize and rice. NDVI is notable for sugarcane, while REIP is crucial for cassava. Other indices, such as NDWI, S2REP, and SAVI, show varying contributions. These tailored indices support the model's strong performance, with ROC values of 86% for rice, 91% for maize, 89% for cassava, and 86% for sugarcane. These results highlight the reliability of the CDAI model in distinguishing drought-affected plots. The CDAI model supports farmers and agricultural officers with accurate assessments, essential for drought management and fair compensation. Accessible via the GISTDA platform (cropsdrought.gistda.or.th), it aids decision-making without requiring GIS knowledge, though ongoing validation and data updates are necessary for improved efficiency.

title: Assessing the Effectiveness of Deep Learning Approaches in Forecasting Cassava Leaf Diseases
abstract: In the Philippines, cassava-one of the most crucial crops-faces significant threats from various diseases, which can severely impact its cultivation and yield. To ensure food security, it is vital to detect these diseases early before they escalate. Disease detection methodologies are currently based on fuzzy logic and the expertise of farmers. This study proposes an automated system utilizing pretrained neural network models, specifically inspired by convolutional neural network techniques, to handle fuzzy data and identify diseases. The proposed system successfully identified anthocyanin and red leach using neural network models. An EfficientNetB3 model, featuring 10,791,220 learnable parameters, was trained with transfer learning to manage fuzzy data for cassava disease identification. The model achieved an accuracy of 89.90%, surpassing the baseline accuracy of 50.46%. This neural network classifier shows strong performance in identifying cassava leaf diseases, even with imbalanced data. The findings are beneficial for farmers and agricultural scientists, potentially enhancing crop yield and aiding in disease prevention. Our approach could automate disease identification processes, thereby reducing crop loss. We recommend further research projects aimed at scaling up plant disease detection efforts.

title: Comparative Analysis of Various Machine Learning Models for Lentil Yield Prediction
abstract: Agriculture plays a pivotal role in India's economy, with a large segment of the population dependent on this sector. As the nation grapples with rapid population growth, ensuring food security becomes increasingly critical, necessitating more accurate crop yield prediction methods. This study focuses on evaluating the effectiveness of various machine learning models for predicting lentil crop yield, using growth attributes as predictors. Traditional approaches like multivariate linear regression (MLR) have shown limitations in accuracy. In contrast, machine learning techniques such as decision trees (DT), support vector machines (SVM), and artificial neural networks (ANN) offer superior alternatives by effectively managing the complex and non-linear interactions between input variables (e.g., soil properties, environmental conditions, and agricultural practices) and yield outcomes. Data from the Agricultural Research Farm at the School of Agriculture, Graphic Era Hill University, Dehradun, were utilized for model training and testing. Model performance was assessed using root mean square error (RMSE) and mean square error (MSE) metrics. The findings highlight that tree-based models and SVMs achieved the highest prediction accuracy, effectively capturing the variability in lentil yield, thus marking a significant advancement over traditional statistical methods.

title: Advancing Plant Disease Identification using Convolutional Neural Networks for Precise Diagnosis in Hibiscus Plants
abstract: The effectiveness and accuracy of deep learning models for the precise diagnosis of diseases in Hibiscus plants are studied. Gray mold, mainly caused by Botrytis cinerea, in diseased Hibiscus leaves is identified using 560 images collected to form the dataset. Preprocessing of the obtained dataset is performed through resizing, data augmentation, and noise reduction, which ensures the variability of the dataset. The preprocessed dataset is employed to train four different deep learning architectures: custom CNN, ResNet-50, VGG-16, and VGG-19. The benefits of using each model are that they are able to extract features and learn the pattern of the distribution of these features in the presence of the disease. The results are obtained based on the accuracy, precision, recall, F1 score, and the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve for comparison purposes. According to the results, the best candidate is VGG-19, which demonstrates accuracy at the level of 98.54%, while the precision of 98.80%, recall of 98.50%, F1 score of 98.65%, and AUC-ROC of 99.00% are also high. The confusion matrices provide details from which the correct classification for VGG-19 of healthy and diseased leaves becomes evident. The real-time implementation of VGG-19 is completely reliable. The applied deep learning models provide numerous benefits in predicting the diseases in plants, and the usage of computational techniques will ensure food security and opportunities for current development.

title: Mitigating Garlic Insect Pests and Diseases Using Knowledge-Driven Decision Support System
abstract: Modern farming practices are being transformed by innovative technological solutions like advanced garlic disease detection systems and cutting-edge weather forecasting applications. By providing garlic cultivators with access to precise and real-time data, these transformative tools empower them to make data-driven decisions that significantly enhance crop management techniques and increase yields. The garlic disease detection systems use state-of-the-art machine learning and image analysis methods to guarantee early identification and classification of potential diseases. The weather forecasting apps utilize sophisticated algorithms that incorporate historical weather data, soil conditions, and pest and disease occurrences to assist in the strategic allocation of resources and the meticulous management of irrigation schedules. The technological marvels have brought about a promising era for garlic agriculture, one that emphasizes sustainability and efficiency, ultimately bolstering global food security through the optimization of garlic cultivation practices.

title: Optimizing Sowing Dates and Crop Yield with Predictive Models
abstract: Effective crop management is crucial for meeting global food demand, yet traditional methods often lead to inefficiencies. This study utilizes data-driven models to enhance sowing date optimization and crop yield prediction (CYP) by integrating real-time sensor data-such as NPK levels and soil temperature-with weather forecasts generated using a linear regression model. Comprehensive data preprocessing ensured high-quality datasets by addressing missing values, scaling data, and selecting regions with at least$\mathbf{3 0}$years of historical records. To determine optimal sowing dates, a Random Forest model was employed to analyze historical trends and forecasted conditions, achieving an impressive accuracy of$\mathbf{9 4 \%}$. Meanwhile, an Extra Trees model captured complex feature interactions to improve crop yield predictions, attaining an accuracy of 92%. Both models underwent hyperparameter tuning to maximize performance. Results highlight the effectiveness of Artificial Intelligence (AI)-driven precision agriculture in optimizing resource utilization and boosting food production. By leveraging Machine learning (ML) for predictive insights, this research demonstrates how AI can transform traditional farming into a more sustainable and efficient practice. Ultimately, the integration of real-time monitoring, historical analysis, and advanced forecasting techniques enhances decision-making, improving food security and promoting agricultural sustainability.

title: Machine Learning for Enhanced Crop Management and Optimization of Yield in Precision Agriculture
abstract: Precision agriculture, utilizing technology to monitor and control crop growth and resource intake, is revolutionizing the agricultural sector. This research focuses on applying machine learning techniques to enhance decision-making in precision agriculture. By combining data from weather forecasts, soil sensors, and satellite imagery, the study aims to estimate crop health, soil characteristics, and yield results. Various machine learning models, including ensemble approaches, regression, classification, and clustering, were employed to analyze these complex datasets. Support vector regression and linear regression were used to predict crop yields based on historical data and environmental factors. Decision Trees and Random Forests were applied to classify crop diseases using image data. Convolutional Neural Networks analyzed satellite and drone imagery to identify agricultural stress and illnesses. Clustering techniques, such as K-Means and DBSCAN, were utilized to segment fields into management zones and detect anomalies in sensor data. Ensemble methods, including AdaBoost and Gradient Boosting Machines, were employed to enhance prediction accuracy by combining multiple models. The research findings demonstrate the significant improvement in prediction accuracy and decision-making capabilities enabled by machine learning techniques. This study lays the groundwork for further research and development in precision agriculture, contributing to sustainable farming practices and food security. By integrating high-resolution data from multiple sources, precision agriculture can optimize resource allocation and maximize crop yields, leading to more efficient and productive agricultural practices.

title: Crop Prediction & Fertilizer Recommendation using AODE Algorithm
abstract: Agriculture serves as the cornerstone of India’s global economic landscape, constituting a substantial proportion of the nation’s GDP. In light of the ever-expanding global population, safeguarding food security becomes an imperative task, and this responsibility rests upon the shoulders of the country’s agricultural productivity. This innovative data-driven solution harnesses the power of the Average One Dependence (AODE) algorithm in conjunction with a wealth of agricultural data to deliver highly accurate predictions of crop yields and tailored recommendations for optimal fertilizer usage. By delving into historical data and relevant influencing factors, and employing well-established Python libraries including Pandas, NumPy, Scikit-learn, Matplotlib, Seaborn, and Streamlit, the system excels in data preprocessing, feature engineering, model training, and the creation of an intuitive web-based interface. Its primary goal is to provide farmers with precise forecasts, enabling them to make well-informed decisions regarding resource allocation and crop management. Designed as a comprehensive framework that encompasses data integration, advanced feature engineering, model training, and rigorous performance evaluation, this pioneering initiative paves the way for the advancement of precision agriculture. By enhancing overall productivity, optimizing resource utilization, and promoting sustainable farming practices, it holds the potential to reshape the landscape of agricultural operations. This system empowers farmers with data-driven insights, aiding resource allocation and enhancing productivity while addressing the challenges of crop selection and optimizing fertilizer use in agriculture. The Accuracy of the machine learning including the crop prediction & fertilizer prediction model is 76.36 %

title: Smart Farming Through a Sustainable Crop Guidance System Powered by Predictive Machine Learning for Enhanced Agricultural Productivity
abstract: Accurate crop prediction plays a vital role in modern agriculture, directly influencing food security, resource efficiency, and sustainable farming outcomes. Traditional approaches often fall short due to the complexity of agroclimatic variations and the ever-changing nature of soil and weather conditions. To address these challenges, this study presents a Machine Learning-based Crop Guidance System (ML-CGS) that integrates agricultural domain knowledge with advanced data-driven models. The system collects and preprocesses relevant datasets, handling issues such as missing values, inconsistencies, and noise to ensure high data quality. Various machine learning algorithms, including Decision Trees, Gradient Boost, and Random Forest, are trained and evaluated using performance metrics. Among them, Random Forest achieved 99.24% accuracy, and Gradient Boost achieved$\mathbf{9 8. 3 3 \%}$, highlighting the robustness of the predictive models. ML-CGS provides intelligent crop recommendations based on soil type and weather conditions, offering adaptability across diverse farming scenarios. This research demonstrates the potential of AI-powered systems in transforming conventional agriculture into a smart, scalable, and sustainable practice. By leveraging the predictive power of machine learning, ML-CGS supports informed decision-making for farmers, enhances crop productivity, and contributes meaningfully to climate-resilient agricultural systems.

title: AI-Powered Food Scarcity Prediction and Nutrition Advisory System: Forecasting Shortages, Surpluses
abstract: Globalfood security, nutrition and the economy are deeply affected by food scarcity and surplus. The project entitled,AI-Powered Food ScarcityPrediction and Nutrition Advisory System: Forecasting Shortages, Surpluses uses a machine learning approaches in order to predict food availability trends and give actionable suggestions to farmers, policymakers, and consumers. Some of these models use archetypes of historical data, including past production data, climate data, and market data, to predict where we will face shortages or surpluses of specific cropsacross various regions. It also has a nutrition advisory component that generates alternative food sources and provides dietary recommendations, given anticipated shortages. It includes a Body Mass Index (BMI)calculator that can advise the users(PDF). Our interactive AI chatbot assistant enriches user experience by providing responses to questions related to food scarcity, crop selection, nutrition and health. The dashboard captures predictive insights, live food scarcity analytics, and nutrition recommendation for end users to aid sustainable food consumption and better public health. The system incorporates AI forecasting capabilities with nutrition guidance and health monitoring to leverage insights; reducing food waste, improving food security, and enabling sustainable data-driven decisions at the intersection of agriculture and nutrition.

title: Machine Learning-Based Forecasting of Weather, Rainfall, and Crop Yield for Smart Agricultural Planning in Tamil Nadu
abstract: The agricultural sector in Tamil Nadu faces significant challenges due to unpredictable monsoon patterns, escalating temperatures, and uneven rainfall distribution. Accurate forecasting of weather and rainfall, combined with crop yield prediction, is therefore crucial for sustainable agricultural planning. This study presents a data-driven Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) framework for forecasting rainfall and predicting crop yield in Tamil Nadu to support smart agricultural planning. Historical weather data comprising temperature, rainfall, and humidity, along with crop yield and soil nutrient datasets collected from government repositories, were utilized for model development. Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), XGBoost, and Random Forest models were implemented for rainfall prediction, while ensemble regression models were used for crop yield estimation. The LSTM model achieved the highest rainfall prediction accuracy with an R2score of 0.92, and the Random Forest crop yield model achieved 90.1% accuracy. The proposed framework also recommends climate-resilient crops based on predicted rainfall conditions. The system supports precision agriculture, optimizes irrigation planning, and enhances food security under climate variability. This work directly contributes to Sustainable Development Goals SDG-2 (Zero Hunger), SDG-6 (Clean Water and Sanitation), and SDG-13 (Climate Action).

title: Machine Learning in Agriculture and Crop Management: A Comprehensive Review
abstract: Machine learning (ML) has transformed agriculture and crop management, revolutionizing modern farming techniques. By leveraging ML, farmers can accurately monitor and analyze agricultural data, gaining valuable insights into crop health, soil conditions, weather patterns, and pest infestations. Through the analysis of satellite imagery, sensor data, and historical records, ML models can predict optimal planting times, forecast yields, and identify potential disease outbreaks, enabling more efficient resource management. These innovations promote precision agriculture, reduce waste, and support sustainability. This paper explores the latest developments in ML applications for agriculture, emphasizing their potential to enhance food security, minimize environmental impact, and boost farm profitability through data-driven decision-making.

title: Enhancing Agricultural Productivity with Machine Learning: A Crop and Fertilizer Recommendation System
abstract: Agriculture is a critical sector for food security and economic stability; however, conventional farming often depends on intuition, causing suboptimal crop choices and fertilizer use. This study presents an intelligent recommendation system that leverages machine learning to optimize both crop selection and fertilizer application.
