It uses a Random Forest classifier to predict the most suitable crops based on soil nutrients ($\mathrm{N}, \mathrm{P}$, and K), pH, and climate (temperature, humidity, and rainfall). Given the chosen crop, it recommends fertilizers tailored to soil nutrient deficiencies. Importantly, the system integrates economic data, such as Minimum Support Prices (MSP) and relevant government subsidy schemes provided by India, to guide farmers' decisions. Experimental evaluation shows that the Random Forest model achieves 99.32% accuracy, outperforming other classifiers. These results align with those of recent studies demonstrating the high accuracy of ensemble methods in agriculture. By combining agronomic predictions with economic insights and visualizations, our system bridges precision farming and financial sustainability, aiming to empower farmers with data-driven decision-making support.

title: Multi-Regional Neighborhood Spatio-Temporal Dynamics for Crop Yield Prediction
abstract: For agricultural planning and food security, accurate crop yield prediction is essential, but it is still difficult because of intricate inter-district spatial dependencies and extremely erratic temporal variations caused by agroclimatic factors. The ability of current deep learning techniques to capture higher-order regional interactions and non-linear temporal behaviour present in agricultural systems is limited because they frequently rely on local neighbourhood assumptions for spatial modelling and smooth temporal evolution. A spatiotemporal framework for modelling multi-regional neighbourhood dynamics in district-level crop yield prediction is presented in this paper. The suggested method creates a series of annual spatial graphs to depict inter-district relationships that go beyond close neighbours, making it possible to examine more extensive regional influences. A multi-neighbor graph convolutional mechanism based on MixHop is used to learn multi-regional spatial representations by aggregating data from several neighbourhood ranges. A chaos-aware Long Short-Term Memory network is used to capture irregular and non-linear yield fluctuations resulting from climatic uncertainty in order to model temporal evolution. Superior predictive performance is achieved by explicitly modelling multi-regional spatial dependencies along with irregular temporal dynamics, according to experimental evaluation on district-level crop yield data. The suggested framework consistently outperforms cutting-edge baselines, achieving an RMSE of 0.103, a$R^{2}$score of 0.790, and a correlation coefficient of 0.890. These findings demonstrate how crucial multi-regional spatiotemporal modelling is for reliable and accurate crop yield forecasting.

title: Evaluating the Performance of Machine Learning Models for Weather Prediction Using Multiple Classification Techniques
abstract: Weather prediction plays a critical role in various sectors, including agriculture, transportation, disaster management, and public safety, particularly regarding humidity and rainfall, plays a critical role in preventing postharvest grain spoilage. By forecasting high-risk periods, such models enable timely interventions such as improved storage practices, drying processes, and supply chain adjustments. This proactive approach helps reduce losses, maintain grain quality, and support food security. This research evaluates the in machine learning (ML) technique to analyze complex historical weather data and identify hidden patterns to improve forecast accuracy. This research evaluates the predictive performance of multiple ML models, including Voting Classifier (LR, SVM, KNN), Gaussian Naive Bayes, K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Logistic Regression, Support Vector Machines (SVM), and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM)-based Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN), in classifying weather conditions based on historical meteorological data. The study investigates various preprocessing techniques such as feature extraction, normalization, and handling missing values impact model performance. The models are assessed using key classification metrics, including accuracy, recall, and F1-score, while computational efficiency is also analyzed in terms of training time and scalability. The findings of this study contribute to the growing body of knowledge on data-driven weather forecasting and provide insights into the strengths and limitations of different ML approaches.

title: Development of a Crop Recommendation System Through the Use of Various Machine Learning Algorithms
abstract: The agricultural sector holds immense significance in ensuring global food security and economic stability. Machine learning approaches have garnered increasing attention for agricultural purposes in the past few years, especially when it comes to crop recommendation systems. This research endeavors to introduce and assess various machine learning algorithms deployed in a crop recommendation system, with the primary objective of aiding farmers in making well-informed decisions regarding crop selection, considering their unique environmental and soil conditions. The study relies on a comprehensive data set encompassing vital elements including soil composition, climatic trends, past crop yields, and agronomic techniques. Predictive models are generated by utilizing a variety of machine learning algorithms, such as neural networks, decision trees, random forests, and support vector machines. To understand the complex interactions between environmental factors and crop performance, these models are trained using historical data. To assess how well these models work in terms of suggesting appropriate crops under circumstances, performance metrics including accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score are used in the evaluation process. Moreover, the research delves into the interpretability of these models to offer insights into the decision-making process, catering to both farmers and agricultural experts. Furthermore, the study discusses the practical implementation of these models into a user-friendly web application, thus enhancing accessibility for farmers. This application solicits input from users, including geographical location, soil attributes, and climate data, subsequently generating personalized crop recommendations based on the insights gleaned from machine learning models. The findings of this study highlight how machine learning algorithms can greatly assist farmers in choosing crops that are specific to their needs. Such help may increase agricultural productivity, maximize resource allocation, and improve agriculture's general sustainability. The study also emphasizes the significance of judiciously selecting appropriate algorithms and data preprocessing techniques to achieve optimal performance. To sum up, this study advances the field of precision agriculture by demonstrating how machine learning algorithms may be applied practically in crop recommendation systems. It highlights the capacity of technology-driven solutions to tackle contemporary challenges in agriculture, ultimately benefiting both farmers and the global food supply chain.

title: Smart Agriculture: Explainable Deep Learning Approach with Gradient-Weighted Class Activation Mapping
abstract: In light of the pressing need to guarantee food security in the face of threats posed by climate change, an increasing global population together with rising incomes, worsening soil erosion, and dwindling water resources, crop yield forecasting has assumed more significance in recent years. A relatively new area of study, “Explainable AI” seeks to provide context for the findings produced by Deep learning models. Nevertheless, there is a pressing need for more comprehensive evaluations of deep learning models for object classification in images. Due to this, the research suggests two steps for implementing Explainable AI: (1) assessing the deep-learning(DL)-strategies accuracy utilizing evaluation methods, and (2) evaluating the feature recognition skill of an scan when recognized by DL utilizing Grad-CAM for model construal. Compared to EfficientNetV2S and Xception, the results reveal that MobieNet model has lower dependability but higher accuracy. When taking the ratio match rate into account, though, MobileNetV2 achieves the best accuracy. Building intelligent agriculture support systems (with the help of automated fruit-picking robots that discard bad fruits) is one application of the study's findings. Another is the utilization of the Explainable AI model's output to determine the best deep learning model for processing.

title: Deep Learning’s Diverse Impact on Sustainability of Agricultural Tech Startup
abstract: This research investigates the transformative impacts of deep learning integration across Agritech enterprises – an ascendant industry synthesizing artificial intelligence and agricultural paradigms. Principally, analysis centers on how cutting-edge machine learning techniques are altering production practices to enhance yield, long-term commercial viability, and operational efficiency. Employing a blended qualitative and quantitative approach, this study examines case histories of Agritech startups successfully leveraging deep learning technologies. This article contextualizes emergent startups within the broader examination of the expansive functions artificial intelligence now serves across the agricultural sector following widespread adoption. Per findings, measurable enhancements are evident in areas including precision agriculture, automated supply chain coordination, agricultural disease identification, and predictive crop and climate modeling analytics. Additionally, research illuminates wider sociotechnical impacts on objectives of food security, environmental sustainability, and equitable rural economic development.

title: Soil Analysis Using Deep Learning for Precision Agriculture
abstract: This research explores the application of deep learning techniques for soil analysis in precision agriculture, focusing on the classification of soil types using convolutional neural networks (CNNs). The study addresses the limitations of traditional soil classification methods, which are often labor-intensive and reliant on expert judgment. The proposed approach involves collecting soil image data, preprocessing it using techniques such as Gabor filtering, and classifying the images with a CNN model. The methodology includes data acquisition, feature extraction, and model training, aiming to accurately predict soil parameters using diverse input data sources like sensor readings and satellite imagery. The potential benefits of this approach include real-time monitoring, optimal fertilizer application, and enhanced crop management, which can contribute to sustainable agricultural practices and food security.

title: A Review of Crop Yield Prediction Strategies based on Machine Learning and Deep Learning
abstract: Crop yield prediction is critical for solving increasing food security concerns, especially in the current climate change situation. Accurate forecasts will aid farmers in making financial and managerial decisions, thereby preventing food shortage. Machine learning (ML) techniques have proven an effective means for predicting the yield of crops, which greatly impact agricultural yield prediction where various Artificial Intelligence as well as deep learning techniques can be utilized. A detailed literature review has been performed in this work to analyze and explore various ML algorithms and to identify the features viz., weather, soil types and properties, fertilizers that highly influence the crop yield prediction. This study confirmed that the prediction accuracy depends mainly on the features considered for improving the crop yield prediction.

title: Tomato Guard: A Predictive Model for Disease Prediction and Treatment Recommendation in Tomato Plants
abstract: India, renowned for its tomato production, faces challenges in terms of quality and quantity of tomato crops due to escalating incidences of diseases. This research introduces “Tomato Guard,” a predictive model specifically designed to forecast diseases in tomato plants, aiming to mitigate these challenges. Utilizing advanced machine learning techniques and integrating diverse datasets comprising environmental variables, plant health metrics, and historical disease trends, the model adopts a proactive stance towards disease management. Rigorous field trials validate the efficacy of “Tomato Guard,” showcasing its superior accuracy in early disease detection compared to traditional scouting methods. Its adaptability to various climates and geographical regions enhances its utility for growers, offering a versatile solution to combat disease outbreaks. Furthermore, the model not only minimizes economic losses but also advocates for sustainable farming practices, thereby contributing to global food security and agricultural resilience. The model’s user-friendly interface facilitates interaction, enabling growers to upload diseased images and receive accurate predictions along with suitable remedies. Overall, “Tomato Guard” stands as a significant advancement in disease prediction and management in tomato cultivation, empowering growers with actionable insights to safeguard their crops and sustain agricultural productivity.

title: Detecting and Monitoring Agricultural Lands in Sri Lanka Using Remote-Sensing and Deep Learning
abstract: Accurate agricultural assessment is essential for improving productivity and ensuring food security in regions like Sri Lanka. This study presents an integrated framework using remote sensing and deep learning to enhance precision agriculture. Multispectral satellite imagery from Sentinel-2 and Landsat, processed via Google Earth Engine (GEE), supports a soft-label Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) for identifying crop types and phenological stages. Geospatial techniques enable precise area mapping and vegetation health evaluation, while Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks model temporal growth dynamics for yield forecasting. The system's web interface provides real-time analytics, interactive maps, and automated alerts on crop performance and underutilized lands, enabling timely, data-driven decisions. This approach offers a scalable, technology-driven pathway for sustainable land management and improved agricultural resilience in Sri Lanka.

title: E-Goyama -A Modern Solution for Profitable Paddy Cultivation
abstract: This research employs cutting-edge machine learning and image processing techniques to transform critical aspects of paddy cultivation, discovering and bridging a research scope of substantial research gap in the Central Province of Sri Lanka. Through the augmentation of advanced technologies like machine learning, convolutional neural networks, and image processing, it revolutionizes four key domains within paddy cultivation. Firstly, it deploys machine learning for precise rice variety identification by analyzing soil nutrition data, thereby optimizing crop selection. Secondly, it implements image processing for the early detection of three major leaf-based diseases, significantly improving disease management and ensuring crop protection. Thirdly, it employs machine learning for forecasting farmers' costs, enhancing economic planning and resource allocation. Finally, the study accurately identifies various paddy growth stages through image processing, facilitating the timing of essential agricultural activities. These innovations promise to markedly enhance paddy cultivation efficiency, deliver valuable insights to stakeholders, and promote sustainable agricultural practices, reinforcing food security and safety. The high accuracy models developed, cater towards promoting the expected efficiency and effectiveness in advancing the paddy cultivation to newer heights.

title: Machine Learning Based Approach to Reduce Food Wastage
abstract: Food wastage is a major issue that affects the economy, society, and environment on a global scale. Over one-third of the food produced worldwide is lost or wasted each year, underscoring the necessity for sustainable food systems. This research proposes an innovative solution that leverages technology to address food wastage reduction. An application is developed with a focus on four key categories: food wastage prediction and analysis, demand prediction and ingredient optimization, forecasting of near-expiry food prices, and accurate recycling method prediction. By incorporating machine learning and predictive modeling, the application provides restaurants and food administrators with comprehensive organizational statistics to effectively mitigate food wastage. The solution offers a data-driven approach to better plan events, reduce waste in the food industry, accurately forecast both demand and ingredient requirements, strategically focus on prices based on shelf life and predict optimal recycling methods. Through this multi-pronged approach, we aim to tackle the complex issue of food wastage and help to establish sustainable food systems.

title: A Comparative Study of Agricultural Crop Yield Prediction Using Machine Learning Techniques
abstract: Agriculture is the most important factor for survival. Crop yield is a valuable component of food security as the population continues to increase rapidly. Previously, crop and yield predictions were made based on the farmer's experience in a specific location. Farmers will prefer the previous, neighboring, or more trending crop in the surrounding region only for their land, and Farmers are unaware of soil nutrients like nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium. This can lead to decreased crop growth. So, crop yield prediction is one of agriculture's most pressing issues. Machine learning (ML) is a method that provides a more practical solution to crop yield issues. To boost crop production, agricultural land uses ML algorithms to decide which crops to plant during the growing season. Various machine learning algorithms are used to implement a crop prediction process in this study. Crop yield can be predicted by analyzing various features and Machine Learning (ML) methods like Logistic Regression (LR), Naive Bayes (NB), Support Vector Machine (SVM), Decision Tree (DT), K-Nearest Neighbors Algorithm (KNN), Extreme Gradient Boosting Algorithm (XGBoost) and Random Forest (RF). This work is to show the importance of feature selection and hyperparameter tuning of various ML algorithms. In this study, the Random forest algorithm gives high accuracy when compared with other models.

title: Enhancing Predictive Accuracy for Agricultural Crop Yields in Indian States Using Power Transformation in Machine Learning Models
abstract: Agricultural productivity is critical for the sustenance and economic growth of India, a country with diverse climatic regions and crop practices. Accurate prediction of crop yields is essential for optimizing agricultural outputs, ensuring food security, and planning resource allocation. Traditional predictive models often struggle with the nonlinear and complex nature of factors influencing crop yields. This study introduces an innovative approach by integrating power transformations, specifically the Yeo-Johnson transformation, within machine learning models to enhance the predictive accuracy of agricultural crop yields in various Indian states. We collected a comprehensive dataset comprising climatic variables, soil properties, crop types, and historical yield data across different Indian states. The Yeo-Johnson power transformation was applied to normalize the distribution of these features, addressing issues of skewness and heteroscedasticity, thereby making the data more suitable for machine learning algorithms. We evaluated several machine learning models, including Linear Regression, Random Forest, and Gradient Boosting, to establish a benchmark for comparison. Our findings demonstrate a significant improvement in predictive accuracy with the application of the Yeo-Johnson transformation across all models tested are shown in table 1. The Gradient Boosting model, post-transformation, exhibited the highest accuracy, underscoring the potential of combining power transformations with ensemble learning techniques for crop yield prediction. This approach not only aids in achieving greater precision in forecasts but also provides insights into the relative importance of various factors affecting crop yields. The study emphasizes the role of advanced data preprocessing techniques, such as power transformations, in unlocking the full potential of machine learning for agricultural applications. By enhancing the predictive accuracy of crop yield models, stakeholders can make more informed decisions, leading to improved agricultural productivity and sustainability in the diverse and challenging landscape of Indian agriculture.

title: Innovations in Agri-Tech: A Review of Artificial Intelligence Applications and Challenges in Modern Agriculture
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is driving a massive shift in the agriculture industry, which is essential to both global food security and economic stability. This review article explores the use of AI technologies in agriculture, outlining their current and potential future applications while charting their evolution. We examine several AI applications such as computer vision, machine learning, robots and the (IoT) Internet of Things, highlighting their contributions to increasing efficiency, streamlining resource allocation, and strengthening decision-making. Machine learning techniques are utilized for predictive analytics in disease identification and crop yield estimation, while computer vision supports plant health monitoring and harvesting automation. Planting, weeding, and harvesting chores are revolutionized by robotics, and data collecting for precision agriculture is made easier by IoT devices in conjunction with sensors. Additionally, by offering indepth analyses of the soil and crops, drones and satellite imagery are essential to precision farming. The technological, financial, and social barriers to the broad adoption of AI are also covered in this study. These barriers include poor data quality, expensive implementation, and moral dilemmas with regard to labour displacement and environmental effects. In this paper, we propose that the future of global food security and sustainability depends on the strategic application of AI in agriculture. In order to fully realize the potential of artificial intelligence in agriculture Strategic implementation will determine the sustain ability and future of global food security. In this order, this study attempts to direct future research and policy development by offering a thorough overview of existing technology, applications, and difficulties.

title: A Comparative Study of Feature selection Methods on HICE Dataset
abstract: The first stage in developing a machine learning model is identifying the dataset's characteristics that may be used to achieve the best possible learning results. Throughout this paper, we will cover feature selection strategies that can be utilized to improve the quality of models while also increasing model interpretability. We used these approaches to predict the status of household-level food security. Several feature selection strategies have been proposed over several decades with their benefits and disadvantages. Despite the thorough investigation and extensive work, the numerous feature selection approaches have not yet been assessed in the Household income, consumption, and expenditure (HICE) scenario. HICE is used in this work to compare three feature selection methods: filter, wrapper, and embedding empirically. This research investigates the adoption of an existing wrapper, filter, and embedded techniques to runtesting with five machine learning algorithms.

title: Corn Crop Yield Prediction using Deep Learning
abstract: Accurate crop yield prediction has emerged as a critical area of research, especially in light of global food security challenges and the need for sustainable agricultural practices. In this study, we focus on predicting the yield of US corn, a staple crop with significant economic and nutritional value. By leveraging data mining techniques, we extract meaningful patterns from large agricultural datasets, aiming to enhance our understanding of the factors influencing crop yields. Accurate predictions can guide farmers and policymakers in making informed decisions, such as optimizing planting schedules, managing resources more effectively, and anticipating potential shortages. In this study, we utilized a variety of machine learning models, such as Logistic Regression, Decision Trees, Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN), Random Forest, Support Vector Machines (SVM), and Long Short Term Memory (LSTM) networks. These models were selected to explore their varying capabilities in handling complex agricultural data and providing accurate predictions. The final outcome, Linear Regression, achieved an impressive accuracy of 93%, demonstrating its effectiveness in predicting crop yields based on the given dataset.

title: AI-Powered Crop Suggestion, Yield Prediction, Disease Detection, and Soil Monitoring
abstract: India’s agricultural sector is crucial for food security. However, factors such as climate change, soil quality, and pest infestations can significantly impact crop yields. This research aims to develop a machine learning-based model to predict crop yields accurately. The proposed model leverages advanced techniques like Inception ResNet V2, AlexNet, Random Forest, Decision Tree, KNN, Naive Bayes, Simple RNN, Logistic Regression, and Voting Classifier to analyze historical data and identify key factors influencing crop yield. By considering variables such as area, crop variety, and climatic conditions, the model provides valuable insights to farmers. The proposed model achieved a high accuracy of 91%, demonstrating its potential to significantly improve agricultural practices. By enabling farmers to make informed decisions regarding crop selection, planting, and resource allocation, this research contributes to sustainable agriculture and food security.

title: Predicting the Future: Using AdaBoost to Forecast Food Commodity Prices Across Indonesian Markets
abstract: Rice prices play a crucial role in Indonesia's food security, making accurate predictions essential for effective decision-making in price stabilization and policy planning. This study aims to predict rice prices in various markets across Indonesia by applying the Adaptive Boosting (AdaBoost) algorithm. Eight modeling schemes were explored using a combination of AdaBoost and Decision Tree Regression, with coefficient of determination$(\mathrm{R}^{2})$and Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) as evaluation metrics. The dataset, comprising 35,107 data points, was obtained from the Strategic Food Price Information Center (PIHPS) and covers the period from May 2023 to April 2024. The results indicate that Scheme 5, utilizing a 90:10 data split scenario, achieved the best performance with an$\mathrm{R}^{2}$value of 99.72% and a MAPE of 0.14%. This significantly outperforms previous research employing the Gradient Boosted Trees Regression algorithm, which achieved an$\mathrm{R}^{2}$of 90.47% and a MAPE of 12.41%. These findings demonstrate the superiority of the AdaBoost algorithm in modeling food commodity prices, particularly in forecasting rice prices in Indonesia. This study contributes to the advancement of more accurate price prediction methods, which can be leveraged by policymakers, market stakeholders, and the agricultural sector to support price stabilization and food security management in Indonesia.

title: Comparative Study of Crop Yield Prediction Using Explainable AI and Interpretable Machine Learning Techniques
abstract: Predicting crop yields is a vital aspect of agricultural planning as well as food security. For this, machine-learning models have become quite effective tools. Using a real-world dataset centered on agricultural production predictions, this research evaluates the interpretability and predictive outcomes of four renowned machine learning models: XGBoost, Decision Tree, Random Forest, and Linear Regression. Key indicators of performance involving Mean Absolute Error (MAE), R-squared (R2), and Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) have been employed to gauge the models' ability to deliver precise predictions. XGBoost Regression consistently performed better than the other models, as shown by its lowest RMSE (1.46), MAE (0.68), and greatest R2 (0.95). The Decision Tree (98.33%), XGBoost (98.48%), Linear Regression (95.60%), and Random Forest (99.09%) models had the highest accuracy rates. To enhance the transparency and interpretability of the models, two explainable AI (XAI) techniques, SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) and LIME (Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations), were employed. These methods were utilized to provide deeper insights into the decision-making processes of the models. These techniques revealed the salient characteristics that shaped the models' forecasts. While LIME produced local explanations forecasts, SHAP values demonstrated the relative significance of factors in predicting crop output.

title: Indonesian Food Price Prediction with Adaptive Neuro Fuzzy Inference System
abstract: Rising food price in Indonesia is an uncertain issue that significantly affects the lives of the people and the country’s economy. In addition, the demand for Indonesian staple foods, namely rice, is very high. Of course, the fluctuations in the price of rice will have a significant impact on the Indonesian population. So, we need a system that functions to predict food prices. Therefore, this study aims to predict Indonesian food prices. Rice price data is taken from the Central Bureau of Statistics (BPS) website and the prediction was built using the Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference System (ANFIS) method. Then the model will be evaluated using Mean Squared Error (MSE) and Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE). In this study, the ANFIS model is made with the number of membership functions (MFs) as much as 2, the number of iterations (epochs) is 300, and the type of membership function (MF type) is gaussmf. The training and testing results using ANFIS show that the MSE and MAPE values are 0.9176 and 0.70059%. These results prove that the ANFIS method can predict Indonesian food prices well.

title: Indonesian Food Price Prediction with Adaptive Neuro Fuzzy Inference System
abstract: Rising food price in Indonesia is an uncertain issue that significantly affects the lives of the people and the country’s economy. In addition, the demand for Indonesian staple foods, namely rice, is very high. Of course, the fluctuations in the price of rice will have a significant impact on the Indonesian population. So, we need a system that functions to predict food prices. Therefore, this study aims to predict Indonesian food prices. Rice price data is taken from the Central Bureau of Statistics (BPS) website and the prediction was built using the Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference System (ANFIS) method. Then the model will be evaluated using Mean Squared Error (MSE) and Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE). In this study, the ANFIS model is made with the number of membership functions (MFs) as much as 2, the number of iterations (epochs) is 300, and the type of membership function (MF type) is gaussmf. The training and testing results using ANFIS show that the MSE and MAPE values are 0.9176 and 0.70059%. These results prove that the ANFIS method can predict Indonesian food prices well.

title: Potato Disease Detection through Leafs: Leveraging Deep Learning Algorithms for Accurate Diagnosis
abstract: The classification of potato diseases is significant for a number of reasons. Diseases can severely lower potato crop output and quality. Early disease diagnosis can assist farmers in taking the necessary steps to stop the illness's spread and lessen its effects on crop output and quality. Farmers can save money by using less costly pesticides and other treatments if diseases are detected early. It can also help prevent the loss of entire crops due to disease. The use of pesticides and other chemicals can have negative impacts on the environment, including water and soil pollution. Early detection of diseases can reduce the need for these chemicals, helping to protect the environment. Potatoes are an important staple food crop worldwide. Disease outbreaks can have a significant impact on food security, particularly in developing countries. Early detection of diseases can help prevent crop losses and ensure a stable food supply. This paper is about the implementation of the CNN (Convolutional Neural Network) models that can help in the detection of various potato diseases with the help of potato leaf. By using some of the deep learning models like VGG16 and VGG19 we will predict whether the potato is diseased or not.

title: Forecasting Prices of Strategic Food Products: Time Series Models in the Context of Post-Crisis Market Disruption
abstract: In a post-crisis context, anticipating variations in raw material prices is essential for smart cities. At the beginning of this decade, two major global crises disrupted various market sectors: the COVID-19 pandemic and the Russian-Ukrainian war. Wheat is an essential product that contributes to food security in many countries. The price of this cereal fluctuated considerably during the two crises. Russia and Ukraine account for up to 28% of the wheat export market. Today, the wheat market seems to be gradually stabilizing from these disturbances. This paper explores reliable forecasting models to estimate wheat prices and support decision-making in the post-crisis period. To this end, two time-series forecasting techniques are compared: the Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average Model (ARIMA), known for its reliability in financial forecasting, and the Long Short-Term Memory Network (LSTM). The results reveal that the LSTM model achieves an accuracy of 97.49%, outperforming the ARIMA model, which registers an accuracy of 77%. These results underline the effectiveness of deep learning models for forecasting during periods of high price volatility, compared with conventional models.

title: Potato Disease Classification: A Review
abstract: Potatoes are one of the world's main foodstuffs after rice, wheat, and corn. They are also an important horticultural commodity with considerable domestic trade and export value. Potatoes are prioritized in agricultural development because they demonstrate strong competitiveness compared to other vegetables. In Indonesia, the role of potatoes continues to increase, both as fresh produce and as processed products. In the future, potato commodities are expected not only to serve as vegetables but also as an alternative source of carbohydrates, thereby contributing to food security. Potato cultivation in Indonesia is concentrated in highland areas ($1,000-3,000 \mathrm{m}$above sea level), with production centers located in Central Java, West Java, East Java, South Sulawesi, North Sumatra, West Sumatra, and Jambi. The objective of this research is to identify the most widely used approaches for potato disease prediction and to examine how these strategies have evolved over time. Both qualitative and quantitative methodologies are employed, with the Scopus database serving as the primary source for scientific journal publications. A total of 113 papers, published between 2020 and 2025, are analyzed. Bibliometric research is conducted using the bibliometrix library and the functions available in Biblioshiny. The findings indicate that potato disease prediction involves the use of diverse technologies. Many supervised machine learning techniques have been applied, with deep learning-particularly Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) emerging as the most extensively used approach for forecasting potato diseases. This rapidly advancing field of computer science highlights the importance of interdisciplinary collaboration, attracting researchers worldwide who are eager to contribute to this area of study.

title: Combining Explainable Machine Learning with Accurate Crop Suggestion and Yeild Calculation
abstract: Agriculture is a keystone of food security and economic constancy, but it facing serious challenges due to abnormal behavior of climate, soil degradation, and resource limitations. The modern machine learning techniques are good for classification and yield predicton, but they are very small and limited in datasets, single-crop prediction, and static data sources. To address these limitations, the study introduces an enhanced framework that combines Internet of Things (IoT) devices, satellite images, and economic indicators with advanced machine and deep learning models. Our system uses ML technology to help with farming. Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and also identifies problems like diseases early on, and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks to handle on how much yield to expect. To make sure our predictions are reliable, we also decided to use ensemble techniques. our system can predict yields for multiple crops, give real-time updates, and also offers recommendations for specific regions. It really boosts productivity, and reduces the risks, helps farmers use resources smarter, and ultimately, make agriculture more sustainable overall.

title: Incorporating Meteorological Data and Pesticide Usage for Crop Yield Prediction Using Machine Learning
abstract: The honest estimation of crop yield is an essential part of contemporary agricultural planning, as it allows the making of right decisions related to food security, resource management, and mitigation of risks. Traditional statistical methods have a tough time dealing with the intricate and nonlinear interactions existing among weather, agricultural inputs, and crop output. In order to overcome this constraint, the authors of this paper introduce a yield prediction system based on machine learning that not only adds meteorological and pesticide usage data to the forecast but also increases the accuracy thereof. The proposed solution handles both types of features, featuring crop and region as the categorical and average temperature, precipitation, and pesticide usage as the numerical ones. The categorical inputs are changed into the matrix form using One-Hot Encoding technique, while the numerical ones are standardized through feature scaling method. The Random Forest regression model is applied to the task of discovering non-linear relationships between the features and giving the output of quantity of yield in continuous form. The model is made available through the web-based application underpinned by Flask that allows for real-time prediction based on the user inputs. The experimental evaluation uses historical data about agriculture and climate, and is enriched by exploratory data analysis and correlation studies whose purpose is to check how the yield of a crop is affected by each of the factors. The findings prove that the model proposed is very effective in capturing the differences in yields among various crops and areas, thus providing reliable predictions. The fusing of the factors of environment and pesticide powerfully fortifies the model above that based on the input parameters alone. The system that researchers created functions as a precise agricultural decision-making tool which first enables current operations and then allows for future expansion through new data acquisition.

title: Explainable End-to-End Crop Recommendation System with Real-Time Weather Integration
abstract: Agriculture has continuously been of high importance for India's economy and food security, yet farmers often face a lack of data-driven tools that can assist them in choosing the most profitable crops under varying climate and soil conditions. This paper presents a machine learning-based crop recommendation system that integrates soil characteristics and weather parameters to provide accurate and interpretable crop suggestions. A Random forest classifier is trained on a benchmark crop dataset comprising 2,200 samples and achieves a classification accuracy of 99.62 %. To enhance transparency, SHAP-based explanations are employed to identify the contribution of individual features to each recommendation. In addition, real-time weather information is incorporated through the OpenWeatherMap API, enabling dynamic updates based on current local conditions. Experimental results demonstrate strong predictive performance alongside meaningful interpretability. The deployment of the proposed technique through a web-based interface will provide farmers with timely and transparent crop recommendations, enhancing existing approaches by uniquely integrating real-time weather data with explainable machine learning.

title: Leveraging Machine Learning for Improved Agricultural Risk Management
abstract: India's population is predicted to reach 1.67 billion by 2050 [1]. The growing urbanized population has higher food demands. Crop production must be enhanced in light of the massive population growth. The greatest impediment to maximizing production is pests and insects and the harm they create. Several machine-learning approaches are implemented to prevent crop damage and boost agricultural output. Our research includes a literature overview on ML approaches applied in agriculture, with an emphasis on the identification, detection, and prediction of crop-damaging diseases and pests. It seeks to further the advancement of smart farming and precision agriculture. The dataset's precise and dependable crop yield forecasts can benefit initiatives aimed at assisting small-scale farmers, advocating for sustainable farming methods, and guaranteeing food security for everyone. It includes a broad variety of environmental and agricultural parameters that can analyze the relationship between different factors and crop yields.

title: Impact of the Price of Petroleum on the Price of Food Items in Sri Lanka
abstract: The rising cost of food presents a significant challenge for households in developing countries, prompting experts to explore effective policies to mitigate price volatility. This concern has recently gained attention in Sri Lanka, sparking discussions on the current and future trajectory of food commodity prices. The increase in agricultural commodity prices is partially attributed to the rising costs of petroleum. This study aims to understand the relationship between coconut prices and fluctuations in the price of Lanka Petrol (LP92), as well as the connection between coconut prices and changes in the price of Lanka Auto Diesel (LAD). It also investigates variations in Samba prices concerning LP92 price changes, given their significance as highly consumed food products and widely used petroleum commodities. Utilizing data from January 2008 to November 2022 sourced from the official website of the Central Bank of Sri Lanka, the study employs Vector Auto Regressive (VAR) models. Model selection is determined by criteria such as Akaike Information Criterion (AIC), Schwarz-Bayesian Information Criterion (SC), and Hannan-Quinn (HQ). The study finds that VAR (2) is optimal for identifying Samba price variations with LP92, VAR (3) for Coconut price variations with LAD, and VAR (3) for Coconut price variations with LP92. The dataset is split into an 80% training set and a 20% test set for model evaluation, utilizing metrics like Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE), and Mean Absolute Error (MAE). Further investigations into the impact of fuel costs on Samba and Coconut prices, using Granger causality and cointegration tests with LAD and LP92 price data, yield no conclusive evidence of causation. The study proceeds to remodel the original datasets using machine learning techniques, with the models demonstrating superior performance compared to traditional VAR models. Based on all the models, the models created through machine learning techniques showed superior performances showing 27%, 30%, 19% MAPE values and 11.12, 14.7, 16.6 MAE values for respective three FFNN models. The findings of this study would be more beneficial for policymakers, researchers, sellers as well as buyers.

title: Deep Learning Based District Level Paddy Production Forecasting: A Study Based on Agricultural Behaviour in Sri Lanka
abstract: Rice production serves as the cornerstone of food security in Sri Lanka, where$\mathbf{1. 8}$million farming families depend on this staple crop. Accurate production forecasting is essential for proactive policy interventions, resource allocation, and market stabilization. This study presents a comprehensive comparative analysis of seven machine learning algorithms for predicting district-level paddy production across Maha and Yala seasons. Authors compiled a 21 -year dataset spanning 2004-2025, encompassing 973 district-season observations from 25 administrative districts. The dataset incorporates 12 engineered features including area harvested, yield metrics, lagged variables, irrigation indicators, and interaction terms derived through domain-informed feature engineering. Seven algorithms were evaluated: Linear Regression, XGBoost, Random Forest, Decision Tree, Multi-Layer Perceptron, Feed Forward Neural Network, and Generalized Regression Neural Network. Models were trained using temporal train-test splitting with$80 / 20$ratio and evaluated using coefficient of determination, root mean square error, and mean absolute error. XGBoost achieved superior accuracy with coefficient of determination equal to 0.9873, root mean square error of 8,521 metric tons, and mean absolute error of 4,234 metric tons, significantly outperforming Random Forest, Decision Tree, linear regression, and neural network architectures. National production forecasts for 2026 range from 2.49 million metric tons to 5.07 million metric tons, with ensemble average of 4.35 million metric tons. Feature importance analysis reveals harvested area contributing 45.2 percent and area-yield interaction contributing 27.8 percent as dominant predictors. Tree-based ensemble methods demonstrate superior performance over deep learning approaches for structured agricultural time-series data with limited sample sizes, providing actionable intelligence agricultural policy formulation.

title: Machine Learning-based Crops Yield Prediction Tool and Deployment through Streamlit Web App
abstract: Yield prediction plays a vital role in modern agriculture for intensive farming, food security, and effective resource utilization. This paper presents a strong application of machine learning using environmental and crop data to predict crop yield in agriculture. The article compares old algorithms with newer ones that use Decision Tree, Random Forest, Support Vector Machine, and Artificial Neural Network to serve the purpose of detecting nonlinear trends in different datasets. Random Forest performed the best among the stated algorithms, having R 2 = 0.94 and RMSE = 0.12 tons/ha. For practicality, the most effective model was implemented as a Streamlit web interface and a MySQL catalog. Such an arrangement indeed allows real-time interaction between users and offers the capability for continuous model improvement through data logging.

title: Feature Extraction with Triplet Loss to Classify Disease on Leaf Data
abstract: This paper addresses the plant disease detection and classification using Deep Learning approach. In particular, we propose a novel model using the Triplet Loss together with the fine-tuned pre-trained MobileNet model to extract good features, classify, and detect diseases of plants from the open-source PlantVillage dataset. Using our proposed model, the achievable results are 99.92%, which outperforms the existing models using the same dataset. Furthermore, our proposed model can support the large-scale agricultural sector, which plays an important role in ensuring food security during the current COVID-19 crisis.

title: Machine Learning for Crop Yield And Irrigation Energy Cost Prediction: Case Study of Five Tropical Crops
abstract: The agricultural sector plays a pivotal role in global food security and resource management. Accurate prediction of crop yields and energy costs is essential for improving agricultural productivity and sustainability. This study presents a novel approach that integrates machine learning techniques with a web-based application to predict crop yields and irrigation energy costs within the context of Ghana’s farming sector. Comprehensive datasets containing historical crop yield records, rainfall, soil fertility status, and energy cost information were collected. Relevant features were extracted through a feature engineering process to improve prediction accuracy. Five machine learning algorithms – Linear Regression, Decision Tree, Random Forest, Feed-Forward Neural Network, and Recurrent Neural Network - were trained using the prepared datasets. Performance metrics such as Mean Absolute Error, Mean Squared Error, and R2 score were evaluated to assess the models’ predictive capabilities and select the best model. The validation process confirmed the superiority of the Random Forest algorithm across the five major crops. A web-based application was developed for user-friendly interactions and real-time predictions. The application provides a user interface that allows stakeholders to access predictions and insights through web and mobile platforms. This study contributes to advancing agricultural technology by presenting a comprehensive framework for predicting crop yields and energy costs in Ghana’s regions. By combining machine learning techniques with web applications, the approach offers accurate, scalable, and accessible predictions. This empowers stakeholders to make informed decisions and promote sustainable agricultural practices.

title: Random Forest Regression Approach for Balancing Vegetable Production and Price Forecasting in Sri Lanka
abstract: Sri Lanka’s agriculture sector, a pillar of the national economy, is extremely vulnerable to price volatility in essential crops such as potatoes, particularly in major production and trading hubs like Welimada, Bandarawela, and Nuwara Eliya. This research project addresses this critical issue by developing a supervised machine learning framework that leverages Random Forest regression to forecast wholesale potato prices, integrating market-specific prices, climatic indicators, rainfall, and inflation to model complex non-linear interactions. The methodology involved comprehensive data preprocessing, meticulous hyperparameter tuning, and rigorous five-fold cross-validation, ensuring resilient generalization despite a limited historical data window. Model evaluation yielded strong results: R2values were 0.470 for Welimada, 0.701 for Bandarawela, and 0.807 for Nuwara Eliya, with corresponding RMSE values of 35.87, 25.24, and 21.30, respectively. The entire workflow, from data ingestion, model training, and result analysis to application deployment, was implemented using Python’s data science stack and presented via a Streamlit web application for real-time access. Unique to this project, the application not only forecasts prices but also provides market analytics tailored to stakeholders, including revenue estimation and oversupply risk detection per region, empowering informed decisions for farmers, traders, and policymakers. By offering transparent, actionable, and context-aware price insights, the system alleviates uncertainty, enhances market participation, and ultimately supports greater stability and sustainability in Sri Lankan agriculture. This solution, designed to be extensible, paves the way for broader crop integration, real-time analytics, and further reinforcement of food system resilience in the future.

title: Prediction of Grain Output in Anhui Province Based on Machine Learning
abstract: Food security has always been concerned by all countries. The grain production data of Anhui Province from 1990 to 2017 are selected, including: total grain production, sown area, etc. Low accuracy of food production forecasts has become a problem. We proposed a machine learning combination model GR-SVR based on Random Forest (RF), Gradient Boosting Decision Tree (GBDT) and Support Vector Regression Machine (SVR) to predict grain yield, using RF, GBDT, and SVR at the same time compare with GR-SVR. The results show that the GRSVR model has an accuracy rate higher than 96% in the prediction of grain output in Anhui Province, which is significantly better than GBDT, RF and SVR.

title: Machine Learning Methods for Crop Pest Incidence Prediction: An Example of Greenhouse Tuta Absoluta (Meyrick)
abstract: Crop pest and disease prediction is a critical component of plant protection engineering, vital for maintaining crop biodiversity and ensuring global food security. Traditional pest and disease prediction methods often rely on statistical techniques, such as plant protection knowledge systems and pestdisease image analysis. However, these methods have limited effectiveness in accurately predicting pest and disease incidence. With advancements in Internet of Things (IoT) and Artificial Intelligence (AI) technologies, machine learning models offer promising potential for improving pest and disease prediction. This study focuses on predicting the incidence of Tuta absoluta (Meyrick), a major pest in tomato agriculture, using environmental data collected in Chengde City, Hebei Province, China, since 2023. The dataset, which spans the entire growth cycle of greenhouse tomatoes, was manually annotated to track pest occurrence. To process the data, principal component analysis (PCA) was applied to reduce the dimensionality of environmental factors. An improved random forest model was then developed to predict Tuta absoluta incidence. For comparison, the study also employed multiple linear regression, Bayesian regression, support vector machine, and BP neural network models as control models. The results revealed that the improved random forest model outperformed all other models, achieving the highest prediction accuracy. It had a root mean square error (RMSE) of 1.4587 and a 10 -fold cross-validation standard deviation of 1.3712. In contrast, the traditional multiple linear regression model had an RMSE of 3.4922 and a standard deviation of 1.4337, demonstrating its lower accuracy in comparison.

title: Explainable Artificial Intelligence for Crop Yield Prediction Using Agro-Climatic Data
abstract: Proper forecasting of crop yield is a requirement of proper agricultural planning and protection of food security. The current work presents a broad machine-learning-driven model of the prediction of crop yield, combining the range of regression models with strict evaluation criteria and elucidable artificial intelligence (XAI) methodologies. Agro-climatic, edaphic and nutrient related predictors were trained in decision tree, random forest, gradient-boosting, k nearest neighbors, support vector regression and deep neural networks. The evaluation of performance was conducted with the help of R2 and Root-Mean-Square-Error (RMSE), which showed that ensemble and deep -learning methods provide the best predictive values. Specifically, the highest accuracy was achieved with the Random Forest and Deep Neural Networks, which underscore their ability to estimate complex non-linear relationships among the dataset. Analysis of feature-importance identified temperature, humidity and soil quality as the most influential predictors of yield. Besides, lack of systematic bias and high generalisation was supported by error residual diagnostics. The explanations provided with SHAP also provided global and local answers to the decisions made by the model, thus increasing transparency and interpretability. Together, the proposed framework provides accurate, consistent and interpretable crop-yield predictions, providing priceless insights into data-driven agronomic decision-making and the promotion of sustainable farming systems.

title: Predicting Crop Yields using Deep Learning Models and Multi-Source Agricultural Data
abstract: It is essential to be able to accurately predict crop yield in advance in order to maintain global food security, use resources efficiently, and have sustainable agricultural practices. The availability of massive multi source agricultural data from satellite imagery, weather conditions, soil profile and yield records, which totally takes prediction to a new level is what really raises prediction to a new level of accuracy. This work is about using deep learning models such as CNN, RNN and hybrid architectures to bring about a powerful as well as a scalable framework for crop yield prediction. The creation of a system for prediction capable of scaling and being reliable is based on the multi-source data of the remote-sensing images, the weather conditions, the soil profile, and the yield records. The tests done on datasets of varieties have shown that the proposed system can be adapted to different data and that the accuracy can be improved to a great extent compared to the traditional methods. The performance of the model is gauged by error metrics like the Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) and the Mean Absolute Error (MAE). Comparative analysis shows that the hybrid model is more efficient in dealing with heterogeneous and incomplete data than other models. Among the main findings are the importance of using both the soil and the climate data and the potential of socio-economic variables to make the predictions richer. This paper is about the agriculture analytics industry, which faces problems such as heterogeneity of data, scalability, and model interpretability. The incorporation of explainable AI tools enables the framework to deliver the most useful insights to the users thus giving support to them in the proper management of resources, crop planning, and risk mitigation. The system is scalable evidenced by the deployment on the cloud which makes it possible to be used in different areas and farming systems.

title: Predictive Analytics for Climate Impact on Agriculture
abstract: The intersection of climate change and agriculture is exhibiting serious challenges that require innovative answers. This research is about understanding how a steered and complex analysis of weather data is bringing some positive results in agriculture as well as reducing its adverse effects. By utilizing the best machine-learning procedures and big data sets like meteorological data, soil quality parameters, normal crop yield records, etc., this study aims to develop a solid tool for estimating climate-related agricultural outcomes. The specific goals are to determine susceptible crops, predict yield fluctuations, and provide mechanisms for optimizing resources use and enhancing confidence in agriculture. The intended model is a combination of real-time data with area-specific and global climate patterns, viewed through the lens of predictive accuracy and the large number of types in agriculture in use at present, where it is also intended that it should work across. The aim of this undertaking is to enable sustainable agriculture through offering empirical and practical insights to stakeholders which will help them take climate action and realize food security despite environmental challenges by the use of data analysis tools.

title: AI for Monitoring Agricultural Supply Chains
abstract: The agricultural supply chain integration of the artificial intelligence (AI)-sourced technologies greatly made such solutions unique for, and a more appropriate way to, address the inefficiencies, the betrayals, and the bad decision-making processes. The object of this research is the application of AI-based technologies like machine learning, computer vision, and predictive analytics in monitoring and managing agricultural supply chains. Leveraging real-time data from IoT sensors, satellite imagery, and supply chain systems AI can render actionable insights about crop production, inventory levels, transportation logistics, and market demand forecasting. The research delves into the potential of AI technologies, in particular, to increase transparency, to prevent loss during transport and storage, and to adapt to the market change. Besides, barriers such as data privacy concerns, integration costs, and the need for proper rural infrastructure are analyzed. The handling of specific cases and in-depth performance analysis in this study indicate how AI-powered solutions can change the traditional ways of the agricultural supply chain thus ensuring both its sustainability and profitability to the stakeholders at the same time solving global food security issues.

title: AI for Forecasting Food Production in Agricultural Markets
abstract: The precision forecasting of food production is an essential component of food safety, supply chain effectiveness, and the agricultural economy's stability within the country's borders. This paper aims to examine the application of artificial intelligence (AI) in estimating food production levels in agricultural markets, which hinges on machine learning, deep learning, and data analytics technology advancements. The methodology proposed integrates various datasets from varied sources like weather conditions, soil characteristics, crop kinds, and market movements, to create a detailed forecasting model. The algorithms selected for the analysis are recurrent neural networks (RNN), convolutional neural networks (CNN), and ensemble techniques, which are thus shown to be superior to previous statistical approaches in terms of both accuracy and scale. The paper also recognizes the issues of data heterogeneity, feature selection, and model interpretability. The outcomes suggest that artificial intelligence (AI)-powered systems could facilitate more effective agricultural planning, policy development, and market analysis by stakeholders. The report concludes with suggestions for the implementation of AI tools in practical agricultural cases, underlining their importance in both sustainable development and global food security.

title: Crop Yield Prediction Using Machine Learning
abstract: The accuracy of crop yield prediction is a significant part of modern agriculture that determines how the farmers, officials, and supply chain managers make decisions. This paper gives insights into the use of machine learning (ML) techniques to make crop yield predictions more accurate and at the same time more scalable. The study utilizes historic agricultural data, weather patterns, soil properties, and crop-specific variability. The effectiveness of numerous ML models such as decision trees, support vector machines (SVM), and deep learning frameworks is evaluated through the experiments. The main principles that were followed were the selection of appropriate features and preprocessing to improve prediction accuracy and to cut the expense for computing. The influence of the suggested method is illustrated by taking a case study that uses publicly available datasets. The results show that ML models, especially those that use an ensemble approach and use a neural network, significantly exceed the traditional statistical methods in crop yield forecasts. The paper also points out such issues as the availability of data, feature engineering, and model interpretability as challenges and gives future research directions and recommendations for usage to achieve precision in agriculture. The work of this paper marks the probable role of machine learning in agriculture and the approach to using these technologies as a solution to the issues regarding global food security and sustainability.

title: AI for Crop Recommendation Systems
abstract: Agriculture is being boosted by serious AI technology to meet the challenges of resource optimization, climate variability, and food security. Farmers’ crop recommendation systems are of great importance like market demand and environmental sustainability. Furthermore, the proposed system also provides crop suggestions based on the analysis of soil properties, the weather conditions, market demand, and environmental sustainability as well. This paper is a contribution to the comprehensive approach to developing an AI-driven crop recommendation system by using large-scale agricultural datasets for training machine learning models. It also includes personal recommendations for specific cases integrating the information from soil quality surveys, weather forecasts, and yield statistics, to name a few. It uses supervised learning techniques such as Random Forests and Gradient Boosting, and the feature engineering of optimizing the model performance is combined, resulting in phenomenal accuracy and adaptability. Moreover, the research looks into blending the frameworks of federated learning with the obligation of the data privacy and collaboration among the members of the group of farmers. The results showed that AI-based crop recommendation systems can improve both agricultural production and sustainability in farming practices. The importance of AI as a tool to revolutionize agriculture, address issues of food insecurity, and implement data-driven decision-making in intelligent farming ecosystems is stressed by the study.

title: Drought Prediction for Agricultural Planning
abstract: The agricultural output is being reduced considerably due to the drought, consequently threatening global food securities. This research is based on very recent and advanced machine-learning models that predict drought to improve agricultural planning. The study uses old weather conditions, soil moisture levels, and satellite images to find the specific key patterns and variables related to drought claims. To predict the occurrence of droughts and thus act, the proposed framework integrates data preprocessing techniques, such as feature selection and machine learning algorithms such as Neural Networks, Gradient Boosting, and Random Forest, with the help of which the proposed method is approximately as good as or even better than using traditional methods in the drought prediction in regions with different climates. The case shows that besides these common climatic regions, the model's predictions can also be highly accurate in other areas and highly reliable and precise ones. The report emphasizes the role of early drought warning in farmers and policymakers' resource allocation, irrigation planning, and crop selection processes. This study supports the progress of intelligent decision-making systems, leading to more resource-efficient and sustainable agricultural systems in the changing climate.

title: Using Machine Learning to Assess the Impact of Climate Change on Crop Yields
abstract: The alteration of extreme weather conditions which may be due to climate change results in significant challenges worldwide in agricultural productivity. Understanding the way climatic factors link with crop yields is vital to food security and developing adaptive strategies. This research aims to provide a framework for machine learning (ML) techniques in the assessment of how climate change affects crop yields. By making use of the significant amounts of historical climate and crop production data, models were rendered to predict yield responses to changing climatic scenarios. Key factors like temperature, precipitation, and soil health were analyzed to assess their impact on the growth of crops. To capture the complex relationships between climatic variables and agricultural outputs, advanced machine learning algorithms like regression models, neural networks, and ensemble methods were utilized. The results indicate that machine learning provides deep predictive capability and thus it can be earnestly utilized to reveal potential yield reductions and to identify appropriate mitigation strategies. This study presents AI-driven methods as a potential support for policymakers and farmers in combatting climate change-related challenges in agriculture.

title: Yield Prediction in Organic Farming
abstract: Organic farming has become a really popular and durable alternative to traditional high input agriculture as it is good for the environment as well as health. On the other hand, however, it is still a really hard job to forecast the crop yield in organic farming because of the complicated interplay of extenuating circumstances such as soil quality, etc., and pest dynamics and crop management practices. Through the use of machine learning (ML) techniques this paper will dive into the yield prediction in organic farming based on various data sources such as soil composition, and weather forecasts, and past yield records. The study will devise advanced ML models that are used in Web services such as random forests, support vector machines, and neural networks for the purpose of creating an intense method for perfect yield predictions. The models presented will be trained on and confirmed by organic farm datasets such as organic soil amendments, pest control methods, and crop rotation patterns. Hence, the results show that the ML-based method is way better than the traditional statistical way as it gives higher accuracy and is more flexible to the recent changes in organic farming. The research is a paradigm of the combination of artificial intelligence with organic farming practices that would give a good harvest to farmers as well as help in global food security and sustainability in an environmentally friendly way.

title: Livestock Health Monitoring Using Machine Learning
abstract: Livestock health and productivity are the primary elements of the agricultural and food supply chain, having a direct influence on the economic sustainability of food security. The traditional methods of monitoring the health of livestock rely on manual observation and delayed responses, which can bring about productivity loss and an increased risk of mortality. The paper focuses on the application of machine-learning (ML) techniques in transforming livestock health monitoring from the current, mostly brained-on, observation-based, and response-based systems to the ML-driven data-wise real-time monitoring. ML models can intelligently predict diseases, detect anomalies, and optimize veterinary interventions by accessing data from wearable sensors, monitoring the environment, and analyzing behavioral patterns. This study assesses various ML algorithms like decision trees, support vector machines, and deep learning models, for their capability in health prediction and anomaly detection. Moreover, it reveals the use of the Internet of Things (IoT) devices for the continual acquisition of data, and of the federated learning system for the integration of data from various farms with the help of IoT devices, which is important for privacy and security of the data. The framework suggests increasing the effectiveness of detecting diseases in the early stages, reducing the costs of intervention, and improving animal welfare. The experimental evaluation shows that ML is a highly accurate and reliable tool in determining the health status of livestock, thus becoming a significant approach for advancing smart agriculture and sustainable farming.

title: Machine Learning for Accurate Yield Prediction
abstract: Accurate crop yield prediction is critical for optimizing resource allocation, meeting sustainability regulations, and ensuring food security. This study integrates multi-source datasets, including NDVI indices, soil profiles, and historical weather information, to develop and evaluate yield prediction models. Random Forest and XGBoost were employed to capture the non-linear interactions among environmental variables and crop performance. Experimental results demonstrate that both methods achieve high predictive accuracy, with Random Forest explaining 88 percent and XGBoost explaining 91 percent of the yield variability. These findings highlight the importance of combining satellite imagery, soil surveys, and climate data, paving the way for more efficient, data-driven agricultural management.

title: Quantum Machine Learning in Crop Disease Monitoring: Opportunities and Challenges to Practical Implementation
abstract: Agriculture is increasingly threatened by diverse global security challenges, including climate change, biodiversity loss, and health security risks, underscoring the need for sustainable practices to ensure food security for future generations. Advanced technologies such as quantum machine learning (QML) offer transformative potential in addressing these challenges by enhancing crop disease monitoring systems. This paper explores the implementation of QML in agriculture, with a particular focus on its application to crop disease detection and prevention. Leveraging image processing, sensory data analysis, and spectral imaging, QML algorithms demonstrate superior accuracy and efficiency in early disease recognition, surpassing traditional methods. A case study of Hungary's crop disease monitoring system illustrates the practical benefits of integrating QML with technologies such as remote sensing and IoT. By enabling real-time monitoring and predictive analytics, QML not only aids in mitigating crop losses but also contributes to sustainable agricultural practices and global food security. Despite current limitations in quantum hardware, advancements in QML present promising opportunities for revolutionizing agricultural systems and ensuring resilience against evolving threats.

title: Crop Yield Estimation in India Using Machine Learning
abstract: Agriculture in India is significant economic support. The population growth is the major challenge for food security. The population growth makes a rise in demand which requires farmers to produce more from the same agriculture land in respect to increase the supply. Technology can help farmers to produce more with the help of crop yield prediction. The main aim of this paper is to predict crop yield using area, yield, production, and area under irrigation. Four machine learning techniques Decision Tree, Linear Regression, Lasso regression, and Ridge Regression have been applied to estimate the crop yield. Cross validations methods, for validation, mean absolute error, mean squared error, and root mean squared error, were used to validate. The Decision tree outperforms other machine learning techniques.

title: Fair Price Prediction of Vegetables for Farmers Using Machine Learning
abstract: Vegetable price fluctuations have a significant impact on farmer revenues, access for consumers, and food security in India. Conventional statistical techniques like ARIMA only capture patterns but cannot model the non-linear and climate-responsive nature of perishable vegetables. In this research, a data-driven forecasting model of vegetable prices for Ranchi, Jharkhand, is introduced, incorporating both machine learning and deep learning approaches. A data set from January 2022 to August 2025 contains day-to-day prices of bottle gourd, green chilli, onion, and tomato and climatic variables like mean temperature and rainfall. Four models—Random Forest (RF), Decision Tree (DT), XGBoost, and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks—were trained and tested their performance using R2, MAE, and RMSE measures. The results indicates that LSTM obtains better accuracy, especially for unstable commodities such as green chilli, whereas Random Forest and XGBoost provide competing performance for comparatively stable vegetables. The results indicate the advantage of using climate information in localized price forecasting, providing useful insights for short-term planning, storage management, and policy making.

title: Forecasting Temperature and Rainfall for Crop Cultivation with Classification of Ground Water Level
abstract: These days, wireless telecommunication networks offer a viable replacement for traditional monitoring systems and rainfall measuring gear. Empirical computing techniques are less accurate representations of real data because to the vast amounts of data connected to rainfall and telecommunication networks. In order to analyse massive data and provide real measurements more accurately, deep learning models are suggested. This project examined the outcomes of experimental measurements used to monitor rainfall. This study's main objective is to demonstrate a neural network-based classification method for rainfall data based on historical production data. Farmers can take the appropriate actions to gauge crop yield in the upcoming season with the aid of classification based on the rainfall from prior years. Understanding and evaluating crop output in the future can assist to protect food security and lessen the effects of climate change. The ARMA (Auto Regressive Moving} {Average) approach is employed in this work for the proposed work. For our country, data from the previous ten years are used to calculate rainfall and ground water levels. In the proposed study, records in the ground water level data set are classified by an ARIMA model, and what the model predicts for additional test record data sets. The brand-new design help in researching past ground water levels and forecasting levels in the upcoming.

title: Blending Forest with Neural Networks: An Insight into Marula Leaf Disease Prediction
abstract: The economic value of Marula trees is investigated here by looking at the impact of disease on fruit production. The prediction of eight major Marula diseases is made possible with the introduction of a novel technology that combines Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Random Forests. This model incorporates the feature-extracting power of a CNN with the robustness of a Random Forests ensemble. It uses four ReLU-activated convolutional layers and a max-pooling layer to process the data, which consists of photos of both healthy and diseased Marula leaves. These features are fed into Random Forest, which uses them to make diagnoses. The model's strong predictive capacity is demonstrated by evaluation measures showing precision and recall rates between 88.65% and 94.92%. Overall accuracy is 98%, and the Fl-Score indicates a well-balanced performance from the model. Metrics like “Macro Average” show how much better the model performs than other approaches. The study demonstrates the potential of combining deep and ensemble learning for disease prediction, and hence makes a substantial contribution to agricultural disease management. It lays the groundwork for the sustainable production of Marula and highlights the broader implications for global food security and future agricultural innovation based on machine learning.

title: Artificial Intelligence for Irrigation System Optimization: Leveraging Predictive Analytics to Enhance Water Management and Decrease Agricultural Resource Consumption
abstract: Irrigation system optimization is of utmost importance for sustainable agriculture in light of the growing worldwide water shortage caused by climate change and rising agricultural needs. In order to improve water management techniques and decrease agricultural resource use, this project investigates the use of AI and predictive analytics.
