An intelligent irrigation system that adapts water distribution in real-time according to predictive analytics is created in this study by combining state-of-the-art machine learning algorithms with real-time data from a variety of sources, such as weather predictions, soil moisture levels, and crop water needs. In order to reduce water waste and maximize irrigation efficiency, the suggested framework uses past data to train artificial intelligence models. Results from field studies on a variety of crops show that water efficiency has been improved, allowing for 30% reductions in irrigation water use without sacrificing or diminishing crop yields. Sustainable farming practices and better resource management are two additional benefits that farmers reap from using AI-driven insights to inform their decision-making. This research emphasizes the revolutionary power of AI to update irrigation methods, leading to more robust agricultural systems. This study highlights the significance of data-driven methods to water management in achieving food security and environmental sustainability through the integration of technology and agriculture. If we want to see optimal irrigation practices adopted all throughout the world, our next step is to improve the predictive models and make the framework function in more diverse agricultural settings.

title: A Comprehensive Analysis Of The Detection And Classification Of Potato And Corn Leaf Diseases Utilizing Deep Learning Methods
abstract: Due to their great nutritional content, potatoes and maize are necessary staple crops that require a strong food security system. Many diseases can negatively impact crop cultivation, thus it is critical to identify them as soon as possible to avoid output losses and agricultural devastation. Traditional methods for diagnosing plant diseases can be labor-intensive, inaccurate, and imprecise. Farms need to use computerized image processing technologies to avoid significant crop losses due to delayed identification. Farmers may more precisely and successfully manage plant diseases by using AI and machine learning techniques for image segmentation, classification, and feature extraction. As a consequence, yields will rise and losses will fall. Researchers have developed a number of techniques to forecast agricultural diseases by examining photos of damaged leaves. Even though different models and approaches are now employed to diagnose plant diseases, there is always room for improvement in light of recent discoveries and conversations. Technology has the potential to significantly boost crop output worldwide, and big data can be used to train models and techniques that more accurately detect plant diseases and deal with low-yield problems. Previous studies have shown that machine learning and deep learning are effective in this situation. In order to classify and identify potato and maize leaf diseases using deep learning techniques, a number of methodologies and approaches have been thoroughly analyzed and critically examined in this research. The study looks into the possible difficulties in using image processing to detect diseases in the leaves of potatoes and maize plants, as well as the advantages and disadvantages of various technological solutions. The findings and forecasts for the future of deep learning-based potato and maize disease detection are presented in the paper’s conclusion.

title: A Comprehensive Analysis of Machine Learning Techniques for Crop Yield Prediction Using Remote Sensing Data
abstract: This paper investigates the application of machine learning techniques for crop yield prediction, focusing on K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Random Forest, and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks. Accurate crop yield forecasting is critical for enhancing agricultural productivity and ensuring food security in the face of climate change and growing populations. The study utilizes diverse datasets comprising climatic, soil, and historical yield data, processed through various preprocessing techniques. Performance metrics such as accuracy, precision, and recall are employed to evaluate the models. Results are tested using LSTM, KNN and Random Forest in terms of prediction accuracy. The findings demonstrate that machine learning can significantly improve yield forecasting, providing essential insights for farmers and agricultural planners. Future research directions include integrating additional variables and exploring hybrid models to further enhance prediction capabilities.

title: Indian French Bean Varieties: CNN vs. Decision Trees Model Analysis
abstract: There is no doubt that crop variety improvement and the use of efficient analytical methods that contribute to high agricultural production and food security are crucial. It is research focused on the Comparison of Indian French bean (Phaseolus vulgaris) varieties: Selection-9, Pusa Parvati, and Arka Suvidha using a hybrid Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and Decision Tree (DT) model. The major aim, therefore, is to assess the effectiveness of this integrated model in correctly sorting and forecasting the yields of these bean types under various agroecological circumstances. This dataset includes observational field data along with morphological and phenological characters of plants collected from various experimental sites. Thus, the proposed CNN-DT model embeds the feature extraction capacity of CNNs with the interpretability and decision-making effectiveness of DT. It is this integration that would endeavor to utilize the inherent advantages of the two approaches to improve the classification of the crops and profitability of crop selection and management. This suggests that the hybrid model improves the classification accuracy and reliability better as compared to the traditional isolated models. The assessment of the model in terms of accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score highlights a performance enhancement when differentiating the three types of French beans. Moreover, the present work suggests the use of state-of-the-art methods in machine learning for agricultural studies and can be useful for the improvement of decision-making mechanisms used by farmers and agronomists. From the findings of this study, it is clear that this is a need to combine modern learning techniques with ordinary farming practices when it comes to picking the right crops and improving production. Altogether, the study provides significant recommendations for AI-domain application in agriculture to increase the effectiveness of crop cultivation more efficiently.

title: Crop Prediction Based on Factors of the Agricultural Environment Using Machine Learning
abstract: Agriculture is a critical sector that supports human life by supplying food, fiber and other necessary goods. It is essential to the world economy and directly related to food security and environmental sustainability. Predicting crop outcomes in agriculture is essential for maximizing yield, relying heavily on environmental factors like temperature, rainfall, and soil conditions. Machine learning (ML) has become a valuable tool in agriculture, transforming traditional farming methods with innovative solutions to tackle these challenges. This study focuses on applying machine learning approaches to crop outcome prediction in agriculture. The dataset, which includes data on weather conditions, soil properties, and crop characteristics, was analyzed. After data preprocessing, feature selection methods were used to identify the most influential variables for predicting crop yields. Subsequently, machine learning models were created and trained using the selected features to forecast crop outcomes. The models’ performance was then assessed, and optimization strategies were implemented to improve their predictive accuracy. Through this research, the project aims to offer valuable insights into the factors that impact crop outcomes, ultimately leading to enhanced agricultural practices and productivity.

title: Strength of Ensemble Learning in Voting Classifier for Crop Yield Prediction
abstract: Crop Yield Prediction (CYP) plays a vital role in mitigating emerging food security challenges, particularly when the rapid shifts in global climate patterns occur. Machine Learning (ML) is crucial for CYP because it can estimate the crop production based on different characteristics such as environmental characteristics, soil fertilizers, and crop management. Researchers have used lots of ML techniques with distinct kinds of data analytics techniques. Thus, this study proposes an ensemble model, named Voting-based Ensemble Expert System for Crop Yield Prediction (VEESCYP) to predict the best crop yield for the Assam state of India. This study tries to present the strength of a voting classifier with Ensemble Learning (EL) approaches. The proposed VEESCYP model has performed some data preprocessing tasks before classification, such as the Multiple Imputation by Chained Equation (MICE) to treat the missing values, Isolation Forest (IF) for outlier detection, Genetic Algorithm (GA) for feature selection and Robust Scaling (RS) for data normalization. To show the strength of EL techniques in voting classifier, the proposed VEESCYP model compares with some standard ML algorithms, a Voting-based EL technique using standard ML algorithms and some existing models presented in the literature.

title: Precision Agriculture: Sensor Network for Optimal Field Monitoring
abstract: Precision agriculture leverages Internet of Things (IoT) technologies and machine learning to optimize crop management and enhance agricultural productivity. This study explores the integration of IoT sensors for real-time monitoring of field and atmospheric conditions, including soil moisture, temperature, humidity, and light levels. By collecting and analyzing this data, machine learning algorithms can identify patterns and predict crop yields with higher accuracy. The predictive models facilitate informed decision-making, leading to increased efficiency and sustainability in farming practices. This research highlights the potential of IoT and machine learning to transform agriculture, reduce resource waste, and improve food security.

title: Agriculture crop recommendation based on productivity and seasons
abstract: Precision agriculture is important in maximizing crop yields through the delivery of customized advice based on environmental and soil conditions. This paper presents a sophisticated crop recommendation system that employs machine learning methods to examine soil characteristics, past yield data, and seasonal trends. It utilizes a convolutional neural network (CNN) for predicting appropriate crops for any particular field based on weather forecasting to enable decision making by the farmer for enhancing output and maximizing resources. High predictability by combining weather parameters with past yields enhances resource reduction for wastage to a high percentage. Testing in experimental processes is shown to surpass conventional outcomes based on efficiency improvement and enhancement in precision with minimal variability during tests under a range of different climates. The findings obtained from this research help in further developing intelligent farm systems to ensure global food security through data-intensive agricultural practices. Image-based extraction of NPK can attain a 83% accuracy rate if trained efficiently using actual soil samples. The crop suggestion model generally has a 91% accuracy, although this also varies with the quantity and quality of the training set and how well the model has been tuned.

title: Pf-Sds: a Framework for Crop Yield Prediction Based on Deep Forest and Interpretability
abstract: Crop yield forecasting is central to maintaining the global food security system. It enables governments and relevant regulatory agencies to anticipate potential supply and demand fluctuations in advance and make countermeasures. Some researchers have used different methods to predict it, including traditional methods based on empirical formulas, statistical models, or expert systems, while many have adopted strategies based on deep learning. In the former research work, accuracy and adaptability are challenging to be guaranteed. The latter has the disadvantage of poor interpretation and opacity. In response to the above problems, We designed a crop yield forecasting framework with high accuracy and high interpretability of variable dependencies, dubbed PF-SDS. In the framework of PF-SDS, a proven and feasible Sequential Forward Selection (SFS) feature selection algorithm was introduced to enhance the model's generalization ability. In addition, we use SHAP values to conduct an in-depth explanatory analysis of the importance of model features, thus providing a scientific and easy to understand basis for crop planting management practices. Numerous experimental results show the excellent performance of the PF-SDS framework.

title: Crop Selection and Cultivaton using Machine Learning
abstract: In the face of the growing global population and the challenges posed by climate change, sustainable agriculture practices are essential. This paper explores the use of Machine Learning (ML) in crop selection and cultivation to address these challenges. Traditional methods are often inadequate given the increasing population and shifting climate patterns. Machine Learning, with its data-driven and predictive approach, has the potential to revolutionize crop management. The study investigates various ML algorithms like neural networks, decision trees, and ensemble models to analyze datasets covering factors such as soil quality, climate conditions, and historical crop performance. By using these algorithms, the goal is to optimize crop selection for specific regions, leading to higher yields and reduced environmental impact. The paper also explores real-time data acquisition methods like IoT sensors and satellite imagery to gain a comprehensive understanding of agricultural landscapes. Furthermore, the paper discusses how ML algorithms can be used in precision agriculture, enabling farmers to make informed decisions regarding irrigation, fertilization, and pest control. By analyzing extensive datasets, these algorithms can predict the best cultivation practices, reducing resource wastage and improving efficiency. The integration of Machine Learning not only provides a data-driven approach to crop selection but also promotes sustainable agriculture, contributing to food security and environmental conservation. This research encourages the adoption of Machine Learning in agriculture, highlighting its transformative potential in global food production systems. By harnessing the power of artificial intelligence, the paper envisions a future where agricultural practices are not only productive and efficient but also environmentally conscious and sustainable.

title: An Enhanced Deep Learning Model for Tomato Leaf Disease Prediction
abstract: The rising need for tomato cultivation has raised concerns about detecting and diagnosing diseases affecting tomato plants. Tomato leaf disease prediction faces several challenges, including the variability of symptoms, limited availability of high-quality data, lack of standardization in disease identification and classification, and difficulty in accounting for environmental factors such as temperature and humidity. These challenges can make it challenging to develop accurate and reliable predictive models, particularly in developing countries. Detecting these diseases in the earlier stage is essential to prevent losses in yield and ensure food security. In current years, deep learning approaches have been increasingly utilized to tackle this issue. In this work, an improved deep learning model is introduced for predicting leaf diseases of tomato plants. The proposed model is based on a visual geometric group VGG-16 architecture, which has been proven effective in image classification tasks. The paper presents a Bayesian optimization method that involves fine-tuning a pre-trained VGG-16 model with a collection of images. To further increase the accuracy of the proposed work, data augmentation techniques are incorporated, such as random rotations, flips, and brightness adjustments, which increase the diversity of the training data. The diseases of tomato leaf prediction model are tested on both a publicly accessible dataset and custom dataset of tomato plant’s leaf images. The experimental results demonstrate that the VGG-16 model with Bayesian optimization approach performs well than other methods.

title: Computer Vision Based Crop Yield Prediction for Precision Agriculture Using Machine Learning Model
abstract: Precision agriculture methodologies, which integrate digitalization and automation, are driving a revolution in agriculture through the use of computer vision technology. This intelligent agriculture could also address significant global issues such as food security and sustainability. Advancements in computer and machine vision have significantly improved the detection, quality assessment, and yield estimation processes for various fruit crops; nevertheless, there are yet no completely established systems capable of generating an accurate yield map for vegetable crops. The objectives of a machine vision-based yield monitor were the classification of size (count) and the continuous enumeration of agricultural produce. The proposed system employs a linear regression machine learning model for feature selection and decision tree machine learning model to predict healthy crop yields and provide the optimal framework for implementing completely autonomous farms in real time. The performance of the proposed machine learning model is accessed by Mean Absolute Error (MAE) and R-squared (R2) ranking scores.

title: Framework for Addressing Agricultural Water Scarcity Using Big Data and IoT
abstract: The intensifying global water scarcity crisis presents an unprecedented challenge to agricultural sustainability and food security. This research introduces an innovative framework that leverages Internet of Things (IoT) technologies, Big Data analytics, and artificial intelligence to address agricultural water management systematically. Our methodology integrates real-time sensor networks, advanced machine learning algorithms, and automated irrigation control systems within a unified architectural framework. Through empirical evaluation conducted on a 50-hectare cotton farm over a 120-day growing season, we demonstrate that our proposed framework achieves significant improvements: 25% water savings, 50% higher water use efficiency, and 12.5 % increased crop yield compared to conventional irrigation methods. The framework incorporates state-of-the-art machine learning models, achieving 91% accuracy in irrigation demand forecasting through ensemble approaches combining LSTM networks and transformer-based architectures. We present a comprehensive analysis of implementation challenges across technological, socioeconomic, and policy dimensions' providing evidence-based recommendations for scaling IoT-based precision irrigation systems. This research contributes to the emerging field of digital agriculture by offering both theoretical foundations and practical implementation strategies for sustainable water management solutions.

title: Deep Learning for Precise Crop Yield Prediction: A Comprehensive Data-Driven Agricultural Review
abstract: Precise estimation of crop yield is crucial for tackling food security issues and enhancing agricultural efficiency. Recent advancements in deep learning techniques have introduced powerful tools for improving crop yield forecasts, utilizing large volumes of data obtained from various sources. This comprehensive review explores the adoption of deep learning strategies for forecasting crop outputs, synthesizing recent research and developments in this field. This study investigates multiple deep learning frameworks such as Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, and integrated hybrid approaches, emphasizing their unique roles and their advantages in crop yield forecasting. The review covers key areas such as the integration of satellite imagery, weather data, soil characteristics, and historical yield records into deep learning models. CNNs are utilized for analyzing spatial data from satellite images to assess crop health and growth patterns, while RNNs and LSTMs are employed to model temporal dependencies in weather and climate data. Hybrid models combine these approaches to enhance predictive accuracy by addressing both spatial and temporal factors. We discuss the advantages of these deep learning techniques, including improved prediction accuracy and the ability to handle complex, non-linear relationships in large datasets. Challenges in applying deep learning to crop yield prediction are also addressed, such as issues with data quality, model interpretability, and computational resource requirements. The review highlights key findings from recent research, organizing them according to the type of deep learning technique employed and the components they focus on. Future research directions are proposed, emphasizing the need for better integration of diverse data sources, improved model transparency, and scalable solutions to enhance the practical applicability of deep learning in agriculture. This review aims to provide researchers and practitioners with a thorough understanding of current deep learning applications in crop yield prediction, guiding future advancements in the field.

title: Evaluation of Rice Yield Estimation from Satellite Data by Integrating Hybrid Regression Models
abstract: Precise prediction of yields in paddy crop provides a safe agricultural pricing that yields to optimal resource commitments that assure food security. Traditional yield estimation techniques struggle to examine changing environmental conditions because they use statistical methods and field survey data. Real-time extensive monitoring through satellite-based remote sensing technology and meteorological data collection serves as a superior alternative to traditional crop observation approaches. This research created an intricate forecasting system that uses Sentinel-2 satellite images and open-meteo meteorological data through machine learning methods. Rice-growing areas are analysed through the use of different regression models together with feature extraction methods. The experimental testing shows how machine learning (ML) combination models beat traditional statistical methods to deliver better forecast predictions. In current study, the rice yield prediction is evaluated by four different models including Lasso Regression, Random Forest, Support Vector, XGBoost and Neural Network Regressor. The highest accuracy achieved by Random Forest Regressor i.e.$R^{2}$value 0.99.

title: Predictive Analytics for Reducing Post-Harvest Losses in Agriculture
abstract: Postharvest losses in agriculture are a major challenge to food security, the economic viability of agriculture, and sustainable agricultural practices all over the globe. Any losses in quantity and quality of an agricultural produce that occur between harvest and consumption are deemed postharvest losses; and these constitute a serious challenge, especially in most developing nations. This study investigates the possible application of predictive analytics as a game changer in minimizing postharvest losses by allowing data-driven decisions along the agricultural value chain. Predictive models will assess environmental parameters in real-time supplemented by historical data on the crops and supply chain metrics to assess spoilage risk, thus optimizing storage and transport environments and timely market interventions. The study utilizes machine learning algorithms such as regression analysis, decision trees, and also time series forecasting in developing models that can predict probable loss scenarios for selected key crops; this data will include satellite imagery, weather data, storage facility records, and also the marketing trends. Results from the predictive models are measured in terms of accuracy, scalability, and usability for farmers, cooperatives, and policymakers. The research further discusses data availability, integration across heterogeneous systems, and the injustice presented to smallholder farmers due to the digital literacy divide. The results indicate that predictive analytics can plug in an early warning and actionable insight so that stakeholders can act before any spoilage occurs, which significantly brings down post-harvest losses. Some case studies from selected regions have demonstrated improvements in storage planning, supply chain coordination, and post-harvest handling practices. The paper concludes with recommendations for integrating predictive tools with agricultural extension systems and policies at the state level with due consideration for capacity building, development of digital infrastructure, and partnership with the private sector. The ultimate expectation is that predictive analytics can therefore allow for increased resilience, efficiency, and sustainability within the agricultural system.

title: Eggplant Yield Prediction Utilizing 130 Locally Collected Genotypes and Machine Learning Model
abstract: Accurate crop yield prediction has long been a challenge for the agricultural community, with significant consequences for food security, farmer livelihoods, and strategic planning. Traditional forecasting methods based on agro-meteorological data have proven inadequate for capturing the wide variety of factors impacting production. Eggplant is also well-known throughout the world as one of the most popular fruit vegetables, and demand for this vegetable is growing as the world’s population grows. Yield, i.e agricultural production per plant is significantly related to fruit diameter, fruits per plant, percent of fruit infestation by brinjal shoot and fruit borer, and fruit weight attributes, indicating that direct selection based on fruit number and fruit weight may be adequate for improving other traits. This study demonstrates a machine learning approach for precise eggplant yield prediction using data from different regions of Bangladesh, analyzing three regression algorithms such as categorical boosting regression (CatBR), light gradient boosting regression (LGBMR), and extreme gradient boosting regression (XGBR), as well as the Bayesian approach used for choosing optimal hyperparameters. CatBR emerged as the best-performing algorithm for eggplant yield prediction, utilizing 10 genetic parameters. The CatBR model we used performed admirably, displaying both reliability and speed in forecasting crop yields based on the most important variables. It achieved an R2score of 68.02%, as well as an MSE score of 3.8117, an MAE score of 1.3090, and a MedAE score of 0.9949. Notably, our proposed model is capable of flawlessly combining and analyzing data sourced from various regions across Bangladesh, ensuring high precision and avoiding model overfitting.

title: Crop Yield Prediction: Robust Machine Learning Approaches for Precision Agriculture
abstract: Accurate crop yield predictions have become crucial for agriculture industries and governments to make intelligent crop management decisions and to guarantee food security. In today’s data driven world, machine learning has been successfully applied in crop yield prediction, helping to determine the appropriate crops to grow in a particular area and how to maximize their production during the crop's growing and reaping seasons. Despite progress in crop yield forecasting, further research is necessary. This work represents a significant advance for the field of Precision Agriculture (PA) and has the potential to benefit farmers and agronomists greatly. By utilizing simple input parameters such as average temperature, area, average rainfall, and usage of pesticides, a helpful tool for enhancing crop yield estimation has been proposed. Machine Learning (ML) algorithms including Random Forest (RF), Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN), Multilayer Perceptron (MLP), Adaptive Boosting (AdaBoost), and Decision Tree (DT) have been employed to enhance the performance of the model and offer more precise forecasting. Out of these six ML-based models, RF (MSE= 1.446, RMSE= 3.803, MAE= 2.11 and R2=0.999) and XGBoost (MSE= 1.542, RMSE= 2.691, MAE= 2.053 and R2=0.999) outperformed other four above-mentioned algorithms. This proposed system helps agronomist make informed decisions about their harvest, maximizing their yields and profits for tropical nations across the globe.

title: Evaluation of Prediction Accuracy in ARIMA and LSTM Algorithms for Agricultural Commodity Prices
abstract: Rice is one of the most important crops in the world because more than 50% of the world’s population consumes this plant as a staple food. Predicting the price of rice is crucial due to its significant impact on inflation. It is expected that this rice price prediction can maintain the availability of rice in the coming period to overcome price fluctuations and help the government in taking the necessary policies. Many studies have been carried out using various time series algorithm methods. However, this study uniquely contributes by not only comparing the predictive accuracy of ARIMA and LSTM models but also by analyzing their computational efficiency and applicability in real-world scenarios. Unlike previous studies, our research highlights the specific conditions under which each model performs optimally, providing practical guidelines for model selection in rice price forecasting. The main objective of this article is to analyze the comparison of time series forecasting methods which produces the best predictions with respect to higher forecasting accuracy and lower forecasting errors. The main contribution of this research is conducting comparative analysis and empirical studies with the aim of investigating the performance of traditional forecasting methods and deep learning-based algorithms using rice price datasets sourced from food stations as a government instrument in controlling rice prices in DKI Jakarta which has a strategic function for food security. In DKI Jakarta and its surroundings and becomes a price reference for the national rice market. This research uses the ARIMA (8,2,1) method with Moving Average and LSTM. Based on the evaluation matrix for the ARIMA Model, each MAE is 6.41, MSE is 146.48, RMSE is 12.1, MAPE is 0.0004. For the LSTM Model, respectively, MAE is 28.92, MSE is 1325.80, RMSE is 36.4, MAPE is 0.9857. Based on the MAPE target, the ARIMA model with a value of 0.0004% has an excellent accuracy level.

title: Enhanced Drought Analysis in Bangladesh: A Machine Learning Approach for Severity Classification Using Satellite Data
abstract: Drought poses a pervasive environmental challenge in Bangladesh, impacting agriculture, socio-economic stability, and food security due to its unique geographic and anthropogenic vulnerabilities. Traditional drought indices, such as the Standardized Precipitation Index (SPI) and Palmer Drought Severity Index (PDSI), often overlook crucial factors like soil moisture and temperature, limiting their resolution. Moreover, current machine learning models applied to drought prediction have been underexplored in the context of Bangladesh, lacking a comprehensive integration of satellite data across multiple districts. To address these gaps, we propose a satellite data-driven machine learning framework to classify drought across 38 districts of Bangladesh. Using unsupervised algorithms like K-means and Bayesian Gaussian Mixture for clustering, followed by classification models such as KNN, Random Forest, Decision Tree, and Naive Bayes, the framework integrates weather data (humidity, soil moisture, temperature) from 2012-2024. This approach successfully classifies drought severity into different levels. However, it shows significant variabilities in drought vulnerabilities across regions which highlights the aptitude of machine learning models in terms of identifying and predicting drought conditions.

title: Agri-Light-Fed: Lightweight Federated Learning with Explainable AI for Efficient and Privacy-Preserving Crop Yield Prediction
abstract: Accurate and efficient crop yield prediction is essential for sustainable agriculture and food security. However, traditional machine learning (ML) models often require heavy computation, centralized data and lack interpretability. This paper proposes a lightweight and privacy-preserving framework that integrates Federated Learning (FL) with eXplainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) for multi-crop yield forecasting. Four lightweight gradient boosting algorithms (LightGBM, XGBoost, CatBoost and PyBoost) were evaluated under both accuracy and computational efficiency metrics. Among them, PyBoost achieved the highest predictive accuracy ($\mathbf{R}^{\mathbf{2}}=\mathbf{0. 9 9 0 2}$, MAPE$=\mathbf{0. 0 1 9}$), while CatBoost offered the shortest training time and the lowest memory utilization, making it suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. The comparative analysis shows that PyBoost balances accuracy with moderate resource use, whereas CatBoost excels in fast inference and efficient memory usage. SHAP-based XAI further provided interpretability by highlighting key features such as soil moisture, humidity and sunlight hours. Finally, federated training preserved data privacy while maintaining competitive performance (average$\mathbf{R}^{\mathbf{2}} =0.977$across three FL rounds) with only a minor trade-off compared to centralized models. Overall, the proposed framework delivers a lightweight, interpretable and privacy-preserving solution for scalable smart agriculture.

title: AgriCast: Weather-Based Forecasting of Staple Crop Prices with Machine Learning and Deep Learning
abstract: This study predicts the prices of three important crops, potato, tomato, and onion, by using weather data. The goal is to strengthen food security in this region, which is sensitive to climate change. For developing countries, sudden price hikes of crops can create hardship for low-income families who depend on them for daily meals. So, reliable forecasts can provide early warnings, which enable households to plan crop purchases earlier, farmers to adjust production, and policymakers to design timely interventions. The research initially focuses on the Sylhet region of Bangladesh as a reference for South Asia, where countries experience similar agro-climatic conditions and weather events such as floods, which can trigger price rises of these crops. To address this problem, a customized and unique methodology has been built to collect the dataset from two renowned websites that combine weekly crop prices with weather variables (temperature, rainfall, and humidity) from January 2010 to June 2025. This dataset is the largest of its kind for weekly agricultural data in the region, with 809 data instances for each crop. After that, several machine learning and deep learning models were evaluated. Among them, Support Vector Regressor (SVR) ($\mathrm{R}^{\mathrm{2}} = \text{0. 9 9 7 3}$) gave the best overall results, while GRU ($\mathrm{R}^{\mathrm{2}} =0.9909$) and ANN ($R^{2}=0.9902$) also performed significantly. GRU ($\mathrm{R}^{\mathrm{2}} = \text{0. 9 5 5 2}$) worked best for potatoes, and ANN and SVR achieved very high accuracy for onions ($\mathrm{R}^{\mathrm{2}} > \text{0. 9 9 6}$and RMSE$\boldsymbol{>}$1.74), outperforming all the existing cutting-edge systems. This work used Sylhet as the reference, but the method can be applied on a larger scale across similar regions of South Asia. For this reason, the codebase and dataset will be publicly available upon publication to encourage future research work.

title: Lightweight Federated and Explainable AI Enhanced Crop Yield Forecasting in Heterogeneous Agricultural Systems
abstract: Crop yield estimation directly affects food security, resource utilization and agricultural decision making. The complexity of environmental interactions with soil properties and farming practices makes accurate prediction challenging by traditional methods. This paper introduces a unified lightweight framework based on advanced machine learning (ML), explainable AI (XAI) and federated learning to address these challenges. Four machine learning (ML) models (Random Forest, LightGBM, XGBoost and CatBoost) were compared across a multi-crop data. Results indicate that all the models obtained high correlations between observed and predicted yields; however, CatBoost appears to have been the best fit with an$\mathbf{R}^{\mathbf{2}}$value of$\mathbf{0. 9 9 2}$, the lowest MSE and MAE as well as MAPE with minimal errors. Computational results indicate that CatBoost is efficient both in terms of inference speed and memory usage. SHAP feature analysis revealed relative humidity, soil moisture, sunlight hours and temperature as the most important predictors providing practical information for crops cultivation. Federated learning experiments showed that training in a decentralized fashion kept most of the data private and protected with only a marginal impact on performance, averaging$\mathbf{R}^{\mathbf{2}}$of 0.977 across 3 rounds in comparison to centralized results. This minimal reduction emphasizes the compromise on precision and data privacy. Still, the method described above yields accurate results and allows for direct reasoning while also keeping the data private and secure, offering a new heterogenous agricultural framework for predicting crop yield that can be used broadly by farmers and policymakers for improving sustainable agriculture practices.

title: Integrating Global and Local Explainability in Machine Learning and Deep Learning for Drought Forecasting of Bangladesh
abstract: Drought represents a major climate hazard to Bangladesh resulting in serious threats to agricultural productivity, water availability, and food security. This study proposes the introduction of XAI (Explainable Artificial Intelligence) techniques for predicting drought through the integration of advanced machine learning and deep learning algorithms with modelling interpretability techniques at both the global and local levels. The use of NASA POWER climate projections (2012-2024) for 38 districts demonstrated that regression analysis produced a very high degree of predictive fit of ($R^{2}=0.953$) for predicting the amount of moisture in soils. The classification benchmarking results showed that Random Forest (RF) and Extra Trees (ET) had the highest predictive performance (approximately$\approx \mathbf{9 8 \%}$), with a balanced precision/recall (positive and negative) across drought vs non-drought classes, while LSTM and GRU also performed well, but were less accurate. Through SHAP analysis, relative humidity, dew point, and surface temperature were identified as being the most important predictors of a drought event; LIME allowed for a case-by-case interpretation of the XAI model's predictions to provide decision support and improve transparency. By combining both high levels of predictive accuracy, along with an explainable model, the proposed framework provides reasonably accurate and interpretable drought forecasting to improve agricultural planning, water management, and climate adaptation efforts in regions that are highly vulnerable to drought.

title: Predicting Agricultural Productivity in Bangladesh using Economic and Environmental Indicators
abstract: Agriculture plays a vital role in the economic stability and food security of Bangladesh. Accurate prediction of cereal yield is important for effective policy design, resource management, and long-term sustainability. This study explores the use of Machine Learning (ML) models to forecast cereal yield using historical data on economic and environmental indicators. The proposed methodology integrates three models: Long ShortTerm Memory (LSTM), Random Forest Regressor, and Linear Regression. These models were trained on key features such as employment in agriculture, fertilizer consumption, irrigated land, Gross Domestic Product (GDP), and inflation. Model performance was evaluated using standard regression metrics. The experimental results show that LSTM achieved the best performance with the lowest error rates and the highest$R^{2}$score, outperforming both Random Forest Regressor and Linear Regression. The findings demonstrate the potential of ML techniques in capturing temporal dependencies and improving the accuracy of agricultural forecasts. The contribution of this work lies in applying advanced predictive modeling to the context of Bangladesh, offering data-driven insights that can assist policymakers and stakeholders. The study also provides a foundation for developing real-time forecasting systems that support sustainable agricultural planning and food security initiatives.

title: AgriNet-Web: An Improved Hybrid UNet-ResNet50 Approach for Potato Leaf Disease Surveillance via Web Platform
abstract: Potatoes (Solanum tuberosum) are among the most widely cultivated tuber crops worldwide and serve as a staple food in global food production. Potato leaf diseases are a significant threat to global food security, reducing both yield and quality. Those diseases can cause substantial economic losses if not identified early and accurately. Traditional methods based on manual observation are time consuming and labor intensive. To address this challenge and bridge the gap between research and practical field deployment, this paper introduces AgriNet-Web, an interactive real time web application that integrates a hybrid framework with a user-friendly application. The system allows users to upload potato leaf images via a web browser and obtain real-time classification results across seven categories: six disease classes (Bacteria, Fungi, Nematode, Pests, Phytophthora and Virus) and one healthy class. This application visualizes and predict diseases. The AgriNet-Web model was evaluated on the PLD dataset under uncontrolled environmental conditions to assess its robustness and reliability in real-world scenarios which achieved 0.9859 % accuracy, 0.9865 % precision, 0.9859 % recall and 0.9860 % F1 score. Through the integration of deep learning with an accessible web interface, AgriNet-Web advances scalable and farmer-friendly plant disease control solutions.

title: K-Means Clustering Algorithm for Crop Leaf Disease Detection
abstract: In these modern days where technology rules the world. There also exists severe threat to the food security due to climatic change, cross-pollination decline, plant diseases etc. One of the main threats are diseases that occur in leaves. Due to plant diseases, there is a threat to the food security at the global scale and it majorly affects the small and big farmers, whose lives depend on farming. Disease detection is extremely important in agriculture since it might impair productivity if it is not done at the beginning of the farming production. India loses 35% of crop yield due to these types of diseases. This article has proposed the possibility of image processing and machine learning (i.e., computer vision) approaches to develop a scalable and early crop detection. To acquire the best accuracy, this study has also evaluated several images to identify different crop diseases. The dataset used here is plant village. Three basic steps are used in the implementation process, they are image preprocessing, feature extraction and then training the machine learning model. Then finally if a new image which is not there in the dataset is given as input to the model it predicts the disease with best accuracy. These results show the effectiveness of the model. In future, an application will be developed to implement smartphones assisted crop disease detection by showing the disease name, type of the disease, and the measures that need to implement to prevent further occurrence of diseases, which is particularly useful for the farmers to take good decisions that lead to the healthy growth of the crop.

title: Identification of Plant Leaf Disease using Image Augmentation and Deep Learning
abstract: Early identification of plant leaf Disease is critical for maintaining agricultural output and food security. Farmers may reduce crop loss and preserve high yields by precisely recognizing illnesses early on and executing prompt preventative steps, such as using pesticides or adopting resistant crop types. Automated disease identification systems offer crop monitoring that is quick and scalable. This study focuses on early stage disease identification using image analysis. This study uses open source the Plant Pathology 2020 - FGVC7 dataset. The dataset consists of more than 7000 images of different plants and categorizes them into Healthy, Scab, Rust, as well as Multiple Disease. The study uses a per-trained Dense-Net and Efficient-Net model for the training and testing of the model. The model uses global average pooling and soft-max activation function due to the multi-classification problem. Dense-Net achieves accuracy for training and testing, 99.87% and 95.26%, while Efficient-Net model archives accuracy for training and testing, 99.22% and 94.54%. However, using DL models such as CNN, and its pre-trained models for plant leaf identification has shown tremendous promise for boosting precision as well as productivity. These algorithms not only give high accuracy rates, but they also pave the way for early identification, individualized treatment strategies, and the development of forecasting techniques to aid illness detection. However, using DL models such as CNN, and its pre-trained models for plant leaf identification has shown tremendous promise for boosting precision as well as productivity. These algorithms not only give high accuracy rates, but they also pave the way for early identification, individualized treatment strategies, and the development of forecasting techniques to aid illness detection.

title: Subsurface Heat stress detection in plants using machine learning regression models
abstract: The heat stress due to the progressive increase in the earth’s atmospheric temperature impacts plant growth endangering ecosystem quality and world food security. Such less favorable climatic conditions create greater risks that affect crop production as well as threatens food security. Tracking plant health can help mitigate the heat stress due to global warming. Technology plays a central role in mitigating the pressure the farming industry is facing. Smart sensor systems take advantage of machine learning algorithms and modern computer hardware to create a smart node that is tailored specifically for sensing applications. These sensor systems combine ML and IoT technologies to assist the agriculture industry with innovative ideas and technological advancements to increase yields and improve farm performance. Also, having a good machine learning model with good performance could help farmers and governments to make early decisions to mitigate the impact of environmental changes that reduce the quantity or quality of crops. In our research, we attempt to detect heat stress by using an in-situ ML-enabled subsurface sensor system in an agricultural field so that the device can independently make inferences. The sensor node is buried in the soil and we need a machine-learning model to predict the ambient temperature based on the soil characteristics data and the heat stress would be detected using the ambient temperature. In order to find a machine learning model, a publicly available dataset with the soil variables was evaluated for performance using different machine learning algorithms to predict the air temperature at the subsurface. This trained ML model would be deployed in an FPGA in the field that is equipped with soil sensors. The heat stress metric is based on the ambient temperature and duration of exposure to heat that would be wirelessly transmitted from the node. This paper discusses the development of the software framework for the subsurface wireless sensor node.

title: AI-Driven Innovations in Food Safety: Bridging Farm Production to Healthcare Wellness
abstract: Foodborne illnesses constitute a frightening global public health concern, resulting in millions of ailments and extensive economic losses, leading to a massive burden on health care systems globally. Traditional methods frequently fail because of inadequate management, lack of resources and delayed detection of contamination in food. AI can revolutionize food safety management through predictive analytics, machine learning, spectroscopy, natural language processing, computer vision technology, IoT, smartphone applications etc. Encouraged by AI's successes in healthcare, especially real-time diagnostics, predictive modelling and patient outcome prediction, we study how these technologies may boost food safety globally by enhancing traceability, response time and cost-effectiveness, enabling early contamination identification, real-time food production monitoring and precise disease outbreak prediction. Stakeholders can identify indicators of foodborne illnesses, predict populations at high risk and offer customized dietary advice to the vulnerable. For wider adoption, however, certain issues required to be resolved including data quality, ethical considerations and regulatory compliance. This study also highlights how blockchain technology, IoT sensors, CNN, NLP and artificial intelligence can work together to improve traceability, transparency and enable quick reactions to contamination incidents and reveals an untapped potential to improve healthcare by customizing interventions for people at risk and tying personalized nutrition. AI provides an ascendable framework for improving global food security and reducing the healthcare cost by collaborative effort between food operators, healthcare professionals and policy makers. The findings highlight the necessity of sustained innovation, investments and strong legislative frameworks in order to fortify worldwide food safety systems and protect public health via unified strategy.

title: Hybrid CNN-Wavelet Approach in Detecting Plant Disease and Classifications
abstract: Agriculture forms the backbone in a country like India, where the greater part of the population engages itself as farmers. Data-driven technologies, deep learning techniques, and CNNs have thus proved to be great improvement tools for agriculture. Introducing wavelet transformations with CNN for plant disease detection and classification will result in an enhanced technique that is presented in this paper. The proposed method identifies and predicts diseases like apple scab, cercospora leaf spot, late blight, and powdery mildew by using a dataset of images of plant leaves. Wavelet transformations are used to preprocess the input images, and they decompose the images into multi-resolution components that highlight critical features such as texture and patterns associated with disease symptoms. This preprocessing step enhances the ability of the CNN to extract meaningful features, improves the accuracy of prediction, and makes it robust, even with noisy or low-quality data. Early detection, which is facilitated by this method, leads to timely treatment and control, thereby reducing crop losses among farmers. The results confirm that the integration of wavelet transformations with CNN models provides a reliable, efficient, and intelligent tool for disease classification. This approach can assist farmers and decision-makers to improve agricultural yields, reduce losses, and thus enhance food security.

title: Application of Intelligence in Agricultural with crop yield prediction
abstract: Crop yield prediction is vital for enhancing agricultural productivity and ensuring food security. Machine learning models such as CatBoost, Bagging Regressor, and Ridge Regression have been utilized to predict yields based on historical data, including crop type, seasonal variations, soil conditions, rainfall, and pesticide usage. Among these, **CatBoost emerged as the most accurate**, achieving an R2score of 0.954, outperforming Bagging Regressor (R2=0.905) and Ridge Regression (R2=0.400). This superior performance is due to CatBoost’s ability to capture complex, non-linear interactions inherent in agricultural data. Evaluation metrics such as RMSE and MAE further validated CatBoost’s precision, consistent with previous studies reporting up to 99.123Exploratory data analysis revealed key factors influencing crop yield, notably rainfall, temperature, and pesticide application. SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) and LIME (Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations) were used to interpret model outputs. SHAP values quantified global feature contributions, while LIME provided local explanations, improving model transparency for stakeholders such as farmers and policymakers. For example, higher rainfall was generally associated with increased yields, whereas extreme temperatures negatively affected output.Future advancements include integrating real-time IoT data to enhance prediction timeliness and exploring deep learning models for greater accuracy. This approach promotes precision agriculture by enabling data-driven decision-making, adaptive resource management, and sustainable farming practices. By combining high predictive power with explainability, AI-driven frameworks like CatBoost contribute significantly to modernizing agriculture and addressing global food challenges.

title: Smart Farm ML-IoT – Focuses on intelligent farming with ML and IoT
abstract: Accurate crop prediction is essential for optimizing agricultural productivity and ensuring food security, particularly in regions where farming decisions are heavily influenced by soil and climatic conditions. Traditional crop recommendation systems often lack real-time adaptability and the ability to integrate diverse data sources such as soil sensors and live weather feeds. This project presents a real-time crop prediction system that uses a Support Vector Machine (SVM) classifier for accurate and trustworthy crop suggestions. The system combines heterogeneous input data, such as soil nutrient levels (N, P, K), pH value from an Arduino-Based sensor, and dynamic weather factors like temperature, humidity, and rainfall fetched through public APIs. A web interface using Flask supports effortless user interaction, gathering environmental information automatically to minimize manual inputs and enhance ease of use. An SVM model trained using the ‘Crop_recommendation.csv’ data set predicts real-time input as the best-fit crops with around 95% accuracy. Label encoding ensures proper categorical handling of crop labels. Experimental results show the system to have precise predictions at low latency, verifying its usability in real scenarios in agriculture. Integrating data from sensors, geolocation-driven weather information, and machine learning, the developed system is an exemplar solution for smart agriculture with scalability leading the way toward sustainable and effective agricultural practices.

title: AI-Powered Predictive Analysis for Pest and Disease Forecasting in Crops
abstract: Artificial Intelligence(AI) has transformed agriculture by enhancing resilience, sustainability, and yield. A new AI-driven crop disease and pest outbreak prediction model is presented in this research. The algorithm uses satellite imagery, meteorological data, historical pest and disease incidence records, and field IoT sensor feeds to dynamically anticipate hazards. Recurrent neural networks (RNNs) for time-series data analysis, convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for high-resolution satellite imagery analysis, and other machine learning techniques to detect diseases and pests are major elements of the system. The model's accuracy has been carefully evaluated against historical epidemics, showing significantly better predictions than conventional methods. This method allows farmers to obtain early warnings and prevent biotic dangers from causing harm. Predictive insights help agronomists and policymakers maximize pest and disease control, promoting sustainable agriculture and food security. To conclude, AI-driven predictive analysis could revolutionize agricultural pest and disease control. This study shows how AI revolutionizes crop harvests using several data sources and cutting-edge algorithms. Future study will improve the model's precision, expandability, and adaptability to different crops and regions.

title: Integrated Deep Learning Framework for Precision Crop Yield Prediction Using Satellite Imagery and Real-Time Environmental Data
abstract: Crop yield prediction is an important for global food security, particularly in a climate of growing populations, resource constraints, and a changing climate. Traditional methods of crop yield prediction have proven inaccurate, as crop types, agricultural practices, and environmental factors interact complexly. New advances in machine learning, satellite technology, and sensor-based data collection are expected to have a high degree of success in increasing the precision of crop yield predictions. This paper reviews and offers an integrated approach for predicting crop yield using deep learning models combined with satellite imagery along with real-time environmental data. We discuss major algorithms involved in processing and analyzing big data to improve precision in crop yield prediction using techniques including ANN, LSTM, and CNN. We also provide an approach that integrates the use of ensemble models and climate data along with precision agriculture technologies in optimizing resource utilization and better farming practices. The proposed model combines several data sources on weather condition, soil moisture levels, and satellite imaging to ensure scalability and sustainability that crop yield forecasting lacks. Further directions also include genetic engineering, nanotechnology, and reinforcement learning for refinement of the predictive models leading to further development in sustainability in agricultural production.

title: LSTM-RNN: An Ensemble Machine Learning Approach for Crop Prediction based on Soil and Weather Properties
abstract: This research paper deals with cutting-edge machine learning (ML) techniques to boost agricultural productivity by providing precise crop recommendations tailored to specific soil and weather conditions. The proposed framework merges Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks and Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN) for reliable weather forecasting, while Random Forest (RF) classifiers are employed for the selection of crops. The study validates the effectiveness of this ensemble approach in optimizing crop selection, which significantly outperforms traditional methods. Utilizing a comprehensive dataset spanning 17 years, the model's predictive capabilities are compared with various ML techniques, showcasing its enhanced performance in reducing errors and improving crop yield predictions. This work signifies a notable advancement in precision agriculture, paving the way for intelligent and scalable solutions to address the challenges of global food security.

title: Predictive Analytics in Agriculture: Enhancing Crop Yield Forecasting for Indian Farmers
abstract: Agriculture is the strength of the Indian economy and the prediction of crop yields is a vital but challenging task for farmers using climate volatility, soil fertility, and market price as variables. Traditional techniques in forecasting have generally produced faulty trend estimates that translate into money loss and waste of resources. This research aims to use predictive analytics and machine learning techniques for better crop yield forecasting. Several machine learning models, including decision tree, random forest, and deep learning, are compared to validate their performance according to the available data sources, including historical climatic trends and soil properties data. This study utilizes feature selection techniques, data preprocessing techniques, and hyperparameter tuning to improve model accuracy. In addition, agricultural parameters can be monitored in real time through the integration of remote sensing information and Internet of Things (IoT) devices, which adds more precision to predictions. The findings support the notion that machine learning-based predictive analytics can significantly improve yield estimation and enable farmers to make decisions based on data-driven applications. Lastly, the results of this research contribute their part to the implementation of ecofriendly farming practices, helping policy makers develop better agronomic policies to ensure food security.

title: Comparative Analysis of Swarm Optimized Machine Learning Models for Soil Fertility Prediction
abstract: Accurate soil fertility prediction is essential for sustainable agriculture and food security, yet conventional models struggle due to high-dimensional attributes, heterogeneity, and class imbalance. This study presents an enhanced framework validated on a real-world imbalanced soil dataset from Odisha, India that integrates a UMAP-LASSO feature engineering pipeline with Swarm Intelligence (SI) for feature and hyperparameter optimization. Three classifiers, including Random Forest (RF), Multilayer Perceptron (MLP), and eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) serve as the baseline models utilizing a dual-scaling strategy (min-max and standard), UMAP dimensionality reduction, LASSO feature refinement, and SMOTE balancing. Three classical meta-heuristic techniques Flower Pollination Algorithm (FPA), Ant Colony Optimization (ACO) and Cuckoo Search (CS) are applied to improve model performance. Results show consistent accuracy and F1-Score improvements across all optimizers, with the ACO-optimized RF and CS-optimized RF achieving the highest accuracy of 0.8011 and highest AUC-Score of 0.8474, outperforming the baseline. These findings highlight the strong potential of swarm based optimization in enhancing soil fertility forecast and data-driven agricultural decision-making.

title: Explainable AI for Hyper-Local Crop Yield Prediction in India
abstract: Accurate crop yield prediction is crucial for food security and economic stability in agricultural-dependent countries like India. However, while machine learning approaches have shown significant capabilities for yield prediction, a major limiting factor remains: most machine learning models are inherently complex and act mostly like a black box, making it difficult for farmers and policymakers to understand the rationale behind such predictions. This lack of transparency erodes trust and practical utility. Therefore, this paper proposed a crop yield prediction system that is not only highly accurate but also transparently explained. To develop the model, we utilized a comprehensive dataset of Indian agricultural data from 1997 to 2020. We applied several machine learning models and performed their hyperparameter tuning; among these models, XGBoost Regressor yielded the best performance, with an R -squared score of 0.93 on the test set. However, this is merely high predictive accuracy, which is not sufficient for any real-world application. In an attempt to address this limitation, an advanced explainable AI technique called SHapley Additive exPlanations was applied to interpret the model's predictions. The interpretability results show that the dominant feature of yield prediction is crop type, where coconut has the most significant impact, followed by controllable inputs like fertilizer and pesticide usages and climatic factors such as annual rainfall. This is realized by combining global and instance-specific explanations to enhance transparency and facilitate practical data-driven decisionmaking by agricultural stakeholders.

title: AgriShield: A Hybrid NLP and Machine Learning Framework for Plant Disease Prediction
abstract: Plant diseases continue to be a significant threat to the world's food security system, and crops are lost yearly. Conventional diagnosis approaches require professional intervention and are not always available to smallholder farmers in developing countries. The paper presents AgriShield, a unified system using Natural Language Processing (NLP) and Machine Learning (ML) to predict plant diseases. The farmers can enter textual queries describing the symptoms or submit images of the crops, and AgriShield guesses at the most likely disease and preventive and remedial actions. The system uses transformer-based NLP models to extract symptoms and ensemble classifiers, utilising textual and visual input. Some of the experimental outputs of AgriShield on benchmark datasets indicate that AgriShield has an accuracy of 90 %, which is better than textonly and image-only systems.

title: Smart Agribot: an IoT-Based Precision Farming Robot with AI-Driven Irrigation and Seed Sowing
abstract: Agriculture plays a critical role in global food security, but traditional farming methods face numerous challenges. Amid rising labor costs, water scarcity, and inefficiencies in traditional farming methods, the current article introduces a Smart Agribot, an IoT-based precision farming robot powered by renewable energy and artificial intelligence. The Agribot integrates sensors, machine learning models, and automated systems to optimize agricultural tasks such as irrigation, seed sowing, and field monitoring. Key features of the Agribot include optimal watering schedules, which leverage soil moisture, temperature, humidity, and weather forecast data to ensure precise irrigation using decision tree and random forest algorithms. Equipped with a soil moisture sensor, DHT sensor, and sonar sensor, the robot navigates autonomously, avoids obstacles, and adapts to the environmental conditions. Further, powered by a solar panel and controlled by an Arduino Uno, the Agribot utilizes a submersible pump for efficient irrigation, and a Bluetooth module for remote operation. This sustainable and cost-effective solution not only reduces human labor; it also enhances productivity, offering a transformative approach to precision agriculture.

title: From Pixels to Policies: An AI-Driven Workflow for Quantifying Agricultural Drought Impact on Food Security
abstract: Agricultural droughts severely impact crop yields, posing a direct threat to global food security. Traditional assessment methods are often slow, spatially sparse, and disconnected from actionable policy frameworks. To bridge this gap, this study presents an end-to-end, AI-driven workflow that transforms remote sensing data into timely and policy-relevant insights. Our method integrates multisource satellite data, including Sentinel-2 (NDVI, NDWI) and MODIS-derived indices, with climate data from CHIRPS and soil moisture information. A hybrid deep learning model, combining convolutional and long short-term memory networks (CNN-LSTM), was developed to first classify drought severity and subsequently predict consequent crop yield impacts. Validated across major agricultural regions (Punjab, India, and Nebraska, USA), the model achieved 92.3% accuracy in drought severity classification and a yield prediction root mean square error (RMSE) of$0.67 \mathrm{t} / \text{ha}$, significantly outperforming conventional approaches. The system culminates in a near-real-time dashboard that quantifies the drought impact and generates specific, localized policy alerts for food security interventions. This study demonstrates a scalable pipeline from pixels to policies, enhancing the responsiveness and precision of drought mitigation and food security strategies.

title: Exploiting Machine Learning and Remote Sensing for Precision Crop Mapping in Africa
abstract: As the global population continues to grow, the demand for food intensifies, making precision agriculture essential for enhancing productivity and resource efficiency. A critical component of precision agriculture is accurate crop mapping, which enables optimized resource allocation and better yield prediction. This study focuses on developing a machine learning-based predictive model for crop mapping using multispectral remote sensing data from the Senegalese groundnut basin. The dataset, collected via Sentinel-2 satellites, includes optical bands and vegetation indices over four time periods in 2023. After preprocessing and addressing class imbalance through data augmentation and SMOTE, several machine learning models were evaluated, with Random Forest emerging as the most effective. The results show a significant improvement in classification accuracy, particularly for underrepresented crop types, with the Random Forest model achieving 93.57% accuracy after SMOTE, compared to 57.43% before SMOTE. The outcomes of this research extend beyond technological advancements, contributing to environmental sustainability by enabling more precise resource use, reducing waste, and minimizing the environmental impact of agricultural practices. Furthermore, this type of crop mapping supports food security by helping farmers optimize yields and manage crops more effectively, directly benefiting communities reliant on agriculture. The integration of machine learning and remote sensing in precision agriculture has the potential to foster a more resilient and sustainable agricultural system globally.

title: Recommendations for a Vertical Farming System Using Hydroponics, Machine Learning and IoT
abstract: Agriculture nowadays faces several problems because of the rise of the global population, which increased the food demand and caused instability in food security. Organic food that is pesticide-free is also in high demand, leading to consuming more arable lands, water, pesticides, and fossil fuels. Vertical farming is a promising solution to these challenges. It is a method of growing plants in vertically stacked layers, which can be done indoors or outdoors. Hydroponics is a method of growing plants without soil, using a nutrient-rich water solution. Vertical farming using hydroponics can solve these problems by integrating IoT and AI technology. It reduces water wastage and eliminates pesticide consumption. The aim of this research is to develop recommendations for a Vertical Farming System using hydroponic based on Machine Learning and IoT technology for a better, controlled, and monitored growth of plants. The hydroponic system and its parameters are monitored and controlled by a GUI using the Blynk app that allows the user to control the food quality by its nutrients and parameters to help in producing more organic food. Crop yield health is being predicted by an AI model that detects the healthy and unhealthy leaves with an accuracy of 82%, hence saving many farmers’ time. The system is also applicable for personal use, allowing individuals or families to plant their own food.

title: Precision agriculture using ML for irrigation and fertilizer optimization
abstract: Precision agriculture utilizes emerging technologies to improve efficiency of use, boost crop yield, and lessen environmental impacts. This paper reviewed the framework for machine learning (ML) methods to manage precision irrigation and fertilization processes, with a bias of real-time and data-based decision-making to supply specific crops with water and nutrients. In summary, ML methods and models such as Random Forest, Support Vector Machines, and Neural Networks were constructed based on inputs of soil moisture sensors, weather observations and data and remote sensing data, which led to determining irrigation schedules and rates of fertilizers that were tailored to crops. These models also minimize over irrigation and nutrient leaching, improving water-use efficiency up to $40 \%$, and reducing fertilizer application. Smart irrigation systems can also be IoT-enabled and combined with ML to allow remote and adaptive management to support sustainable farming practices. While we build precision irrigation and fertigation processes, we need to collect data on soils that are heterogenous, moreover produce standardized indices which can be accomplished with predictive modelling and advanced sensor technologies, which opens the door to precision irrigation and fertigation to produce a higher and better-quality crop that serves the dual purposes of sustainable environmental resource management and food security.

title: Deep Learning with LSTM for Agricultural Commodity Price Prediction in Indonesia: From Data Collection to Visual Forecasting
abstract: Agricultural commodities are essential for food security and livelihoods, supporting millions of small-holder farmers and traders. Some commodities are highly susceptible to price volatility due to seasonal production, weather conditions, and market demand. These fluctuations significantly impact inflation and household purchasing power, which makes accurate price prediction crucial for effective decision making across the agricultural supply chain. Recent advances in deep learning have positioned LSTM networks as a powerful solution, outperforming traditional models by capturing nonlinear patterns and long-term dependencies in time-series data. This paper presents an experimental study on end-to-end forecasting framework that integrates real-time data collection from an official website, automated preprocessing, and a two-layer LSTM model to predict prices up to 30 days ahead, with evaluation metrics showing high accuracy for stable commodities like garlic while revealing challenges in forecasting sudden spikes in more volatile items such as chili peppers and red chilies. The results confirm LSTM’s effectiveness over other naïve models, demonstrating its potential to support farmers, traders, and policymakers, especially when applied within a system that bridges data acquisition, modeling, and visualization.

title: Towards precision agriculture in Morocco: A machine learning approach for recommending crops and forecasting weather
abstract: Statistical models predict that the world's population will reach 8.5 billion by the end of 2030. This represents a real threat to our food security and puts the current food production system under pressure. Efficient use of Earth's natural resources is the only solution to facing future challenges such as global hunger. The implementation of precision agriculture using new technologies such as artificial intelligence, big data, IoT and remote sensing is the first step towards this goal. In this paper, we investigated several machine learning models to create two services: one for recommending the best crop to grow based on soil and the region's weather characteristics, and another for the forecasting of the hourly average air temperature. Performance evaluation results for the first service show that Random Forest has the best metrics as a classifier (accuracy = 100%, precision = 100%, recall = 100%) compared to K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Decision Tree, Naive Bayes, Logistic Regression, Convolutional Neural Network, and Feed Forward Neural Network. This is a confirmation that classic machine learning algorithms perform better on small-size datasets. In our case, we used a dataset of 2200 instances available online. On the other hand, Facebook Prophet was more accurate (R2 = 0.81, RMSE = 3.74) than our proposed LSTM architecture in time series forecasting at hourly scale using historical weather data provided by the weather station of our study area. These two optimal models are then integrated as the first building blocks in our decision support platform, intended for both farmers and policymakers with the aim of making agriculture in Morocco more efficient and more sustainable.

title: Application of ML in Crop Selection for Precision Agriculture
abstract: Agriculture is a major industry contributing significantly to economic development. It is essential to study the agriculture system to provide food security. Despite technological advancements such as vertical farming, traditional farming methods, and beliefs still dominate the sector. By examining essential factors like soil composition, pH level, humidity, and rainfall using a variety of machine learning models, such as kernel naive bayes, Gaussian naive bayes, linear support vector machine (SVM), quadratic discriminant, quadratic SVM, this research aims to offer crop suggestions to farmers. Accurate crop prediction is essential for optimizing farming practices and ensuring a stable food supply. Machine learning algorithms effectively predict crop yields by utilizing historical weather patterns, soil quality, and crop production data. The study can help in improving crop management and ensuring food security.

title: Enhancing Maize Cultivation with Intelligent Decision Support: IoT, Deep Learning, and Blockchain Integration for Land Data Analysis
abstract: Maize cultivation is essential for global food security and economic growth, yet it is complex with difficulties owing to climate change and resource constraints. Traditional agricultural methods frequently result in optimum productivity, resource usage, and sustainability. Hence described a novel method to enhance maize production that combines IoT, deep learning, and block chain technology. Existing methods are incapable of providing real-time data-driven insights, resulting in poor crop management. The proposed method makes use of IoT sensors to capture continuous data, deep learning for predictive analytics, and blockchain for secure data administration. The integration empowers farmers with intelligent decision support. Following the insights provided by the recommendation model, the study shows consistent gains in agricultural output of 24%, reduced resource usage and sustainability over three batches. The integrated system exceeds the existing system in terms of accuracy with 92.5% and F1 score of 0.915. These findings illustrate the system's ability to greatly improve maize production methods, eventually contributing to food security and sustainable agriculture.

title: A Deep Learning Hybrid Approach for Automated Leaf Disease Identification in Paddy Crops
abstract: The agriculture sector is facing unprecedented chal-lenges, including the need to increase crop yields to meet rising global food demand. Paddy agriculture provides a significant portion of the global population's food supply, therefore finding innovative ways to increase productivity and resource utilization is critical. This study proposes an intelligent automated approach using deep learning techniques to boost paddy crop productivity. We employed a deep learning hybrid model comprising Convo-lutional Neural Networks (CNN) and Support Vector Machine (SVM) classifier to predict the presence of three common paddy leaf diseases: brown spot, bacterial leaf blight, and leaf smut. The proposed system is implemented as a web application that uses deep learning approach to predict diseases. With this technology, diseases can be recognized and diagnosed early on, allowing for rapid treatment to reduce output losses and ensure paddy crop sustainability. The proposed model exhibits excellent accuracy, with an accuracy rate of over 98 %.
