Deep learning predictions of paddy leaf diseases help farmers in a variety of ways, including early detection and intervention, improved resource management, greater crop productivity and quality, reduced dependency on pesticides, and increased food security. This allows farmers to optimize their farming operations for increased productivity and sustainability, as well as make more informed decisions.

title: Optimizing Crop Selection Using Bagging and Boosting Models Based on Soil Composition and Environmental Factors
abstract: Crop selection is vital for sustainable agriculture and food security, demanding careful consideration of soil properties and environmental factors. This study presents a predictive model that forecasts optimal crops based on 12 input features, including soil composition like electrical conductivity, organic carbon, nitrogen, phosphorous, potassium, magnesium, calcium, zinc, and pH, as well as environmental conditions such as temperature, humidity, and rainfall. Leveraging advanced machine learning techniques like bagging, AdaBoost, gradient boost, and extreme gradient boost which using decision tree as a base model to develop models using a dataset featuring 21 crop types categorized into cereal crops, fruit crops, vegetable crops, and commercial crops, extensive hyperparameter tuning enhances model performance. The aggregation of individual models via a stacking classifier yields an ensemble model for crop selection with a remarkable accuracy of 97.77%. This high-performing model offers valuable insights for crop cultivation, tailored to soil and environmental conditions, thereby promising to bolster agricultural productivity and global food security initiatives.

title: Soil Fertility Assessment and Crop Recommendation for Sustainable Farming using Machine Learning and Deep Learning
abstract: “Soil Fertility Assessment and Crop Recommendation for Sustainable Farming using Machine Learning and Deep Learning” represents a pioneering endeavor at the intersection of agriculture and data science. It harnesses a diverse dataset encompassing soil properties, historical rainfall data, and temperature records, meticulously collected from reliable sources. This project employs advanced machine learning algorithms to predict soil fertility levels accurately and offer precise crop recommendations based on the unique conditions of each agricultural region. By bridging the gap between traditional farming practices and cutting-edge technology, the initiative addresses key challenges faced by modern agriculture. It facilitates enhanced crop yields through optimized resource allocation and reduced environmental impact by tailoring planting schedules and nutrient management. Moreover, it fosters sustainability by promoting responsible land usage, which is crucial in the face of evolving climate patterns and the increasing global demand for food security. In essence, Precision Agriculture emerges as a transformative solution that empowers farmers with actionable insights, ushering in an era of data-driven farming practices. By combining the strengths of data science, environmental science, and agriculture, this project contributes significantly to the broader goals of sustainable farming, economic viability, and ecological resilience.The dataset consists of 2200 instances and 8 features. We train several machine models and also implement deep learning models to check for its performance. It was observed that the Naive Bayes shows 99.5 percent accuracy after hypertuning and with CNN showing the least at 87.1 percent accuracy. These conclusions help in building better recommendation systems and farming techniques.

title: Remote Sensing Image Classification of Sugarcane Harvest based on Tensorflow
abstract: In this paper, deep learning is mainly introduced into remote sensing image processing, and the convolutional neural network model is used to process remote sensing images, so that the remote sensing images can be classified after the crops are harvested and after harvesting, and then the unknown harvested remote sensing images are processed. classification, which is of great significance in the field of agriculture. We can roughly estimate the harvesting and unharvesting of sugarcane through remote sensing images. In this paper, the harvesting situation of sugarcane and remote sensing images are used to train the harvesting situation, and then the harvesting situation of sugarcane is predicted, so as to monitor the harvesting situation of sugarcane. Make the relevant state departments have an advance plan for the import and export of sugar. The second objective of Sustainable Development (SDGs) is to eradicate hunger, food security, improve nutrition and promote sustainable agriculture, and this paper is an experiment in response to the needs of this objective.

title: Agricultural Yield Prediction Using Hybrid Metaheuristic Optimization and Token-Based Transformer
abstract: In modern agriculture, accurate crop yield prediction remains a crucial challenge that impacts food security and economic planning. This paper introduces a novel hybrid approach combining the Monkey Cluster Algorithm (MCA) which is a metaheuristic optimization algorithm and a modified Token-based Transformer architecture for predicting agricultural yields. Unlike traditional sequential models, the proposed approach treats agricultural parameters as independent tokens, allowing the Transformer to learn complex relationships between various farming factors without temporal constraints. The MCA algorithm optimizes both the feature selection process and the Transformer's architecture, resulting in a more efficient and accurate prediction model. Experiments across diverse agricultural datasets from different regions show that the hybrid model demonstrated an average improvement of 18 % in prediction accuracy as compared to machine learning and deep learning algorithms. The model showed particular strength in handling complex scenarios involving multiple crop varieties and varying environmental conditions. Furthermore, the token-based approach provides better interpretability, allowing farmers and agricultural experts to understand which factors most significantly influence yield predictions. This research contributes to precision agriculture by offering a more reliable and interpretable tool for crop yield forecasting, potentially improving resource allocation and farming decisions.

title: Smart Agriculture Comparative Study of K-Nearest Neighbours and Random Forest for Real-Time Crop Monitoring and Yield Prediction
abstract: The success of agricultural productivity depends on food security and sustainability with limited resources, population and climate change. “Smart Agriculture” is the recent trend in the agriculture where IoT, sensor networks, machine learning etc. are used to monitor in real-time and more accurate yield forecasting. The aim of this paper is to compare the performance of two of the widely used algorithms K-Nearest Neighbours (KNN) and Random Forest (RF) for on-the-go crop monitoring and yield prediction in a smart farming approach. The data set used in this paper is taken from IoT based smart farming systems which are also capable of accounting for other environmental factors such as soil moisture, temperature, humidity, pH and other factors that directly affect the health and output of crops. The data set is prepared using various data preparation techniques such as feature selection, treatment of missing values and normalization to achieve the best performance of the model. The Random Forest method is compared with the K-Nearest Neighbour method which is simple and effective in recognizing patterns. Performance of both the algorithms is measured using ROC AUC, F1-score, Accuracy, Precision and Recall. Based on the experimental analysis, Random Forest has been claimed to have better prediction accuracy and robustness with larger and more complicated data sets than KNN which performs well in smaller data sets and under low noise conditions. The work also highlights the computational trade-offs, where Random Forest requires more computing power in training but faster predictions whereas KNN has shorter training time, but with more prediction latency.

title: Deep Learning Approach for Recognition and Classification of Tomato Fruit Diseases
abstract: Diseases devastate food crops, causing significant losses for farmers and jeopardising food security, resulting in a low production rate. Health monitoring and disease detection are critical for sustainable agriculture. Monitoring the fruit diseases manually is extremely difficult. It necessitates a significant amount of work, knowledge of fruit diseases, and an extended processing time. Hence, deep learning is used to detect fruit diseases with high accuracy. This paper proposes the method to detect the tomato fruit diseases in color images. In the proposed method, convolutional neural network is used for extracting the features and classification. Further, the augmentation strategy is applied on existing samples to create the dataset with large number of samples. The convolutional neural network method based on VGG16 will be used to train augmented data for recognition and classification of tomato diseases. The results of the CNN after testing affirms that the tomato disease can be predicted efficiently, and it can be utilised for early detection purpose.

title: OEL: Optimized Ensemble Learning for Datadriven Rice Yield Prediction
abstract: xRice is one of the staple food item for a substantial people in the universe, calculating perfect predictions of its production crucial for food security and agricultural planning. This study leverages Machine Learning (ML) approaches to predict rice production using a samples of historical agricultural data. Five ML models Linear Regression (LiR), Polynomial Regression (PoR) with Lasso Regularization, Random Forest (RFR), Gradient Boosting (GBR), and Support Vector Regression (SVR) were implemented with optimal parameters using GridSearch Cross-Validation (GridSearchCV). This research work proposed correlation coefficient feature selection and ensemble technique to predict the rice yield. The rice yield case study has been conducted using the cultivation data of a few districts in Andhra Pradesh. The models have been assessed based on key measures such as$\mathbf{R}^{\mathbf{2}}$Score, Mean Squared Error (MSqE), and Mean Absolute Error (MAbE) to prove the effectiveness. The ensemble approach resulted an optimal performance with an$\mathbf{R}^{\mathbf{2}}$score of 0.9891 compared to individual ML models. The findings underscore the importance of combining data-driven ensemble learning in agricultural farming to improve yield predictions, optimize resource allocation, and support sustainable farming.

title: Overcoming Challenge of Yeild Capacity: Machine Learning Approach Towards Precision Agriculture
abstract: Agriculture is the backbone of the Indian economy, providing a living for more than half of the country's people. Weather, climate, and other environmental factors have become important threats to agriculture's long-term viability. Crop yields vary annually due to climate, operational, and economic reasons. Predicting agricultural yields improves field operations and management. Crop production predictions can contribute to national food security efforts. This is a global step towards achieving the Asian Sustainable Development Goal of Zero Hunger. This study identifies and predicts key elements influencing staple crop productivity in India. The current study focuses on a systematic review that extracts and synthesizes the features used for CYP, as well as a number of approaches created to examine agricultural yield prediction with artificial intelligence techniques. After experimenting with several strategies, Random Forest was found to be the best fit for this particular scenario providing a detailed analysis in terms of accuracy using the techniques.

title: Prediction of Crop Yield by Using Artificial Intelligence Techniques: A Systematic Review
abstract: The agriculture industry has been essential in the development of the national economy in recent years. Agricultural harvests are vital to the national economy. Enhancing crop output and fostering sustainable agriculture depend on effective agricultural planning, in which the strategic selection of crops plays a crucial role. Crop yield forecasting is a crucial endeavor in modern agriculture as it optimizes resource use, enhances food security, and elevates production. Machine learning (ML) techniques have largely improved the accuracy and efficacy of forecasting farm harvests. The current study provides a critical examination of over 45 research articles on crop yield prediction. The articles range from conventional machine learning methods such as Decision Trees and Random Forests to more complex deep learning techniques such as Convolutional Neural Networks and Long Short-Term Memory networks. Moreover, the articles address cutting-edge transformer-based structures such as Trans poral Fusion Transformers (TFT) and hybrid or multi-modal architectures. As per our analysis, classical ML models perform adequately with smaller data and more traditional agronomical parameters, but in the presence of big, complex, or time-critical datasets, deep learning models particularly those of transformerbased architectures and hybrid setups would perform adequately.

title: Advancing Agricultural Sustainability: Enhancing Crop Yield Prediction Through Regression Modeling
abstract: Crop yield prediction is essential for advancing agricultural practices and ensuring global food security. This study aims to enhance crop yield forecasts by employing regression models. We highlight the significance of improving crop yield prediction for agricultural advancement. The methods incorporated Machine learning algorithms, particularly regression techniques, are utilized with an emphasis on thorough data preprocessing, including feature selection and engineering. Various regression models, such as linear regression, decision trees, and ensemble methods, are employed to forecast crop yields based on diverse input variables. The research demonstrates the efficacy of the methodology in accurately predicting crop yields across different crops and geographical regions. The outstanding accuracy demonstrated by the Random Forest Regressor model, achieving an impressive R-squared score of 98.5%, indicative of its proficiency in capturing the variability inherent in crop yield data. The model performance is evaluated using the R-squared score, providing a comprehensive assessment of predictive accuracy. Our findings underscore the importance of employing regression models for crop yield prediction and emphasize the value of data-driven approaches in agricultural research. The study’s findings contribute to sustainable farming practices and initiatives aimed at addressing global food security concerns by furnishing farmers and stakeholders with dependable tools for yield prediction.

title: A Review on the Use of Smart Agriculture Systems to Protect Crops
abstract: Smart agriculture systems leverage the possibilities offered by cutting-edge technologies such as IoT, AI, and remote sensing to revolutionize conventional farming by enhancing resource utilization, production, and crop damage mitigation. Real-time monitoring of soil and crop health, predictive analytics, pest control, and precision irrigation measures are all enabled by these systems. They are able to address major Indian agriculture issues, consequently boosting yield and profitability and promoting environmental sustainability. The largescale deployment of intelligent agriculture systems will change the agriculture landscape in India and will assure long-term food security for an ever-growing population. Challenges include adequate research and future studies in order to better install and achieve smart agricultural systems to protect crops. Intelligent agriculture involves all advanced research, including science and innovations, in national development through space technologies to enhance soil quality, conserve water, and facilitate agriculture information. Space ventures will undergo improved modernization through the introduction of crop sprayers, precision gene editors, epigenetics, big data analytics, IoT, wind and photovoltaic smart energy, AI-enabled robotic applications, and wide-scale desalination technologies. Implementing digital farming systems in developing economies will help their sectors as 85 percent of the global population is set to live in developing countries by 2030. Automation will prove to be necessary since food scarcity is on the rise along with resource wastage. Control strategies such as the IoT, aerial imagery, machine learning, and artificial intelligence will boost production and prevent soil degradation. These advanced technologies are also able to alleviate such issues as plant disease detection, pesticide management, and water application. The introduction of the Internet of Things in the agricultural research world has started with an urge for such communication technologies to communicate and connect devices. The overall assessment of these technologies is, however, vague. This study, therefore, critically analyses 94 papers published on the IoT communication technologies in smart agriculture to highlight the challenges, suggest resolutions, and set recommendations for their application. The need to integrate technology with research was underscored.

title: Remote Sensing and IoT based Global Crop Disease Detection and Treatment System using Machine Learning
abstract: A global crop growth monitoring system based on remote sensing technologies, Arduino-based hardware and machine learning for accurate plant disease diagnosis and management has been proposed. It consists of a set of sensors such as soil moisture and humidity connected to an Arduino platform, which monitors environmental factors critical for the sustenance of crops. The data is sent in real time to a web page through an Internet of Things (IoT) network that allows the monitoring or even decision making from remote. In this method, a MATLAB-based machine learning algorithm is implemented on the system which predicts diseases in crops like Pepperbell (Bacterial Spot), Potato (Early Blight) and Grapevine (Esca or Black Measles) with very high accuracy. The system is designed to automatically identify and treat crops affected by disease conditions, using pump motors to dispense specific medicines when the appropriate condition is identified in the plant. By avoiding chemicals for disease management, it maximizes the efficiency of disease management with a focus on sustainability in agriculture and minimizing the usage of chemical inputs. In this manner, the adaptation and expansion of crop monitoring strategies in different environments by utilizing remote sensing, machine learning, and IoT are facilitated with the help of this system which ultimately supports sustainable food security on a global scale while also optimizing crop yield.

title: Soil-to-Seed Forecasting: Machine Learning for Crop Yield Prediction
abstract: Accurate crop yield prediction is a major advantage of precision agriculture and is essential for maintaining food security, allocating resources as efficiently as possible, and assisting with economic planning. Farmers, legislators, and agribusinesses can make well-informed decisions about planting dates, irrigation plans, logistics, and risk reduction with the help of accurate yield forecasts. Because they rely on historical averages or oversimplified statistical models, traditional methods frequently fall short in capturing the nonlinear interactions among crop-specific, soil, and climate factors. New developments in machine learning have made it possible to create complex models that can handle high-dimensional agricultural data. The performance of three machine learning methods Linear Regression (LR), Random Forest (RF), and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) for crop yield prediction using various agronomic and environmental characteristics, such as soil type, temperature, rainfall, and crop management techniques, is examined and contrasted in this study. Although LR provides a straightforward and comprehensible baseline, its applicability is constrained by its linear assumptions. Because it can model intricate feature interactions, RF, an ensemble approach based on decision trees, performs better. CNNs, which are typically used for image processing, have a lot of promise for finding spatial patterns in structured agricultural datasets. The effectiveness of sophisticated machine learning techniques in boosting data-driven decision-making in agriculture is demonstrated by experimental results showing that models perform noticeably better in predictive accuracy than LR.

title: Precision Agriculture Through Smart Irrigation and Real-Time Nutrient Monitoring Using IoT and AI
abstract: The increasing challenges of resource scarcity, environmental variability, and food security have accelerated the demand for intelligent and sustainable agricultural solutions. This paper presents an enhanced precision agriculture framework that integrates Internet of Things (IoT) sensing technologies with advanced machine learning models to optimize irrigation scheduling and soil nutrient management. Real-time environmental data, including soil moisture, temperature, humidity, and NPK nutrient levels, are collected through a NodeMCU ESP8266-based wireless sensor network. A Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network is employed to forecast future soil moisture trends, enabling proactive irrigation decisions, while an Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) classifier predicts nutrient status categories (Deficient, Optimal, Excess) for nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium. By combining sequential pattern learning and highaccuracy classification, the proposed system dynamically controls irrigation and fertilizer application through automated actuators. Experimental validation demonstrates that the hybrid LSTM-XGBoost model achieves significant improvements, attaining 89.5% irrigation prediction accuracy and 88.2 % nutrient classification F1-score, resulting in approximately 47 % water savings and optimized fertilizer utilization. This integrated approach enhances agricultural sustainability by minimizing resource wastage, maintaining soil health, and improving crop productivity. Future work will explore multi-sensor fusion and deep reinforcement learning for further system robustness under diverse agricultural conditions.

title: Sustainable Aquaculture Management through IoT and Deep Learning-Driven Remote Monitoring
abstract: Aquaculture, as a critical component of global food security, faces challenges in maintaining optimal conditions for aquatic organisms. The paper presents an innovative IoT and Deep Learning-based remote monitoring system designed to enhance sustainable aquaculture management. In order to monitor water quality factors including temperature, pH, dissolved oxygen, and feeding behavior in real time, the system incorporates a network of sensors. These sensors’ data are locally processed on edge devices before being sent to a cloud-based platform for centralized storage and analysis. Convolutional neural networks (CNNs), in particular, are used in deep learning algorithms for image identification tasks to track the health and activity of fish. The system utilizes YOLOv8 for real-time detection and classification of fish diseases, ensuring early intervention and minimizing losses. User-friendly interfaces provide actionable insights through smart dashboards displaying trends, alerts, and recommended actions based on predictive analytics. By facilitating proactive management decisions, this IoT and Deep Learning-based system aims to optimize resource utilization, improve productivity, and promote sustainable practices in aquaculture. Case studies demonstrate its efficacy in enhancing operational efficiency, reducing environmental impact, and fostering long-term viability in aquatic food production systems.

title: AI-Driven Optimization for Urban and Vertical Agriculture Planning: A Multi-Model Approach
abstract: Urban agriculture has emerged as a critical strategy for enhancing food security, mitigating urban heat islands, and promoting community well-being in densely populated areas. However, the complexity of urban environments poses significant challenges for effective planning and implementation. This paper presents an AI-driven framework to optimize urban and vertical agriculture planning by leveraging advanced machine learning models, including Artificial Neural Networks (ANN), Spiking Neural Networks (SNN), and Large Language Models (LLM). The proposed framework integrates diverse dataset that includes as socioeconomic data, geographic information, and urban zoning regulations to provide actionable insights for decision-makers. The Spiking Neural Network model demon-strated superior predictive accuracy in identifying optimal sites for urban agriculture by effectively handling complex patterns and temporal dynamics in the data. Additionally, the integration of an LLM-powered chatbot into a user-friendly web application enhances interactivity and supports real-time decision-making, guiding users through the prediction process with context-specific recommendations. Experimental results validate the robustness and scalability of the framework across various urban settings, demonstrating its potential to transform urban agriculture practices by providing precise, data-driven recommendations. The findings of this study highlight the transformative potential of AI in urban planning and agriculture, offering a novel approach to fostering sustainable urban development and food security. Future research will focus on expanding the dataset, refining model performance, and enhancing the application's capabilities to support more complex user queries.

title: Agricultural Analysis and Crop Yield Prediction of Habiganj using Multispectral Bands of Satellite Imagery with Machine Learning
abstract: Bangladesh is predominately an agriculture-based country, which faces uncertain crop yields and inefficient farming infrastructure resulting in adverse effect in food security. Habiganj is selected as the study area because of its vulnerability to floods and drought due to its unique terrain. This paper aims to present a combinational agricultural mapping and monitoring of Habiganj with crop growth and yield prediction. Multi-spectral band images of Habiganj from Landsat 8 are processed and remote sensing indices are extracted. With options of K-means and Mask R-CNN methods, crop growth is evaluated using both Python and MATLAB. Then using two type of machine learning algorithms crop yield of Habiganj is predicted from its existing parameters and the datasets are predicted by using two type of time series model. Furthermore, comparative studies are concluded between two platforms and time series model to determine the most suited environment for this research purpose.

title: Prediction of Crop Yield Using AI Approach
abstract: Agriculture remains vital to both the economy and food security of India, but accurate crop yield forecasting remains hampered by climatic variability, soil heterogeneity, and limitations in traditional estimation methodologies. Traditional methods are mainly based on historical records, which hardly consider real-time environmental conditions and thus cannot produce reliable predictions. This paper, therefore, proposes a hybrid machine learning-based framework for crop yield prediction using multi-source agricultural data. The given framework combines weather parameters, soil nutrient data, and historical data of crop yield, collected from Medak district. Individual models such as Decision Tree (DT), Random Forest (RF), Support Vector Machine (SVM), and Artificial Neural Network (ANN) are trained and evaluated to assess their predictive capabilities. A hybrid ensemble model has been further developed in order to address the limitations of single model approaches by synergistically integrating the advantages of these techniques. To validate the generalizability of our findings, we utilized the standard metrics of $\mathbf{R}^{\mathbf{2}}$ score, Mean Absolute Error(MAE), Root Mean Square Error(RMSE), and accuracy besides $\mathbf{k}$-fold cross-validation to ensure robustness. The experimental results indicate that the proposed hybrid ensemble model achieves a maximum prediction accuracy of 95.82%, outperforming individual machine learning models in terms of stability and error reduction. The key contributions of this research are three-fold: (i) the integration of multi-source district-level data such as weather and soil nutrients for crop yield prediction (ii) the design of a hybrid ensemble model that combines DT, RF, SVM, and ANN to address the limitations of individual models when data is limited, and (iii) the evaluation of the model using accuracy, $\mathbf{R}^{\mathbf{2}}$, MAE, and RMSE, which outperforms the individual models. The dataset is for a period of ten years, from 2015 to 2025, covering important nutrients in the soil.

title: Integrating Deep Learning and Predictive Modeling for Smart Agriculture: Disease Detection and Yield Estimation
abstract: Crop diseases and erratic weather patterns pose serious problems for modern agriculture, lowering yield and compromising food security. In order to improve precision farming, this paper proposes a clever web-based system that combines deep learning and machine learning. In order to predict the best crop types and yields, hybrid crop prediction uses Decision Tree and Random Forest Classifiers, which use soil and environmental parameters. While a Label Encoder guarantees efficient preprocessing of categorical data, a Convolutional Neural Network is utilized for disease detection through leaf image analysis. The suggested system helps farmers make timely decisions, lowers crop losses, and promotes sustainable, data-driven agricultural practices by giving them real-time insights into plant health and productivity.

title: CNN-Transformer Fusion Network for Multi-Class Leaf Disease Classification
abstract: The precise and automated identification of plant leaf diseases is essential to maintain agricultural productivity and ensure global food security. Deep learning models show potential, but individual architectures face a significant compromise: Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) are excellent at recognizing local disease characteristics but often overlook global context, while Vision Transformers (ViTs) are adept at modeling global interdependencies but may miss detailed local nuances. This paper introduces an innovative dual-branch hybrid architecture that combines a CNN with a Transformer to achieve effective multi-class leaf disease classification. The model utilizes a pretrained EfficientNetB3 backbone for extracting detailed local features, while parallel Transformer blocks use self-attention to capture global contextual dependencies. It was trained and assessed using a well-balanced 24-class subset of the PlantVillage data set, consisting of 24,000 images. Evaluation of a set of tests held - out shows that the proposed model performs very well, achieving an overall accuracy of 98.2%. On this split, the macro-averaged precision and F1-score both reach 0.983, indicating a high level of reliability. The network contains 16.23 million parameters in total, of which 9.00 million are trainable, providing a good compromise between predictive accuracy and computational cost. This hybrid model offers a scalable and generalizable approach for automated leaf disease detection, demonstrating considerable promise for use in modern precision agriculture.

title: CropNet-XAI: An Explainable 1D-CNN Framework for Transparent Crop Yield Prediction
abstract: One predictor of food security and sustainable agriculture is crop yields. Nevertheless, despite their accuracy, traditional machine learning techniques frequently lack transparency, which restricts their uptake by non-expert stakeholders. This paper presents XAI-Yield, an interpretable deep learning framework that combines a one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D-CNN, also known as CropNet) with Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) processes (SHAP, LIME). For performance comparison, several models were benchmarked, including deep CNN architectures (VGG16 and VGG19), RF, DT, XGBoost, and SVM. CropNet outperformed conventional machine learning techniques by up to 18.2%, achieving the highest test accuracy of 93.46%. The strongest positive yield predictors were Fertilizer_Used_True (0.2074) and Rainfall_mm (0.1946), while Irrigation_Used_True (-0.1649) had the opposite effect.XAI Yield connects data-driven modeling with real-world agricultural decision-making by combining high predictive accuracy with transparent interpretability to provide farmers and policymakers with actionable insights.

title: Smart Crop Recommendation System with Plant Disease Identification
abstract: Agriculture is the backbone of many countries, including India, and provides livelihoods to millions of people facing challenges such as climate change and plant disease outbreaks. Through research, a web application has been developed that provides real-time recommendations for crop selection based on various factors such as soil nutrients, temperature, humidity, pH levels, and rainfall. Recent advances in machine learning and artificial intelligence offer promising solutions to these problems, enabling accurate, data-driven decision-making in agriculture. These technologies have the potential to transform how we predict crop yields and detect plant diseases, thus improving agricultural practices. To achieve this, we trained and examined seven machine learning models, Decision tree, Naive Bayes, SVM, Logistic Regression, Random Forest, XGBoost, and KNN. Among these, Random forest gives the highest accuracy, making it the best choice for crop forecasting. In addition to crop recommendation, the web application also integrates a Plant Disease Identification system using Convolutional Neural Network (CNN). By analyzing leaf images, CNN detects and accurately classifies plant diseases, allowing farmers to intervene early to prevent crop losses. This study aims to empower farmers with accessible technology to make informed decisions, improve crop selection, and effectively cure plant diseases. Combining crop recommendation with disease detection, intelligent crop recommendation systems with plant disease detection contribute to sustainable agriculture, economic stability, and food security in India and beyond.

title: Optimization of Boosting Classifier Method for Paddy Growth Phase Classification Using Oversampling and Hyperparameter Tuning
abstract: The agricultural sector has a significant contribution to the achievement of the second Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), which are zero hunger, ensuring food security, enhancing nutrition, and fostering sustainable agriculture. This goal is in line with the regulation issued by the Indonesian Government No. 68 of 2002 regarding food security. To achieve that goal, it is necessary to have timely and accurate agricultural data available. Machine learning can predict paddy growth phases more quickly and efficiently. In this study, the optimization method was carried out on the machine learning Boosting Classifier with the aim of this study being to find out which optimization method has the best performance on the Boosting Classifier model in classifying rice growth phases based on the evaluation results of 7 comparative metrics namely overall accuracy, precision, recall, F1 score, kappa score, cross-validation, and time execution. The optimization Boosting Classifier algorithm is carried out using the hyperopt hyperparameter tuning method, imbalance data handling, and a combination of hyperopt hyperparameter tuning and imbalance data handling. As a result, the hyperopt hyperparameter tuning method is a method that can improve the performance of the Boosting Classifier machine learning model in classifying paddy growth phases based on the results of the values in most of the comparison metrics (6/7 comparison metrics) which are on average higher by 0.04 when compared to the other three methods are the baseline method, the imbalance data handling method, and a combination of hyperopt hyperparameter tuning and imbalance data handling.

title: Analysis of Staple Food Price Forecasting Results Using Various Approaches
abstract: Some fields of science often use events in the past as a guide to determine activities that can occur in the future. Forecasting mechanisms are needed to determine uncertain future events. Forecasting results should be able to approach the actual situation with a small error value. The type of data and the forecasting algorithm used can affect the quality of the forecasting results. In this study, we make forecasts to estimate the prices of 11 staple foods in 2017. The data used are time series with a composition of 70% training data and 30% testing data. This study compares Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (ARIMA), Double Exponential Smoothing (DES), and Support Vector Regression (SVR) with three types of kernels to determine the quality of forecasting results. The test results show that SVR with Radial Basis Function (RBF) kernel provides the best performance compared to other algorithms with an average RMSE of 1520.20 and MAPE of 9.16%. The SVR algorithm with the RBF kernel can predict the price of staple foods close to the actual price in the market.

title: Smart AgriTech with Machine Learning: Enhancing Crop Yield via Intelligent Recommendation and Irrigation System
abstract: A fully intelligent agritech platform is developed using advanced machine learning techniques to improve the crop yield through smart irrigation and intelligent recommendations. An model for the recommendation of crops is incorporated where in the system indicates the best-fitting crops suited for a location depending on surroundings like soil condition, weather conditions, and the availability of water. It uses historical data sets to predict yield returns with high accuracy, facilitating optimized resource allocation, enhanced profitability, and environmentally friendly farming. The irrigation status system is driven by Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, which have a remarkable accuracy of$\mathbf{0.96}$, facilitating accurate prediction and monitoring of irrigation needs. Particularly, the system forecasts whether irrigation is needed or not for the plant based on input features such as soil moisture, temperature, and weather conditions. For crop recommendation, Naive Bayes with 0.99 accuracy and Decision Tree with 0.97 accuracy are utilized to examine environmental conditions and recommend the most appropriate crops. Besides, XGBoost and Random Forest algorithms are utilized for highly accurate yield prediction and decision-making. These models process vast amounts of agricultural data at a large scale to reveal buried patterns and correlation that aid well-informed planning in agriculture. Model training and validation datasets utilized were accessed through Kaggle and contained detailed data about soil composition, weather conditions, types of crops, and irrigation levels to allow solid data-driven development. By incorporating a smart advisory mechanism, the system optimizes agronomic decision-making, facilitates precision agriculture, and ensures eco-efficient irrigation specific to crop requirements. This technology enables farmers to enhance productivity, safeguard food security, lower operational expenses, and preserve natural resources.

title: Real Time Crop Recommendation System Using Machine Learning
abstract: Food security depends heavily on agriculture, and crop selection based on environmental factors is essential for optimizing production. This project, Real-time Crop Recommendation System Using Machine Learning, combines machine learning and Internet of Things-based sensor technologies to offer real-time crop suggestions that are adapted to climate and soil conditions. Several sensors, including soil moisture, pH, temperature, humidity, sunlight lux, and a raindrop module, are linked to the NodeMCU ESP8266 hardware system. Real-time ambient and soil characteristics are gathered by these sensors and sent to the Blynk Cloud IoT platform for monitoring. A machine learning model based on the Random Forest Classifier is then trained using the collected data and a dataset that includes ten distinct crops (onion, potato, tomato, rice, banana, maize, guava, pomegranate, and sugarcane). After analyzing these variables, the algorithm forecasts which crop would be best to grow. This method maximizes agricultural output by giving farmers data-driven insights to help them make wise decisions. This strategy guarantees real-time adaptation to shifting environmental circumstances, in contrast to conventional approaches that depend on experience and broad weather patterns. Future improvements will involve adding more sensors, growing the dataset, and improving the model's accuracy.

title: Four-Layered IoT-WSN Framework for Data Acquisition and Pest Classification Using Efficientnet in Sustainable Smallholder Farms
abstract: Smallholder agriculture, a critical source of livelihood for a significant portion of the global population, faces numerous challenges in adopting modern technology. In developing countries, nearly 86% of farmers rely on small plots of land, contributing to low yields due to traditional farming methods. To address these challenges, this paper proposes an architecture that connects Internet of Things (IoT) devices and Wireless Sensor Networks (WSN) for reliable data acquisition, alongside a deep learning model for efficient pest classification, aimed at improving the productivity and sustainability of smallholder farms. The proposed solution integrates IoT and WSN to create an efficient system for collecting real-time environmental parameters, such as soil moisture, temperature, humidity, and pest activity, using sensors deployed across farmlands. A comprehensive dataset is then used to train a deep learning model for predictive pest classification. The model, based on EfficientNetB4, achieved an impressive accuracy of 90.17%, with precision, recall, and F1-score values of 90.10%, 90.17%, and 90.02%, respectively, demonstrating the efficacy of deep learning in pest detection. This paper highlights the role of deep learning in enhancing pest classification and presents a sustainable architecture for data acquisition, enabling farmers to gain valuable insights into pest activity and optimize their practices. This approach not only contributes to the "United Nations’ Sustainable Development Goal Number 2: Zero Hunger", promoting sustainable agriculture, but also significantly improves food security and farming resilience, revolutionizing smallholder agriculture to meet global food production demands.

title: Enhancing Nutrient Regulation in Aquaponics Using CatBoost and LightGBM
abstract: Aquaponics is an innovative farming method that integrates aquaculture, the raising of fish and other aquatic organisms, with hydroponics, the cultivation of plants in nutrient-rich water without soil. This closed-loop system operates on a natural cycle, where fish provide nutrients for plants, and plants purify the water for fish. It is increasingly recognized for its sustainability, offering benefits such as efficient nutrient recycling and reduced water consumption. However, maintaining precise nutrient balance remains a critical challenge, as imbalances can disrupt fish health, hinder plant growth, and reduce overall productivity. To address this, the study combines advanced machine learning techniques with real-time monitoring. A network of sensors tracks key parameters, such as nutrient levels and environmental conditions, while machine learning models like CatBoost and LightGBM analyze the data to predict and implement necessary adjustments. This automated approach minimizes manual intervention, enhances accuracy in nutrient management, and increases the system's scalability. The findings highlight the potential of integrating smart technologies into aquaponics to create efficient, low-maintenance farming systems. By addressing critical issues in nutrient regulation, the approach supports sustainable agriculture, contributing to resource conservation, food security, and environmental stewardship while advancing precision farming practices.

title: Time-Series-Conscious Ensemble Learning Approach for Maize Yield Prediction
abstract: Agricultural yield prediction is relevant in the process of ensuring food security and facilitating decision making in farmers in unpredictable weather patterns. This paper is a maize yield prediction ensemble learning model that combines both the machine learning methods and the time-series analysis. In the proposed system, soil fertility predictors have been used including nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium, and climatic variables including rainfall, temperature and water stress and past yield information to reflect spatial-temporal fluctuations of agricultural data. The feature engineering techniques such as lag variables and moving averages are used to capture temporal trends in order to enhance the performance of the model.Machine learning models such as Random Forest, XGBoost and Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) are trained and tested on classic measures of regression such as the coefficient of determination (R2) and Root Mean square error (RMSE). The suggested model enhances the reliability of prediction and preserves the model transparency by the explainable methods of artificial intelligence, including SHAP. The system offers scalable and interpretable solution to maize forecasting solution, which could enable farmers and policymakers to plan agriculture using data.

title: Hybrid Machine Learning approach and Statistical Ensemble Model for Spatiotemporal Crop Yield Prediction
abstract: Prediction of crop yield is necessary to ensure food security, timely and accurate strategic agricultural planning and management of resources. The proposed research presents a new hybrid modeling system, which is Statistical Ensemble Stacked-Hybrid Machine Learning System (SES-HMS) and the aim of this paper is to predict crop yield using spatiotemporal environmental, meteorological, and geospatial data. It combines satellite-derived NDVI, soil parameters, rainfall, temperature, and past yield statistics via uncommon processing methods including Spatiotemporal Kriging, Empirical Mode Decomposition (EMD), and Symbolic Aggregate approximator (SAX) to preprocess and upscale the data respectively. The ensemble structure is consisting of Bayesian Hierarchical Yield Modeling with sophisticated machine learning architectures such as Gradient Boosting, LSTM and Gaussian Process Regression. Quantile Regression Averaging is used to refine and conformal prediction is used to calibrate yield prediction to assure uncertainty estimation. Ranging experiments carried out in five different agro-ecological zones also indicate that SES-HMS is significantly more effective at prediction with a mean accuracy of 94.6 and lowering of RMSE by more than 18 % relative to conventional methods. The suggested approach guarantees the spatiotemporal compatibility of the predictions and demonstrates a high level of generalizability to various climatic scenarios. These findings confirm the possibility of using SES-HMS as a powerful, scalable and interpretable tool in data-scarce settings to determine precision agriculture and agricultural policy-making.

title: Integrated IoT and Deep Learning Architecture for Real-Time Crop Stress Detection and Irrigation Optimization
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has become a crucial instrument of solving the resource optimization problems, climate resilience, and food security in poor countries due to precision agriculture. To implement real-time monitoring and decision support, this study proposes a combined architecture comprising of deep learning algorithms, multispectral drone cameras and appliance of the IoT, soil moisture sensors and nutrient sensors of the soil. A time-series predictor based on LSTM generated $\mathbf{9 2. 1 \%}$ accuracy in irrigation forecasting, and a crop-stress detection model based on CNN generated 94.8% classification accuracy. The system was introduced and evaluated over two crop cycles over a $\mathbf{1 5 0}$-hectare area of smallholder farms in rural India with significant improvements in agricultural productivity. The accuracy rate of 89.4% in identifying early diseases and pests led to a 28.6% decrease in water use, $17.5 \%$ decrease in the use of fertilizers and $14.2 \%$ decrease in the use of pesticides compared to the traditional methods. Yield performance was greatly improved with an average increase in crop production of $21.3 \%$ and reduction in post-harvest losses of $19.6 \%$. Socioeconomic effects of the system were also proved with the reduction in labor dependency $(32 \%)$, a reduction in operating costs $(18.7 \%)$, and a net farmer income increase ($24.5 \%$). The AI-based decision-support tool was also scalable by adapting to changing weather trends, with a $96.2 \%$ generalization accuracy in different types of crops and soils. These results show that AI-enabled precision agriculture is a sustainable, flexible and cost-effective way to transform agricultural practices in poorly developed regions that ensure long-term stability and enhance livelihoods.

title: Predicting Temperature and Humidity for Cotton Field Using Deep Learning Models in Smart Agriculture System
abstract: Agriculture demonstrates a pivotal part in sustaining world economies as it proves to be the backbone of human civilization. Cotton crops, contributing to the textile industry and the livelihoods of millions of farmers worldwide, ensure food security and hold immense importance for a country's economy. There are many imposed challenges for the farmer due to unpredictable weather conditions, making it a problem in making informed decisions about planting, crop management and harvesting. Extreme temperature and weather conditions can lead to loss of crop and yield causing financial instability for farmers. To counter these challenges, an artificial intelligence (AI) enabled Smart Agricultural System based on deep learning (DL) models is deployed to assist farmers in providing optimal cotton crop management. The main objectives of conducting this research involve overcoming the challenges of poor crop management through effective usage of DL models to make accurate predictions regarding weather conditions for crop maintenance. The DL models are trained using data such as temperature and humidity. Different models such as convolutional neural networks (CNN) model, long short-term memory (LSTM) model and the most powerful model convolutional neural network - long short-term memory (CNN-LSTM) are implemented, and a fair comparison is done through evaluating the most suitable and accurate performing model in terms of prediction. The insightful evaluation metrics errors are root mean squared error (RMSE), mean squared error (MSE) and the mean absolute error (MAE). The results of this study demonstrate promising outcomes as per the used evaluation metrics. The adaptation of powerful deep learning models in an AI-enabled system provides optimal crop management for farmers through accurate prediction of weather parameters, leading to better crop quality and yield. The integration of machine learning and deep learning techniques enable data-driven approaches in agriculture, showcasing the value of technological advancements and sets the stage for future innovations in this sector.

title: AI-Driven Crop Yield Prediction with State-Level Customization
abstract: Accurate crop yield prediction is essential for agricultural planning, enabling farmers and policymakers to optimize resource al location and risk management. This work develops an AI-driven crop yield prediction model incorporating regional parameters such as seasonal rainfall, evapotranspiration, and soil texture. To enhance predictive accuracy, missing values were imputed using the ARIMA model, and categorical features were encoded using Label Encoding. Various machine learning models were tested, including XGBoost, Random Forest, Extra Trees, and a stacked ensemble of XGBoost and Extra Trees. Out of all the models tested, the Extra Trees algorithm came out on top in terms of prediction accuracy. When checking which features mattered most, it be- came clear that Extra Trees leaned heavily towards the crop type, while the stacked model seemed to spread the importance across more variables. This kind of difference suggests that ensemble models might offer a more rounded view of the factors involved, even if sometimes a single model performs better on its own. These findings show how the choice of model and how much weight each feature carries can really affect the prediction results. With better preprocessing and smarter model selection, this work helps improve how we estimate crop yields — a small but meaningful step toward better agricultural planning and food security.

title: Integrating IOT And AI For End-To-End Agricultural Intelligence Systems
abstract: The present-day global agricultural sector has been faced with numerous problems related to world population growth, climate change, diminishing natural resources, and labour shortages. The traditional ways of farming are less likely to meet the increasing demands of food security, sustainable farming and operational efficiency. In such context, inclusion of Internet of Things (IoT) technologies and artificial intelligence approaches creates a transformation. In this study, the author proposes comprehensive end-to-end agricultural intelligence in which IoT sensor-networked environmental sensing and edge computing, along with AI-powered smart farming analytics, collaborates with performance enhancement in farming operations. The aforementioned architecture encloses the sensor network for real-time soil monitoring like soil moisture, temperature, humidity, crop health, and weather condition so that AI algorithms like convolutional neural networks (CNNs), support vector machines (SVMs), as well as deep-learning-based regressors can play a significant role in various applications such as yield prediction, disease diagnosis, and intelligent irrigation scheduling. The predicted system was evaluated with huge real datasets from PlantVillage, IEEE-CIS Crop Yield, and AgroDataCube against accuracy of prediction, communication efficiency, and resource usage. Service results confirmed that AI-improved models have significantly outshone traditional baseline models, whereby AIimproved models boast $18.4 \%$ accuracy improvement in crop yield prediction, F1-scores up to 0.91 in detecting pests/diseases, and around $23 \%$ water savings through AI-aided irrigation. Edge computing also greatly enhances latency, with inference time lessening by $45 \%$ compared to cloud-only methods, thus enabling real-time decision making in a rural or power connectivity scenario. This study illustrates how an IoT-AI integration in a scalable, modular architecture may possibly trigger precision agriculture and sustainable farming. Practical challenges for implementation in the field include sensor calibration, energy management, protection of data security, and model generalization across crops and regions. Many potential research fronts were raised, such as federated learning for frameworks in decentralized farming practiced by land users, integrating blockchain to ensure food traceability, and coordination of artificial intelligence of things unchaperoned by drone-manned systems. Through the merger of data collection and intelligent decision-making, the study presents an analytical organization for the modernization of agriculture, thanks to potential use of next-generation computing technologies.

title: Advancing Crop Yield Forecasting with Random Forest: Enhancing Accuracy and Sustainability in Agriculture
abstract: Crop yield prediction has a potential to become an essential component of agricultural systems, which will enable optimization of food security, maximum production and sustain- able resource management. There are high degrees of complexity and variability in the agricultural environment and, thus, crop yield prediction by conventional methods is complex and leads to suboptimal results. Lately, the trend has been growing for the use of ML algorithm for crop yield simplification. Random forests are shown as one of the most effective methods for this task. Random Forest method is used for overcoming the overfitting problem which is typically present in some machine learning methods and to improve prediction accuracy on large datasets. In this paper, we discuss the random forests based on decision trees for crop yield prediction. Random Forest models combine also predictions from many decision trees in order to overcome the overfitting problem. This research investigates how Random Forest could transform the way we predict agricultural production through its strength and robustness as a framework for agricultural research. Random Forest has already been shown to be extremely effective across many different fields, making it an ideal candidate for addressing the challenges associated with predicting crop yields to promote and improve sustainability and efficiency in crop production. The results presented in this paper represent significant progress in predicting the productivity of crops, as they provide useful information to scientists, policymakers, and others working in the area of agriculture.

title: CNViS-Net: A Self-Attention Framework for Predicting Soil Nutrients from Hyperspectral Data
abstract: Automating soil parameter analysis simplifies fertilization, resulting in time and resource savings. This efficiency reduces agricultural production costs and fosters better resource utilization, contributing to sustainable farming practices and improving food security. This research presents CNViS-Net, a novel self-attention framework for soil nutrient prediction using hyperspectral data, combining Deep Learning (DL) with Machine Learning (ML) techniques. The focus is on predicting four soil nutrients: Phosphorus (P), Potassium (K), Magnesium (Mg), and soil pH, using the HYPERVIEW hyperspectral dataset. The proposed CNViS-Net framework performs feature extraction through a combination of Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and Vision Transformer (ViT), capturing complex spectral patterns across 150 channels of hyperspectral data. It passes the extracted features to four ML models, which are K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Random Forest (RF), Partial Least Squares Regression (PLSR), and Support Vector Regression (SVR) for final prediction. The combination of SVR with CNN and ViT outperforms other prediction models, achieving significantly lower score metrics of 0.164, 0.074, 0.307, and 0.66 for P, K, Mg, and pH, respectively. These remarkably lower scores demonstrate CNViS-Net's superior performance over previous state-of-the-art methods in accurately predicting soil nutrient levels, advancing precision agriculture through efficient hyperspectral data analysis.

title: AloeGreen: Smart IOT-Based System for Aloe Vera
abstract: Agriculture plays a vital role in food security, yet Aloe vera cultivation remains vulnerable to environmental variability, nutrient imbalance, disease occurrence, and unstable market conditions. This study presented AloeGreen, a crop-specific AI–IoT smart agriculture framework designed to support Aloe vera cultivation through integrated sensing, forecasting, and decision-support modules. The system combined real-time IoT-based field monitoring with machine learning models for yield prediction, environmental forecasting, disease detection, fertilizer recommendation, and price forecasting. A key contribution of the study was a forecast-informed yield prediction strategy in which short-term environmental forecasts were incorporated into the yield estimation pipeline to support future-aware decision-making. In addition, domain-specific agronomic features, including water stress and heat stress indices, were introduced to better represent Aloe vera growth conditions. For the yield prediction module, the cleaned hourly cultivation dataset contained 1,048,330 observations after removing missing critical fields and duplicates. Experimental results showed that XGBoost achieved the best yield prediction performance with an RMSE of$\mathbf{1 0. 0 2}$and an$\mathbf{R}^{\mathbf{2}}$of$\mathbf{0. 8 9 2}$, while the environmental forecasting module achieved strong performance for temperature and humidity prediction, although rainfall prediction remained comparatively weaker. The disease detection module achieved balanced classification performance of approximately 77% accuracy, and Random Forest performed best in both price forecasting and fertilizer recommendation tasks. Overall, the findings showed that integrating IoT sensing with intelligent analytics in a unified Aloe vera cultivation platform can improve decision support, reduce uncertainty, and contribute to more sustainable smart agriculture practices.

title: Smart Agri-Suite: A Globally Deployable Machine Learning Platform for Satellite-Driven Idle Land Mobilization and Smallholder Agricultural Decision Support
abstract: Across the tropics, 500 million smallholder farmers drive global food security. However, they face three connected, systemic failures. First, fertile land often remains undetected and idle. Second, market transactions lack legal or technical safeguards. Third, farmers make critical pricing, inventory, and labor decisions without reliable data. These challenges are not isolated inefficiencies. Instead, they act as planetary-scale barriers to agricultural prosperity. This study introduces the Smart Agri-Suite. It is a modular, mobile-first platform designed to address these exact barriers. The system integrates satellite intelligence, machine learning, and digital governance. Together, these form a comprehensive, field-ready solution. The platform processes Sentinel-2 Level-2A imagery using an XGBoost classifier. This enables precise, parcel-level land mapping and crop suitability analysis. Consequently, the system identifies previously undetected arable land with 80% accuracy. The platform features a compliance-driven marketplace. The marketplace strictly enforces spatial and legal verification for every transaction. Data-driven pricing and forecasting components incorporate demand signals, transportation costs and Net Present Value. These algorithms support financially sound decision-making. Furthermore, quantile regressionbased inventory management provides probabilistic demand forecasts. It also generates automated stock alerts. The system features a crop-agnostic and language-neutral architecture. This design demonstrates direct transferability to other smallholder systems. It can easily adapt to Sub-Saharan Africa, South and Southeast Asia, and Latin America. These findings highlight the power of targeted technological integration. It can transform persistent agricultural inefficiencies into measurable prosperity. Ultimately, this creates equitable growth for farming communities worldwide.

title: Implementation of the Exponential Smoothing Method for Forecasting Food Prices at Provincial Levels on Java Island
abstract: Food is an important basic requirement because it affects human survival. The availability of food affects the economic stability of a country, one of which results in volatility in food prices. This happens, because of an imbalance between the number of requests and offers. Therefore, a method is needed to identify uncertainties in the pattern of food prices, namely the forecasting method. This study aims to forecast food prices at the provincial level in Java. The stages of research consist of: (1) historical data collection, (2) preprocessing, (3) split datasets, (4) forecasting, (5) validation and evaluation. The dataset is obtained from the National Strategic Food Price Information Center (NSFPIC) page. Testing is done using a comparison of 3 methods, namely Single Exponential Smoothing (SES), Double Exponential Smoothing (DES), and Triple Exponential Smoothing (TES). The optimum parameter validation process uses the Sum of Squared Error (SSE) and error level evaluation process using the Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE). The testing scheme is formed through scenario 1 (5 periods) and scenario 2 (20 periods) to forecast future food price predictions. The testing scheme using scenario 1 obtained an MAPE average of 3.08% and scenario 2 was 8.24%. The level of accuracy produced is very good because it produces an error rate below 10% Scenario 1 gets better results because the forecasting period is shorter, so the causes of factors that influence prices are relatively more constant and create a higher level of data relevance between forecasting data and actual data.

title: Performance Evaluation of Ensemble Learning Stacking in Rice Price Prediction
abstract: Rice prices in Indonesia play an important role in maintaining economic and social stability. However, unpredictable price fluctuations often compromise people purchasing power and national food security. This challenge is compounded by uncertainties in production, population growth, and climate change such as EI Nino that affect rice production and distribution. In addition, the limitations of traditional prediction methods often result in inaccurate price forecasts, making it difficult for policymakers and market players to make timely decisions. In this context, machine learning has great potential to improve the accuracy of rice price prediction. To address this issue, this research applies the Ensemble Learning (EL) Stacking method using Random Forest (RF) as the meta learner and Recurrent Neural Network (RNN), Least Square (LS), and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) models as a basis learner. Evaluate indicates are used to measure such performance. As a result, EL Stacking significantly improved prediction accuracy, with Coefficient of Determination ($\mathbf{R}^{2}$) 0.9996 and very low error Mean Absolute Error (MAE) 9, Mean Squared Error (MSE) 288, Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) 16, and Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) 0.0007, on a 60:40 percentage ratio dataset split. This study demonstrates the potential of EL Stacking in predicting rice prices with high accuracy, helping stakeholders maintain price stability and strengthen national food security.

title: Region-based Crop Yield Prediction using a Transformer-CNN Hybrid Model for Agricultural Forecasting
abstract: Efficient agricultural implementation and food security largely depend on precise prediction of crop yield: Traditional methods struggle to capture the diverse dependency factors, spatial and temporal, that influence yield productivity. In this paper, we tackle this issue systematically using a hybrid model where CNNs are used for spatial feature extraction and transformer networks for modeling data dependency in the sequential sense. The model works with historical yield records, weather data, soil information, and crop type which eliminates the need of image data. The CNN portion captures the spatial dependencies, while the transformer discriminates and models the long-term temporal dependencies’ seasons. A regional crop yield dataset was utilized for testing this model. The results of the tests yielded a 12% decrease in Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) along with 0.08 increases of the R2value in comparison to the baseline models of the linear regression, CNN, and Transformer only models. This data infused spatial and temporal dynamics showcases the hybrid model’s strength in predictive accuracy enhancement. The proposed framework integrates various subsystems and serves as a base for a scalable, resource effective, and data-based solution for precision agriculture; contributing towards improved policy making, agriculture resource management, and crop production planning. This method guarantees greater applicability in various agricultural areas where satellite data could be restricted by removing the dependency on remote sensing imagery. In this study, we stress the use of hybrid deep learning algorithms in the agricultural forecasting systems to eliminate the adverse effects of climate change variability and food supply shift.

title: The Impact of Soil Moisture and Land Surface Temperature on Crop Yield: A Remote Sensing-Based Machine Learning Approach
abstract: Accurate and timely prediction of crop yields is paramount for ensuring global food security, supply chain management, and informed policy-making. Traditional methods that rely on field surveys and historical data are often inadequate for large-scale, in-season forecasting. The convergence of remote sensing (RS) and machine learning (ML) has emerged as a transformative paradigm that enables high-resolution spatially explicit yield predictions. This study presents a systematic review of how RS-derived Soil Moisture (SM) and Land Surface Temperature (LST), two critical biophysical variables, are leveraged within ML frameworks for crop yield estimation. We detail the principles and methods for retrieving and downscaling SM and LST from various satellite platforms. Furthermore, we explored a wide array of ML algorithms, from ensemble methods to deep learning architectures, which decode the complex nonlinear relationships between these variables and the final yield. This review also evaluates the performance of these integrated systems, highlighting the superiority of hybrid models. Finally, we discuss the persistent challenges related to data quality, model interpretability, and scalability, and outline future research directions aimed at developing robust operational tools for sustainable agricultural management.

title: Enhanced Crop Prediction using Environmental Factors and Advanced Machine Learning Techniques
abstract: Predicting crop yield is vital for food security, economic stability, and resource efficiency. The research makes use of machine learning (ML) techniques for making crop suitability predictions by analyzing soil conditions and environmental elements. The accuracy of data increases through feature selection approaches that include PCA and RFE. Multiple classifiers including SVM, Naïve Bayes, Decision Tree and Logistic Regression, KNN, and Random Forest are evaluated but ensemble methods particularly Random Forest shows superior performance. The predictive model development requires multiple stages that begin with data cleaning followed by selecting essential features and model training to finally evaluate performance metrics including precision, accuracy, F1-score and recall. The study highlights ML's role in agricultural decision-making, enabling data-driven crop selection. Future improvements may incorporate real-time climate data and remote sensing for better predictions.

title: Predicting Crop Yields with Random Forest: A Data-Driven Approach
abstract: Crop forecasting is among the key aspects of modern agriculture, with the potential for food security and maximizing yield. In this research work, we call upon the capability of innovation that advanced machine learning and deep learning techniques can bring to crop forecastingthrough a dataset of determinant parameters on agricultural yield held herein. Direct productivity variables to crop health form good bases to build predictive models and offer actionable decisions to farmers and related agricultural stakeholders. Random Forest Regressor, Gradient Boosting Regressor, RNN, and LSTM are some of the various algorithms that were tried. Among them, the performance of Random Forest Regressor was outstanding with a better accuracy score: 99.87 %. The measures of performance are precision of 96 %, recall (sensitivity) of 87 %, specificity of 100 %, and an F1 score of 91 %. The measures indicate the performance of the Random Forest Regressor in handling complex agriculture datasets and the accuracy of high prediction for crop yields

title: An Effective Prediction and Recommendation System for Smart Farming using Machine Learning Techniques
abstract: It is obvious that the agriculture industry and the methods we currently practice to raise our crops are inefficient. Despite the fact that there are several issues at play here that require immediate attention in light of the ever-rapid pace of climate change, one that stands out is the general lack of knowledge among farmers about modern farming practices and the complete absence of access to even the most basic tools, technologies and services. In this paper, we propose a productive system built on machine learning algorithms that may provide farmers with insightful predictions and recommendations to raise crop output and revenue. The proposed system is implemented using a web application that makes use of Decision Tree, Random Forest and Support Vector Machines (SVM) classifiers to predict crops, fertilizers, rainfall and crop yield. The proposed approach intends to make farming methods simpler, more effective and more accessible by making it easy for the government officials to offer better services to those who work to ensure food security for all of us. Further, the proposed system aid farmers in implementing more productive and environmentally friendly farming methods, resulting in higher crop yields and increased productivity.

title: Enhancing Farming with Predictive Analytics and Artificial Intelligence
abstract: Farming is vital to global food systems, especially in agrarian economies like India, where it remains the economic backbone for millions. However, challenges such as unpredictable weather, soil nutrient depletion, and limited access to expert agricultural advice continue to affect productivity. This paper proposes a machine learning-based framework to address these issues by offering accurate crop and fertilizer recommendations. The system employs two Random Forest Classifiers that analyze critical agricultural variables, including soil nutrients (nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium), temperature, humidity, pH level, and rainfall. Based on these inputs, it suggests the most suitable crop for prevailing conditions and recommends fertilizers to correct soil nutrient deficiencies, thereby ensuring optimal growth with minimal environmental impact. Built on open-source libraries and deployed via cloud infrastructure, the framework is scalable and user-friendly, enabling farmers to make data-driven decisions. By improving resource utilization and yields, it fosters sustainable agriculture and strengthens long-term food security.

title: Enhancing Agricultural Yield Predictions with Real-Time IoT Sensor Data and Machine Learning Integration
abstract: This research extends previous studies on the effects of climate change on agricultural yield predictions by integrating advanced Machine learning (ML) methods with real time environmental sensing data. It builds on the basic usage of Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) and Random Forest (RF) methods by employing real time data streams from IoT based field sensors that measure soil moisture, nutrient levels and pest activity. The aim is to enhance the prediction model's adaption to changing climatic circumstances, therefore increasing their utility in agricultural management. This study proposes a dynamic adaptation feature that uses real time data to make timely adjustments to crop management predictions. Moreover, the integration of Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) with LSTM is being investigated to increase the spatial and temporal accuracy of these predictions. By integrating conventional climatic data with detailed micro environmental elements from IoT sensors, this method obtains a aspects which affects the crop growth. This study also focuses on developing a userfriendly interface that allows farmers to easily access predictive developments and recommendations, allowing for more informed decision making. This technique is predicted to make substantial advances in precision agriculture, giving more effective methods for regulating agricultural productivity in dynamic climatic variability. These results may improve food security and sustainability by optimizing resource utilization and reducing the environmental impact of farming operations.

title: Enhanced Genomic Prediction for Maize Breeding Using Deep Learning and K-mer-based Sequence Encoding
abstract: Maize (Zea mays L.) plays a pivotal role in global food security due to its substantial economic and nutritional value. With advancements in agricultural technologies, crop yields have surged, but challenges remain in optimizing maize breeding for even higher productivity. This research explores cutting-edge approaches in maize breeding, focusing on novel genomic prediction tools that enhance crop yield. While numerous studies have demonstrated the potential of genomic prediction in accelerating maize yields, current models often suffer from suboptimal data quality and lengthy processing times due to the use of raw data for genotype prediction. To address these challenges, this study introduces a deep learning- based model that leverages polymorphism data, employs k-mer methods to shorten sequences, and applies one-hot encoding for preprocessing. This data is then processed by a convolutional neural network (CNN) to predict genotypes efficiently. The proposed model aims to achieve a 98% accuracy in genomic prediction, outperforming existing models in both speed and accuracy, thereby contributing to the generation of superior maize traits.

title: Weather-Driven Machine Learning Approach for Predicting Rice Production in East Java
abstract: This research develops a machine learning-based prediction model that uses weather variables for predicting rice production in East Java, Indonesia's largest rice-producing province. The increasing variability in climatic patterns requires precise prediction models to support planning and improve food security. This study employed four machine learning models, including Random Forest, Support Vector Regressor, Multiple Linear Regression, and Decision Tree, trained and evaluated on 15 years of weather and rice production data spanning 2010-2024. The models went through comprehensive data preprocessing stages that involved outlier detection, temporal aggregation (converting daily weather observations to annual data points), standardization, and feature selection based on correlation analysis. Hyperparameter tuning was conducted using GridSearchCV on all four models. The Random Forest model achieved the most consistent performance across all evaluation metrics, with the Mean Absolute Percentage Error of 16.53% and Root Mean Square Error of 58751.71. This research highlights the effectiveness of machine learning while utilizing weather variables to predict rice production in East Java.

title: Hybrid Statistical and Machine Learning Approach for Forecasting the Global Food Price Index Based on Oil Prices
