abstract: Food price inflation has become a significant global challenge, adversely affecting human well-being and emerging as a key concern within the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). This inflation is closely linked to the dynamics of the global food price index. Thus, accurately forecasting this index is crucial, particularly when accounting for exogenous factors such as global oil prices. This study aims to predict the global food price index by comparing three analytical approaches: a statistical method (ARIMAX), machine learning methods (Random Forest and XGBoost), and a hybrid approach that integrates both. Parameter estimation was conducted using the Least Squares method for ARIMAX and Grid Search for the machine learning models. The models were evaluated using Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) and Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) to assess predictive performance. The results indicate that global oil prices have a significant influence on the food price index. Moreover, the hybrid ARIMAX-XGBoost model demonstrated the best performance, with RMSE and MAPE values of 0.02 and 1.95%, respectively, outperforming each individual approach. These findings highlight that integrating statistical and machine learning techniques enhances prediction accuracy for the food price index influenced by global oil prices, thereby supporting more effective policy decision-making in addressing the impacts of global food inflation.

title: Disclosing the Potential of Deep Learning in Cassava Leaf Disease Analysis by using CNN and Neural Networks Approach
abstract: The identification and classification of cassava infections are paramount due to their detrimental impact on agricultural productivity. This study conducts a comparative analysis to assess the effectiveness of various deep learning techniques in classifying cassava leaf diseases. Transformer-Embedded ResNet, EfficientNetV2 with visual attention, and a mobile-based model are explored to address the challenges posed by an imbalanced dataset. Leveraging deep Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and attention mechanisms, these models exhibit enhanced precision and effectiveness. Evaluations measure accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score, considering feasibility and computational complexity. Results indicate that the proposed models effectively control cassava infections compared to current methods. This study underscores the precision and efficacy of plant disease identification using deep learning techniques, presenting modern methodologies for thorough evaluation. With agriculture supporting a significant portion of the world's population, AI-powered automation offers solutions to production challenges. AI enhances agricultural precision, monitors crop health, identifies diseases, and forecasts weather conditions, particularly advantageous in addressing manpower shortages. Automated detection is crucial for mitigating agricultural disease risks and ensuring food security. Focusing on the examination of CNNs and neural networks, this study utilizes deep learning techniques to identify cassava leaf diseases using the Kaggle dataset and real-time photographs. Performance evaluation and enhancement are discussed, with a specific focus on the impact of disease on the Thai cassava crop. Experimental trials demonstrate the effectiveness of deep learning in automating cassava disease categorization, particularly in detecting brown streak virus illness, yielding notable F-measure and accuracy. This study advances disease classification and calls for further research in the field.

title: Explainable Hybrid CNN Framework for Accurate Multi-Crop Disease Detection and Yield Enhancement
abstract: Global agriculture is seriously threatened by plant diseases, which drastically reduce crop yields, economic productivity, and food security. Conventional methods of disease detection rely on manual inspections, which are time-consuming, error-prone, and often inconsistent under various field conditions. To overcome these limitations, the current study proposes an explainable hybrid CNN (Convolutional neural networks) method for precise plant disease identification and yield enhancement. The proposed architecture combines CNNs for dependable feature extraction with classifiers that make complex decisions using machine learning. A comprehensive preprocessing pipeline that incorporates noise reduction, augmentation, and normalization improves the model's predictive power in a variety of lighting scenarios, crop types, and occlusions. Explainable AI (XAI) methods, like Grad-CAM, demonstrate the important elements affecting classification results, improving interpretability and boosting user confidence. Even in the face of challenging lighting and background changes, experimental evaluations show superior efficacy over traditional models, achieving high F1-scores, recall, accuracy, and precision. Furthermore, by including yield-related insights that support data-driven agricultural decision-making, the methodology extends beyond simply identifying illnesses. A comprehensive strategy reduces crop losses, promotes sustainable farming methods, and allows for proactive disease management. For modern precision agriculture, the suggested system provides an open, scalable, and useful solution.

title: Taxonomic Classification and Sorting of Plant Leaf Diseases using DenseNet for Enhanced Detection and Categorization
abstract: Striking a balance between the predicted agricultural yield to meet the needs of an increasingly populous world is critical if food security on a global scale is to remain hopeful. As a result, a global food crisis may have begun because an agreeable balance was not achieved in this area. So, it's vital to stop anything, direct or indirect, from making this happen. To ensure that the world's food supply is adequate in both quality and quantity, it is crucial to cultivate plants in an environment free from harmful diseases. By applying deep learning to plant disease recognition, we can speed up the development of new technologies, make feature extraction more objective, and reduce the negative effects of artificially selecting disease spot features. A methodology for detecting leaf diseases using deep learning techniques is proposed in this research article. Ultimately, this research paper can help farmers and guarantee global food security by contributing to the development of efficient and effective methods for detecting and identifying leaf diseases.

title: Accurate Yield Forecast for Sustainable Agriculture
abstract: Food security around the world is being threatened by climate change as well as the overuse of pesticides within the agricultural sector. This research provides an automated crop yield prediction system based on machine learning (ML) for the years 1990 to 2023, taking into consideration historical yields, meteorological data, and pesticide usage. The chosen models were XGBoosting, K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), and Linear Regression owing their successes to complex pattern recognition, speed, and ease of understanding, respectively. GridSearchCV with K-Fold Cross-Validation was utilized to fine-tune hyperparameters to increase precision and generalization. Data scarcity issues were dealt with by generating synthetic data which increased performance in low-data situations. The best algorithm was chosen by evaluating all models based on predictive accuracy, and metrics such as prediction accuracy, overfitting, scalability across crops and regions were met. This system enables more reliable yield predictions, fostering progress towards sustainable agriculture, relevant to the altered climate conditions.

title: Rice Yield Prediction in Sumatra Indonesia Using Machine Learning and Climate Data
abstract: Sumatra Island has over 50% of agricultural land in each province, with rice as the dominant food crop. Climate change poses a significant threat to agricultural production, impacting crop patterns, planting times, and yield quality. Rising temperatures and climate variations can further jeopardize agriculture in Sumatra. This study addresses rice yield prediction across eight Sumatran provinces in Indonesia. In this study, four combination climate and crop production data were tested to predict rice yields across eight Sumatran provinces in Indonesia using machine learning (ML) regression-based method. Six regression algorithms are employed for predictive modeling. We employed hyperparameter tunning methodologies such as Grid Search CV or Randomized Search CV for each model to improve its performance. Cross-validation (CV) with k-fold splitting is used to evaluate unbiased models. XGBRegressor appears to be the best-performing model among the six, with 88.48 R2-score, followed by Random Forest Regressor with 86.39 and Support Vector Regressor with 85.21. The XGBRegressor also has the lowest Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Mean Squared Error (MSE) and Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), which implies it explains more variance and makes more accurate predictions. This indicates its potential as the most dependable model among those examined. The research aims to provide actionable insights to enhance food security in Sumatra amidst climate challenges, aiding both farmers and policymakers in making informed decisions for stable agricultural production and food security in the region.

title: Price forecasting by ICA-SVM in the competitive electricity market
abstract: Price forecaster is one of the important aspects in the researches of the electricity price. But because of the special properties of electricity, the price of electricity is far more volatile than that of other relatively volatile commodities. Due to such significant volatility, it is difficult to make an accurate forecast for the spot market of electricity. To solve above problem, a hybrid algorithm for price forecasting is proposed. The procedure comprises two main steps. The first step is feature extract of price feature by independent component analysis that has special effect on extracting the latent source feature. The second step is regression modeling by support vector machine training with the refined features that can realize higher-dimensional nonlinear regression with good generalization ability. In this way, the two algorithms have combined, whose advantages have been made a full use. Case studies are applied to test the proposed model.

title: Beyond Deep Features: Fusing Deep Learning with Local Textures for Enhanced Plant Disease Classification
abstract: Precision plant disease type plays a vital role in powerful crop control, ailment control, and safeguarding agricultural productiveness and food security. Deep getting-to-know fashions, mainly deep convolutional neural networks (DCNNs), have established themselves as surprisingly effective in diagnosing plant illnesses from huge image datasets. However, they now and again struggle with differentiating sicknesses that appear visually similar due to confined nearby texture elements. This technique combines DCNNs for high-level function extraction with neighborhood texture descriptors like Local Binary Patterns (LBP) to predict the plant leaf diseases and to improve ailment category accuracy. Even in hard conditions, this framework considerably increases sensitivity and specificity by means of combining worldwide and neighborhood information. Experiments on benchmark datasets show that this model outperforms traditional techniques with an accuracy of 96%. This answer gives a realistic, reliable device for real international agriculture, permitting farmers to make properly knowledgeable choices for preserving crop output and health

title: Smart Agriculture in the Era of Big Data: IoT-Assisted Pest Forecasting and Resource Optimization for Sustainable Farming
abstract: The goal was to facilitate quick development and revitalisation of rural areas by utilising IoT knowledge to accomplish smart agriculture against the backdrop of big data. Depleted soil fertility, increased pest attacks, and diseases are some of the climate-related risks that the agricultural sector is battling. Predicting Utilising directly sensed environmental conditions as input, a machine learning model incorporating Random Forest and the Catboost algorithm determines, based on the current environmental conditions, whether pest populations are present or not. Next, Hybrid Weighted Ant Colony Optimisation (HW ACO) is used to fine-tune the Catboost algorithm. This method evaluates the machine learning model's accuracy and precision in making predictions using test data. Predictions have been made using data from 2028 to 2022, a span of five years. Weekly forecasts are produced by the pest prediction model. With high F-measure, Precision, and Recall, the weekly predictions have an overall accuracy of 93%. Over time, the precision of the pest forecast steadily rises. Predictions for the next week are made by averaging all weather data from the past seven days. For immediate defences against pests, the weekly forecasts are crucial. The findings support sustainable farming methods and food security by showing that the device can maximise crop yields while decreasing resource consumption.

title: HABARALA - A Comprehensive Solution for Food Security and Sustainable Agriculture through Alternative Food Resources and Technology
abstract: Hunger is a pressing global issue affecting up to 828 million people of the world's population, and the problem is projected to worsen without intervention. Sri Lanka is one country that continues to suffer from rising food prices and insecurity, affecting millions of people. To combat this challenge, this proposed solution “Habarala”, is a novel technological solution that uses Deep Learning, Augmented Reality, and Machine Learning to provide alternative plant identification, recipe suggestions, plant recommendations based on climate conditions, space evaluation, 3D modeling, and personalized product recommendations. “Habarala” aims to contribute to the global effort to eradicate hunger and promote sustainable agriculture, revolutionize food production and distribution, improve food security, and enhance the quality of life for millions of people in Sri Lanka and beyond. The proposed method for plant identification, plant and product recommendation, and area evaluation has shown promising results with an accuracy range of 84% – 99%.

title: Rice Yield Prediction using Hybrid Quantum Deep Learning Framework: Comparison Study of using Optical Remote Sensing, UAV-based Multispectral Imagery, and Weather Data
abstract: This research study proposes a novel hybrid quantum deep learning architecture for accurate prediction of rice harvest timings. This system incorporates data from diverse origins such as, UAV-acquired spectral images, optical remote sensing and daily meteorological data. This research employs a comprehensive dataset comprising environmental data, rice yield information, and images captured from aerial heights. Because of the design of the study, the methodology is the way it is in several contexts. Furthermore, our approach is not only improving forecast accuracy and system reliability, but also outperforming traditional machine learning and deep learning methods. The method accounts for all factors, as the results show. Improved yield estimates will support progress in nutritional health and food security in regions where rice is a major crop, even though healthcare and more accurate predictions are not directly linked. More broadly, this type of more detailed prediction could inform health system strategic planning, create policy and inform resource allocation which would all translate into a preventive stance on anything related to food. The researchers then concluded that agricultural monitoring in combination with the computational approaches presently applied could provide a number of benefits for public health and sustainable development.

title: IoT-Integrated Gradient Boosting Model for Soil Fertility Prediction
abstract: The population of the world is growing, and hence the need for the food is also growing and that needs more efficient methods of farming. This utilizes the Internet of Things (IoT) to help farmers monitor their crops and soil conditions in real time, thereby improving efficiency as well as sustainability. IoT technology allows for quicker data collection and improves decision-making by offering critical insights into farming environments. Through this new farming system, farmers are able to monitor key variables relating to plants and soil using sophisticated sensors. A machine learning-driven recommendation system based on real-time data assists in determining the optimal crops to be planted based on sensor data. The proposed work used a GBM model to predict crops to plant using real time data. The model worked very well, with an accuracy of 98.18%. This approach not only maximizes productivity but also minimizes waste of resources through proper utilization of water, fertilizers, and other inputs. The system is created for reliability and simplicity of operation with sensors that monitor the parameters such as soil nutrients, temperature, humidity and moisture level continuously. The compiled data is shown on a readable, user-friendly interface, making it simple for farmers to interpret the data and make sound judgments regarding their crops. By fusing innovative technology with agriculture, this solution assists farmers in maximizing resources, increasing yields and aiding sustainable farming. With a scalable architecture, it can add extra features and sensors whenever necessary and accommodate different agriculture needs. Overall, this system enables farmers to produce more with better quality, thus promoting food security and ecological protection.

title: Machine Learning Approach for Predicting Rice Yield Based on Rainfall Data in Java Island
abstract: Rice production plays a vital role in Indonesia’s food security, where climate variability particularly rainfallstrongly influences agricultural output. This study aims to analyze the relationship between rainfall and rice yield across six provinces on Java Island from 2020 to 2024 using supervised machine learning techniques. Four models were implemented: Linear Regression (LR), Support Vector Regression (SVR), Random Forest (RF), and Gradient Boosting Regression (GBR). The dataset, compiled from BPS and BMKG sources, underwent cleaning, aggregation by province–year, and yield computation before a 70:30 train–test split. Model performance was evaluated using R2, RMSE, and MAE metrics. Results show that all models produced negative R2values, indicating that rainfall alone is insufficient for accurate yield prediction. Among the models, SVR achieved the best performance (R2= −0.878, RMSE = 1.151, MAE = 0.892), capturing weak nonlinear trends more effectively than others. These findings highlight that rainfall is a relevant but incomplete predictor of rice yield. Future research should incorporate additional climatic and agronomic features such as temperature, humidity, and soil conditions to enhance the accuracy of rainfall-based agricultural forecasting models.

title: Agriculture Recommender System for Precision Farming using Machine Learning(ARS)
abstract: Precision farming has a way of revolutionizing agronomy, by optimizing utilization of resources, helping improve the crop yield, and reducing environmental impact. The Agriculture Recommender System, developed with the help of advanced technologies, can help farmers and agriculturists make crop management and resource utilization decisions. We analyze and use various features such as weather conditions, quality of soil, history of crop yields, and other important agricultural parameters. Deep learning models are used to analyze the patterns, predict outcomes, and give crop recommendations. The Agriculture Recommender System provides personalized recommendations from scheduling the plants to various strategies for fertilization, and pest control methods. It considers past performance of the region, and characteristics of the farm, such as soil, adapting to specific needs of the region and according to the weather conditions. The benefits of a recommender system include substantially improved crop yield and resource usage optimization and it introduces environment-friendly farming practices. By including advanced analysis of data and machine learning into the ecosystem, the Agriculture Recommender System brings increased agricultural productivity and sustainability in modern farming practices. This contributes to the ongoing effort to establish sustainable and productive farming, ensuring food security for the ever-growing population, and also reducing the ecological footprint of farming practices.

title: Integrating Genomic Selection and Support Vector Machines to Improve Genetic Resistance in Crops
abstract: Improving genetic resistance in crops is essential for maintaining global food security in the face of rising biotic stress and climatic unpredictability. Conventional breeding techniques, while efficient, are laborious and sometimes constrained in their capacity to include complex trait structures. Genomic Selection (GS) provides a robust alternative by utilizing genome-wide markers to forecast phenotypes, therefore expediting selection cycles. Conventional GS models may exhibit suboptimal performance when confronted with high-dimensional data and non-linear trait-marker associations. This study integrates Support Vector Machines (SVMs), a supervised machine learning technique, into the GS framework to enhance prediction accuracy for disease resistance features. SVMs are proficient in managing non-linearity and high-dimensional datasets, rendering them particularly appropriate for genomic data interpretation. The SVM-GS hybrid model, utilizing real-world crop genomic datasets, exhibited superior prediction accuracy relative to conventional GBLUP and ridge regression models, especially for features characterized by complex genetic architecture. The findings underscore the promise of integrating machine learning with GS to improve the efficacy and accuracy of resistance breeding. This integration facilitates the fast creation of robust crop varieties while promoting sustainable agriculture by reducing dependence on chemical controls and protecting food systems from disease risks.

title: AgroHeatAI: An AI-Powered Framework for Real- Time Thermal Extremes Prediction to Support Climate-Resilient Agriculture in India
abstract: The increasing frequency and intensity of thermal extremes pose a serious threat to agriculture in India, affecting crop yields and food security. To address this challenge, we propose an AI-powered framework for real-time prediction of thermal extremes, enabling climate-resilient agricultural planning and interventions. Current approaches to predicting thermal extremes often rely on purely statistical or black-box machine learning models. These methods may perform well with dense data but struggle in data-scarce regions, usually failing to account for underlying physical laws and resulting in reduced accuracy and interpretability. To overcome these limitations, we propose utilizing Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) within our framework. PINNs integrate physical principles such as heat transfer dynamics, soil heat flux, and atmospheric processes into the training process of the neural network. This combination allows the model to learn from both observational data and physical laws, enhancing generalizability and ensuring physically consistent predictions, even in areas with limited or missing climate data.The proposed method is applied to forecast thermal extremes, icy waves and heatwaves, at a regional scale across key agricultural zones in India. These real-time predictions are intended to support early warning systems, adaptive crop scheduling, and climate-resilient farming practices.The results show that PINNs outperform conventional machine learning models in both accuracy and robustness, especially in data-sparse regions. By delivering timely and physically consistent forecasts, the framework supports evidence-based decision-making for farmers and policymakers, contributing to a more resilient agricultural sector in the face of climate variability.

title: AgriVision: An Intelligent Crop Recommendation System Using Machine Learning Model
abstract: In the field of agriculture, efficient crop selection plays a crucial role in ensuring food security. There is a need to introduce modern methods in agriculture for optimizing crop selection to increase productivity and gain sustainability. This paper proposes an intelligent crop recommendation based on past data and real-time monitoring data. The proposed system captured soil composition (NPK values), weather conditions, and pH of the soil as significant factors. By using these data, the proposed system trains the data with machine learning models like Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, Support Vector Machine, Multi-layer Perceptron, Linear Discriminant Analysis, AdaBoost, Bagging, and Extra Trees to develop predictive models. As compared to other models, the gradient boost algorithm achieved 90% accuracy in less than 0.01 seconds, which is the best model to overcome an accuracy rate for farming the crops.

title: Smart Agricultural Bird Deterrence Using Invariant Feature-Aware Detection and Cloud-Based Alerting System
abstract: The problem of bird predation in agriculture is a long-standing issue, resulting in significant crop loss, particularly in areas that rely on large-scale farming for food security and farm incomes. While previous solutions such as scarecrows, flashy tape, and fireworks can garner temporary relief, birds quickly adapt and ignore them, rendering these solutions ineffective. With recent advances in computer vision and deep learning, it is now possible to access real-time object detection in outdoor conditions that pose many challenges. Nevertheless, many available models remain too expensive, too complex, and ill-suited for agricultural areas. We present an AI- based system to detect and alert of birds that is scalable for lightweight mobile use in a real agricultural setting. The YOLOv8-Small model provides a foundation for classification and is chosen for its balance of accuracy and minimal inference latency on mid-range devices and edge devices. An alert will be sent via edible messaging using Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM) and via Email along with a beep sound for field-level deterrence. We created a dashboard that is powered by React.js that allows users to get live streamed video, bounding boxes, an activity log, and interactive graphs powered by Plotly that can help farmer users see the activity of birds and determine peak bird attack times. [7] Strategies like compression of models, performing confidence calibration, and adaptive thresholding techniques enable reduced false positives, while still providing robust detection despite robust environmental and changing lighting conditions. Trials in the field achieved detection levels above 90% for common species (crows, parrots, and pigeons), showing strong real-time performance even with multiple cameras. The systems architecture is scalable and provides opportunities for flexible features such as zone-based monitoring, customizable alerts for bird behavior, and long- term data storage via Firebase for short, medium- and long- term predictive analytics. The goal is to advance functionalities into on-farm drone surveillance, GPSenabled geo-fencing, and solar-powered energy for remote applications. Additional enhancements to prediction can be facilitated by adding features capable of utilizing the weather and seasonal data; introducing adaptive, non-lethal, and “deterrent” techniques such as ultrasonic sound, flashing lights, and playback calls of natural predators can be used to automatically act on bird behavior.

title: Agriculture Crop Yield Forecasting using Deep Learning Techniques
abstract: Crop yield predictions offer valuable insights for various peoples such as farmers, policymakers, and commodity traders, guiding them in making strategic decisions concerning food security and market entry. The complex dynamics between crop-specific attributes, environmental conditions, and management practices significantly impact crop yields. This complexity not only poses a challenge in understanding crop yields. Hence, this work proposes a crop yield prophecy model by comparing the deep learning algorithms such as Long ShortTerm Memory (LSTM) and 1-Dimensional Convolutional Neural Network (1DCNN) to find the optimal model for overcoming such difficulties.

title: Machine Learning-based Plant Disease Severity and Progression Prediction System
abstract: The Agriculture has remained under the menace of plant diseases, which are a significant pillar of the global food security, causing immense losses in revenues and wastage of produce more so in key crops like potatoes. Manual methods of detection are slow, subjective and laborious, and are linked with delay that which encourages the spread of diseases in resource limited settings. To address these problems in this paper, a Machine Learning-Based Plant Disease Severity and Progression Prediction System has been advanced by automated image processing, severity, and prediction of progression. Using a hybrid structure containing Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) to detect and localize diseases, quantify their severity with U-Net segmentation, and predict its evolution with a 1.2-day MAE with a pool of 400 potato leaf images of healthy, Such ends can identify and localize 94.5 percent of the diseases, estimate the area of the affected area with 0.86 IoU, and forecast how the disease will evolve with a 1.2-day MAE. It compares this to the current detection-only systems demonstrating 9-11 percent accuracy improvements and new progression models that can be utilized to implement proactive interventions that would significantly reduce by 25-30 percent the quantity of fungicides utilized. The implementation of the system, which relies on the React.js frontend and Flask backend, is an easy-to-use solution to sustainable agricultural practice, and scalable precision farming can be suggested.

title: A Deep Learning Framework for Crop Yield Prediction in Precision Agriculture
abstract: Crop yield projections is quite significant in the present-day agricultural sector because it aids in proper resource management, food security arrangement and sustainable agriculture. The traditional predictive models are usually faced with challenges in handling nonlinear and complex agricultural data that is dictated by weather conditions, soil type, plant species, pests activity, and agriculture. The area that has been examined in this paper is the hybrid methods that have merged both machine-learning and neural-network methods to facilitate the accuracy and credibility of the crop-yield forecasts. A set of multi-spectral satellite images 10,000 in total was used by them and the images captured the states of vegetation during different levels of growth. Anisotropic Diffusion Filtering and Contrast Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization were used to pre-process the images to remove noise and emphasize important characteristics in the crop. The Enhanced Fast Fuzzy C-Means (EFCM) algorithm was used to divide the crop regions and Multiscale Gray-Level Co-Occurrence Matrix (MGLCM) was used to extract the texture features. Instead, Enhanced Convolutional Neural Network (ECNN) was applied in yield prediction through deep residual connection to predict finer spatial patterns, yet highly robust to noise and different illumination conditions. The hybrid model that is proposed performed better than the traditional models such as RNN, DBN, and BPNN with a total accuracy of 97%. Its results were compared in terms of such measures as accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. The findings prove that the combination of preprocessing, feature extraction, segmentation, and state-of-the-art deep-learning systems can increase the reliability of the predictions by a significant margin. The paper identifies opportunities of hybrid methods as feasible solution to precision agriculture to allow farmers and researchers to make sound decisions, manage crops, and enhance the productivity of the entire agricultural processes.

title: Machine Learning based Mobile Applications for Autonomous Fertilizer Suggestion
abstract: To ensure food security, advanced agriculture and the Green Movement haveincreased overall output, but with a yield gap. However, the use of agrochemicals such as fertilizers and pesticides, as well as modern cultivars, irrigation, and other inputs, continues to suffer agriculture in some locations. The agriculture-based on traditional agrochemicals may result in soil and environmental degradation, acidification, and a reduction in soil fertility. Only by utilizing appropriate fertilizers and limiting the number of soil resources that are exploited, can help to maintain soil quality and crop yield. As a result, fertilizer recommendations in agriculture are crucial to meeting productivity, and financial needs, and minimizing nutrient losses to the environment. In this research, the smartphone app will be used to construct an autonomous fertilizer suggestion system for farmers. The dataset was gathered from the website Kaggle. The encoding technique is done to make the data entries numeric. Three Machine Learning (ML) models like K-Nearest Neighbour (KNN), Random Forest (RF), and Decision Tree (DT) are employed to predict fertilizer based on environmental and soil characteristics. The best model is identified using performance metrics and deployed on the mobile app. From the performance analysis, the RF gives high accuracy of 90%.

title: A Data-Driven Approach to Optimize Millet Intercropping Systems Using Machine Learning Techniques
abstract: Millets, which have long been grown in India for centuries, are receiving fresh interest due to their climate resilience, nutritional content, and potential to be grown sustainably. This research discusses the strategic relevance of millet intercropping with complementary crops like legumes and vegetables to make agriculture and food security more sustainable. By agronomic analysis and machine learning-based modeling, we determined best pairings of crops for five prominent millet types Finger Millet, Foxtail Millet, Little Millet, Barnyard Millet, and Pearl Millet based on compatibility measures such as Growth Compatibility Index, Soil Nutrient Complementarity, and Temporal Spacing Index. Classifiers like XGBoost, LightGBM, and SVM were utilized to predict and assess crop compatibility, with XGBoost proving to be the most accurate (0.89), precise (0.91), and recalling (0.87). Agronomic verification established that intercropping millets with nitrogen-fixing legumes like Green Gram and Cowpea greatly improves soil health, decreases input reliance, and enhances yield stability. The results underscore intercropping as a critical agroecological strategy for Indian smallholder farmers, providing a route to resilient, diversified, and nutrition-focused farming systems in the face of increasing climate stresses.

title: Smart Farming Assistant Using ML
abstract: In several nations, such as India, agriculture is a crucial economic sector that sustains billions of jobs and addresses future challenges like climate change and climate change related pest and disease outbreaks. Based on continuous research, a web based system has been created that uses real-time data to recommend specific crops to grow, taking into consideration the state of soil nutrient availability, weather, and moisture. With the advancement of technology in both machine learning and artificial intelligence, we can now be more precise with our agriculturerelated data analysis and provide farmers with accurate, data driven predictive outcomes (or predictions) regarding their crop yields and the timing of crop diseases. All of the above mentioned technologies are revolutionising the agriculture sector, as they allow for greater accuracy and efficiency in predicting crop production and identifying pests or diseases. We applied machine learning models to train and assess seven different machine learning models (Decision Trees, Naive Bayes, SVM, Logistic Regression, Random Forest, XG Boost, and KNN). The best performing model for predicting the yield of crops is Random Forest, as it achieved the highest level of accuracy. The web application also includes a Plant Disease Identification Application that uses Convolutional Neural Networks to detect plant diseases. CNN detects and accurately classifies plant diseases by analysing leaf images, helping farmers to take early action to mitigate crop loss. The purpose of this research is to provide farmers with easy to use technology so they can make informed choices regarding what crop to plant, and how to treat their plants when diseased. The combination of disease detection and crop recommendation will lead to the implementation of smarter crop recommendation systems that incorporate plant disease detection, these will aid in creating sustainable agricultural systems, promoting economic stability, and ensuring food security in India and other countries across the World.

title: Machine Learning Approaches to Predict Rice Yield of Bangladesh
abstract: Rice is one of the most grown and consumed crops of the world which largely depends on the weather. To assure global food security, it is extremely important to predict rice yield production for the near future. Machine Learning (ML) can be used to predict or estimate values of different parameters almost accurately. Agriculture and Weather Forecast are two sectors where ML techniques are used extensively. In this paper, we have used weather forecast scenarios to predict rice production in the region of Bangladesh. Data from different sources are integrated to predict the yield production of rice which is considered as the target prediction for this experiment. After predicting the weather parameter values of a particular time frame, we have used the values for target prediction. Several ML-based regression models such as Linear, Polynomial, Support Vector Regression are implemented and results are collected according to the accuracy for each parameter of weather. Finally, Support Vector Regression (SVR) is used for target prediction and achieves 95.89% accuracy to predict the rice yield production amount.

title: Prediction of Breed Lineage for Small Ruminant Production using Deep Learning Technique
abstract: According to UN Committee on World Food Security, people must always have access to sufficient food supplies such as meat, chicken, and sheep. Although important to Malaysian Muslims which account for about 60% of the population, sheep are in short supply locally due to the high mortality rate caused by fatal diseases such as Foot and Mouth Disease (FMD), Tetanus, etc. Because of inbreeding, qualities such as disease resistance, fertility, prolificacy, vigor, and survivability are reduced in animals, often referred to as inbreeding depression. It is important to note that infected sheep may cause contaminated sheep meat produce, transmitting foodborne bacteria such as E.coli and Salmonella to humans during different stages of food preparation. Previously, other papers compared hundreds of images of sheep to deep learning models to learn of its breed. Although successful, both methods took a long period to complete. This paper proposes a framework based on deep learning techniques that will identify and predict breed lineage and inherited disease in sheep. The adopted deep learning algorithm will improve time efficiency in retrieving immediate information while still maintaining a high accuracy rate. From a wider perspective, the proposed framework has the potential to be used across domains as it can be trained with any other dataset.

title: Enhancing Crop Yield Prediction using Machine Learning Techniques
abstract: The advanced machine learning technique is important in enhancing the accuracy of crop yield forecasting, which is crucial for advancing agricultural productivity and ensuring global food security. This project aims to create a reliable model for predicting crop yields by incorporating diverse data sources, such as rainfall trends, soil characteristics, and farming inputs. By building a detailed dataset, the model is trained using the proposed Random Forest (RF) machine learning algorithm. The performance of the proposed model is assessed using evaluation metrics like Mean Squared Error (MSE) and R-squared (R2) and it is compared with traditional Linear Regression and Gradient Boosting algorithms. The analysis of feature importance indicated that average temperature, pesticide utilization, and rainfall were key factors that played critical roles in the prediction of crop yield. These variables have greatly influenced the accuracy of the model when forecasting, therefore critical towards agricultural productivity. Likewise, it featured an interactive widget interface for accessing real-time yield predictions by inputting some conditions such as climate and agronomic practices. This interfaces would serve efficient, yet instant access tools for borrowers and other stakeholders to draw insights from one another and make better decisions for early interventions towards enhancing crop yield management outcomes.

title: A Systematic Literature Review: IoT-Based Soil NPK Sensing Using Machine Learning
abstract: Efficient soil nutrient management is fundamental to achieving sustainable agriculture and ensuring long-term food security. Conventional laboratory-based methods for soil nutrient analysis, while highly accurate, are often time-consuming, costly, and unsuitable for real-time field applications. In recent years, Internet of Things (IoT)-based systems have emerged as a transformative solution, enabling real-time, in-situ monitoring of soil nutrients. These systems, particularly when integrated with machine learning (ML), have shown great promise for monitoring key macronutrients such as Nitrogen (N), Phosphorus (P), and Potassium (K). This systematic literature review synthesizes and critically examines peer-reviewed studies published between 2018 and 2025 that focus on IoT-enabled NPK sensing in agricultural contexts. It classifies sensor technologies-ranging from optical and electrochemical to MEMS/NEMS, polymer-based, and nanobiosensors-used in conjunction with various IoT architectures and ML models. The review also evaluates the predictive performance of different ML algorithms applied for nutrient estimation and fertilizer recommendation. The findings reveal a growing trend toward the adoption of integrated, realtime, and data-driven monitoring systems in precision agriculture, offering enhanced scalability, adaptability, and accuracy in smart farming practices.

title: A Random Forest Regressor Model for Forecasting Agricultural Yield Using Agronomic and Climatic Parameters
abstract: This project builds a data-based system to predict crop yield per hectare in Tamil Nadu, India. Crop yield prediction is difficult because it depends on many changing factors like rainfall, temperature, soil type, and nutrient levels. To handle this, the system uses a machine learning method called the Random Forest Regressor, which is strong and can find complex patterns in data. The model uses six main inputs rainfall, temperature, soil$\mathbf{p H}$, nitrogen$(\mathbf{N})$, phosphorus$(\mathbf{P})$, potassium (K) content, district, and crop type. It is trained and tested using past data and synthetic data, and it performs well based on MAE(Mean Absolute Error), RMSE(Root Mean Square Error), and$\mathbf{R}^{\mathbf{2}}$scores. A MySQL database is used to manage data efficiently and support real-time updates, creating a full system from data collection to prediction. This system gives useful insights to farmers and policymakers, helping them choose crops wisely and use resources effectively. It supports sustainable farming and food security in Tamil Nadu. In the future, it can include real-time weather data, satellite images, and profit analysis to make predictions even better.

title: Crop Yield Prediction on Worldwide Data Using Tabnet Regressor
abstract: Quantities of global crops are influenced by multiple elements composed of climate change and farming practices, and land utilization patterns. Wrong predictions regarding crop yields play a vital role in protecting world food security. The proposed research utilizes TabNet Regressor as a Deep Learning (DL) regression model to forecast crop yields from worldwide agricultural data covering multiple crops and multiple countries. The implementation of Optuna as a hyperparameter tuner resulted in the best possible predictive results. Using Optuna enables the process to identify optimal parameters such as optimizer function, learning rate, batch size, and number of steps within the TabNet architecture framework. Multiple agricultural records obtained from several countries allowed the model to become robust while being evaluated across various crops under multiple environmental scenarios. Model optimization yielded an R2value of 95.8% which indicates great capability to forecast. The research demonstrates that TabNet Regressor serves as an efficient model for yielding better predictions of crop yields. DL combined with hyperparameter optimization techniques delivers important insights which enable policymakers together with farmers and agricultural organizations to conduct data-driven sustainable farming practices decisions. One of the key challenges that this study is overcoming is that extant models lack a wide range of data. The analysis of a global dataset and TabNet Regressor improvement allow the research to reach high levels of prediction and, therefore, make credible projections in a wide range of agricultural conditions.

title: AMF-Net: A Multimodal Attention-Based Network for Rice Yield Prediction
abstract: Precise prediction of rice yield is essential to world food security and climate-resilient agricultural planning; although it is rather difficult since meteorological and soil characteristics are highly non-linear and crop phenology is quite sensitive. Current Multimodal deep learning models are mainly based on static feature concatenation and do not readily adapt to the dynamic agronomic changes, which occur over the growing season and do not distinctly distinguish different sources of data. In this regard, this paper introduces a new architecture, Attentive Multimodal Fusion Network (AMF-Net), which is a dynamic form of integrating spatial Sentinel-2 multispectral images, phenology-constrained meteorological time-series, and a prior physicochemical soil characteristics. The framework uses modality specific encoders: Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) for spatial-spectral features, a Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) encoder with seasonal weather dynamics, and a dense encoder with soil constraints. They are incorporated through a multi-head self-attention which selectively weighs cross-modal contributions at different stages of growth. Assessed in various agro-climatic areas of Andhra Pradesh, the experimental findings indicate that AMF-Net significantly outperforms single-modality and fixed-fusion baselines. The model proposed has a Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of$0.2024 \mathrm{t} / \text{ha}$and a Coefficient of Determination ($R^{2}$) of 0.6765, demonstrating high predictive consistency within a$\pm 0.5 \mathbf{t} / \mathbf{h a}$tolerance band. Also, the attention mechanism offers critical interpretability to agricultural decision-making. With a very small footprint of 191,009 trainable parameters, the AMF-Net provides a very scalable, robust, and resource-efficient basis of real-time precision agriculture systems.

title: Prediction of Egg Price in Traditional Markets using Deep Learning
abstract: The agricultural sector, especially livestock, contributes significantly to the Indonesian economy. One of the many livestock products produced is chicken eggs. The problem for farmers is the uncertainty of selling prices, which exploitation by intermediaries causes. So, in solving this problem, information in the form of a prediction of the price of chicken eggs is needed to help farmers know the price before they sell them to the market. Predictions are made using deep learning algorithms, namely Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) and Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU), which are evaluated using Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), Mean Squared Error (MSE), Mean Absolute Error (MAE), and R Square to determine the performance of the two algorithms in predicting prices. This study uses data from April 2017 to December 2023 from the National Strategic Food Price Information Center (PIHPSN). Based on the experiments that have been carried out, the algorithm that is more dominant in making predictions is the GRU algorithm with the evaluation metric values of RMSE, MSE, MAE, and R Square in the Manis market, respectively of $0.034621,0.001199,0.022617$ and 0.952266. At the same time, the metric values in the market are $0.036574,0.001338,0.023991$, and 0.944691. With this research, the GRU algorithm is more dominant than LSTM.

title: Optimizer Exploration on Long Short-Term Memory Architecture for Dry Bean Soybean Price Movement Prediction
abstract: The volatility of agricultural commodity prices requires reliable prediction models to assist in making informed decisions in the market. This study evaluates the performance of various optimization algorithms in training Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) architectures to predict daily dry soybean prices. The dataset is from the Indonesian National Food Price Panel, covering the period from April 1, 2021, to February 10, 2025. Data pre-processing steps include missing value imputation through linear interpolation and normalization through Min-Max Scaling. The LSTM model is evaluated based on three activation functions (Tanh, ReLU, Sigmoid) and seven optimization algorithms: Adam, RMSprop, SGD, Adagrad, Adadelta, Nadam, and AdamW. The model's predictive performance is evaluated based on the metrics MAE, RMSE,$\mathbf{R}^{\mathbf{2}}$, loss value in the last epoch, and training time. The best results were obtained by combining the Sigmoid activation function with the Nadam optimizer, achieving an MAE of 0.011890, an RMSE of 0.022985, and an$R^{2}$of 0.639292, reflecting highly accurate predictions with stable training and low volatility. In contrast, combinations involving the SGD, Adagrad, and Adadelta optimizers consistently performed poorly. These results highlight the importance of determining the activation function and optimization algorithm in LSTM-based price-prediction models. The proposed best configuration can be optimally used for monitoring commodity prices and for decision-support systems in agriculture. This configuration can be further improved by adding external variables such as weather conditions or government policies.

title: Enhancing Agricultural Forecasting with GLCM Based Image Features and Ensemble Learning
abstract: Agriculture is crucial for global food security but faces challenges like climate change, land degradation, and population growth. While these issues impact the entire agricultural sector, this study focuses on two key crops, potato and tomato, to allow for a controlled and detailed evaluation of crop yield prediction and plant health detection models. These crops were chosen because of their economic significance, variety of diseases, and the availability of reliable tabular and image datasets. A machine learning framework is proposed that combines FAO and World Bank tabular data with image-based features extracted using the Gray-Level Co-Occurrence Matrix (GLCM). Ensemble and gradient-based models are used, resulting in an overall prediction accuracy of 98%. The proposed framework can scale and could be applied to more crops in future research.

title: Enhanced Paddy Yield Prediction Utilizing a Hybrid Convolution Transform Framework Integrated with Soil-Weather Interaction Analysis for Precision Agriculture
abstract: India is the world's second largest producer of rice, contributing about 20 % to global rice production. Global food security and related health issues require accurate, timely, and reliable paddy yield predictions in India. The existing approaches have two drawbacks, despite their ability to predict crop yields, namely inability to establish direct linear or nonlinear mapping among raw data to crop yield values and strong reliance on quality of extracted features. In this manuscript, Enhanced Paddy Yield Forecasting under Hybrid Convolution Transform Framework Integrated with Soil Weather Interaction Analysis Precision Agriculture (EPYP-HCTF-SWIPA) is proposed. Initially, paddy seed data are collected from Quantum Paddy Seed Selection India dataset. The collected data are pre-processed using Adaptive Tracking Dual Nested Kalman Filter (ATDNKF) to handle missing values and normalize dataset. From the pre-processed data, the features like Variety, State, Soil Type, Sand Percent, Silt Percent, Clay Percent, Soil pH, Nitrogen, Phosphorus, Potassium, Rainfall-mm, Temp-C and Yield-t-per-ha are extracted using Newton Time Extracting Wavelet Transform (NTEWT). The extracted features are given into Hybrid Convolution Transform Framework, where a Binarized Simplicial Convolutional Neural Network with Vicinity Vision Transformer (BSCNN-VViT) predicts paddy yield by combining data from each growth period. To enhance model performance, the Warthog Optimization Algorithm (WOA) is used to optimize the weight parameters of BSCNN-VViT, resulting in more accurate predictions and reduced error rate. The proposed EPYP-HCTF-SWIPA model is evaluated based on accuracy, precision and error rate, achieving 99.56% accuracy, outperforming existing models. Its performance is superior when compared to models like Advanced Prediction of Rice Yield Gaps under Climate Uncertainty under ML Techniques in Eastern India (APRY-CML-EI), Harnessing Multi Source Data and Machine Learning (ML) for Enhanced Rice Yield Estimation (HMSD-MLRYE), Deep Learning Enhanced Remote Sensing Integrated Crop Modelling for Rice Yield Prediction (DLERS-RYP).

title: Deep Learning-Driven Big Data Analytics in the Agri-Food Sector: A Systematic Review
abstract: The agri-food sector is a key promoter of global food security and economic stability. Post-harvest loss, wasteful resources, climatic uncertainty, and sustainability requirements are risks that require intelligent, data-driven solutions. Evolving opportunities in Big Data Analytics (BDA) and Deep Learning (DL) have been found to have massive potential to revamp agricultural models, food processing, and preservation networks. This systematic review covers 20 studies between 2022 and 2025 based on deep learning approaches through big data predictive analytics, crop monitoring, yield estimation, quality inspection, and smart preservation methods. The review lists the application of convolutional, recurrent, and attention-based neural networks on different agricultural datasets for better decision-making, process automation, and optimization of efficiency. The review also covers the issues of data management such as heterogeneity, scalability, interpretability, and integration throughout the agri-food value chain. Summarizing the latest success, the review presents its position on how big data systems powered by DL can transform the agri-food industry for dedication to resilience, accuracy, and sustainability in the global food system.

title: Predicting Crop Yield in Quezon Province, Philippines Using Gaussian Process Regression: A Data-Driven Approach for Agriculture Sustainability
abstract: This study presents a predictive application for rice and corn crop yields in Quezon Province, Philippines, using advanced machine learning techniques, with a focus on the Gaussian Process Regression model. The desktop application utilizes weather parameters as inputs to forecast crop volumes, offering farmers valuable insights for optimized planting and harvesting decisions. Through rigorous evaluation, the Gaussian Process Regression model consistently outperforms other models, demonstrating its accuracy and potential for practical use in the agricultural sector. With an overall Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) of 3.39%, this tool holds promise for enhancing food security and sustainable agriculture while serving as a model for similar initiatives in other regions. Furthermore, this research highlights the crucial role of data-driven approaches in addressing climate change impacts on agriculture, offering a tangible solution for a more food-secure future. The study underscores the wider potential of data science and machine learning in addressing pressing global concerns, promoting more resilient and sustainable agricultural practices and ensuring a food-secure future for all.

title: Crop Yield Prediction with Suitable Fertilization Using Deep Learning
abstract: Crop yield prediction and fertilizer recommendation are critical for enhancing agricultural productivity and resource efficiency. This research presents a machine learning-based system utilizing advanced algorithms, including Decision Tree, LightGBM, XGBoost, AdaBoost, Random Forest, ExtraTree, Gradient Boosting, and Bagging Classifier, to forecast agricultural production based on key agricultural parameters. The ExtraTree model achieved an R2score of 99.4% for yield prediction, while ensemble methods like Stacking and Voting Classifiers reached 100% accuracy in fertilizer recommendations using soil and crop data. A Flask-based interface with SQLite authentication was developed for real-time predictions, allowing users to input data and receive actionable insights. This scalable solution integrates machine learning with practical agriculture, helping farmers optimize crop management, adopt sustainable practices, and contribute to global food security.

title: IoT-Integrated Leaf Analysis for Early Plant Disease Detection in Agriculture Using Hybrid Ensemble Models
abstract: Crop diseases threaten food security and agricultural production. For prompt interventions, disease management, and loss reduction, crop disease outbreaks must be detected early. Precision Agriculture (PA) promotes sustainable agriculture by developing predictive plant disease prevention technology using ICTs. This paper presents a multi-step illness detection system using contemporary sensors and images. System architecture includes preprocessing, feature extraction, model training, and disease detection. Crop conditions are monitored using temperature, colour, and humidity sensors. High-resolution (HR) picture preprocessing improves raw images for predictive analysis. Leaf pictures provide geometric characteristics including area, perimeter, and rectangularity to improve model correctness. Model Driven ERL trained a plant disease prediction model. Combining sensor data with machine learning algorithms in PA yielded 89.47% plant disease prediction accuracy. A scalable technique to early disease identification in agriculture makes this technology potential for proactive plant disease control. This model's precision makes it suitable for real-world PA systems, reducing disease-related crop losses and ensuring agricultural output sustainability.

title: Plant Disease Prediction Using Ensemble Risk Scoring Engine
abstract: Plant diseases are a significant menace to food security in the world since they largely decrease crop yield and agricultural output. Diagnostic methods that make use of traditional diagnostic techniques are usually time-consuming, subjective and error-prone because of manual observation. This paper will overcome these shortcomings by introducing an Ensemble Risk Scoring and Evaluation (ERSE) model, which utilizes machine learning algorithms to predict the early presence of the disease in plants based on environmental factors like temperature, humidity, rainfall and soil pH. The ERSE framework produces an output of a risk nature as opposed to the traditional binary classification methods, providing farmers and other parties within the agricultural industry with the opportunity to make decisions that are more balanced. The system combines several learning algorithms namely Random Forest, Logistic Regression and Isolation Forest into one integrated ensemble mechanism that combines the probability scores to provide better prediction reliability. Environmental factors that affect the development of the disease are analyzed to give more insight on the causal relationships. Moreover, the model includes data distribution, correlation, and performance measures visualization, which provides the comparative insights prior to and after the model implementation. It is proved by experimental results that the ERSE model enhances accuracy and robustness in prediction and risk-based scoring mechanism of ERSE model contributes to proactive intervention and long-term management of agriculture.

title: A Hybrid Model Integrating Weather Forecasts with Soil Parameters for Seasonal Yield Prediction
abstract: Agriculture has always been at the mercy of the elements, but today, the combined pressure of climate volatility and declining soil health has made predicting crop yields a massive challenge for global food security. Most existing models tend to look at either the weather or the soil in isolation, missing the critical connection between the two. In this paper, we propose a more holistic “hybrid” approach. By merging real-time weather forecasts-like rainfall and temperature-with the chemical makeup of the soil (pH and NPK levels), we've built a framework that understands the full picture of a farm's potential. To find the best results, we put three powerful machine learning tools to the test: Random Forest, XGBoost, and an ANN. Using a detailed dataset of 5,000 records, our experiments show that bringing environmental and soil data together significantly sharpens the accuracy of seasonal predictions. This study offers a practical, scalable way for farmers to stop guessing and start using data to choose the right crops and protect their livelihoods in an increasingly unpredictable climate.

title: Research on Food Price Prediction Based on BP Neural Network Optimized by Immune Algorithm-Particle Swarm Optimization Hybrid Algorithm
abstract: Food price prediction is an important part of food supply chain management, and food price prediction is of great research significance and application value. Due to the problems of local optimization and slow learning convergence of traditional back propagation (BP) neural network, this paper proposed a BP neural network optimized by immune algorithm-particle swarm optimization hybrid algorithm (IA-PSO-BP) model for food price prediction, and selected relevant indicators. After neural network training and testing, it is found that compared with the BP neural network model optimized by particle swarm optimization algorithm (PSO-BP), the BP neural network model optimized by immune algorithm (IA-BP) and the BP neural network model, the IA-PSO-BP neural network model has the smallest prediction error and the highest accuracy. Compared with PSO-BP neural network model, IA-BP neural network model and BP neural network model, the mean absolute error (MAE) of IA-PSO-BP neural network model is reduced by 39.20%, 67.00% and 140.80%, the root mean square error (RMSE) is reduced by 39.60%, 67.50% and 141.20%, and the mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) is reduced by 0.46%, 0.79% and 1.67%. The predicted value of the IA-PSO-BP neural network model is closest to the actual value, which is more accurate to predict the actual food price. The conclusion shows that the IA-PSO-BP neural network model is a forecasting tool with higher accuracy and stronger applicability, and can be better used in food price prediction.

title: Effective Crop Yield Prediction Using Gradient Boosting To Improve Agricultural Outcomes
abstract: Crop production forecasting is a huge challenge nowadays, resulting in inaccurate results such as food shortages, economic instability, inefficient resource allocation, environmental impact, and lower farmer profitability. Our proposed machine-learning algorithm forecasting yield can help address these difficulties and enhance agricultural outcomes. Crop yield prediction is used to estimate the potential harvest of crops, providing valuable information to farmers, policymakers, and agribusinesses for planning, resource management, and making informed crop production decisions. It helps to improve food security, reduce food waste, and increase the efficiency of food production. Gradient Boosting Agricultural Yield Prediction is a machine learning approach that employs decision trees and gradient descent optimization to create accurate crop yield predictions. This approach and strategy are useful in predicting crop yields. They can assist farmers and agricultural organizations in making better-educated planting, harvesting, and resource allocation decisions. The results of crop yield prediction based on gradient boosting with an accuracy rate of 87.2%, precision of0.84, recall ofO.90, and F1-Score of0.87 indicate that the model is making accurate predictions about crop yields with a good balance of precision and recall. Our work suggests that the model performs efficiently and makes accurate predictions for crop yields. It increases crop production prediction, which improves decision-making, increases efficiency, effectively allocates resources, supports planning, and reduces agriculture’s environmental impact. It has a tremendous impact on the agriculture sector because it promotes sustainability, reduces waste, and improves overall performance.

title: "Optimizing Agriculture: Harnessing Machine Learning for Enhanced Farming"
abstract: Agriculture plays a crucial role in food security and economic development, particularly in developing countries. However, traditional farming practices face challenges such as inefficient resource utilization, climate variability, soil degradation, and lack of real-time decision support. To address these issues, this paper proposes an intelligent web-based agricultural decision support system that leverages Machine Learning (ML) and Deep Learning (DL) techniques for data-driven farming.The proposed system integrates three key functionalities: crop prediction, fertilizer recommendation, and crop disease detection within a unified platform. Support Vector Machine (SVM) is used to predict suitable crops and optimal fertilizer usage based on soil nutrients, pH, temperature, humidity, and rainfall. A Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) is employed to detect plant diseases from leaf images with high accuracy. The system is implemented using a Flask-based backend and a multilingual user interface to ensure accessibility for farmers. Experimental results demonstrate strong performance, achieving accuracies of 94.3% for crop prediction, 91.6% for fertilizer recommendation, and 96.2% for disease detection. The proposed system provides an integrated, scalable, and user-friendly solution that enhances decision-making, improves agricultural productivity, and promotes sustainable farming practices.

title: An Intelligent Hybrid Ensemble Framework for Crop Yield Forecasting in Precision Agriculture
abstract: Problems of proper prediction of crop yields stand as a very serious issue in the food security and sustainable agriculture. This paper has presented a proposal of a Novel Hybrid Ensemble (NHE) machine learning model that predicts intelligent crop yield using three variables (i.e. environmental, soil and crop physiological variables) in consideration. The model combines Gradient Boosting, Random Forest, and Neural Networks using an adaptive weighted voting technique with the aim of acquiring complex non-linear relationships. The preprocessing and stratified validation are extensive, which means that the results have high generalization on full agricultural datasets. The evidence of the experiments shows that the NHE model is very predictive in terms of its R2 (0.9813) and RMSE (5.14) and its MAE (4.06), which is much higher than the majority of the comparative models and its robustness is higher than of the individual algorithms. The proposed structure enables precision farming whereby it would be possible to predict yield and resources are managed efficiently and decisions are made using data and relevant to the sustainable farming methods. The suggested NHE model supports agriculture by being climate-resilient with proper yield predictions in changing conditions to facilitate adaptation, resource optimization, risks reduction, climate effects alleviation, food security and sustainable agriculture.

title: Multi-Modal Yield Prediction and Interim Crop Grading
abstract: Accurately predicting crop yields continues to challenge Indian agriculture, largely because of the country’s diverse agro-climatic zones, sparse plot-level data, and the complex, nonlinear interactions between environmental and management factors. Conventional statistical methods struggle to deliver the precision and timeliness farmers need for effective decision-making. We present AgriFusionTech, a multi-modal deep learning framework that tackles yield prediction and interim crop assessment by combining ground-level imagery with contextual data including weather patterns, soil characteristics, and farming practices. Our approach uses intermediate fusion: an EfficientNet-based vision module generates what we call a Crop Wellness Score, while XGBoost captures intricate patterns in tabular data. These outputs feed into a neural prediction module that produces localized yield forecasts. To make these predictions understandable and useful, we employ SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) to break down each forecast into interpretable contributions from individual features, translating model outputs into practical recommendations farmers can act on. Testing on rice and wheat datasets yielded excellent results (R2reaching 0.9997), confirming that fusing multiple data types outperforms single-source approaches. This framework offers reliable support for farmers, agribusinesses, and policymakers working toward food security and sustainable agriculture in India.

title: A Machine Learning-based Approach for Crop Yield Prediction and Fertilizer Recommendation
abstract: Agriculture plays a critical role to Indian global economy and contributes a major part to GDP. With the expansion of the human population, it is necessary to maintain food security, it is achieved and controlled by the agricultural yield produced by the nation. The yield of a crop is mainly determined by the climatic conditions like temperature, rainfall, soil conditions, and fertilizers. Due to these variable factors, the production gets affected and remains a huge problem for the agricultural sector to strengthen the need for exactness for proper analyzing the crop production in variable climatic conditions. Recently, the machine learning algorithms are used by the researchers to predict the yield of a crop before its actual cultivation. This research study has proposed a machine learning algorithm: AdaBoost to predict the yield of crops based on the parameters like state, district, area, seasons, rainfall, temperature, and area. To enhance the yield, this research study also suggests a fertilizer based on the soil conditions like NPK values, soil type, soil PH, humidity, and moisture. Fertilizer recommendation is primarily done by using the Random Forest [RF] algorithm.

title: Automated H yperparameter Tuned Stacked Autoencoder based Rice Crop Yield Prediction Model
abstract: Rice crop production had greatly contributed to the food security of India, with over 40% of the entire crop production. Its productivity depends on favourable weather conditions. Changeability from season to season is unfavourable to the agronomist's livelihood and income. Enhancing the capability of agriculturalists for predicting crop production in distinct weather situations, can help farmers and other shareholders in making significant decisions concerning crop choice and agronomy. This estimation can assist agriculturalists and other shareholders to make better decisions on crop yielding. Prediction of crop yields using contemporary methods like Machine Learning (ML) techniques is in high demand for increasing the productivity of crops under several environmental circumstances. Therefore, this article develops an intelligent Hyperparameter Tuned Stacked Autoencoder Based Rice Crop Yield Prediction (HTSAE-RCYP) model. The proposed HTSAE-RCYP technique performs three stages of initial pre-processing: data conversion, null value removal, and data normalization. For the yield prediction process, the presented HTSAE-RCYP technique employs the SAE model which accurately forecasts the level of rice yield. To improve the predictive outcomes of the SAE model, a root means square propagation (RMS Prop) optimizer is utilized in this work. The experimental result analysis of the HTSAE-RCYP technique is tested using a series of simulations and the outcomes inferred the betterment of the HTSAE-RCYP technique over other existing models.

title: Predictive Model for Crop Disease and Management System Using Machine Learning with Deployment Through Flask
abstract: Crop diseases have a disproportionately large economic effect on farmers and threaten food security. Predictive Model for Crop Disease and Management System, which uses machine and deep learning to automate disease identification and management is this project. Consuming the VGG19 pre trained model for multi class classification, the system is able to distinguish between crop diseases based on leaf images at high accuracy. Users can upload crop images, receive real time disease predictions and obtain actionable management recommendations, including use of pesticides, with a web application that is on top of Flask. By integrating data augmentation techniques for model generalization, a robust knowledge base for disease management, and feedback mechanisms for continuous refinement, the proposed system constitutes an amalgam of many of the above techniques. This system bridges this gap between the latest technologies and what is truly practical farming needs, and enables early detection of diseases, sustainable agriculture and effective disease management. Future additions are to expand the disease database, include real time field data, and multiple languages for better accessibility.

title: Decision Support System for Selection of Staples Food and Food Commodity Price Prediction Post-COVID-19 Using Simple Additive Weighting and Multiple Linear Regression Methods
abstract: In the pandemic after the occurrence of COVID-19, there are significant changes in economic statistics, this is influenced by economic activity that is not stable compared to before. The price of food staples was also affected by the pandemic, meetings between buyers and traders, usually held in traditional and modern markets, were hampered due to government restrictions on the territory. This causes a decrease in existing transactions in the market, therefore foodstuffs have the possibility of price volatility. Multiple Linear Regression (MLR) algorithm is a method that can overcome predictions with the type of seasonal dataset prediction, therefore the MLR algorithm is implemented to predict food prices, especially in the modern market, based on the predicted prices, then a decision support system is made to make an alternative ranking of food selection accumulation. Based on the available food ingredients there are nutrients contained in these foods, therefore experts are needed to determine the weighting of nutrition in each food ingredient. Simple Additive Weighting (SAW) method is a method that can do weighting and ranking of alternatives. Therefore the SAW method is applied to rank alternative food staples that have nutritional weight and price. Based on the application of MLR, the error level testing concluded that the prediction of the price of food “Rice” has the least error results compared to other foodstuffs with the value of MSE 21261.04, MAE 145.79, RMSE 145.812, MAPE 0.81 while for the best R2 values found at food ingredients “Garlic” with a value of 0.576. Based on testing of the application of SAW, the same results are obtained between manual calculations and calculations provided by the system, so that the accuracy of the system can be ascertained.

title: Deep Learning-Based Plant Classification: VGG16 and Leaf Morphology
abstract: Recent developments in deep learning, especially with regard to convolutional neural networks (CNNs) such as VGG16, have greatly increased automated leaf trait-based plant species classification. This work focuses on the identification, strictly from leaf photos, of four economically significant plant species: maize, cashew, cassava, and tomato. The study approach consists of careful dataset curation, thorough pre-processing to standardize image quality and VGG16 model training applied with transfer learning approaches. Accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score evaluation measures show how well the model can correctly identify several plant species depending on their leaf form. The result depicts how efficiently it can enhance precision farming strategies and support tasks involving disease diagnosis, crop analysis, and the forecasting of yield. This study aims to provide sustainable farming strategies and preserve the overall biodiversity, therefore adding to the enhancing the field of artificial intelligence applications in viticulture, supporting food security, sustainable agriculture, climatic conditions as well as economic growth.

title: Early Prediction of Rainfall Using Automated Integrated Prediction Approach (AIPA)
abstract: Agriculture is one of the significant fields in the world nowadays. It is essential to improve agricultural yield by using various advanced techniques. Rainfall prediction is the most challenging task for regular users, and it helps to improve crop yielding based on rainfall. Prediction of rainfall in the early stages provides accurate information to the farmers who need preventive measures. The proposed approach is an Automated Integrated Prediction Approach (AIPA) which is the combination of machine learning models, such as deep neural networks (DNNs), support vector machines (SVMs), and gradient boosting devices (GBMs), to accurately predict rainfall. Finally, the algorithm's versatility suits various geographical regions and climates, promoting sustainable agriculture and food security. Finally, merging DL and meteorological data analysis to develop a hybrid algorithm shows significant promise for increasing rainfall prediction accuracy. This research addresses climate change challenges while promoting agricultural sustainability and increased food production. Experimental results show that the proposed approach obtained high performance in terms of performance metrics.

title: Predicting Staple Food Materials Price Using Multivariables Factors (Regression and Fourier Models with ARIMA)
