abstract: Staple food material prices can be a trending topic in the market. The fluctuation of the price is influenced by many factors. For instance, the weather, oil price, and etc are the external factors of the staple food price. Indeed, the prediction of staple food fluctuation price is important for the farmers, consumers, even government. In this paper, the Linear Regression and Fourier model with ARIMA (Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average) will be used to predict the staple food price which consider the external influences. Here, the results using those two methods are shown in a good agreement with the observation price at market. However, the highest accuracy in predicting price using Fourier regression with ARIMA is obtained for staple food onion which is 96.57%. Meanwhile, using multiple linear regression with ARIMA, the highest accuracy is obtained for staple food red chili with 99.84%. Overall, in this research, Fourier regression with ARIMA is observed better than multiple linear regression with ARIMA method, since the accuracy of Fourier regression with ARIMA is quite stable without disturbance of fluctuation existing data.

title: Predicting Crop Yield: A Comparative Analysis Using Machine Learning Models
abstract: Predicting crop yields accurately is essential to maintaining sustainable agricultural methods and guaranteeing food security. The intricate relationships between soil characteristics, crop management techniques, and climatic factors are frequently missed by traditional methods. In order to solve the issue, this study applies sophisticated ensemble machine learning models for yield prediction, namely Random Forest (RF), Gradient Boosting (GB), and XGBoost. To guarantee accurate and objective results, the dataset was preprocessed using Min-Max normalization and missing value imputation. Stratified K-Fold Cross-Validation was then used for evaluation. According to experimental results, Gradient Boosting consistently performed better than the other models, obtaining the lowest mean squared error ($\text{MSE}=\mathbf{0. 0 7 4 3}$) and the highest coefficient of determination ($\mathbf{R 2} \boldsymbol{=} \mathbf{0. 9 7 2 1}$). While Random Forest produced comparatively lower accuracy, XGBoost also produced competitive performance..The findings demonstrate that ensemble learning techniques provide a reliable and scalable approach to crop yield prediction by successfully capturing nonlinear relationships in agricultural datasets. By providing dependable, data-driven insights for decision-making, this study highlights the potential of machine learning in agricultural forecasting for farmers, policymakers, and agribusinesses. Additionally, it establishes the groundwork for upcoming developments that might integrate remote sensing and frameworks to improve predictive capabilities even more.

title: Advanced Crop Yield Prediction through Granger Causality-Inspired Graph Neural Network Optimized with Serial Exponential Coati Optimization Algorithm
abstract: The agriculture industry is becoming more vulnerable to the bad consequences of climate change and too much usage of pesticides, which is a big danger to food security around the world. Accurate crop production forecasting is necessary to mitigate these risks and offers insights into sustainable farming practices. In this paper, Advanced Crop Yield Prediction through Granger Causality-Inspired Graph Neural Network Optimized with Serial Exponential Coati Optimization Algorithm (ACYP-GCGNN-SECOA) is proposed. Input data are gathered from the crop yield dataset. Then, the collected data are pre-processed using Cross-Grained Neural Collaborative Filtering (CGNCF) for handling missing values and normalization. The preprocessed data are given into Feature affine residual network (FA-ResNet) to extract statistical features such as mean, standard deviation and standard scalar. The extracted features are fed into Granger Causality-Inspired Graph Neural Network (GCGNN) is used to forecast crop yields accurately under varying climate scenarios, thereby enhancing decision-making for sustainable agriculture. Finally, the Serial Exponential Coati Optimization Algorithm (SECOA) is used for improving the weight parameters of GCGNN. The proposed ACYP-GCGNN-SECOA technique is executed and efficiency is assessed with several performance metrics like Accuracy, F1-score, Recall, Precision, Mean Absolute Error (MAE) and Root Mean Square Error (RMSE). The proposed method attains$\mathbf{6. 2 8 \%}, / \mathbf{5. 7 8 \%}$and$\mathbf{7. 2 9 \%}$higher accuracy compared with existing techniques such as Incorporating meteorological data and pesticide information to forecast crop yields using machine learning (IMD-FCY-ML), Crop yield prediction using multi-attribute weighted tree-based support vector machine (CYP-MAWT-SVM) and Crop yield prediction using effectual deep learning and dimensionality reduction approaches for Indian regional crops (CYP-DL-IRC) respectively.

title: Development of a Visual Inspection System with Machine Learning for Automated Food Price Estimation in Restaurants
abstract: A YOLOv5 object detection model was trained on a custom-labelled dataset of dummy food images to identify single and combined food items. The system integrates a webcam and structured lighting for consistent image capture. Training involved data augmentation, label smoothing, and OneCycleLR scheduling to optimize performance. The best model achieved high classification accuracy and F1-score, enabling real-time food detection and pricing. This solution aims to reduce manual pricing errors and streamline restaurant operations.

title: Maize Disease Prediction Using RESNET and LSTM
abstract: In a vast country like India, Agriculture is meant to be the back and bone of our country which also plays a major role in our country’s economy. Among the major crops cultivated, maize is considered one of the important crop due to its economic value and versatility. But the main concern is that maize is being affected by various diseases which can also lead to economic crisis. Common Maize Diseases are Grey Leaf Spot, Northern Corn Leaf Blight, Common Rust. To overcome this problem, our project develops a Maize Crop Disease Prediction System using deep learning. As we know that prevention is better than cure, it is important to predict the disease at early stage for increasing agricultural productivity in a sustainable way. This project will accept the two types of inputs from the user. We can input the image or the text which is convenient to the user. This system uses Convolution Neural Networks (CNN) for image - based disease detection and Natural Language Processing (NLP) for text - based symptom detection. In CNN we will be using ResNet-50 for our image processing. For the text detection, we use some techniques like Long Short-Term Memory(LSTM).Our project will allow farmers and agronomists to input data either it may be in image or text format and predict the accurate disease. This project also aims sustainable agricultural productivity and food security in India.

title: Zomato Review Analysis Using Machine Learning
abstract: Restaurant ratings and reviews have a noteworthy influence on shaping the public’s perception of a restaurant and influencing the dining decisions of individuals. With the rise of online platforms and review websites, it is now easier for customers to share their experiences and opinions about restaurants. Potential diners can easily access information about the quality of food, service, atmosphere, and value for money offered by a restaurant. Many customers visit a restaurant based on reviews given by the customer or other app users. India has a rich culinary heritage and offers a diverse range of cuisines that cater to different tastes and preferences. The restaurant industry in India is growing rapidly, and new restaurants are popping up all the time, offering customers an ever-increasing variety of dining options. Starting a new restaurant can be challenging, especially in a highly competitive market like India, where there are already many established restaurants. Major challenges that persist in the industry comprise elevated real estate expenses, escalating food prices, insufficient skilled labour, and customer acquisition. The system aims to perform sentimental analysis and exploratory data analysis on Zomato reviews. Sentimental analysis is performed using the SVM approach to determine the accuracy of the sentiment model. The model would deliver the top three cuisines in a location based on sentiment analysis, which would help new restaurants make decisions. The system shows factors affecting restaurant businesses by doing data analysis on various parameters of the dataset. The SVM model has adequate accuracy.

title: Thailand Food Price Forecasting: Comparative Analysis of Machine Learning Models
abstract: This study aims to address food price fraud and predict pricing trends for key commodities-Cassava flour, Maize, Meat (chicken), and Rice-in Thailand, using advanced machine learning techniques to enhance forecasting accuracy and detect anomalies. We utilized historical food price data from 2000 to 2020 and incorporated USD exchange rate fluctuations to build and evaluate several regression models, including Linear Regression, Decision Tree Regressor, Random Forest Regressor, Gradient Boosting Regressor, and Support Vector Regressor. The Decision Tree and Random Forest models demonstrated superior performance with the lowest mean squared error (MSE) and root mean squared error (RMSE), effectively capturing price trends and fluctuations. In contrast, Linear Regression and Support Vector Regressor showed higher errors and less effectiveness in handling non-linear patterns. This study highlights the efficacy of machine learning in improving price prediction accuracy and detecting potential fraud, offering a robust framework for analyzing commodity pricing dynamics. The findings provide actionable insights for policymakers and stakeholders to implement proactive strategies, promoting greater market stability and fairness in Thailand's agricultural sector.

title: Deep Learning Based Prediction of Commodity Prices Using LSTM
abstract: Commodity price prediction using deep learning, specifically LSTM models, is a challenging task due to limited data, price volatility, and the complexity of capturing temporal dependencies. In recent years, various techniques have been explored to address these challenges, such as transfer learning, model interpretability, handling seasonality, and ensemble learning. However, existing systems still face issues related to model interpretability, uncertainty quantification, and adaptability to evolving market conditions. This article aims to analyze one of the machine learning methods and what applications it can have in the financial world. Specifically, it aims to explore a technique called deep learning. To do this, some methods are analyzed, which are most relevant and most used in the industry, which are found within the deep learning method. Once the selected methods are analyzed, it is intended to implement them in a programming environment, in this case Python is chosen, and then a practical case is developed and evaluated. The case in question is the forecasting of commodity prices, with particular focus on the price of Brent. Different technical analysis indicators will be used in this forecasting model, knowing that there is no solid statistical basis in their use, but in practice most traders use them and, in the absence of shocks, on a macroeconomic basis, the results obtained when using them are, in general, quite adequate. Finally, the results of the predictions obtained are compared under different models to calculate which model gives us the greatest advantage.

title: Detecting Diseases in Potato Leaves using Deep Learning and Machine Learning Approaches: A Review
abstract: As a mostly agricultural country, India is deeply concerned about its crop production rate. When crop yields drop, food prices rise, and people who can't afford even potatoes go hungry. Physical examination is a component of conventional approaches for spotting diseases in plants. This approach is exceedingly costly, laborious, and doesn't yield good outcomes. A unique approach for diagnosing potato leaf ailments should be developed to detect sick leaves at the start of their developmental period, which will assist to boost the output and consequently reduce the financial losses suffered by agriculturalists. Fortunately, new Deep Learning (DL) and Machine Learning (ML) models have flourished as a method of reducing plant disease and increasing crop yields, alleviating some of the burdens on farmers. Deep Neural Networks (DNN), a kind of artificial intelligence technology, may be used to identify disease-infected plants so that they can be treated early on, in the bud stage, before the sickness has spread too far. Based on a comprehensive literature assessment, the authors of this research concluded that Convolution Neural Networks (CNN) are superior to other methods for detecting leaf diseases and it is determined that CNN provides the highest achievable accuracy of 91% to 100%.

title: Revolutionizing Aquaculture Practices: IoT and Deep Learning-based Remote Monitoring for Sustainable Fish Farming
abstract: Aquaculture plays a vital role in meeting the growing demand for seafood while addressing sustainability concerns in fisheries. To optimize fish growth and ensure efficient resource utilization an innovative IoT and Deep Learning-based remote monitoring system is proposed tailored for aquaculture operations. Our system integrates sensor technology, IOT connectivity, and Deep Learning algorithms to provide real-time monitoring and control of key environmental parameters such as water temperature, pH levels, oxygen concentration, and feeding behavior. By leveraging a network of sensors deployed in aquaculture facilities, our system collects and analyzes environmental data to optimize aquaculture practices and ensure optimal conditions for fish growth. Through a user-friendly interface accessible via web or mobile applications, aqua-culturists can remotely monitor the status of their facilities and adjust operational parameters as needed. Additionally, our system utilizes Deep Learning algorithms to analyze historical data and predict optimal feeding schedules, thereby enhancing feed efficiency and fish growth rates. Field trials demonstrate the effectiveness of our IOT and Deep Learning-based monitoring system in improving fish health and productivity while reducing environmental impacts and operational costs. Our findings highlight the potential of IoT and Deep Learning technologies in revolutionizing aquaculture practices, promoting sustainability, and enhancing food security in fisheries

title: Crop Yield Prediction using Hybrid Deep Learning and Geo-Spatial Data Integration
abstract: Agriculture is critical to food security, means of survival, and the economy of India. Hence there are challenges due to climatic variability, and at times worsening climatic systems which can lead to reduced stability in weather and available resources, we feel crop yield prediction is essential. Crop yield prediction does not only help farmers make improved decisions or more informed choices, it reasonable allows agri-tech stakeholders to optimise resource use and efforts for better productivity. The varying weather and insecure nature of weather have impacted agricultural productivity with respect to India, necessitating crop yield forecast with utmost accuracy. The proposed research put forth a new kind of hybrid deep learning forecast model that integrates Temporal Fusion Transformer (TFT) and the 1D Convolution Neural Network (CNN) models to increase forecasting accuracy through capturing both temporal and spatial dependencies in agricultural data. Differing from classic machine learning models considered earlier, the system incorporates geospatial inputs such as satellite-derived NDVI and soil moisture, along with historical weather variables including rainfall, temperature, and humidity. The Temporal Fusion Transformer takes advantage of the latest developments in attention mechanisms so that the model can pick up long-range temporal patterns and variable importance varying in time. District-level micro-climatic clustering has been incorporated to create localized prediction capability, and a crop recommendation module is provided considering both environmental and market factors. Explainable AI (XAI) techniques, especially SHAP, have been employed to interpret the feature contributions and thus render the model transparent and trustworthy. Comparative study against baseline models such as Random Forest and SVM has established that the presented framework is up to 12% more efficient in predictions, hinting at the real agricultural decision-making potential of the system. The study intends to furnish farmers with useful accurate data-based insights.

title: Strategic Food Commodity Price Forecasting Using LSTM and SARIMAX: A Case Study of Bandung City and Bogor Regency, Indonesia
abstract: Food price volatility threatens food security and economic stability, especially for strategic commodities. Despite various forecasting methods, accurately predicting regional food prices in Indonesia remains challenging due to nonlinear trends and location-specific dynamics. This study compares Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks and Seasonal Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average with Exogenous Variables (SARIMAX) for forecasting weekly prices of 10 strategic food commodities in Bandung City and Bogor Regency, using daily data aggregated from March 2021 to May 2025.Forecast accuracy was evaluated using Root Mean Square Error (RMSE), Mean Absolute Error (MAE), and Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE). LSTM outperformed SARIMAX in 17 of 20 region-commodity combinations. For instance, LSTM reduced MAPE from 63.5% to 20.9% for Curly Red Chili in Bandung, and from 39.0% to 19.5% in Bogor. SARIMAX slightly outperformed LSTM in stable series such as rice and garlic. These results demonstrate LSTM's advantage in modeling volatile, nonlinear patterns while SARIMAX remains effective for regular seasonal trends.The findings support the adoption of deep learning-based forecasts in regional food security systems. Accurate predictions can inform early warning mechanisms, buffer stock management, and targeted interventions. Future research should explore hybrid SARIMAX-LSTM models, multivariate inputs, and uncertainty-aware forecasting for broader deployment.

title: End-to-End Implementation of Efficient YOLO on NPU for Real-Time Plant Disease Detection
abstract: With the worsening global food crisis, ensuring food security and reducing food losses have become national strategies for many countries. Traditional methods for detecting plant diseases and pests heavily rely on manual inspection, which is time-consuming, labor-intensive, and prone to human errors. This has prompted scientific researchers to explore innovative and effective approaches to mitigate agricultural losses. Deep learning-based object detection offers a promising solution; however, deploying such models in real-world agricultural environments remains challenging because of the high computational demands and associated hardware costs, particularly when relying on GPU-based systems. This paper presents a lightweight, real-time plant disease detection system based on neural processing units (NPUs) and the YOLOX-Nano object detection model. By leveraging the high energy efficiency, low power consumption, and compact integration capabilities of NPUs, we address the limitations of GPU-based inference, including excessive power requirements, high cost, and limited mobility. The system allows deployment on embedded and mobile platforms such as smart agricultural robots, unmanned ground vehicles, and handheld inspection devices to enable real-time, on-site diagnosis. Furthermore, the framework supports multi-domain and multi-functional applications through algorithmic adaptation, paving the way for scalable and sustainable smart agriculture solutions.

title: Smart Meal Revival System for Economically Challenged People
abstract: The Smart Meal Revival System is a digital platform designed to address food insecurity among economically disadvantaged populations by redistributing surplus food. The system integrates technological solutions for food recovery, quality control, and optimized distribution to ensure the efficient allocation of resources. Machine learning techniques predict demand patterns, while computer vision assists in real-time food quality assessment. A web and mobile application provide users with food availability details, nearby distribution centers, and meal recommendations based on dietary needs. Collaborations with local businesses, restaurants, and food suppliers strengthen the food supply network and enhance waste reduction. The platform fosters transparency by allowing users to monitor stock levels and delivery logistics. Future enhancements aim to expand accessibility, refine recommendations, and establish a scalable model for sustainable food redistribution. This initiative contributes to reducing food waste and enhancing food security for underprivileged communities.

title: Advances in Crop Monitoring Technologies: A Comprehensive Review
abstract: Agricultural optimization and food security rely on effective plant monitoring. This essay probes the evolution and comparative analysis of modern technologies that are revolutionizing agricultural monitoring. In this paper, we show how artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning algorithms, and drones combined with the power of IoT sensors (smart agriculture) along rural data collection using remote sensing technologies will help to improve precision farm management by understanding the pros and cons in implementing these AI-driven new tools into smart devices capable of supporting higher crop yields and higher efficiency. Through a review of case studies and market trends, this article delves into how these technologies provide farmers with real-time data, predictive analytics, and actionable insights. Moral, monetary, and ecological reverberations of bonding these advances universally are likewise discussed. Ultimately, this comparative study to develop resilient and sustainable food production systems through the inclusion of modern technologies is an important opportunity for many difficult socioeconomic and climatic issues.

title: Assessing a Machine Learning Model for Predicting Maize Grain Yield Based on Chlorophyll Content and Vegetation Indices
abstract: This study investigates maize productivity using remote sensing data, vegetation indices, and machine learning techniques. Utilizing a multi-temporal dataset of 17,100 images captured by unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) across three crop cycles, we extract essential vegetation indices. These indices, along with ground-truth data on maize yields and chlorophyll content, serve as inputs for twelve machine learning models, including CatBoost, random forest, and XGBoost regressions. Rigorous evaluation, including RMSE, MAE, and R2, assesses each model’s capacity to predict maize yields.Key vegetation indices with strong positive correlations to maize yields emerge, offering predictive markers for precision agriculture. The best-performing model, linear regression, achieves an impressive R2of 0.77, while the worst-performing model, support vector regression, exhibits a negative R2of −0.74.These results emphasize the significance of model selection in maize yield prediction, guiding agricultural decision-making. Future research can delve deeper into enhancing agricultural practices and food security through refined yield prediction dynamics.

title: Computer Vision for Agricultural Automation - Algorithmic Solutions for Crop Yield Predictions
abstract:
Computer vision is defined in this study and one of the applications demonstrated is crop yield prediction in agricultural automation. Here we have emphasized on its use for computer vision for the agricultural domain. Using multispectral images that can be obtained from drones satellites and pairs with ground truths of average crop yield, weather conditions and parts of the soil treated with practices performed by an agronomist the proffered methodology would take advantage of the uniqueness of the concept to predict crop production. Further, elaborate machine learning methods such as line regression, decision trees, Random Forest, Support Vector Machine and CNN models are applied in order that the ultimate selection of the model would be contingent on the accuracy in relation to a crop yield. The DL based approaches as seen majority of this work and particularly the CNN exhibited improved results over regression models since there are more of classification than regression; In addition DL models are more appropriate for spatial relations and variations characteristic of crop data. title: Analysing the Impact of Climate Change on The Crop Yields of Irrigated Crops and their Water Requirements in India Using Neuro Evolutionary Algorithm
abstract: Global food security, facing the threat of climate change, is one of the major challenges of the 21st century for sustainability that is already under scrutiny with adequate food security for population growth. Current challenges include water shortages, unaffordable costs due to production and demand, and unpredictable weather conditions. They urged farmers to provide improved farming. In particular, uncertainty about climate change, lack of irrigation facilities, lack of land resources, and lack of crops from traditional farming techniques. In agriculture. Different machine learning techniques such as perception, division, regression, and aggregation are used to predict crops. Artificial networks, vector support systems, linear and linguistic lines, decision trees, and Bayesian intelligence are some of the mathematical methods used to implement the prediction. Obviously, choosing the right algorithm for the sample design algorithms presents a challenge for researchers about the selected plants. In this work, research has been conducted on how many algorithms of machine learning can help predict the dissolution of crops. Methods have been developed to generate predictions. Use machine learning technology in a large computer control system.

title: Machine Learning Approach for the Prediction of Consumer Food Price Index
abstract: The price of food and food related items are dynamic. A measure change in the price affects the buying behaviour of the consumer and monetary policies by the Government. The Consumer Food Price Index (CFPI) reflects the variations in food prices during a certain period. In India, the CFPI is released monthly by the Central Statistical Organization. It also reflects the inflation and helps the Government to take corrective measures in time. In this paper we have applied the machine learning approach in forecasting the consumer food price index in India. In specific, this work has focused on the applicability of Artificial Neural Network (ANN) models with back propagation learning in predicting the future values of CFPI. The monthly data for rural, urban and combined from the period 2013 to 2021 have been used to train and validate the models. The Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) values have been used to validate the accuracy of the models. The experimental results show that a simple ANN model with back propagation algorithm is highly capable in forecasting the future values of CFPI.

title: Predicting Low and Normal Phosphorus Tolerance in Maize Using Advanced Ensemble Classifiers
abstract: Maize cultivation is vital for global food security, making the precise management of phosphorus levels crucial for optimizing crop yields. This study explores the prediction of maize phosphorus levels under low phosphorus (LP:$2.5 \times 10^{-6} \ \text{mol} \ \mathrm{L}^{-1}$of KH2PO4) and normal phosphorus (NP:$2.5 \times 10^{-4} \ \text{mol} \ \mathrm{L}^{-1}$of KH2PO4) conditions using machine learning, focusing on eight key plant traits: shoot length, root length, shoot fresh weight, root fresh weight, root dry weight, root-to-shoot length ratio, total dry matter, and shoot dry weight, from 550 maize genotypes. We evaluated eight classifier algorithms, including Gaussian Naive Bayes, Gradient Boosting, Support Vector Classifier, K-Nearest Neighbors, LightGBM, XG-Boost, Random Forest, and Stochastic Gradient Descent, using metrics like precision, recall, F1-score, and accuracy. XGBoost, LightGBM, and Random Forest emerged as top performers, achieving an ensemble F1-score of 0.9849. By integrating these three algorithms into an ensemble model, we enhanced model robustness and reduced individual model bias, leading to more accurate predictions. This study demonstrates the potential of ensemble learning for improving agricultural decision-making, with future research suggested to expand datasets, integrate temporal-spatial data, and explore advanced ensemble methods to further optimize crop management.

title: Data Science for Climate Resilience and Smart Agriculture
abstract: Climate change is one of the biggest challenges facing world agriculture, impacting crop yields, accessible resources, and food security. Traditional methods of agriculture are, however, less receptive to the adaptive demands required to deal with the changed environmental setting. The present research has, thus, attempted to address this issue by maximizing data science in support of climate resilience and intelligent agriculture through a multi-tiered approach for methodology. These range from the acquisition of satellite images, IoT-enabled sensor data in the field, and historical climate information, pre-processing, analytical modeling, system integration, and output validation. Machine learning techniques deployed include Random Forest and time-series forecasting to improve yield forecasting and estimation of climate risk. Results indicated that the enhancement in the accuracy of yield prediction attained 25 %, water consumption was reduced by 30 %, fertilizer usage dropped by 20 %, and the correct forecast for climate risk reached 85 %. A cloudintegrated platform featuring real-time analytics integrated with the decision support proved to be very flexible and easy to use in multiple agro-climatic zones. This research has shown the way data-driven models can influence the agricultural sector to an adaptive system, assuring a more efficient and sustainable system contributing good practices for climate-resilient farming and resource-informed management in the uncertain environmental scenario.

title: Development of a Naive Bayes-based Framework for Optimizing Crop Recommendation System and Enhancing Agricultural Yield Prediction
abstract: This research study proposes a comprehensive Crop Recommendation System that uses advanced machine learning to boost agricultural productivity. By analyzing key environmental and soil factors, including soil composition, pH, temperature, humidity, and rainfall, the system offers customized, data-driven crop suggestions to optimize yield and promote sustainable farming. The system evaluates several algorithms, including Naive Bayes, Decision Tree, Logistic Regression, and Random Forest, and identifies Naive Bayes as the top performer for accurately predicting crop suitability. This multi-algorithm approach represents a significant advancement in precision agriculture, empowering farmers and policymakers with actionable insights to drive improvements in the agricultural sector. Leveraging historical data, the Crop Recommendation System supports farmers, consultants, and policymakers in making more informed and strategic crop selection decisions. The system's precision and adaptability make it a valuable resource for stakeholders focused on improving resource efficiency and fostering sustainable agriculture, ultimately enhancing food security and minimizing environmental impact.

title: Machine Learning Technique for Prognosticating Crop Yield Variability with Air Quality Index
abstract: Rice production in India holds significant importance in terms of its contribution to the economy and food security. However, the expansion of this sector is currently facing challenges due to the increasing levels of air pollution, including ground-level ozone and particle matter. The objective of this study is to examine the influence of air quality index (AQI) factors on rice productivity, namely during the winter season, with a particular emphasis on the exceptional year of 2020-2021. By utilizing Internet of Things (IoT) technology, the collection of real-time air quality data is combined with rice yield analysis through the implementation of decision tree regression, k-nearest neighbors (KNN), and support vector regression (SVR) methods. The research findings emphasis the effectiveness of the decision tree model in accurately representing the complex relationship between AQI and rice yield. This model demonstrates higher predictive accuracy when compared to SVR and KNN. This study highlights the importance of managing air quality in order to achieve sustainable rice production. Additionally, it emphasizes the potential of monitoring systems based on the Internet of Things (IoT) to significantly transform agricultural practices. By doing so, these systems may effectively connect environmental stewardship, technological innovation, and food security.

title: Intelligent Water Management System Utilizing AI for Precision Agriculture
abstract: Water scarcity is a growing concern, particularly in agriculture, where efficient water management is essential for sustainability and crop yield. This work presents an AI-based irrigation management system aimed at optimizing water utilization through the analysis of real-time soil moisture data, meteorological forecasts, and crop-specific water needs. The system employs IoT-enabled soil sensors and predictive machine learning algorithms to dynamically modify irrigation schedules, thereby substantially minimizing water waste and optimizing crop output. The suggested approach amalgamates several data sources and machine learning methodologies to provide a fully automated and adaptive irrigation system tailored to the distinct requirements of each crop type and growth phase. Experimental findings demonstrate significant enhancements in water efficiency and productivity, underscoring the promise of AI and IoT in enhancing precision agriculture. This study offers a scalable and sustainable methodology for agricultural water management, aiding global initiatives in water conservation and food security enhancement.

title: Study on Machine Learning and Back Propagation for Crop Recommendation System
abstract: India may be the largest exporter of farm products, but the country’s farms are not very productive. Inadequate agricultural production means farmers bring home much less money. The producers need a performance improvement if there is a rise in their revenue. Farmers may boost output by cultivating land more effectively by first determining what will thrive there. The land’s potential production can be enhanced by growing the correct crops. As a result, crop recommendation algorithms may be quite useful for agriculturalists. Crop yields are influenced by a wide variety of external influences. The production is affected by environmental conditions like as heat, moisture, soil pH, precipitation, and the availability of nutrients like potash, ammonium, & phosphate. There is a lot of confusion among farmers regarding which crops should be produced in particular regions to get the highest possible yield and financial return. As a result, the purpose of this study is to show how a ml algo may be used to forecast crops and associated prices. Soil is fundamental to the proper functioning of the terrestrial ecosystem, and its primary duty is the cultivation of crops for the purpose of providing food for the world’s ever-increasing population. Yet global soil deterioration poses a serious challenge to food security. The stresses of urbanization and industry, among others, contribute to soil degradation. Habitat loss, altered green spaces, soil erosion, unchecked livestock, illegal dumping, and ineffective land management are all major contributors to soil deterioration. More than 1.5 billion people are in danger of losing their way of life due to the rapid pace of land degradation, which now stands at 24 percent (350M sq.km). In this situation, keeping up with the rising demand for food is a problem made more difficult by the need to maintain soil quality). As a result, maintaining agricultural output and adapting to the uncertainties brought by climate change needs constant evaluation and monitoring of SQ. However, assessing soil quality is challenging owing to subjectivity and complexity because of the wider range of soil uses. Soil quality may be measured using an index that allows for chronological & geographical comparison between various land use & control strategies.

title: SpectraCrop: A Hybrid AI-GIS Framework with Adaptive Decision Algorithms for Precision Agriculture
abstract: The SpectraCrop Management System is a futuristic smart agriculture platform that combines satellite images, artificial intelligence (AI), and machine learning (ML) to transform geospatial analytics and make farming sustainable for farmers. This paper proposes a unique hybrid approach using spectral vegetation indexing as the primary technique to model an AI-based adaptive decision algorithm (ADA) to dynamically reschedule irrigation and pesticide application schedules. Through GIS, real-time satellite data and soil sensors located via the Internet of Things (IoT) are combined to produce high-resolution crop health maps. Analytics performed in the cloud can also increase scale, and machine-learning models that use historical as well as current information facilitate early identification of crop stress and disease epidemics. The systematic ADA approach improves advice based on the responses obtained in the local fields constantly, making it accurate, efficient, and flexible. There is actionable insight, real-time alerts, and a trend-forecasting, user-friendly web and mobile interface. Water use efficiency, the number of pesticides that have to be used, and yield predictability are dramatically improved by the experimental results. This system will lead to a more sustainable and resilient agricultural system that approaches global food security and environmental issues.

title: Privacy-Preserving Edge Intelligence for Agriculture: A 6G-Enabled Federated Learning Architecture
abstract: The fastest growing wireless communication technologies and artificial intelligence are changing the face of agriculture making it a highly data intensive industry. Scalability, latency, privacy and energy efficiency pose a challenge to conventional cloud-centric methods of agricultural analytics. This paper introduces a 6G enabled Federated Learning (FL) model to large-scale smart agriculture applications to overcome these limits. This framework is based on the ultra-low latency, massive connectivity, and high reliability features of 6G networks that allow solving one of the major challenges of machine learning: the ability of distributed agricultural apparatus, including IoT sensors, drones, and autonomous machinery, to collaboratively learn machine learning without exchanging raw data. This methodology preserves the privacy of data, leads to reduced communications overhead, and real-time decision-making capabilities in precision agriculture. The framework offered combines intelligent edge computing, blockchain enhanced security, and dynamic model combining approaches to process disparate sources of data and the changeable nature of agricultural settings. Some common applications are measuring the health of crops, predictive irrigation control, soil fertility, and detecting pests. The simulation findings and the case studies illustrate that 6G-FL framework can attain high levels of scalability, accuracy and very high efficiency in contrast to traditional centralized learning paradigms. This study indicates the possible applications of 6G and federated intelligence to deploy sustainable, resilient, and massive smart agriculture applications into food security in the future.

title: Machine Learning Algorithms used in Crop Yield Prediction for Precision Agriculture
abstract: Agriculture is a crucial sector that plays a vital role in producing food for human consumption. However, predicting crop yield accurately can be a challenging task due to various natural factors, such as soil quality, climate, rainfall, and resource availability. In the past, farmers relied on their expertise and judgment to determine crop yield, but their traditional methods have become less effective due to the unpredictable nature of these factors. To address this challenge, researchers have developed various algorithms and models for predicting crop yield based on different parameters, such as soil quality, climate, and image analysis. These algorithms can help farmers make informed decisions about when and where to grow their crops, leading to improved productivity and higher yields. Among these algorithms, neural networks are showing great promise as they can analyze vast amounts of data and identify patterns that may not be immediately apparent to human observers. By training neural networks on historical crop yield data, researchers can develop models that accurately predict crop yield based on a variety of factors. Ensuring accurate crop yield prediction is critical to ensuring food security and preventing famine, particularly in developing countries such as India. As technology continues to advance, we can expect even more advanced algorithms and models for predicting crop yield that will help farmers make better decisions and ultimately lead to increased productivity and better outcomes for agriculture.

title: Inter-Crop Management for Price Resilient Farming using Interactive Machine Learning & Decision Support System: A Farm-Safe Method
abstract: In a farming nation, agricultural planning is essential to economic growth and food security. However, a lack of information about farming activities in India is causing the farming sector to go through a challenging period. Most of the time, farmers are unaware of the best crops to plant based on the condition of their soil. As well as the composition of the soil. Inter-cropping has emerged as a promising agricultural practice to enhance productivity and resilience, particularly for small-scale farmers facing resource constraints and climate variability. The Farm-safe method determines the optimal crop for cultivation by considering several factors, including the weather forecast and the state of the soil. Utilizing the crop predictor can help reduce losses in the event of unfavorable circumstances. When ideal growth circumstances are possible, farmers can employ this technology to increase agricultural yield rates. In addition, the method forecasts agricultural prices as well as giving a proper land utilization plan for intercropping.

title: Musa Base - Mobile Application for Banana Farmers to Minimize the Challenges in Banana Production during the Pre-Harvest and Post-Harvest Period
abstract: This research paper presents an innovative solution to address the multifaceted challenges encountered by banana farmers in Sri Lanka, encompassing the entire spectrum of banana production from pre-harvest to post-harvest stages. The proposed system, titled "Musa-Base," is a user-friendly mobile application that seamlessly integrates cutting-edge technologies, including machine learning, IoT-based approaches, natural language processing, and image processing methodologies. This holistic approach aims to elevate the quality and productivity of banana cultivation. The Musa-Base system comprises several interlinked modules: crop yield prediction, disease identification through advanced image processing and interactive chatbot interactions, personalized recommendations for optimal watering and fertilizer strategies, and comprehensive guidance on best agronomic practices. The research rigorously employs a diverse range of algorithms, including deep learning models, for accurate crop yield prediction, rapid disease diagnosis, and finely tuned recommendation systems. The system empowers farmers with informed decision-making capabilities, enabling them to mitigate losses, efficiently allocate resources, and ultimately enhance banana production and product quality. The integration of images of banana plants, sensor data, and user input data forms the backbone of the data-driven research methodology that underpins the development of the Banana Mobile Application. The pivotal outcomes of this research include precise disease detection, reliable harvest forecasting, and the dynamic integration of a chatbot for timely assistance, all of which collectively contribute to superior banana crop management, heightened agricultural efficiency, and enhanced sustainability. This comprehensive solution caters to the needs of both smallholder farmers and commercial producers, representing a significant advancement in modernizing banana farming practices and ensuring food security.

title: Comprehensive Analysis of FUTCOM and NASDAQ Commodities for Gold using Machine Learning and Technical Analysis
abstract: This paper covers commodity stock market (FUTCOM and NASDAQ) data using machine learning and technical analysis. Commodity stock markets play a crucial role in global economies, affecting everything from raw material prices to consumer goods. Their inherent volatility and sensitivity to geopolitical and economic factors make them challenging to predict. Addressing the prime problem of price fluctuations, this research highlights the need for accurate forecasting models, where machine learning can significantly enhance decision-making and risk management. It includes data preprocessing, RNN model creation, future price prediction, descriptive stats, correlation analysis, volatility, trend analysis, seasonality, volume analysis, and Monte Carlo simulation. Using Pandas, NumPy, TensorFlow, and Plotly libraries, it provides insights into market trends and forecasting. Results are intended for market participants and decision-makers,

title: Crop Yield Prediction Based on Various Environmental Factors Using Machine Learning
abstract: The increasing impact of climate change and global warming highlights the urgent need for sustainable agriculture practices to ensure food security. This research focuses on utilizing machine learning techniques to accurately predict crop yield based on weather conditions. By analyzing historical weather data and crop yields, the proposed machine learning models provide valuable insights for farmers in selecting suitable crops for cultivation. This approach offers a more data-driven and reliable alternative to traditional methods that rely solely on farmers' experience and local knowledge. The study evaluates the performance of various machine learning algorithms, including Random Forest, XG Boost, and KNN. These models demonstrate exceptional accuracy in predicting crop yield, with values ranging from 92.12% to 97.56%. This research contributes to the advancement of sustainable agriculture by providing farmers with a powerful tool for optimizing crop selection and improving yields. By leveraging machine learning techniques, farmers can make informed decisions and mitigate the challenges posed by climate change.

title: GPU-Powered Crop Quality Forecasting: Integrating CUDA-YOLO Detection with RF-XGBoost Classification
abstract: Smart agriculture combines drones, artificial intelligence (AI), Internet of Things (IoT), and data analytics to solve major problems in the field, including increased food prices, water shortages, climate change, and labor shortages. IoT sensors can be used to track the health of crops in real-time, whereas edge computing can be used to make quick decisions on farms. The AI models can be used to predict diseases of plants, pest attacks, and even the optimal time to plant a particular plant, which will enhance the efficiency of resources and environmental sustainability. The given paper draws a comparison between deep learning and traditional machine learning in terms of crop quality prediction and suggests a fast and real-time CUDA-based hybrid model of RF-XGBoost and YOLO. The result of the experiments reveals that the suggested method has a precision of approximately 96 percent, which is higher than the accuracy of SVM (88 percent) and Decision Tree (91 percent) in precision, speed and scale and can support data-driven and sustainable precision agriculture.

title: Machine Learning Algorithms for Crop Yield Prediction in Real-Time Scenarios
abstract: The main pillar of the Indian Economy is Agriculture as it ensures food security and financial stability for all people in ancient days. However, due to the unnatural weather conditions, the production of yield crops has severely affected the income of farmers. This work helps early-stage farmers by guiding them through the process of sowing the right crops based on soil using the help of machine learning algorithms. The seeds are collected based on the soil parameters such as Nitrogen, phosphorous, potassium, temperature, and humidity. The system is trained using the Random Forest algorithm to suggest and help the farmers to achieve a successful harvest. A web-based application is also being developed which will allow users to get data about nutrients required for the crop. Experiments are conducted on the collected data samples from the web application and predict the crop yield with good accuracy of 91.2 % and in less response time.

title: Predictive Insights in Precision Agriculture: Leveraging Deep Learning for Crop Yield Estimation
abstract: The prediction of crop yield stands as a pivotal component within precision agriculture, aiding farmers and policymakers alike in making informed decisions to optimize resource allocation and ensure food security. We begin by presenting an in-depth discussion of the importance of crop yield prediction in the context of global food security, resource management, and economic sustainability. The core of this survey is a detailed examination of the various methodologies and techniques employed in crop yield prediction systems useful in precision agriculture. We categorize the methods used into traditional statistical models and neural networks, providing insights into their strengths and limitations. Additionally, we explore the utilization of remote sensing data such as weather information, soil characteristics, rainfall, pesticides used, and crop-specific factors in the prediction process. In conclusion, this comprehensive survey paper is a valuable resource for researchers, practitioners, and policymakers interested in crop yield prediction systems. It provides an understanding of the current landscape, the methodologies employed, and the challenges that need to be addressed. Moreover, it offers a roadmap for the future of crop yield prediction, underlining the innovation potential and continued improvement in the domain of agricultural sustainability.

title: Machine Learning Approaches for Wheat Yield Prediction Using Multiple Features: A Case Study on Indian State-Level Data
abstract: Accurate forecasting of wheat yields is essential for food security, agricultural planning, and sustainable resource management. Recent advancements in Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) enable modeling of complex interactions among climatic, soil, and environmental factors. This study utilizes a state-level Indian dataset spanning the period 1997-2022 to evaluate the performance of five supervised machine learning models for wheat yield prediction. Model performance was evaluated using the coefficient of determination R2value, adjusted R2value and the Root Mean Square Error (RMSE). The evaluated models include Linear Regression, Ridge Regression, Lasso Regression, Decision Tree, and Random Forest. Experimental results indicate that the Random Forest model (R2= 0.817, RMSE = 0.35) and Ridge Regression model (R2= 0.828, RMSE = 0.34) exhibit superior generalisation performance. The feature importance analysis identifies fertilizer application as the most influential factor, followed closely by rainfall and the cultivated area, consistent with established agronomic principles. The findings demonstrate the effectiveness of ensemble and regularized learning approaches as decision-support tools for precision agriculture across diverse agro-climatic regions of India.

title: Crop Yield Prediction: Leveraging Machine Learning for Sustainable Agriculture
abstract: : Accurate crop yield prediction is essential for ensuring food security and optimizing agricultural practices. Traditional methods often rely on historical data and expert knowledge, which may not always be sufficient. This research explores the application of machine learning techniques to predict crop yield based on various factors such as soil properties, weather conditions, and crop management practices. By analyzing historical agricultural data, this research study aims to develop robust predictive models. The research utilizes Random Forest, a abstract- powerful machine learning algorithm to extract patterns from the data and make accurate yield predictions. The results of this study can provide valuable insights to farmers, enabling them to make informed decisions about crop selection, resource allocation, and risk management. By integrating machine learning, this research contributes to the development of sustainable agriculture practices and improves food security.

title: FarmSense Pro: A Data-Driven Approach to Crop Yield and Price Estimation
abstract: The economic development and food security of every nation require farmers and policymakers to forecast future crop yields and market prices through systematic analysis of multiple data sets. The research project presents Farm Sense Pro as an advanced web-based platform which scientists can use to predict crop yields and market prices through the application of machine learning methods. The platform uses agricultural data and environmental data and market data to help farmers make better decisions about their crop production and sales activities. For example, when predicting crop production, several variables are considered, including soil type, amount and timing of rainfall, temperature and weather conditions, amount of fertilizer applied, irrigation methods, area of the country are farming, and time left until the crop is harvested. For predicting the selling price per crop, the platform will consider a demand index, supply index, seasonal variations in price, previous price at the market, temperature and amount of rain in a particular geographic area, and month. Recent machine learning algorithms, including Linear Regression, Decision Tree, Random Forest and XGBoost are used in developing predictive models in order to improve the accuracy of predicting crop production and selling price. The platform was developed using Python and Stream lit to create an interactive, user-friendly web-based dashboard that allows users to enter data, generate predictions and visualize predictions through charts and analytics. Additionally, the platform contains support materials such as insights about the market and seasonality outlooks on prices to help users understand the seasonal price swings of their crops.

title: A Novel Based Crop Prediction using Machine Learning and Internet of Things
abstract: Generally speaking, India's economy depends heavily on agriculture, which also contributes to food security by producing a certain proportion of household goods. In India, agriculture accounts for about 33% of the GDP and employs 62% of the population. India ranks second in the world for farming food production. The input of technology might enable the farmer to increase output. But today's unnatural climate changes are reducing food output and crop production, which will hurt farmers' economies by resulting in a low yield and also make them less adept at predicting future crops. This study employs machine learning, which is among the most cutting-edge techniques for crop production, to assist new producers by directing them in planting reasonable crops. Machine learning is primarily used to teach computers how to use information or experience to handle issues in the real world. In this research, we will concentrate on applying machine learning to address practical issues in agriculture.

title: Crop Prediction using Machine Learning
abstract: In general, agriculture is the backbone of India and also plays an important role in Indian economy by providing a certain percentage of domestic product to ensure the food security. But now-a-days, food production and prediction is getting depleted due to unnatural climatic changes, which will adversely affect the economy of farmers by getting a poor yield and also help the farmers to remain less familiar in forecasting the future crops. This research work helps the beginner farmer in such a way to guide them for sowing the reasonable crops by deploying machine learning, one of the advanced technologies in crop prediction. Naive Bayes, a supervised learning algorithm puts forth in the way to achieve it. The seed data of the crops are collected here, with the appropriate parameters like temperature, humidity and moisture content, which helps the crops to achieve a successful growth. In addition as the software, a mobile application for Android is being developed. The users are encouraged to enter parameters like temperature and their location will be taken automatically in this application in order to start the prediction process.

title: Micronutrient Classification in IoT Based Agriculture Using Machine Learning (ML) Algorithm
abstract: Agriculture appears to be the demographically most important economic area in India's socioeconomic structure. People are now unaware of crop cultivation's proper timing and location. As a result, they cause food insecurity since seasonal climatic settings dependent on agriculture practices are changing against essential assets such as air, water, and soil. As a result, Machine Learning (ML) techniques are the best option for agriculture and are being tested to predict agricultural growth. This paper proposed horticulture IoT monitoring sensor board to develop an IoT architecture in agriculture industry for monitoring the Micro and Macro Nutrients of Soil and analyze various soil parameters present in the Thiruvarur District in Tamil Nadu. The framework aids in generating right decisions based on data collected from IoT sensors and saved on the server before being evaluated using ML algorithms. The ML model is used to categorize the dataset based on the micro and macronutrient threshold values acquired from the National Food Security Mission (NFSM). The evaluation can be done by using various ML classification algorithm such as Naive Bayes (NB), Logistic Regression (LR), Random Tree (RT) and K-Nearest Neighborhood (KNN). The classification method is compared and evaluated through accuracy, Relative Absolute Error (RAE), Root Mean Square Error (RMSE), Root Relative Squared Error (RRSE), Mean Absolute Error (MAE). The KNN classifier attains lower MAE, RMSE and RRSE value of 0.2398, 0.3908, and 94.1845 and outperforms the other three classifier but RT algorithm attains lower RAE value of 66.24 than KNN.

title: Optimizing Agricultural Yields Using AI and Machine Learning
abstract: The paper explores the profound impact of AI and ML on sustainable farming practices and the optimization of agricultural production. The article highlights significant developments in data-driven decision-making for producers, such as autonomous systems, predictive analytics, and precision agriculture. Modern precision agriculture utilizes advanced technology to continuously monitor the health of crops, while predictive analytics leverages cutting-edge techniques like Support Vector Machines and regression models to forecast yields using historical data and present circumstances. Through the integration of AI, autonomous robots play a crucial role in minimizing chemical usage and labor costs by enabling precise pesticide application and effective weed removal. There are still lingering challenges related to data accessibility, scalability, quality, and adoption. Addressing these challenges requires the implementation of comprehensive training programs and enhanced data acquisition methods. It will empower farmers and ensure the successful integration of AI and ML in agriculture. Through the implementation of these innovations, the agriculture sector has the potential to see significant improvements in output, environmental impact, and food security.

title: Forecasting Crop Yields Using Machine Learning Techniques For Sustainable Farming
abstract: Crop production plays a crucial role in agriculture planning resource allocation and food security management with the advancement of technology and the availability of vast amounts of agriculture data, machine learning and statistical modelling techniques have emerged as powerful tools for predicting crop yields and identifying potential factors including crop growth. the data set utilized in crop production includes data such as whether data, soil quality is obtained through soil sampling algorithms commonly applied in crop production including Gaussian naive bayes this algorithm leverages the extracted features from the data set to build predictive models that estimate crop production for specific region and the period. Additionally, it highlights the significance of Accurate crop prediction in optimizing agriculture practices mitigating risks associated with climate change, and ensuring sustainable food production. furthermore, the discussion challenges data availability model complexity and interpretability along with the potential Avenue of further research to enhance the accuracy and applicability of the crop production model.

title: Monthly Rainfall Analysis in Southern Parts of India Using Machine Learning and Ensemble Methods
abstract: Rainfall analysis has a vital function for raising awareness of the dangers of excessive rainfall and for boosting the travel and tourism sector, agriculture, and food security in southern India. Because rainfall is influenced by many different causes, it is challenging to forecast. In this research work, four different machine learning techniques are used: Naïve Bayes, KNN, SVM, and LR, and the accuracy for each model is determined. To improve the accuracy of each model, three different ensemble learning techniques are employed: Stacking, Bagging, and Voting Classifier, to analyze the rainfall data in southern parts of India. Given that Bagging attains the maximum accuracy of 99.5%, it is proposed that Bagging is the best model. The study shows that the ensemble model can enhance prediction quality and boost forecasting accuracy in meteorological applications by replacing traditional forecasting instruments.

title: Climate-Aware Agricultural Land Suitability Prediction using Machine Learning and Deep Learning Ensembles
abstract: Food security is increasingly threatened by the impacts of climate change, which alter agricultural land suitability and irrigation requirements. This study investigates the influence of climatic variability on cropland suitability across Eurasia using interpretable machine learning techniques. A single integrated dataset was created by combining ERA5 climate reanalysis data (2000-2010) with GFSAD1km cropland classification labels. This unified dataset provided both climatic predictors and cropland categories for model training and evaluation. The data were preprocessed through spatial alignment, temporal averaging, and reclassification into four categories-major irrigation, minor irrigation, rainfed, and non-cropland. A range of classical and deep learning algorithms, including Random Forest, SVM, Gradient Boosted Trees, CNN, Bi-LSTM, and GRU, were trained to classify land suitability. To enhance robustness, a voting ensemble was developed by combining the strongest models. Model performance was assessed using accuracy, precision, recall, F1score, and average precision, while permutation feature importance was applied for interpretability. The results demonstrated that deep learning approaches, particularly BiLSTM and CNN, achieved superior performance compared to traditional ML models, with the ensemble further improving overall predictive accuracy. Analysis of feature importance indicated that precipitation and temperature-related variables were the most significant predictors of land suitability. The findings highlight critical shifts in cropland viability, suggesting potential northward expansion of suitable areas and increasing pressure on irrigation-dependent regions. These insights provide a valuable foundation for policymakers to design sustainable agricultural strategies in response to climate variability.

title: Leveraging machine learning models for food security and crisis management in Algeria
abstract: The food sector in Algeria and many countries around the world faces multiple challenges, ranging from environmental pollution and climate change to fluctuations in production and distribution processes, increasing the complexities of maintaining food safety and mitigating health and environmental risks. This paper addressed analysis and prediction of food insecurity risks through the development of predictive models. Various models were reviewed and applied to real market data, focusing on predicting product prices and assessing food safety risks. The results showed that Polynomial Regression and Decision Tree models were the most efficient in accurately predicting and classifying the products, confirming their effectiveness in food safety applications. These findings contribute to providing accurate recommendations and making informed decisions to enhance food safety and better crisis management in the future.

title: Identifying Risk Factors and Predicting Food Security Status using Supervised Machine Learning Techniques
abstract: In 2018, more than 821 million undernourished people were registered all over the world. Of these, 239 million were in Sub-Saharan Africa. The numbers are particularly high in Ethiopia, Kenya, Somalia, and South Sudan. The determinant factors of food insecurity in Ethiopia are multidimensional encompassing climate change, civil conflicts, natural disasters, and social norms. This study, hence, aims to identify risk factors and predict food security status at household level in North West Ethiopia using supervised machine learning techniques. To this end, a dataset was gathered from the Dabat Health and Demographic Surveillance and statistically interesting risk factors were identified using logistics regression at a threshold level of p<0.05. Three experiments were also conducted using random forest, support vector machine and decision tree (C4.5) to predict food security status at household level and the performance of each model was evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, and f1- measure. As a result, the C4.5 algorithm is selected as the best appropriate supervised machine learning algorithm with 97.23% of recall, 91.58% of accuracy, 80.97% of f1-measure, and 69.38% of precision. Family size, level of education, age of the household head, number and types of communication media, numbers of livestock, cultivated land size, access to credit, and access to irrigation are some of the risk factors of food security.

title: Retracted: Optimization of Crop Yield Using Machine Learning
abstract: The economic growth and food security of an agriculture-based nation are significantly influenced by agricultural planning. The choice of crop(s) is a crucial issue for agricultural planning. It is based on a variety of factors, including market and production growth rates as well as governmental regulations. For agricultural planning utilizing information approaches or system learning methodologies, several studies explored crop yield price forecast, weather prediction, soil category and crop type. The choosing of crop becomes challenging if there are several options for planting a crop at once with limited land resources. In order to overcome crop selection challenges and maximize net crop yield charges over the course of a season, K-mean algorithm is applied on the dataset to find the results as the accuracy comes out to be as 97%.

title: Forecasting the Geopolitical Impact among Russia and Ukraine on Commodity Export Prices: An AI-Based Analysis
abstract: The study Leverages machine learning techniques to understand the complex relationship between the Russia-Ukraine conflict and its impact on commodity export prices for the two countries. While conventional economic indicators like global demand and currency exchange rates are essential, they fall short in capturing the nuances introduced by geopolitical tensions. Both Ukraine and Russia are significant players in the global commodities market, specializing in agricultural exports and natural resources, respectively. Using a dataset spanning from 1992 to 2022 and incorporating key economic variables, the study introduces a conflict-specific dummy variable to account for periods of heightened geopolitical stress. Our AI-based model reveals that the ongoing conflict has a substantial impact on commodity export prices in both nations: leading to decreased prices in Ukraine due to disrupted commerce, and increased volatility in Russia's markets The study underscores the vital role of geopolitical factors in distorting traditional economic indicators and offers a more robust framework for forecasting in the face of conflicts. Its findings are crucial for stakeholders, from policymakers to investors, and call for diplomatic efforts to mitigate further economic impact.

title: AI in Agriculture: Yield Optimization and Food Security
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is remarkably automating the agricultural methods. In this process, AI is helping to optimize yield, and improving food security in a world with growing population and environmental concern(s). AI technology integration in agriculture is the focus of this paper which includes predictive analytics, machine learning and IoT. These applications led to precision farming and resource management which lead to efficient use of resources. The discussion on the benefits of AI in increasing productivity and sustainability is based on the summarization of the latest literature and empirical studies. Yet, these technologies bring along their own issues such as initial capital investment to implement the systems in emergence economies as well as the need for the rapid upgrading of the infrastructure and human capital. This research demonstrates that AI has the potential to change agriculture radically, while at the same time acknowledging the pending problems that hinder full-fledged implementation.

title: IoT and Machine Learning Framework for Precision Agri-Business and Smart Crop Forecasting
abstract: The convergence of Internet of Things (IoT) and Machine Learning (ML) paradigms is poised to revolutionize agri-business by transitioning from traditional practices to data-driven, intelligent farming. This paper proposes a novel integrated framework that leverages a distributed sensor network for real-time, in-situ monitoring of critical agronomic parameters, including soil moisture, nutrient levels, microclimate, and crop health. The voluminous, multi-modal data streams generated by these IoT devices are processed and fed into a predictive ML model, architected for robust crop yield forecasting. The model employs ensemble learning techniques to analyze historical and real-time data, accounting for spatial and temporal variability to generate accurate, high-resolution predictions. The proposed framework is designed to empower stakeholders with actionable intelligence for precise resource allocation, optimized irrigation and fertilization, early disease detection, and informed market decisions. By enhancing operational efficiency, mitigating risks, and maximizing profitability, this IoT and ML synergy establishes a new benchmark for sustainable and economically viable precision agri-business, ultimately contributing to global food security.

title: Can Pixel-Based Approach Achieve Similar Performance to Area-Based Approach in Crop Yield Forecasting Using Sentinel-2 Imagery and Deep Neural Networks? A Probabilistic Analysis
abstract: A key solution to addressing food security challenges is the accurate forecasting of crop yields. Satellite imagery and historical remote sensing data play a crucial role in forecasting agricultural yields, particularly at the scale of individual fields. In the context of a small field, selecting between a pixel-based or area-based approach is essential, especially with deep learning (DL) models where having too little data can pose problems and acquiring more data can be difficult and challenging. In this study, we introduce two frameworks for forecasting corn yield: one using a pixel-based method and the other an area-based strategy, both utilizing Sentinel-2 imagery from a public image yield dataset and leveraging deep neural networks. The two methods were compared using key statistical metrics and also probabilistic techniques and analyses including error histogram of the strategies and their cumulative distribution function (CDF) plots considering the shapes of the lines, and the general distribution of the differences. Our findings underscored nuanced distinctions in the predictive capabilities, highlighting that the area-based model leaned towards greater accuracy in predictions, and the pixel-based approach emerged as a feasible substitute, delivering comparable performance despite slightly larger discrepancies.

title: Deep Learning for Predicting Food Commodity Prices in Traditional Markets
abstract: Banyumas is one region with a history of fluctuating food prices, especially the price of shallots and chicken meat. Several factors affect fluctuating food prices, such as harvests, seasons, market demand, and so on. Farmers or ranchers often experience losses in selling crops and livestock products. This phenomenon occurs due to intermediaries monopolizing prices, and farmers need more knowledge about market prices, so traditional transactions are detrimental. Price forecasting can be one of the practical solutions to help farmers and ranchers understand the prices of their crops and livestock yields. Therefore, Deep Learning is applied to the experience of food commodities with LSTM and GRU. In this study, the LSTM model achieved the highest performance by producing an MSE value of 0.00035, while the GRU model produced an MSE value of 0.00036. LSTM models perform better with layer LSTM, epoch 100, batch size 64, optimization Adam, and neuron 128.

title: AGRI-SMART HUB: A Multilingual Integrated Platform for Comprehensive Farming Solutions and Support
abstract: This research work proposes an integrated web platform that uses machine learning and web development to solve pressing challenges in agriculture. While the world population increases exponentially and the land for farming is constant, deforestation and climate change lower crop yields, posing a threat to food security. For a growing population's demand, we need to shift from conventional farming to a technological approach. Nowadays everybody has access to phones and the internet. Our website aims to strengthen farmers by providing them with new resources and government schemes for enhanced productivity and sustainability. This study integrates the multiple machine learning models that fulfill the farmers' needs. These include a crop recommendation system that uses parameters such as rainfall, humidity, soil pH, and moisture to suggest suitable crops. our crop yield prediction model that analyzes rainfall and NPK (nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium) levels to forecast yields; and a transfer learning-based CNN model that takes the leaf as input and detects the disease in the early stage. Moreover, we use Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to assist farmers so that they can use the government's issues pdf regarding agriculture and ask questions based on that pdf, which they did not understand in their regional language. This study highlights the potential of technology-based solutions in revolutionizing agriculture and responding to the global issue of food security in an increasingly dynamic world.

title: 6G-Enabled Architecture for Smart Farming: Machine Learning Driven Yield Forecasting and Decision Support
abstract: The new enhancement of wireless communication and smart systems is transforming traditional farming to make it highly interrelation-based and data oriented. This paper sets forth a proposal of the integration of sixth-generation (6G) networks, machine learning (ML), and drone-based image processing to build a next-generation architectural structure of smart agriculture and yield forecasting. The high-resolution crop images can be captured in real time using the capabilities of 6G such as the ultra-low latency, enormous connectivity and enormous bandwidth of 6G technology by using drones with multispectral and hyperspectral cameras. These images are processed with advanced ML algorithms to deliver valuable agronomic information such as plant health, nutrient status, disease and growth trend development. By combining environmental information streams and visual analytics, the proposed system will empower farmers with the knowledge of effective decisions regarding resource management and pests and irrigation timing by offering them helpful information on when and where to deploy the required resources. Such challenges as the scalability of the data, the model generalization to different kinds of crops, and the fusion with the Internet of Things (IoT)-enabled farm structures, are also addressed in the research. According to the initial simulations of 5G vs 6G, the precision of predictions and efficiency of decisions are highly enhanced in comparison with the current methods of precision agriculture. The piece of work advances sustainability and better food security and the achievement of smart, resilient farming ecosystems in 6G.

title: Deep Learning Based Vegetable Price Forecasting for Nepalese Markets: An STL Attention LSTM Approach
abstract: Agricultural price volatility poses significant challenges to food security in developing economies. This paper proposes a hybrid deep learning architecture that combines Seasonal-Trend decomposition using local Estimated Scatterplot Smoothing (STL) with attention-enhanced Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks for daily vegetable price forecasting. The STL component explicitly decomposes price series into interpretable trend, seasonal, and residual patterns, while the attention mechanism automatically identifies temporally important observations.
