The model integrates 11.5 years of historical price data from Kalimati market with meteorological variables and cultural event indicators. Evaluation on five major vegetables demonstrates strong predictive capability with mean coefficient of determination of 0.833 and mean absolute percentage error of 15.67%. Analysis of the attention weights further demonstrated that the vegetable price forecasts made by the LSTM and Attention model rely heavily upon data from vegetables traded on the market approximately 18-22 days prior to the forecast day, which confirms that the LSTM+Attention model is best suited to detect relatively short-term trends in the agricultural market.

title: Machine Learning-Based Early Warning System for Food Security Threats in Transitional Bioeconomies
abstract: This paper presents a machine learning-based early warning system designed to anticipate food security threats in transitional bioeconomies. The system integrates agro-climatic, market, logistical, and socio-political variables into a composite Food Vulnerability Index (FVI), constructed using open-access quarterly data from 2010 to 2023 for Ukraine, Moldova, and Serbia at the Nomenclature of Territorial Units for Statistics Level 2 (NUTS-2) scale. The modeling framework employs an ensemble of CatBoost, Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis within a stratified spatiotemporal structure to ensure both high predictive accuracy and interpretability. Empirical validation for 20222023 yields strong performance (Mean Absolute Error, MAE $=0.057$), with consistently elevated risks observed in the second quarter due to seasonal climate anomalies. Forecast simulations for 2024-2025 indicate that disruptions to export routes - such as the Black Sea “Green Grain Corridor” could increase FVI values by more than 0.1 in vulnerable regions. SHAP analysis identifies a decline in the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI), grain price volatility, and logistics constraints as dominant drivers. Risk projections are visualized through geospatial heatmaps to support regionally targeted interventions. The system is designed for integration into digital monitoring platforms with open application programming interfaces (APIs) to assist governmental and donor decision-making. Future work will focus on scaling the model to Central and Southeastern Europe, incorporating Shared Socioeconomic Pathways and Representative Concentration Pathways (SSP/RCP) climate scenarios to enhance long-term adaptability. Further research is needed to address data uncertainty, temporal granularity, and regional disparities in information availability.

title: Yield Prediction of Rabi Crops in India Using XGBoost Regressor
abstract: Agriculture is at the heart of India's economy, with two key cropping seasons: Kharif, grown in the summer, and Rabi, grown in the winter. Rabi crops like wheat, gram, and mustard are cultivated from October to April, particularly in Northwest India. Accurately forecasting the yield of these crops is vital for efficient planning, resource management, and ensuring food security, especially given the unpredictability of climate patterns. In this study, we predict yield based on rainfall and various climatic factors which impact Rabi crop. Using data from different states on crop production and rainfall, we built predictive models to estimate yields. After processing and refining the data, we utilized advanced machine learning methods like Random Forest, XGBoost, and LightGBM to assess how rainfall affects crop performance. Additionally, we improved the accuracy of the Random Forest model through hyperparameter tuning. The models' accuracy was evaluated using metrics like Mean Squared Error (MSE) and R-squared (R2), with cross-validation ensuring consistent results. Of the models tested, Random Forest, XGBoost, and LightGBM performed best, with the latter two offering the most precise predictions. The results show that XGBoost achieved the best accuracy with a maximum of 96% and after hyperparameter tuning showed a better result of 97%. In this paper we highlight how integrating cutting-edge machine learning algorithms can improve the precision of crop yield forecasts, aiding agricultural planning and helping to secure food supplies for the future.

title: AgriVision: Deep Learning-Based Plant Disease with Daily Progress Tracking and Severity Classification
abstract: Agriculture remains the foundation of food security, while crop diseases persist as a threat to yield and farmer incomes globally. Early diagnosis and timely action are essential, but conventional manual surveys are slow, inconsistent, and impractical for great farmlands. The available deep learning-based applications show robust disease detection capabilities; however, they offer static, one-time accuracy without information on disease severity, progression, or recovery. The new system presents a multi-featured deep learning architecture that combines Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) for disease classification with a tracking of progression and predictive feedback module. Through the examination of sequential symptom and leaf image sequences, the system tracks the health of plants over time and offers actionable advice, specifying whether the health of the plants is recovering, stable, or declining. The architecture provides for adaptability, scalability, and real-time prediction, increasing the accuracy and explainability of the evaluation of plant health. By integrating classification with predictive analytics, the study adds to the development of intelligent, sustainable, and data-driven agricultural applications.

title: Interpretable AI Enabled Solutions for Crop Selections, Yield Estimation and Rainfall Analysis in Precision Agriculture
abstract: The rapid growth of the world's population and the growing need for food security have made modern farming very difficult. Traditional farming methods often don't work well with changes in the environment, low yields and changes in rainfall. In order to solve these limitations this study focuses on the creation of usable artificial intelligence driven solutions for crop selection, yield prediction and rainfall analysis thus enabling precision agriculture. The goal is to give farmers accurate and simple data-driven insights so that they can make important decisions about crop management that are both economical and clear. The suggested method combines a number of machine learning and deep learning models such as Decision Tree, Random Forest, AdaBoost, XGBoost, Support Vector Machine, Gradient Boosting Machine, k-Nearest Neighbors, Artificial Neural Network, Recurrent Neural Network, Long Short-Term Memory and Convolutional Neural Network. To make predictions easier and build trust among those involved clear techniques are used. The framework's test outcomes show that it has a very high prediction accuracy of 98.9% which makes agricultural forecasting much more accurate. The study finds that the combination of advanced algorithms and understanding not only improves predictive performance but also makes it possible for farming practices that are both smart and economical and can adjust to future agricultural needs.

title: Design of an Improved Model Using Hyperspectral Imaging, Data Fusion, and Transformer-Based Deep Learning for Crop Disease Identification Operations
abstract: Accurate and timely diagnosis of crop diseases is crucial for food security and agricultural sustainability. Current methods lack accuracy, interpretability, data integration, and advanced imaging techniques. The current research aims to address such issues by proposing a broad-perspective approach that brings into play hyperspectral imaging in tandem with 3D reconstruction, multimodal data integration, advanced machine learning models, and finally, trickled-down with XAI techniques. Up to now, approaches in the detection of crop diseases have been basically dependent on RGB imaging information and single-information sources that are incapable of accounting for interactions amidst the variety of factors affecting crop health. These methods have poor spatial and spectral analysis; thus, leading to limited accuracy and also offering little elucidation on the implication of the models. Overcoming these limitations, we employed a hyperspectral imaging approach with the 3D reconstruction for achieving fine spectral and spatial quantification of the crops. Through this approach, accuracy in disease detection was improved from 85% to 92%, and this approach drives a holistic view of the crops. Through data fusion, hyperspectral images, soil health parameters, and weather data were integrated. Their integration significantly improved the predictive accuracy—all the way up to 89% from 78% overall accuracy. We also developed an explainable Transformer-based deep learning model with in-built attention mechanisms and Grad-CAM for explainability. Such an advanced model architecture allowed draft feature extraction and provided visual explanations on the decisions made by the model, increasing classification accuracy from 88% to 94% and interpretability by 70%. A combination of hyperspectral imaging, data fusion, and advanced machine learning with XAI improves the model's accuracy and its robustness and therefore improves the latter's transparency in the decision-making process.

title: A Comparative Analysis of Hybrid Approach for Rice Production Forecasting
abstract: Accurate forecasting of rice production is essential for ensuring food security, stabilizing prices, and guiding agricultural policy decisions. This study develops a hybrid forecasting model by combining linear time series models (Linear Trend and Error, Trend, Seasonal (ETS)) with Neural Network Autoregression (NNAR). Using annual rice production data from East Kalimantan Province, Indonesia (1995–2023), the model's accuracy was evaluated using the Symmetric Mean Absolute Percentage Error (SMAPE). The results show that hybrid models consistently outperform their individual components, with the ETS-NNAR model achieving the highest accuracy. Among individual models, the ETS model demonstrated better performance than the Linear Trend model, suggesting a correlation between the accuracy of the individual model and its hybrid counterpart. These findings imply that improving the baseline model's accuracy could further enhance the hybrid model's performance. Future research should consider integrating alternative neural network architectures, such as deep learning and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, and other machine learning techniques into hybrid frameworks to further improve rice production forecasting.

title: Advanced Predictive Analytics for Agricultural Weather Forecasting Using Machine Learning
abstract: Agriculture faces growing challenges due to the impacts of climate change, which affect crop yields and farm management practices. Accurate weather forecasting has become essential for farmers to mitigate risks and optimize agricultural decisions. This study proposes the use of a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network to predict weather conditions based on time-series data from BMKG, focusing on parameters such as temperature, humidity, rainfall, and wind. The research involves optimizing key hyperparameters, including the number of hidden layers, neurons per layer, learning rate, batch size, and epochs, to enhance the model's predictive accuracy. After systematic tuning, the model was able to achieve Mean Squared Error (MSE) values in the range of 0–1 for most weather parameters. However, parameters related to rainfall and wind direction resulted in higher MSE values, indicating the need for further refinement. These findings suggest that future work should explore integrating additional data sources and hybrid models to improve predictions. The LSTM model developed in this study provides farmers with actionable insights, enabling them to make more informed decisions regarding planting, irrigation, and harvesting. The integration of machine learning into agricultural practices offers a significant advancement in precision farming, contributing to sustainable agricultural development and food security. By leveraging advanced predictive analytics, this study underscores the potential of data-driven approaches in transforming traditional farming practices to better adapt to the challenges posed by climate change.

title: Convex-hull & DBSCAN clustering to predict future weather
abstract: Machine learning methods are increasingly being used in conjunction with conventional meteorological observations in the synoptic analysis and conventional weather forecast to extract information of relevance for agriculture and food security of the human society in India. Density based clustering approach is incrementally used to predict the future weather conditions in this paper. One famous preprocessing approach, known as Convex-Hull is also used before fed the pollutant data into the clustering algorithm. This Convex-Hull method is strictly used to convert unstructured data into its corresponding structured form. These structured data is efficiently and effectively used by the DBSCAN clustering algorithm to form resultant clusters for weather derivatives. This forecasting database is totally based on the weather of Kolkata city in west Bengal and this forecasting methodology is developed to mitigating the impacts of air pollutions and launch focused modeling computations for prediction and forecasts of weather events. Here accuracy of this approach is also measured.

title: Smart Agriculture Prediction System for Vegetables Grown in Sri Lanka
abstract: Agriculture planning plays a dominant role in the economic growth and food security of agriculture-based countries such as Sri Lanka. Even though agriculture plays a vital role, there are still several major complications to be addressed. Some of the major complications are lack of knowledge about yield and price resulting in the farmers selecting crops based on experience. Machine learning has a great potential to solve these complications. To this end, this paper proposes a novel system comprises of a mobile application, SMS (Short Message Service), and API (Application Programming Interface) with yield prediction, price prediction, and crop optimization. Several machine learning algorithms were used for yield and price predictions while a generic algorithm was used to optimize crops. The yield was predicted considering the environmental factors while the price was predicted considering supply and demand, import and export, and seasonal effect. To select the best suitable crops to cultivate, the output of yield and price prediction have been used. Yield prediction has been implemented using elastic net, ridge, and multilinear regression. R2 of yield prediction is varied from 0.74 to 0.89 while RMSE value is between 15.69 and 35.05. Price prediction has been implemented using the algorithms of Gradient Boosting Tree, Random Forest, Facebook Prophet, and R2 is varied from 0.72 to 0.92 while RMSE value is between 26.81 and 140.72. Crop optimization has been implemented using the genetic algorithm.

title: Assimilating seasonality information derived from satellite data time series in crop modelling for rice yield estimation
abstract: The agricultural sector is facing important global challenges due to the pressure of food demand, increased price-competition produced by market globalization and food price volatility (G20 Agriculture Action Plan), and the necessity of more environmentally and economically sustainable farming. Earth Observation (EO) systems can significantly contribute to these topics by providing reliable real time information on crop distribution, status and seasonal dynamics. ERMES FP7 project aims to create added-value information for the rice agro-sector by integrating EO-products in crop models. Time series of moderate resolution satellite data are analyzed exploiting the PhenoRice algorithm to retrieve seasonal occurrence of agro-practices and phenological stages. Eleven years (2003-2013) of rice seasonal metrics were derived and used in WARM crop model to set up a crop forecasting systems, with the aim to provide crop yield estimates for regional authorities. Preliminary test conducted in Italy on indica rice ecotype demonstrated that the system can provide rice yield estimates explaining up to 90% of interannual variability.

title: 3D Fully Convolutional Neural Networks with Intersection over Union Loss for Crop Mapping from Multi-Temporal Satellite Images
abstract: Information on cultivated crops is relevant for a large number of food security studies. Different scientific efforts are dedicated to generate this information from remote sensing images by means of machine learning methods. Unfortunately, these methods do not take account of the spatial-temporal relationships inherent in remote sensing images. In our paper, we explore the capability of a 3D Fully Convolutional Neural Network (FCN) to map crop types from multi-temporal images. In addition, we propose the Intersection Over Union (IOU) loss function for increasing the overlap between the predicted classes and ground reference data. The proposed method was applied to identify soybean and corn from a study area situated in the US corn belt using multi-temporal Landsat images. The study shows that our method outperforms related methods, obtaining a Kappa coefficient of 91.8%. We conclude that using the IOU loss function provides a superior choice to learn individual crop types.

title: A Review Of Soil Organic Carbon (SOC) Prediction Techniques In Agricultural Lands Using Remote Sensing
abstract: The geological, ecological, and biological ecosystems of the planet have changed because of the global climate crisis, and this poses a serious threat to humanity as well as the conservation of agricultural productivity and food security. The European Commission outlined the continent's objective to become climate neutral by 2050 with zero net Greenhouse Gas (GHG) emissions. Soil organic carbon (SOC) is closely related to soil quality and has a significant impact on how soil and plants interact. SOC monitoring gives a unique role in agricultural sustainability thus precise prediction and monitoring of SOC is essential. Remote Sensing (RS) evolution, big data accessibility and Deep Learning (DL) architectures present enormous potential for extensive SOC monitoring. Several RS applications (e.g., Sentinels, MODIS, Landsat etc.) along with machine learning and DL methodologies (e.g., RF, ANN, CNN etc.) used in literature for SOC prediction. The current review paper emphasizes on the latest RS approaches used for SOC monitoring.

title: Early-Season Crop Classification Utilizing Time Series Based Deep Learning with Multi-Sensor Remote Sensing Data
abstract: Early-season crop type classification provides crucial information for monitoring in-season crop growth and predicting crop diseases, supporting global food security. In remote sensing practices for agriculture, it is technically challenging to perform early-season prediction mainly due to factors such as significant soil interference to crops on the ground and limited availability of remote sensing data. In this work, we propose a time series based machine/deep learning approach which is able to utilize all useful features of satellite images captured by multiple sensors (RCM, Sentinel-1, and Sentinel-2) in the early season. The algorithm is implemented iteratively on data sequences such that when a new satellite image becomes available, new features will be appended to existing time series data, thus providing a more accurate prediction map in updated regions. In the study, four (4) machine/deep learning algorithms, including XGBoost, CNN, and LSTM, are evaluated for their performance in terms of prediction accuracy and computational complexity. The proposed approach is tested in three study areas in the Canadian Prairie provinces in the 2021 season. Crop type mapping results are obtained from the available early-season images from June 10 to June 30, 2021, with extended results to July 31, 2021. The validation results on independent crop survey data show that the proposed algorithms can achieve crop type classification accuracy around 85% at the end of June and above 90% at the end of July.

title: Rice Yield Monitoring Using Satellite Data and AI for Food Security and Sustainable Landscapes in Myanmar
abstract: Rice production in Myanmar is severely affected by the uncertain weather changes and political unrest especially due to the conflicts of coup after February 2021. Although recent improvements in satellite remote sensing have helped national to field-scale yield estimation and forecasting, the challenges through quality of reference data questions the quality of forecasts and estimation. In Myanmar, agricultural production data is publicly available at regional scale (equivalent to province level in USA) from 2012 to 2020. The consistent, timely and granular information on yield estimates at lower to higher admin unit level is crucial need to support sustainability of livelihood. In support to these efforts to improve food insecurity analysis and climate resilient livelihood formation, SERVIR – a joint USAID and NASA initiative – has implemented rice yield model using machine learning and satellite data to guide the decision makers in the region. This study used time-series (2012-2023) information on satellite derived vegetation indices, weather variability, topography and water use to predict the rice yield at regional to field scale using artificial neural network, random forest and boosted decision tree based artificial intelligence (AI) modeling. The model was tested spatially as well as temporally and overall average R2observed varied from 0.6 to 0.7. The presented rice yield model in this study provides carefully evaluated rice yield estimations at regional to field-scale across Myanmar rice-growing region. The consistent rice estimates from this study will help decision makers in the region. This study is the first to model rice yield at this high-resolution with locally tuned information. The model and algorithm developed in this study have the potential of operational use for further needs.

title: Soil Total Nitrogen Spectral Inversion Based on the DANN Model
abstract: Soil degradation threatens agricultural sustainability and food security. This study explores the effects of spectral preprocessing methods and machine learning models on predicting soil total nitrogen using the LUCAS2009 dataset. Preprocessing techniques, including first derivative (FD) and detrending (DT), enhanced spectral sensitivity. Machine learning models such as partial least squares regression (PLSR), support vector machines (SVM), random forest (RF), and a novel Density-Aware Neural Network (DANN) were evaluated. DANN achieved the best performance on FD data, with R2= 0.872, RMSE = 1.362, and RPD = 2.795. These findings provide insights into optimizing soil spectral analysis for precision agriculture.

title: A Spatial Hybrid Model for Crop Yield Prediction in Western Australia
abstract: Accurate crop yield estimation is crucial for ensuring food security and policy making; however, traditional methods are labor-intensive, and machine learning models often struggle to capture the complex interactions between soil, weather, and temporal data. To address these challenges, this paper first introduces a comprehensive resource—named the WA Paddock Dataset—comprising soil, climate, and satellite data for approximately 450,000 paddocks across Western Australia (WA) over a three-year period. This dataset is designed to enable high-resolution and large-scale modeling and supports other diverse research applications. Building on this resource, we present a novel hybrid regression model for predicting paddock-level crop yield that integrates MAMBA blocks, Transformer attention mechanisms, and Slot Attention to effectively capture spatial and temporal intricacies. This architecture effectively captures spatial and temporal complexities by leveraging diverse geospatial data, including soil properties, weather patterns, and Sentinel-2 imagery, to enhance predictive accuracy. Evaluation against classical machine learning models and ResNet50 demonstrates that our hybrid model significantly improves accuracy while achieving faster inference speeds compared to ResNet50 and some traditional approaches. These results establish the proposed method as a robust and efficient solution for precision agriculture and guiding impactful policy development at regional scale. Our code and relevant dataset will be made publicly available through GitHub repository.

title: Environment-Based Oil Palm Yield Prediction Using K-Nearest Neighbour Regression
abstract: Oil palm is a profitable tree crop, producing two types of oil from fresh fruit bunch (FFB). Oil palm yield prediction is required for import/ export, global food security, and field management. However, complex variations in oil palm yield on account of weather and soil conditions complicate the predictability. Supervised machine learning models can learn nonlinear patterns from complex agrometeorological data. However, environment-based predictive analysis of oil palm yield with machine learning methods is not widely explored. Therefore, this work presents the application of a non-parametric regression algorithm k-nearest neighbor (KNN) for oil palm yield prediction using weather and soil data. This work utilized 35 years of yield, soil, and weather records from Pahang state Malaysia. Data visualization during preprocessing assessment led to an in-depth understanding of environmental impacts on yield patterns. After model selection and training, the statistical evaluation using six different metrics along with an examination of the model's learning process was performed. Results suggested that a substantial amount of data from multiple sources allows reliable forecasts with machine learning models. It is concluded that machine learning is a great potential tool for oil palm yield prediction as an essential part of precision agriculture.

title: Multispectral Deep Learning for Crop Health Monitoring and Sustainable Food Security Planning
abstract: The growing pressure on the world agricultural systems due to population increase and climatic changes requires a paradigm shift to precision agriculture, which is data-oriented. The study paper examines how to combine the multispectral imaging and the deep learning constructions to ensure effective crop health monitoring and proactive food security plans. Multi spectral data is a vital non-invasive indicator of plant physiological conditions and conditions since it records reflectance signatures outside the visible range that reflect biotic and abiotic stresses even before such effects are visibly experienced. We examine the effectiveness of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and vision transformers (ViTs) in applying spectral-spatial features to segment and classify them to positively identify diseases, nutrient deficiencies, and water stress of different crop types and environments. The suggested framework will help to shift the reactive to the predictive model of farming because the early and targeted intervention will be possible, which will result in the efficient utilization of resources and the reduction of the loss of yields. The solution offers a scalable solution to decision-makers to plan on how to provide resilient and sustainable food security approaches to protect against current global challenges in food security by synthesizing high-resolution geospatial crop health data with predictive analytics to model yield projections, vulnerability assessments of each region, and formulate a way to create sustainable food security policies, ultimately resulting in assurance of global food sovereignty.

title: Graph Neural Networks for Smarter Plant Disease Diagnosis and Classification
abstract: Agriculture is the backbone of any country like India, where this large population rests highly on farming. The data-driven technologies, the deep learning techniques, and Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have been established as very powerful tools for improvement in agricultural productivity. This paper presents an advanced GNN-based model for plant disease detection and classification. The proposed method uses a dataset of plant images containing leaves to detect and predict apple scab, cercospora leaf spot, late blight, and powdery mildew. Instead of the traditional CNNs and wavelet transformations, GNNs are applied in this study in order to model the spatial relationships between diseased and healthy regions in the plant leaves. These images are then represented as graphs with nodes as representations of the leaf's various parts and edges for their structural associations. GNN-based model learning features from graph-structured data improves disease classification accuracy without degradation in noise and lowquality inputs. Results show that the integration of GNN with plant disease prediction provides a scalable, efficient, and intelligent approach for real-time disease detection. This method will help farmers and agricultural experts diagnose diseases early on, which may lead to timely interventions, reduced crop losses, and improved food security.

title: Satellite Images and Deep Learning Tools for Crop Yield Prediction and Price Forecasting
abstract: The ability to predict crop yield is vital for food security worldwide and forecasting crop prices can help farmers avoid price crash. In this work, an investigation of using satellite images and deep learning models to predict crop yields as well as forecasting farmers' prices is conducted. For tractability, dimensionality reduction is achieved by converting the images to histograms representing the pixel frequency. The models tested are LSTM, CNN, CNN-LSTM, CNN-LSTM ensemble as well as a Gaussian Process added to each for enhanced performance. It is found that the proposed ensemble of CNN-LSTMs is the best in predicting the yearly soybean yields in addition to forecasting the daily strawberry yields and prices. It outperforms models suggested in the literature with an improvement of 31% in terms of average Root Mean Square Error (RMSE).

title: Data Analytics in Farming: Rice price prediction in Andhra Pradesh
abstract: The variances regarding prices of horticultural commodities adversely affect the nations GDP. The ranchers are genuinely and monetarily influenced as their long stretches of difficult work go to no end. Forecast of the prices might help the farming production network in settling on vital choices in limiting and dealing with the danger in value variances. By the way of outcome of the diminution of crop yield making due to uneven atmosphere circumstances and global warming. Rice is a significant yield developed in India, with Andhra Pradesh (AP) state being second as far as creation. At present ranchers in AP are moving from rice development to different harvests on account of worth variances and environmental variation. In this research, the costs of rice in AP remain anticipated utilizing time-series using data analytics like Machine Learning (ML) models. The prototypes SARIMA, Holt-Winter's Periodic technique, and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) Neural Networks (NN)be situated and utilized, and their recital was assessed dependent on the RMSE esteem on the rice database whose costs from 2001 to 2020. The conclusions demonstrate that the recommended process, LSTM neural network method is actual expectant and finest method which is suitable for the data.

title: Advancing Farming Practices: Machine Learning Algorithms for Optimal Crop Selection
abstract: This study underscores the critical importance of the agricultural sector for ensuring global food security and economic resilience, emphasizing the role of machine learning (ML)-enhanced crop recommendation systems. These systems are increasingly crucial for guiding farmers in choosing crops that are best suited to their unique soil and environmental conditions. Through the analysis of a comprehensive dataset, including soil composition, climate variations, historical crop yields, and agricultural practices, this research evaluates the performance of several ML algorithms–such as neural networks, decision trees, random forests, and support vector machines–in forecasting the most appropriate crops. Training on historical data allows these algorithms to decipher the complex dynamics between environmental factors and crop results. The success of these models is gauged by metrics including accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. This study also delves into the models' interpretability, offering crucial insights to both agricultural practitioners and researchers. Moreover, it presents the creation of a user-friendly web application that applies these ML models to provide personalized crop recommendations, requiring user inputs like geographical location, soil characteristics, and weather data. The findings reveal that ML algorithms can significantly empower farmers with knowledge to select suitable crops, thereby boosting agricultural efficiency, optimizing the use of resources, and enhancing the sustainability of agricultural operations. The research highlights the necessity of selecting the right ML algorithms and preprocessing techniques for achieving superior results. Notably, we have enhanced the accuracy of the random forest algorithm to 99.92% and ADABOOST with the Decision Tree Classifier to 99.02%. This contribution to precision agriculture showcases the practical use of ML in crop recommendation systems as a technological approach to addressing agricultural sector challenges and bolstering the global food supply chain.

title: Agritech Harmony: Real-time ESP32 Automation and Cloud Computing for Socially-Informed Crop Suggestions
abstract: Accurately predicting long-term crop yield trends remains a crucial challenge in optimizing agricultural practices and ensuring food security. This paper proposes a novel frame-work that merges real-time data acquired from Internet of Things (IoT) sensors with a Bi-directional LSTM model with an attention mechanism to achieve this objective. This architecture extracts insights from historical and future environmental conditions and prioritizes critical factors influencing yield through attention weighting. The framework incorporates an ESP32-managed sensor network measuring humidity, temperature, moisture, rainfall, and NPK levels, providing a continuous stream of real-time field data. Evaluation of real-world datasets demonstrates the framework's superiority over traditional methods, yielding significantly higher prediction accuracy and exposing key drivers of yield fluctuations through attention analysis. An accessible API facilitates seamless integration with farm management systems, empowering farmers with data-driven decision-making capabilities. This paper highlights the transformative potential of integrating deep learning, real-time IoT data, and APIs for revolutionizing agriculture, paving the way for a more sustainable and resilient agricultural futur

title: A Hybrid Approach for Crop Prediction Using Bi-Directional LSTM-RNN
abstract: In terms of managing food production and fostering economic growth, crop growth conditions and productivity are crucial. Prompt and accurate yield estimations are pertinent for ensuring food security. Farming is bnased on multiple factors including crop rotations, consistencies in soil types, air, surface temperatures, patterns of precipitations and others in addition to soil’s elements like nitrogen, phosphate, and potassium. Selecting crops using Random Forest (RF), Decision Trees (DT), Artificial Neural Networks (ANN)) are a part of the current corpus of research in this field. In this work, the suggested model uses deep learning (DL) for enhanced crop predictions alog with recommendations on required soil components with costs.The proposed work constructs LSTM-RNN based on LSTM (Long-Short Term Memory) and RNN (Recurrent Neural Network) reinforcement model in order to change the learning balance necessary for Q-Learning Reinforcement count to compute yield. The three essential characteristics approach should be used for future predictions of crop yields. (1) The proposed LSTM-RNN model captures temporal interdependences of environmental factors and seeds’ genetic developments without knowledge on their genotypes (2) The model demonstrates that there was no loss in forecast accuracy when the yield prediction was applied to untested situations (3) When used in conjunction with the backpropagation technique, the model may show how weather patterns, weather prediction accuracy, soil conditions, and crop production variations are all related. It evaluates imputdata and assists farmers in crop forecasts snf thud increased revenue. Our results showed a trustworthy and promising method for raising yield Prediction.

title: Aqua growth: Data-Driven Approach to Predict Plant Growth and Recommend Optimal Hydroponic Systems
abstract: Hydroponic farming offers a groundbreaking alternative to traditional agriculture, providing sustainable solutions to global food security challenges. By enabling soilless cultivation in nutrient-rich solutions, hydroponics allows precise control over environmental and nutrient parameters, leading to improved yields, reduced resource consumption, and adaptability in urban or arid areas. Among various hydroponic systems, the Nutrient Film Technique (NFT), Drip System, and Ebb and Flow stand out for their effectiveness, but selecting the optimal system and growth parameters for specific crops remains a complex task. This study addresses these challenges by employing machine learning techniques to predict plant growth and recommend optimal configurations.Regression models including Linear Regression, Decision Tree, Random Forest, and XG Boost were implemented to predict plant growth using a dataset of environmental and nutrient parameters, such as light intensity, pH, electrical conductivity (EC), and nutrient flow rate. The dataset also included system-specific labels, enabling targeted recommendations. XG Boost outperformed other models with the lowest Mean Squared Error (MSE) and highest R2score, demonstrating superior predictive accuracy. Results indicate that light intensity and pH levels are universally critical for all systems, while flow rate and cycle timing significantly influence growth in NFT and Ebb and Flow systems, respectively.Feature importance analysis identified the most influential parameters, guiding system-specific optimization. For instance, the NFT system benefits from precise control of nutrient flow rates, while the Drip System requires adjustments in drip frequency to ensure optimal water retention. These insights can be integrated with IoT devices for real-time monitoring and adjustments, transforming hydroponic farms into intelligent, self-regulating systems. Additionally, this framework supports diverse crop types, making it versatile for various agricultural scenarios.The implications of this research extend beyond yield improvement. By leveraging predictive modeling, farmers can make informed decisions, reducing resource wastage and environmental impact while optimizing productivity. Furthermore, this work sets the stage for future exploration into advanced methods, such as deep learning for time-series prediction and economic analysis to assess cost-effectiveness.In conclusion, this study demonstrates the potential of machine learning in hydroponic farming, enabling data-driven recommendations for system selection and parameter optimization. The integration of these techniques with hydroponics promotes sustainable, efficient, and scalable agricultural practices, addressing global food production challenges.

title: Fertilizer Classification for Identifying Effectively Commodity to The Crop Land Using Naïve Bayes and Decision Tree Classifier
abstract: Agriculture has a crucial role in meeting the food needs of the community and other farmer groups. One of the efforts to empower farmers is through farmer groups that aim to increase productivity, income, and welfare among farmers. Farmer groups must develop communities as a condition for obtaining subsidized fertilizer from the government. This study uses machine learning classifier methods, especially ID3 and Naïve Bayes algorithms, to identify farmer group communities’ data and predict subsidized fertilizer orders for subsectors and commodities. The evaluation show that both classification algorithms have a high accuracy rate, reaching about 99%. The ID3 algorithm provides high precision for the Urea fertilizer class, while Naïve Bayes has a lower precision for the nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium (NPK) class. However, Naïve Bayes showed a higher recall value for the NPK class. This algorithm provides valuable insights and information to more effectively manage farm resources. The results of this research are expected to increase agricultural output, improve the welfare of farmers, and support community food security. In conclusion, this study successfully used machine learning to predict subsidized fertilizer orders for subsectors and commodities. Both algorithms give accurate results, and the use of any of them depends on individual preferences and needs.

title: Crop Quality Prediction with GPU-DLCQPA: Comparing Deep Learning and Traditional Machine Learning Techniques
abstract: Smart agriculture, a field combining technology like drones, AI, IoT, and data analytics, aims to address challenges like rising food prices, water shortages, climate change, and labour scarcity. IoT sensors enable real-time crop health mon- itoring, while edge computing ensures timely decision-making. AI algorithms analyze data from sensors and drones to provide insights on crop diseases, pest infestations, and planting times, enabling farmers to make informed decisions, optimize resources, and minimize environmental impact. This paper compares deep learning and traditional machine learning techniques for crop quality prediction in smart agriculture. We proposed GPU- DLCQPA model, which uses GPU acceleration and YOLO classifier for accurate estimation of crop quality features from real-time images. The proposed deep learning model is compared with base classifiers in machine learning like Support Vector Machine (SVM) and Decision Trees. With an accuracy of almost 96% for crop quality prediction, our results show that GPU- DLCQPA performs much better than standard models in terms of accuracy, processing speed, and scalability. The potential of deep learning and GPU-accelerated computing to revolutionize agricultural practices and empower farmers to make data-driven decisions for yield and resource allocation optimization is the main objective of this study.

title: IoT-Driven Real-Time Soil Health Monitoring for Precision Agriculture Using Bi-Directional Transformer-CNN Models
abstract: Global population growth has fuelled food consumption for 60 years. The Green Revolution and genetically altered crops addressed this issue. Synthetic fertilisers, herbicides, and GMO seeds improve productivity. Simple treatments may hurt people and the environment. Precision agriculture, a greener method, optimises farming techniques by monitoring soil health, temperature, moisture, and weather. Using data-driven precision agriculture, this study uses a CNNTransformer hybrid model to evaluate soil health. Transformer-based architectures examine sequential data and CNNs extract features. WICL and LFS improve soil parameter estimates and resolve missing data. CNNTranNet outperformed other machine learning methods with $98 \%$ accuracy. Deep learning and random forest classifiers predicted soil temperature, climate, and moisture content to improve crop selection and production. Tech innovation and environmental conservation must be balanced to maintain agricultural yield. The CNNTranNet model delivers accurate and efficient soil health monitoring for precision agriculture data-driven decision-making. This method can improve food security and sustainability by picking crops by soil type.

title: RH-GNN: Regional Heterogeneity Enabled GNN for Agricultural Fertilization Prediction
abstract: The prediction of fertilization rates is a critical area of research in the agricultural field and is essential for ensuring global food security. With the ongoing expansion of the global population and the escalating repercussions of climate change, precise crop fertilization rate predictions have become paramount. This is because accurate predictions can optimize resource allocation and improve agricultural productivity. Moreover, they can provide scientific support for policy-making and agricultural input management, thereby promoting sustainable agricultural development. Despite its importance, the complexity of agricultural systems, which is influenced by multiple factors including climate, geography, soil conditions, and management practices, poses significant challenges to prediction accuracy. In this paper, we propose a deep learning framework based on Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) that effectively incorporates geographical knowledge and multi-dimensional feature information. By modeling spatial relationships through graph structures (nodes and edges), our framework enhances fertilization rate prediction accuracy. We validate the model using two datasets of different scales. The results demonstrate excellent predictive performance across all datasets and strong scalability, highlighting its potential for agricultural fertilization rate prediction.

title: PotatoLeafGuard: A Novel Hybrid CNN Architecture for Advanced Detection of Potato Leaf Diseases
abstract: Potatoes assume a crucial role as a global food crop, contending with challenges posed by various pathogens affecting their growth. Ranked as the third-largest agricultural food crop, potatoes are indispensable for delivering essential nutrients. One significant threat to potato health arises from leaf diseases. The accurate detection of these diseases is imperative for effective intervention. This research introduces a novel hybrid model integrating deep learning and transfer learning to predict the risks associated with potato leaf diseases. To train the model, a dataset comprising 3,076 images categorized into seven classes is used. These classes delineate various types of leaf diseases, including those affected by viruses, bacteria, fungi, pests, nematodes, phytophthora, and healthy leaves. The methodology leverages Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), recognized for their efficacy in identifying potato leaf diseases through image analysis. To enhance accuracy, Transfer Learning algorithms such as VGG16 and Xception are incorporated. This hybrid model addresses the intricate classification challenges arising from the distinct characteristics and data limitations inherent in potato leaf diseases. Furthermore, data augmentation techniques are employed in conjunction with CNNs to mitigate classification challenges associated with unique features and limited data. The stacking of outputs from these models substantially enhances the accuracy of potato leaf disease detection. In summary, this research endeavors to provide a novel methodology for the precise classification of diverse types of potato leaf diseases, contributing to improved crop management and food security. The proposed model achieves an overall classification accuracy of 94.70%, accompanied by commendable precision, recall, and F1-score values of 93.75%, 93.6%, and 92.75%, respectively. These results validate the model's efficacy in advancing research on potato leaf disease detection, attesting to its high accuracy.

title: Integrating IoT and AI for Automated Crop with Smart Urban Farming
abstract: This research paper delves into the symbiotic relationship between Internet of Things (IoT) and Artificial Intelligence (AI) technologies, and their pivotal role in revolutionizing crop management within the sphere of smart urban farming. Urban agriculture is rapidly emerging as a crucial solution to the challenges of food security and sustainability in densely populated areas. By harnessing the capabilities of IoT and AI this paper outlines a comprehensive framework for real-time monitoring and intelligent decision-making processes that are vital for the optimal growth of crops in urban settings. The core of this research lies in the seamless integration of IoT devices, such as sensors and automated systems, with advanced AI algorithms. This combination enables the continuous monitoring of various environmental parameters like soil moisture, temperature, and nutrient levels, leading to more informed and data-driven agricultural practices. The AI component of this integration is particularly significant in analyzing vast amounts of data collected by IoT devices, predicting potential issues, and making proactive decisions to enhance crop health and yield. The paper discusses in detail the methodology adopted for implementing this IoT-ai integration in urban farming scenarios. It includes the design and deployment of IoT networks, the development of AI models tailored to agriculture, and the establishment of a communication framework for effective data exchange. The results of experimental studies conducted to validate the efficiency of this integrated system are presented, showcasing significant improvements in crop yield, resource utilization, and overall farming efficiency. The paper also explores the broader implications of this technology. It discusses how the IoT-AI integration could be a game-changer in urban agriculture, potentially leading to more sustainable and self-sufficient urban communities. This study concludes with a forward-looking perspective, examining future prospects and potential enhancements of this technology, including the integration of advanced machine learning techniques and the scalability of the system for larger urban farming projects. This research not only demonstrates the immediate benefits of integrating IoT and AI in urban agriculture but also opens new avenues for future innovations in smart farming practices.

title: Understanding the Trends in Indian CPI and Inflation: Forecasting the Future Values Using Machine Learning Model
abstract: The Consumer Price Index (CPI) is an economic indicator for every country and it reflects the inflation rate also. It calculates the percentage difference in prices that consumers pay for a selection of goods and services over a specific timeframe. It represents changes in prices as experienced by consumers in India. Every month, the Central Statistics Office (CSO) under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation releases the monthly Consumer Price Index (CPI) data in India. The Government and central banks use the CPI data for inflation control and price monitoring. This work aims at producing a detailed analysis of the Indian Consumer Price Index, inflation related factors and the future directions. The base year considered at present is$2012=100$. The CPI is calculated for three different segments like Rural, Urban and Combined. The CSO calculates the CPI values considering the segments like food prices, clothing, footwear, transportation, fuel etc. A total of 26 such segments are used to calculate the India CPI. This work performs an Exploratory Data Analysis on these segments and finally forecasts the General Index (CPI) for next six months. This work also analyses the inflation rate for the period 1993 to 2024 and implements LSTM machine learning model to forecast the inflation rate of India for the period July to December 2024.

title: Machine Learning-based Pest Count Forecasting for Solar Insecticidal Lamps
abstract: Agricultural pests severely threaten food security, resulting in significant economic, social, and environmental impacts. This paper uses weather data and machine learning models to forecast pest counts. Data from solar insecticidal lamps, including pest counts and meteorological conditions, were collected. Using this data, we developed a multidimensional forecasting model. The model integrates crucial variables, including pest counts, temperature, humidity, and geographical coordinates. The genetic algorithm back propagation neural network model has demonstrated excellent performance in forecasting pest numbers, with an R2value of 0.73, confirming its effectiveness in the early detection of crop diseases and pest infestations. Moreover, this high-accuracy forecasting model provides a scientific basis for intelligently adjusting the insecticidal working time of solar insecticidal lamps, thereby enhancing pest control efficiency and energy utilization. This research not only reinforces the application of machine learning in agricultural pest management but also provides significant support for precision agriculture.

title: Cloud Computing-Enabled Hybrid Machine Learning Models for Crop Yield Prediction
abstract: The combination of the cloud computing and the machine learning can be regarded as the prospective solution of the issues related to modern agriculture, where predicting the crop yields is more accurate and scalable. In this work, we introduce an integrated machine learning system that uses cloud computing to support data-driven, near-real-time crop yield prediction. To enable the algorithm to learn in addition to time-based trends as well as nonlinear relationship(s) in agricultural datasets, we will then propose a model that combines the ensemble learning techniques of random forest and gradient boosting with the deep learning architecture of long short-term memory (LSTM) networks. With the scalability of processing, cloud infrastructure offers an easy access to several sources of data like satellite images, weather, soil, and yield history among others. In experiments, Model is tested using large scale agricultural data and model performance is measured using as RMSE, MAE, R2score. Just like all other collaborative filtering (CF) algorithms, they fail to work as sole models and produce low prediction accuracy and computational performance. The findings indicate that cloud enabled hybrid models suggested in this paper offer good support to precision farming and data driven decision making in agriculture which will contribute in the rising food security and sustainability in the farming processes. Such modifications are to be implemented in the future work as embedding real time sensor data and adaptive learning processes to make more accurate predictions.

title: AI-Driven Precision Agriculture in the Context of Smart Cities: A Pathway to Food Security and Environmental Resilience
abstract: Smart farming is becoming an integral component of smart cities, offering transformative potential across multiple dimensions. The integration offers several advantages including enhanced food security, data-driven urban planning, and economic and social benefits. This paper presents a comprehensive cyber-physical aquaponics monitoring framework that integrates sensor fusion, Edge AI, and time-series forecasting to enable resilient, intelligent, and sustainable urban food systems. Aquaponics systems are inherently complex due to the interplay between environmental conditions and aquatic life. Monitoring them reliably in real-time remains challenging, particularly in urban contexts where scale, reliability, and automation are critical. Relying solely on water-quality sensor data can lead to a partial and sometimes misleading assessment of system health. To overcome this, we propose an architecture that combines structured data from environmental sensors and unstructured data from camera streams. We convert visual fish behavior into structured features using DeepSORT tracking and fuse these with traditional water metrics to form a holistic view of the aquaponics environment. Our machine learning pipeline includes XGBoost for classification and Prophet for forecasting future system states. Experimental evaluations on a real-world dataset show significant improvements in early warning detection and future state prediction.

title: Early Stage Recognition and Classification of Different Diseases on Rice Plant Leaf by Modified Approach with Attention Mechanism
abstract: Generally India is an agricultural country because most of its economy relies on agriculture. Different types of crops yield and cultivate in India but wheat and rice are two major crops produced in large scale and has their own capability and importance role due to feeding large population of the country. Rice has the second position in food index by food security community in term of consumption by the Asian people. It is also the greater source of energy after the wheat crop in India. Indian food security community has concern about the production of rice crop because large percentage of yield diminishes due to the rice plant diseases. There are various rice plant diseases infected to rice plant leaf in which some diseases has large impact on reduction in yields of rice crops and it may go 20 to 50% in severe cases. This is significant to identification of paddy leaves illness at an initial stage. Currently, farmers have to detect and classified infection by manual way, which is a time consuming process. To concern about it, an automatic method may be applied to locate plant leaves disease at their earliest stage. The major goal of this article is to mine the multi scale characteristics in an image and focus on special features which generally not predicted and focused by ordinary methods. We proposed a modified approach in the deep learning method to optimize the loss and improve the performance of prediction and classification accuracy. The output and performance of the proposed modified deep learning method with attention mechanism across the different existing methods on rice field image dataset proved as the best classification approach and achieved 96.5% average accuracy.

title: AAR-LSTM: An Interpretable Attention based Auto Regressive LSTM for volatile temporal dynamics
abstract: Accurate crop yield forecasting is crucial for ensuring food security, especially in agro-climatic zones susceptible to high environmental variability. Traditional statistical models fail to capture complex non-linear dependencies, while standard deep learning methods operate as black boxes with rigid autoregressive capabilities. To address these limitations, this study proposes an Attention-based Autoregressive LSTM network (AAR-LSTM), a novel hybrid architecture that explicitly integrates a dynamic, context-dependent autoregressive component with the LSTM cell state. By leveraging an attention mechanism, AAR-LSTM dynamically weights the most relevant historical yield observations at each time step, effectively creating an adaptive lookback window. The model was evaluated on a multi-crop dataset (wheat, rice, and maize) from the Jammu district (2009–2019), utilizing daily multivariate meteorological variables. The proposed model was able to achieve the lowest RMSE, MAE, and SMAPE values at all times in comparison with a conventional LSTM and an ARIMAX model. Results highlight that incorporating a context-aware autoregressive component is an effective technique for modelling the intricate temporal dependencies inherent in agricultural time-series data.

title: A Machine Learning Approach to Forecast the Food Prices for Food Security Issues
abstract: Food security is one of the major challenges that must be addressed to provide sufficient and nutritious food to everyone. In this work, we have used Ethiopia's monthly food price data from 2000 to 2023. The work aims to effectively predict food prices by applying machine learning models. We have applied the SVM, KNN, LR, DT, and RM models, in which it is found that RF is one of the best models with the highest accuracy 98.98%. Further, to consolidate it, we have applied the Friedman test to measure the model's ranking, and we have observed that RF is the highest ranked among all the applied models. The findings of the work conclude the same.

title: Soil Quality Analysis and Yield Prediction Using Remote Sensing and Machine Learning
abstract: Wheat yield prediction is crucial for ensuring food security in India, where Uttar Pradesh contributes significantly to national production. This paper introduces a machine learning-based framework that combines in-situ soil quality indicators with Sentinel-2A vegetation indices for forecasting wheat yield at the field level. A synthetic dataset comprising 85 farms, representing authentic agronomic conditions in the Indo-Gangetic plains, was created utilising soil nitrogen (N), phosphorus (P), potassium (K), pH, electrical conductivity (EC), and organic carbon, in addition to vegetation indices such as NDVI, SAVI, and EVI. We trained and tested three supervised models—Random Forest (RF), Support Vector Machine (SVM), and Gradient Boosting (GB)—using 10-fold cross-validation. RF had the best results ($\mathrm{R}^{2}=0.87$, $\mathrm{RMSE}=2.14 \mathrm{q} / \mathrm{ha}, \mathrm{MAE}=1.73 \mathrm{q} / \mathrm{ha}$), beating both kernel-based and boosting methods. Feature importance analysis revealed NDVI, organic carbon, nitrogen, phosphorus, and SAVI as the most significant predictors, consistent with established agronomic principles. The study shows that ensemble tree-based models are better at capturing nonlinear interactions between soil and crops. It also shows how combining soil and remote sensing data can lead to accurate, understandable, and spatially explicit yield forecasts. This framework can help with precision farming, early warning systems, and planning for food security in a region. It also makes it possible to use multi-modal Earth Observation and cloud platforms in real time.

title: Predicting Plant Health and Stress Levels Using Machine Learning Techniques for Smart Agriculture
abstract: Plant stress poses a notable challenge in agriculture, as it reduces crop yield and threatens global food security. Accurate and timely detection of stress conditions is therefore essential for ensuring sustainable agricultural practices and minimizing productivity losses. This study investigated the effectiveness of a multilayer perceptron (MLP) framework trained using two conjugate gradient optimization algorithms: Conjugate Gradient with Fletcher-Reeves updates (CGF) and Conjugate Gradient with Powell-Beale restarts (CGB). The models were tested under two hidden layer configurations (5 and 10 neurons), and classification performance was evaluated on training, validation, and testing datasets. Results disclosed that CGB consistently outperformed CGF, with the best performance observed using 5 hidden neurons, achieving 97.63% training, 96.83% validation, and 96.18% testing accuracy. In contrast, CGF attained lower accuracy but exhibited higher variability, particularly in the testing phase. Overall, the findings highlight the robustness of CGB in neural network optimization for plant stress classification and suggest its strong potential for deployment in precision agriculture systems aimed at improving early stress detection, reliable monitoring, and timely intervention.

title: Smart Crop Predictor and Soil NPK Optimizer
abstract: Agriculture faces challenges like population growth, land loss, and climate change. Existing methods are inefficient, relying on imprecise techniques that degrade soil and reduce yields. This study proposes a machine learning-based web platform to optimize crop selection using soil NPK levels, environmental data, and historical trends, enhancing sustainability and efficiency.The system employs advanced machine learning models to predict suitable crops based on different soil and weather parameters, offers recommendations to optimize soil fertility in the form of effective fertilizer management, water management with temperature for perticular crop and integrates plant disease detection for early intervention. By focusing on data-driven insights this platform enables farmers to make on-ground decisions of fertilizer, water for specific crop of specific weather condition, thereby promoting sustainable agricultural practices. Additionally, the inclusion of a crop disease prediction module aids in minimizing losses, reducing dependency on chemical pesticides, and this all result in enhancing overall yield quality. This comprehensive solution not only supports efficient resource utilization but also aligns with long-term agricultural sustainability goals, directly benefiting farmers and addressing global food security concerns.

title: Multivariate Time Series Forecasting Based Cloud Computing For Consumer Price Index Using Deep Learning Algorithms
abstract: Multivariate time series forecasting affords an opportunity to forecast future recent trends or possibility incident based on historical observations. Forecasting in economic world becomes global interest particularly for researchers seeking for best accuracy result using several methods. Consumer Price Index is the primary instrument used by central banks to set inflation targets. However, most of previous studies commonly only used univariate factor to forecast Consumer Price Index. Furthermore, mostly model development of forecasting system is done by personal and physical server facing the problem of impractical yet time consuming. Since measuring method of Consumer Price Index commonly is pick an average of the period-to-period price move for the different products, we conducted multivariate Consumer Price Index forecasting based Cloud Computing utilizing 28 types of Surabaya daily food price from 2014 to 2018 using Multilayer Perceptron and Long Short Term Memory (LSTM) of deep learning. Furthermore, we implement architectural variations of the number of neurons, epoch, and hidden layers. The whole development of forecasting system is built in Amazon Web Service (AWS) Cloud. The result indicated the best accuracy value was obtained from the Multilayer Perceptron with 3.380 of RMSE consist of a configuration of 2 hidden layers, 10 neurons of first hidden layer, 10 neurons of second hidden layer also 1000 of epoch.

title: Implementation of Hyperparameter Tuning of CATBoost Regressor Model for Climate Change Detection
abstract: Climate change will impact everyone. From more extreme weather to rising food prices, recreation, and reduced opportunities to appreciate nature, people everywhere will feel the impact. This study aims to develop and compare climate change prediction models with the CATBoost Regressor model. The dataset used includes historical climate data such as air temperature, greenhouse gas concentrations, and other atmospheric parameters. The research methods include data understanding, preprocessing, dataset sharing, modeling, model evaluation, and result analysis. The results show that the accuracy of the CATBoost Regressor is better than the XGBoost Regressor and Random Forest Regressor and provides the best performance with a Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) of 0.0559.

title: A Robust Machine Learning Framework for Estimating Crop Production Using Ensemble and Quantile Techniques
abstract: This study proposes a novel data-driven approach for crop yield prediction by integrating Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) with Quantile Regression. The comprehensive dataset includes multiple environmental and soil attributes (rainfall, effective accumulated temperature, and multi-layer soil parameters), as well as management factors such as conservation tillage practices, yield, and emergence rates. Additionally, creative computing enriches feature engineering to uncover emergent patterns. By leveraging XGBoost's robust ensemble learning capability, the model efficiently captures complex interactions among climate, soil, and farming techniques, while Quantile Regression refines yield forecasts by providing interval estimates that quantify predictive uncertainty. To evaluate performance, more innovative measures were supplemented including the Continuous Ranked Probability Score, to assess predictive distribution quality. Additionally, the Prediction Interval Coverage Probability was calculated to determine interval reliability, with improved calibration reflecting the model's capacity to address nonlinearities. Experimental results show that this hybrid framework significantly reduces forecast errors and provides well-calibrated uncertainty bounds, outperforming traditional regression approaches. Moreover, interval-based predictions help decision-makers evaluate risks under dynamic environmental conditions. The proposed system thus represents a valuable decision-support tool for optimizing agricultural practices in resource-limited settings. Further enhancements may be achieved by integrating real-time data streams and advanced neural network architectures to improve spatiotemporal modeling and adaptability. This research contributes to precision agriculture by providing a scalable, high-accuracy predictive framework that informs farmers and policymakers in developing more effective strategies for crop management, resource allocation, and food security in volatile agricultural environments.

title: Time Series: Predicting Nigerian Food Prices using ARIMA Model and R-Programming
abstract: The majority of food commodities in Nigeria have seen persistent price instability. this is brought by elements like insecurity/insurgency, poor storage facilities, seasonal price changes, inconsistent government policies, COVID-19 containment measures, poor access to credit, technical inputs, lack of modern farm tools and implements. This study focused on comparing the prices of four different food items - beans, onion, tomato, and yam using the ARIMA model to forecast future prices. Two out of the six geopolitical zones of Nigeria were used for the study; the North-Central and North-West. The National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) provided the raw data between 2017 and 2018, and the items were weighed in kilograms (Kg). The data was extrapolated into a time series data by executing in R Studio. The stationarity of the series data was obtained by a Unit root Test using the KPSS test (If p<0.05 means the time series is stationary). Results from the forecasted values indicated that food commodities' prices increase with time, making ARIMA a good model for forecasting prices. It was recommended that necessary measures should be put in place to ameliorate the high cost of food prices being experienced in the country of Nigeria.

title: Deep Learning-Based Price Prediction of Red Bird’s Eye Chili: An LSTM Approach with Hyperparameter Variation
abstract: The volatile pricing of red bird’s eye chili (Capsicum frutescens) presents a serious challenge to Indonesia’s agricultural market stability, particularly in Central Java. This study investigates the use of a Long ShortTerm Memory (LSTM) neural network to forecast chili prices by examining the effect of hyperparameter tuning, including training epochs, activation functions (tanh, sigmoid, ReLU), and optimizers (Adam, RMSprop, SGD). Daily price data from the National Food Price Panel (April 1, 2021-February 10, 2025) were preprocessed using linear interpolation for missing values and Min-Max normalization. Multiple configurations were tested, with performance measured through MAE, RMSE, MAPE, $R^{2}$, final epoch loss, and runtime. The best configuration-sigmoid activation, Adam optimizer, and 300 epochs-achieved an MAE of 0.0197, RMSE of 0.0434, MAPE of $81.05 \%$, and $\mathbf{R}^{2}$ of 0.9702. These findings highlight the importance of hyperparameter selection in improving both predictive accuracy and efficiency. The research contributes to methodological discussions on LSTM tuning and provides practical insights for developing AI-driven price forecasting platforms to support policymakers, agribusiness stakeholders, and technology innovators in managing volatility in Indonesia’s food markets.

title: Deep Stacking Ensemble with Stacked LSTM and SVR for Analysis and Forecasting: A Case Study of Rice Price in East Java
abstract: Fluctuating food prices, especially rice is pose a significant challenge in obtaining accurate predictions. Classical models like Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (ARIMA) face limitations in handling non-linear behavior and long-term dependencies in time series. To address these limitations, this study develops and evaluates a forecasting framework by comparing the performance of classical statistical methods, deep learning models, and ensemble techniques. The comparison includes ARIMA as the baseline, alongside Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) models with different architectural configurations (1, 2, and 3 layers) using lag 1 and lag 7, and the proposed Deep Stacking Ensemble Learning model with its meta-learner using Support Vector Regression (SVR). The models performance was assessed on the testing dataset using Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), and Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE). The Deep Stacking Ensemble outperforms LSTM and ARIMA, with lag 1 being most robust (MAPE 0.098%) and lag 7 more accurate than ARIMA (MAPE 0.126%). This study concludes that the deep stacking ensemble method improves forecasting accuracy and reliability by integrating multiple models, making it suitable for highly fluctuating time series.

title: 3MTL: A Multi-Modal Multi-Task Learning Approach for Plant Disease Detection and Analysis
abstract: This paper attempted to addresses the critical need for automated plant disease detection and analysis, which is crucial for bolstering global food security and agricultural sustainability. We propose a Multi-modal Multi-Task Learning (3MTL) system that combines state-of-the-art Transformers (ViT) and Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) models to perform joint visual and textual analysis. The system tackles fundamental key tasks including Image-based classification, caption and annotation generation, and question-answering generation. Leveraging multi-modal information to enhance the performance of machine learning tasks, from vision-language to natural language processing, such as question answering. Using a late fusion approach, we merge visual and language encoders to enhance performance across these tasks. Extensive experiments on a newly curated dataset, consisting of plant images paired with corresponding textual metadata, demonstrate the slightly superior accuracy of our BERT-ViT architecture compared to a Contractive Language-Image pre-trained (CLIP) mode in most tasks. The ViT-based model achieves a classification accuracy of 93% for predicting plant name, healthy status, and disease name and causes, a BLEU Score of 0.79 for generating annotations, and an accuracy of 89% for question-answering tasks. In contrast, the CLIP-based model achieves accuracy of 92%, 78%, and 88% for the same tasks. Our findings underscore the potential of integrating visual and textual cues to enhance plant disease management and ultimately resulting in scalable and intelligent agricultural solutions.

title: Simplified Prediction-Based AI-IoT Model for Energy Management Scheme in Standalone PV Powered Greenhouse
abstract: Automated greenhouse is essential for sustainable development and food security. Photovoltaic (PV) power with physical sensors-based control using Internet of Things needs high initial investment and operational cost. This also needs significant installed storage capacity. In the proposed solution, the dependency on physical sensors like temperature, humidity, soil moisture sensors, etc., are eliminated due to the application of eXtreme Gradient Boosting-based machine learning (ML) algorithm. The training and testing of ML algorithm are performed with one-year physical data (approx. 50k @10 min interval) from greenhouse which provides accurate mapping (Temperature MAPE: 1.51%,R2: 0.9785 and Humidity MAPE: 1.68%,R2: 0.9867) between predicted and sensor data. Also, a novel priority-based demand side management scheme is implemented which includes load shifting which reduces the requirement of installed PV and storage capacity. A reduction of 63.27% storage capacity is possible with proposed control approach. ML algorithm is programmed using Python language and implemented in Raspberry Pi-3B+ SBC. For physical verification of the proposed control unit, a laboratory-based prototype is developed with PV emulator (1.5 kW), programmable electronic load box, and relay unit controlled through Arduino UNO, Raspberry Pi-3B+ SBC, ESP-32 Combo unit.

title: Nondestructive Technology for Real-Time Monitoring and Prediction of Soybean Quality Using Machine Learning for a Bulk Transport Simulation
abstract: Grain moisture content and shipping time can interfere with postharvest logistics on soybean quality. Thus, the study aimed to evaluate the use of a nondestructive technology, equipment including a mechanical-portable sampler with a hardware device and sensors for real-time monitoring of temperature, relative humidity (RH), and intergranular carbon dioxide (CO2) to predict the quality of soybean in the function of different moisture contents (11%, 14%, and 18% w.b.), sampling positions in the grain mass profile, and shipping time (0, 60, 480, and 1440 min). The monitoring of indirect quality measurement variables associated with the application of machine-learning (ML) models satisfactorily predicted the physical quality of the grain mass, over the shipping time, for the different conditions tested. The moisture content associated with time was the factor with the greatest influence on the quality of transported grains. The shipping time is the determining factor for controlling the quality of grains. Lots of soybeans harvested from crops with moisture content between 14% and 18% must not exceed 120 min of shipping time to maintain quality. It is recommended that the shipping time of grains shipped from storage units to processing industries, with moisture contents between 11% and 14%, should not exceed 840 min. The M5P and reduced error pruning tree (REPTree) algorithms were the ones that best performed the prediction of grain quality. The monitoring system and grain quality prediction has application in grain-producing farms, grain storage, the grain-processing industry, and companies providing services in grain transport. The technology contributes to grain loss reduction and conservation in the context of logistics, sustainability, and food security.

title: Multilevel Deep Learning Network for County-Level Corn Yield Estimation in the U.S. Corn Belt
abstract: Accurate and timely estimation of crop yield at a small scale is of great significance to food security and harvest management. Recent studies have proven remote sensing is an efficient method for yield estimation and machine learning, especially deep learning, can infer a good prediction by integrating multisource datasets such as satellite data, climate data, soil data, and so on. However, there are some bottleneck challenges to improve accuracy. First, the popular remote sensing data used for yield prediction fall into two major groups-time-series data and constant data.
