Moreover, our predictive model is designed to adapt and evolve over time, leveraging machine learning algorithms to refine the predictions continuously based on real-time data inputs in smart cities. By staying abreast of shifting agricultural dynamics and emerging trends, the model remains relevant and effective in facilitating optimal decision-making processes in smart cities. Ultimately, our chapter endeavors to empower farmers with a robust toolset that enables them for the navigation of complexities of modern agriculture with confidence and foresight in smart cities. By harnessing the power of predictive analytics and visualization technologies, we aim to foster sustainable agricultural practices while enhancing food security and livelihoods in farming communities in smart cities.

title: Decision Support System for Sustainable Farming
abstract: The majority of India’s populace resides in rural regions, where agriculture serves as the primary source of sustenance and income. This sector is not only pivotal for the country’s economy but also fundamental for providing food to its burgeoning population. As the number of inhabitants continues to rise, the significance of meeting the escalating demand for food becomes increasingly evident, emphasizing the critical role played by agriculture in India’s economic growth and food security. Crop yields in India vary depending on factors like region, crop type, weather conditions, and agricultural practices. In recent years, crop yields in India have shown fluctuations. Farmers are cultivating the same crops repeatedly without experimenting with different crop varieties. Additionally, they use fertilizers without proper knowledge of the specific nutrient deficiencies and appropriate quantities. Crop recommendations using machine learning are of immense importance in modern agriculture. It revolutionizes farming practices by leveraging data-driven insights to make informed decisions about crop selection. This has several far-reaching benefits. Machine Learning optimizes crop selection by considering factors like soil type, climate, and historical data. By recommending crops that are best suited to a specific area, farmers can significantly improve their yields while minimizing risks. The proposed system, ’Smart Farming’, considers farmers&s; inputs, soil properties, rainfall, and past used pesticides and applies machine learning techniques to predict suitable crops. This enables farmers to know which crop is more suitable based on the given soil conditions and environmental characteristics. The objective of this article is to forecast suitable crops to enhance crop productivity and benefit the agricultural sector. Increased productivity is another key outcome. Accurate recommendations lead to higher yields, improving farmers’ income and food security.

title: Empowering Agriculture
abstract: The agriculture industry is essential to both economic growth and global food security. But farmers have a lot on their plate, from uncertain markets to erratic weather patterns. This article investigates the transformative potential of artificial intelligence (AI)-driven virtual tutors in empowering agriculture through better investment strategies and farmer education in order to address these difficulties. Traditional farmer education techniques could be completely transformed by the incorporation of AI technologies, especially virtual tutors. These clever solutions use machine learning algorithms to deliver adaptive and customized learning experiences, customizing instructional materials to meet the needs of each farmer. AI-driven virtual tutors enable farmers to make more educated decisions, increasing resilience and production. They do this by providing insights into market trends, crop management, and sustainable farming methods. Additionally, the study looks at how AI might be used to optimize investment plans in the agriculture sector. Predictive analytics-enabled virtual tutors may examine market trends, weather patterns, and historical data to provide farmers with insightful advice on the best ways to invest their money. This helps to make farming operations more productive and lucrative by offering advice on crop selection, resource allocation, and risk management. The research also explores the possible socio-economic effects of AI-driven agricultural solutions, highlighting the democratization of resources and information. Farmers of all backgrounds and locations can benefit from improved agricultural insights through the provision of easily available and reasonably priced AI-based instructional tools, which promotes inclusivity and sustainable growth.

title: Artificial Intelligence Algorithms and Models for NextGen Agriculture
abstract: In the evolving landscape of NextGen Agriculture, traditional farming is replaced by means of a technologically sophisticated approach. This chapter explores the transformative position of AI in agriculture, highlighting precision farming, sustainable `practices, and AI-driven solutions to modern challenges. Key AI applications like machine learning, neural networks, and predictive analytics optimize resource usage, enhance crop yields, and ensure sustainability. Predictive analytics, time series evaluation, and computer vision revolutionize farming schedules and weed control. The chapter underscores the importance of collaboration amongst researchers, technologists, and farmers, envisioning a future wherein AI continues to innovate and cope with international agricultural challenges, ensuring food security and environmental sustainability.

title: Soil Health Restoration—A Focus on Microbiome Engineering and Prediction
abstract: Soil pollution and land degradation are critical global issues exacerbated by industrialization, urbanization, and intensive agriculture. Soil health, encompassing nutrient cycling, biodiversity, and pathogen suppression, is vital for ecosystems, food security, and human well-being. While traditional restoration methods, such as conservation agriculture and integrated nutrient management, emphasize minimal disturbance and organic amendments, recent insights highlight the soil microbiome as a key indicator of soil health. Microbiome engineering presents promising opportunities, yet its application remains constrained by limited understanding of complex microbial dynamics. This chapter aims to advance this understanding by examining pivotal aspects of soil microbial dynamics, including community context, interaction range, and interaction strength, which are essential for predicting and managing microbial communities. We then discuss ecological models, including the generalized Lotka–Volterra and microbial consumer-resource models, alongside data-driven tools like Empirical Dynamic Modeling that further improve our understanding and predictive skill. Despite context-dependency challenges, advancements in machine learning and high-quality datasets offer new opportunities for sustainable soil health management. This comprehensive approach seeks to foster stable microbial communities that enhance soil health and resilience, contributing to sustainable agriculture and ecosystem management in the face of widespread soil disturbance.

title: Predictive analytics in agriculture
abstract: In order to forecast agricultural yields and suggest suitable crops, this chapter examines the use of machine learning techniques, including Random Forest (RF), Decision Trees, Support Vector Machines, and K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN). Predicting crop yields accurately is essential for enhancing food security and streamlining farming methods. The study shows that by utilizing crop traits, soil composition, and meteorological data, these systems improve predictions. Key findings show that KNN performs best in crop recommendation tasks with 98.18% accuracy, while the RF model obtains 96.67% accuracy. These findings demonstrate how machine learning may be used to address issues in sustainable agriculture.

title: Combining CRISPR and AI to Facilitate Food Security and Sustainable Development Goals
abstract: Increasing crop productivity with limited land available in face of climate change and increasing biotic and abiotic stresses is urging scientists to emphasize food security as well as sustainability in agriculture. A diversified strategy is needed to meet the increasing demand for food. CRISPR as a gene-editing tool has been a breakthrough technology in agriculture due to its widespread applications. CRISPR has transformed crops by its targeted gene modification. Artificial intelligence (AI) is an emerging field, integrating language processing, machine learning, and computer vision. The combination of these two technologies has the potential to solve food security and sustainability problems. CRISPR’s precise gene-editing capabilities allow the creation of crops with improved features. AI enhances this by providing advanced data analysis, predictive modeling, and optimization tools, allowing CRISPR to be used more effectively and efficiently. The combination of CRISPR and AI not only tackles the critical problem of food scarcity, but also paves the way for more sustainable agricultural techniques. This chapter begins with an overview of CRISPR and AI technologies. It then investigates practical applications such as pest and disease control, nutrient enhancement, and sustainable resource management. Finally, challenges and future perspectives are examined.

title: Upholding ethical standards in modern agriculture
abstract: The agriculture industry, traditionally reliant on conventional methods for crop production, now has the opportunity to enhance its practices through the integration of machine learning and Internet of Things (IoT) applications, leveraging new technologies for improved outcomes. Machine-learning algorithms and IoT devices can revolutionize agriculture by reducing resource consumption and enhancing farm management. This review explores the applications of machine learning and IoT in crop monitoring, disease detection, and water management while addressing challenges related to data collection, privacy, and security. It highlights the integration of IoT networks with sensors and the incorporation of machine-learning techniques by using IoT sensors to gather data on soil moisture, temperature, and nutrient levels, and applying machine-learning algorithms to analyze this data; precision agriculture can predict yields, detect diseases or pests, and recommend optimal planting and harvesting times. This fusion of technologies promises to transform agriculture and improve food security. This chapter addresses two main objectives. First, it presents an app-based solution that displays current sensor values, enabling efficient remote management of agricultural fields. Second, it proposes an IoT-based prototype surveillance system that utilizes multi-class classification techniques with machine learning and deep learning to identify labels.

title: Exploring the effectiveness of decision trees for comprehensive detection of crop diseases in agricultural environments
abstract: The accurate and timely detection of crop diseases is crucial for maintaining agricultural productivity and ensuring food security. This research explores the application of decision tree algorithms for the comprehensive detection and classification of crop diseases in agricultural environments. Leveraging a dataset containing various features indicative of crop health, the study implements and evaluates decision trees to identify disease patterns with high precision. The proposed approach involves preprocessing the data to handle noise and outliers, followed by feature extraction to enhance the algorithm’s predictive capabilities. Experimental results demonstrate that decision trees achieve an accuracy of 90%, precision of 91%, recall of 89%, F1-score of 90%, and an AUC-ROC of 92%, outperforming several other machine-learning methods such as support vector machines, random forests, K-nearest neighbors, and logistic regression. These findings indicate that decision trees provide a reliable and efficient means for early disease detection, which can facilitate proactive intervention and management in agricultural practices. The study also highlights the scalability and robustness of decision trees in handling large datasets, making them suitable for real-time applications in diverse agricultural settings. This research contributes to the ongoing efforts to integrate advanced machine-learning techniques into agricultural practices, offering a promising solution to enhance crop health monitoring and disease management. Future work will focus on integrating additional data sources and refining the model parameters to further improve detection accuracy and robustness, ultimately aiming to support sustainable agriculture and food security initiatives.

title: Remote Sensing for Automatic Disease Monitoring in Wheat
abstract: Wheat, the food security crop of the world, is being increasingly threatened by diseases such as rusts, blights, and smuts that cause significant yield losses worldwide. With climate fluctuation and resource limitations on the rise, effective disease management is important in ensuring the sustainability of wheat production. The chapter explores the transformative role of remote sensing technology in enabling automated, scalable disease monitoring in wheat production. By combining satellite, unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV), and ground sensor data, remote sensing provides critical information on environmental conditions and plant health, like soil properties, meteorology, and spectral signatures. Advanced big data analytics and artificial intelligence (AI) techniques process the data to detect disease patterns, predict outbreaks, and guide precision agriculture operations. Specific emphasis is placed on spectral imaging, LiDAR, and data fusion techniques&s; contributions toward early detection—often with no visible signs—to early diagnostic precision. While challenges in data alignment, quality assurance, and scalability in systems continue, their integration offers tremendous benefits in optimized resources, targeted interventions, and robust decision-making. The chapter concludes by addressing new trends in sensor technology, machine learning, and real-time monitoring that are on the horizon to revolutionize disease management and inspire sustainable wheat production globally through optimization, enhanced accuracy, and informed decision-making. Future advancements in sensor technology, machine learning, and real-time monitoring systems promise to revolutionize wheat disease management further, promoting sustainable agriculture and global food security.

title: Health Impacts of Food Insecurity
abstract: Persistent food insecurity affects 800+ million people, worsened by climate change, conflicts, and systemic inequalities. Current solutions lack real-time predictive capabilities, leading to ineffective interventions that fail to address root causes or prevent health crises. This study leverages machine learning to analyze food insecurity using 2019–2023 Global Food Security Index data, capturing post-pandemic disruptions. Gradient boosting achieved R 2 = 0.85 in predicting health impacts, while neural networks maintained 91% classification accuracy despite recent volatility. The 2023 data reveals a critical shift: supply chain resilience (weight = 0.47) now outweighs affordability (weight = 0.39) as the top risk factor, reversing pre-pandemic trends. Long short-term memory networks (LSTM) forecasts show a 12% accelerated decline in food security scores across vulnerable regions since 2020, with models identifying emergent crisis hotspots (87% precision). Notably, pre-pandemic models show 23% more false positives in 2023, proving the need for dynamic retraining. Validated by consistent F1-scores (0.88–0.91), these findings highlight two urgent policy needs: (1) upgrading trade infrastructure to address supply chain vulnerabilities, and (2) developing adaptive prediction systems for climate and conflict-related shocks. The study illustrates how artificial intelligence may shift food security responses from reactive to preventive, with real-time risk mapping allowing for targeted interventions where they are most required.

title: Precision agriculture meets machine learning
abstract: Agriculture is a cornerstone of global food security, yet crop productivity is increasingly threatened by the complex interplay of climatic and agronomic factors. This chapter employs Random Forest Regression (RFR), a robust machine learning algorithm, to predict crop yield by analyzing key variables such as temperature, precipitation, solar radiation, fertilization, and irrigation. Using a dataset sourced from Kaggle, the model achieved an R² value of 0.9773 and a Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) of 14,134.64 hg/ha, demonstrating its strong predictive capability. Feature importance analysis revealed that crop type and geographical region were the most influential factors, followed by average rainfall, pesticide usage, and temperature. The findings underscore the importance of localized and crop-specific agricultural strategies to enhance productivity and resilience in the face of climate change. This research contributes to the growing field of precision agriculture by providing data-driven insights for optimizing farming practices and ensuring sustainable food production.

title: Digital Guardians
abstract: This chapter has studied the use of artificial intelligence (AI) in smart pest management in the agricultural field. Our focus is on smallholder farmers who reside in low- and middle-income countries. For a living, approximately 100 million farmers rely on cotton. An effective pest control system increases productivity. They mitigate pests and threats of variable climate. Image recognition, machine learning (ML) algorithms, and predictive analytics are the AI-driven approaches we have talked about. They help the professionals control the pest by making fast decisions. The chapter examines the utility of AI tools in diverse range of agricultural settings. We focus on how effective they are to deliver localized recommendations and improve crop management techniques. Key findings from recent studies show that adapting AI helps us to gain crop yields, reduce the use of pesticides, and ensure more profits for farmers. These breakthroughs are significant because they can transform the process of managing resources. With them, major global issues, including food security and climate change, seem to be solved. Future AI research in agriculture will focus on improving the flexibility of the model so that it can work in different situations. Data should be more accessible, and AI solutions should be affordable to smallholder farmers. Ultimately, our chapter calls for continuation in innovation that will empower farmers and promote sustainability in agricultural practices all over the world.

title: Predictive Analytics for Better Crop Management and Production using Machine Learning
abstract: Predictive analytics and machine learning have appeared as powerful tools, capitalizing on the wealth of agricultural data to inform data-driven decisions for farmers and agribusinesses. Traditional crop management relied on historical practices, often limited by their inability to leverage modern data sources such as climate data, soil characteristics, and real-time sensor data. In contrast, predictive analytics, underpinned by machine learning algorithms, taps into this data to offer accurate forecasts and actionable insights. Ensuring food security and sustainable agriculture relies significantly on the effective management and production of crops. This paper presents a comprehensive overview of the utilization of predictive analytics and machine learning in the context of crop management and production, focusing on their applications, challenges, and potential benefits. It emphasizes the necessity for interdisciplinary collaboration between scientists, agriculturalists, technology developers, and policymakers to overcome barriers and foster the widespread adoption of predictive analytics in agriculture.

title: Unlocking the Potential of AI in the Water Sector
abstract: The growing challenges in water quality (WQ) management driven by population growth, industrial activity, and climate change, pose serious risks to public health, food security, and environmental sustainability. Traditional monitoring methods often fall short in dynamic or resource-limited contexts. This chapter explores how artificial intelligence (AI), in conjunction with the Internet of Things (IoT), cloud computing, and advanced analytics, is transforming water management across critical sectors such as surface and river waters, drinking water systems, aquaculture systems, and wastewater treatment. A particular focus is placed on the integration of continual learning (CL), a branch of machine learning (ML) that enables systems to adapt to new data without forgetting prior knowledge. By addressing issues like catastrophic forgetting, CL enhances the robustness of predictive models over time. The chapter presents two use cases of modern aquaculture and the enhancement of wastewater quality forecasting through a CL approach. Comparative insights highlight the relevance of CL techniques such as experience replay (ER), adaptive experience replay (AER), and learning without forgetting based on knowledge distillation (LwF-KD). Overall, this chapter argues that AI and CL offer sustainable, real-time, and adaptive solutions to the complex demands of modern WQ management, particularly in decentralized or water-scarce regions.

title: The Role of Artificial Intelligence in Agriculture
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has recently seen widespread use in farming. The agriculture sector is leveraging AI technology to grow healthier crops, control pests, track soil growth conditions and improve various other management aspects within the food supply chain. AI models, especially those using machine learning and computer vision, support quick, data-driven decisions, improving farm activities and reducing waste. Remote sensing, robotics, and automated machines are also transforming harvesting and post-harvest handling, cutting down labor needs and enhancing food quality. AI aids climate-resilient agriculture by analyzing large data sets from weather, soil, and crop sensors to predict environmental stresses and maintain equipment. This helps ensure food security in the face of climate challenges. However, adopting AI in farming faces challenges, including high setup costs, data privacy concerns, and the need for technical knowledge among farmers. This chapter explores how AI supports various agricultural activities, such as crop monitoring, precision farming, yield forecasting, pest and disease detection, and smart irrigation. By making AI tools accessible, agriculture can meet the needs of a growing global population while protecting natural resources. Achieving this requires collaboration among researchers, policymakers, and farmers to overcome AI adoption barriers for sustainable agriculture.

title: Forecasting Agricultural Commodity Prices with ARIMA Models
abstract: Agricultural product sales represent a critical convergence within the supply chain and act as the essential bridge between consumer and farmer. It also impacts overall product availability and economic stability. In countries like India, where a major number of people depend on agriculture directly or indirectly, accurate prediction of agricultural commodity prices becomes useful for ensuring financial stability and food security. The price of agricultural products is a critical measure of market focus framed by a complex interplay of factors like production costs, consumer demand, and government policies. However, a significant information asymmetry between producers and markets often leads to pre-eminent price fluctuations, posing challenges for farmers and consumers. The outcome of this paper is to show how historical price data helps forecast future prices, how these predictions help make better decisions, and how they affect the supply chain system. Also, several forecasting techniques exist, like time series analysis regression techniques and machine learning algorithms. This paper uses historical data to forecast global grain prices such as coffee, wheat, and corn for the next one years. The results were obtained using Python and a univariate ARIMA (Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average) technique. These forecasts help farmers make better decisions and impact investment tactics, crop selection, and resource plans.

title: Artificial Intelligence for Advancing Plant Genome Editing and Precision Breeding
abstract: This chapter details the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into plant genome editing and precision breeding, focusing on how AI is revolutionizing crop improvement through data-driven decision-making and enhanced genetic innovation. The content explores AI-powered methods for guide RNA design, off-target prediction, and functional genomics, demonstrating how deep learning models increase the precision and efficiency of CRISPR and other genome editing tools. Case studies across major crops highlight practical applications where AI and machine learning optimize traits like disease resistance, stress tolerance, yield, and quality by leveraging multi-omics data, trait mapping, and predictive phenotyping. Ethical, regulatory, and technological challenges are also examined, highlighting the role of explainable AI and evolving computational platforms in ensuring responsible, future-ready agricultural biotechnology. Collectively, these advances position AI-guided genome editing and precision breeding as transformative technologies for sustainable food production and global food security.

title: Artificial Intelligence Approaches in Plant Digital Multiple Omics
abstract: The artificial intelligence (AI) integration in plant digital multiple omics has transformed plant research by increasing data assessment, explanation, and predictive modeling. AI-driven applications, encompassing deep learning (DL) and machine learning (ML), enable the extraction of impactful insights from large-scale genomic, proteomic, phenomic, metabolomic, and transcriptomic datasets. These technologies facilitate correct trait choice, gene expression analysis, and stress tolerance prediction, thereby increasing crop advancement programs. AI models, such as recurrent neural networks and convolutional neural networks (CNNs), have been successfully used for accurate breeding and high-throughput phenotyping. Furthermore, incorporative AI frameworks permit a systems biology strategy and bridge gaps among omics layers to elucidate complicated plant-climate interactions. Current innovations in AI-assisted image analysis and natural language processing further increase digital farming by yield forecasting and automating disease detection. Despite its revolutionized potential, AI applications in plant multiple omics pose problems such as limited annotated datasets, data heterogeneity, and the requirement for standardized computational frameworks. Determining these constraints needs interdisciplinary cooperation between agronomists, data scientists, and biologists. Future AI-driven multi-omics applications promise to develop climate-resilient crops, improve agricultural sustainability, and increase food security through automated decision-making and predictive analytics. Future studies should focus on producing AI-powered, multi-omics platforms based on clouds with organized data-sharing protocols to increase reproducibility and interoperability in plant sciences.

title: Technical Advancements and Emerging Applications of Artificial Intelligence in Plant Research
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is revolutionizing plant research by offering innovative solutions to enhance productivity, understand plant systems, and tackle global challenges like food security and climate change. The topic explores the application of AI technologies such as machine learning, computer vision, and predictive analytics in precision agriculture, phenotyping, plant breeding, and stress management. AI optimizes resource use in precision agriculture by analyzing data from satellites, drones, and sensors to monitor crop health, predict yields, and manage inputs efficiently. High-throughput phenotyping powered by AI accelerates trait measurement, enabling rapid analysis of growth and environmental interactions. In plant breeding, AI identifies genetic markers for desirable traits, streamlining the development of climate-resilient crops. It also plays a critical role in stress management by predicting and mitigating biotic and abiotic stresses while addressing climate change through applications like carbon sequestration modeling and smart greenhouse automation. Through real-world examples, this chapter demonstrates how AI-powered tools are reshaping plant science, providing scalable solutions to boost productivity, promote sustainability, and enhance resilience against environmental challenges, paving the way for a sustainable, food-secure future.

title: Machine Learning in Plant Biology
abstract: This chapter provides a critical and comprehensive examination of the transformative role of machine learning (ML) in plant biology, seamlessly bridging its fundamental principles with a diverse array of high-impact applications. It begins by delineating core ML paradigms, including supervised learning (e.g., linear/logistic regression, decision trees, random forests, support vector machines for classification and regression), unsupervised learning (e.g., K-means clustering, principal component analysis for pattern discovery and dimensionality reduction), and deep learning through artificial neural networks, convolutional neural networks for image analysis, and recurrent neural networks for sequential data. The text meticulously details the essential ML workflow in plant research, covering critical steps from meticulous data collection and preprocessing (e.g., high-throughput imaging, omics data normalization), to feature engineering and selection, robust model training and validation (emphasizing cross-validation and overfitting mitigation), and sophisticated model evaluation and interpretation, including the emerging role of explainable AI. Crucially, this chapter rigorously explores the diverse, high-impact applications of ML that are revolutionizing data-driven discovery in plant science. These applications span: plant phenotyping (accelerated high-throughput image analysis for growth and development, precise disease detection and stress identification, and accurate yield prediction); plant genomics and genetics (enhanced gene prediction and annotation, inference of gene regulatory networks, accelerated genomic selection and marker-assisted breeding, and epigenetic analysis); plant physiology and metabolism (reconstruction of metabolic pathways, prediction of environmental stress responses, and optimization of nutrient uptake and efficiency); plant pathology and pest management (rapid pathogen identification and classification, assessment of disease severity and spread prediction, and intelligent integrated pest management strategies); and ecology and environmental plant science (species distribution modeling for climate change impacts, large-scale biodiversity monitoring, and advanced ecosystem modeling for carbon sequestration). This chapter also addresses key challenges to the full realization of ML’s potential, such as data quality and availability, the need for increased model interpretability, scalability issues with large datasets, and the necessity for enhanced interdisciplinary collaboration. It projects immense opportunities for predictive plant biology through emerging trends, including advanced multi-omics data integration, causal inference, the rise of Automated ML (AutoML) platforms, the synergy with robotics and autonomous systems, and the implementation of Edge AI for real-time applications. This comprehensive overview serves as an indispensable guide for researchers, practitioners, and policymakers aiming to leverage advanced computational methodologies for transformative breakthroughs in agricultural innovation, fundamental botanical understanding, and global food security.

title: Artificial Intelligence for Plant 3D Spatial Omics
abstract: Recently, omics and artificial intelligence (AI) have been emerging as important tools for biological studies, including plants. It begins with outlining those four core disciplines, including genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, and metabolomics, which combine to strengthen plant systems-level research through multi-level analyses. The 3D omics concept surpasses classical omics by gaining spatial dimensions to map cellular components inside plant tissues, hence giving much larger perspectives on developmental processes and stress responses. Processing of large datasets that flow out of these technologies highly improves AI 3D omics. These algorithms can be easily integrated with data, predictive modeling, and advanced phenotyping of crops through machine learning and deep learning. Subsequently, this results in the discovery of complex molecular interactions that develop crops with resilient varieties. Besides this, several applications of AI in developing disease resistance markers and crop development through targeted breeding strategies have been narrated in this chapter. It presents challenges such as a lack of clarity in the transparency of the algorithm and requires heavy intensive computation. Such would need interdisciplinary collaborations among plant biologists, data scientists, and AI experts to fully unleash the total potential of AI-assisted 3D omics, which aims to attempt to solve some of the global challenges about climate change and food security issues. All this synergy is promised to revolutionize crop improvement strategies and promises much deeper insights into plant biology in increasingly complex environments.

title: Artificial Intelligence-Accelerated Crop Improvement
abstract: The growing challenges of food security and climate change demand a rapid transformation in crop improvement strategies. Traditional breeding and crop development methods, while foundational, are often time-intensive and limited in their capacity to address the complexities of modern agricultural needs. Artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a disruptive technology, providing the tools to significantly accelerate crop improvement processes. This chapter delves into the integration of AI across the crop improvement pipeline, focusing on advancements that enhance the speed and precision of trait identification, genomic selection, and breeding optimization. Cutting-edge machine learning, deep learning, and reinforcement learning algorithms have enabled precise genotype–phenotype predictions and real-time decision-making. AI-powered high-throughput data integration, encompassing genomics, transcriptomics, and phenomics, accelerates the identification of stress-resilient genes and pathways. Furthermore, the application of AI in optimizing gene-editing workflows, designing CRISPR-based interventions, and automating phenotyping processes has dramatically shortened breeding cycles. The use of predictive models in speed breeding and climate-resilient crop development is also discussed, emphasizing the transformative potential of virtual environments and real-time analytics. Despite these advancements, challenges such as data quality, computational scalability, and ethical implications persist. The chapter concludes by exploring emerging trends like explainable AI, federated learning, and edge computing, underscoring their potential to revolutionize agricultural systems. By bridging technological innovations with sustainable practices, AI promises to redefine global agriculture, accelerating crop improvement to meet the growing demands of a rapidly changing world.

title: Introductory Chapter
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is going to shift the way one thinks about plant protection in agriculture. Powered by AI, solutions underway will disrupt best practices in pest and disease management: early detection, diagnostics, and prevention with accuracy at high-speed navigator information on issues to do with plant health. Machine learning, computer vision, and predictive analytics drive more informed data-driven decisions made by farmers and agronomists, reducing waste of resources and impacts on the environment. The interplay of AI with IoT devices, smart sensors and drones wins in real-time collection of data regarding the state of health of plants, weather patterns, and soil conditions. From this rich trove of information, it elaborates highly tailored, precision-based avenues for the management of pests and diseases leading to crop productivity and reduction in costs, hence enhancing food security. Today, scientists and professionals take a step further as AI in plant protection serves the evolution with generative models pointing to novel, environmentally friendly bioinsecticides. Coupling them with autonomous robotic systems introduces targeted on-demand interventions, this can someday revolutionize sustainable agriculture and pave ways toward resilient and food-secure futures.

title: Integration of AI with Precision Agriculture for Targeted Pest Control
abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) with precision agriculture has revolutionized targeted pest control by enabling early pest detection, predictive analytics, and precise pesticide application. With AI-driven technologies, such as remote sensing, IoT, drones, and machine learning models, it is possible to monitor crop health and pest population in real-time, minimizing the relevant use of chemicals and environmental impact. These technologies can facilitate proactive management policies, enhance crop productivity, reduce the cost of inputs and encourage eco-sustainable farming. This chapter covers AI-based pest detection system, autonomous robots, and data analytics to enhance the decision-making process, which ensures efficient solutions to pest control that are accurate and environmental-friendly. Focusing on the future of the possibility, the chapter shows the continuing innovations and obstacles to using AI to manage pests as a key to sustainable agriculture and world food security.

title: Plant Pest Monitoring Remote Sensing, Image Processing and Artificial Intelligence
abstract: Plant pest infestations represent a major constraint in agricultural productivity, causing significant yield losses and threatening global food security. Timely and accurate pest monitoring is essential for effective pest management and sustainable crop production. Traditionally, monitoring practices have relied on manual observation methods, which are labor-intensive, inconsistent, and inadequate for large-scale farming systems. Recent advancements in digital technologies have introduced more efficient and scalable solutions. This chapter explores the integration of remote sensing, image processing, and artificial intelligence (AI) in plant pest monitoring. Remote sensing techniques, using satellite imagery and unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), enable large-scale surveillance by capturing critical data on crop health. Image processing plays a pivotal role in detecting and identifying pests through techniques such as image enhancement, feature extraction, segmentation, and classification. Furthermore, AI algorithms, including machine learning models and deep neural networks, automate the interpretation of complex datasets, enabling real-time detection and predictive modeling of pest outbreaks. The synergy of these technologies offers a transformative approach to precision agriculture, enhancing the speed, accuracy, and reliability of pest monitoring systems. This chapter also presents real-world applications, analyzes current challenges, and discusses future prospects for the widespread adoption of these methods. The insights provided aim to support researchers, practitioners, and policymakers in developing advanced pest surveillance strategies for resilient and sustainable agriculture.

title: Evaluating smart farming technologies: A comprehensive review
abstract: The combination of cloud computing, machine learning, and the internet of things has created smart agriculture a possible answer to current agricultural issues. This study investigates how the aforementioned technologies affect agriculture, with an emphasis on enhanced agricultural productivity, sustainability, and resource control. IoT sensors in the smart farm detect environmental conditions and soil moisture in real time, as well as the plant&s;s health. Large-scale IoT data enables machine learning algorithms to do predictive analytics in pest management, disease diagnosis, water application, and other fields. Cloud technologies allow for centralized processing, analysis, and storage, as well as collaboration with partners and the farm. Farmers may take use of the cloud&s;s scalability and flexibility to produce more with less. Cutting-edge agriculture allows for greater inventiveness and adaptable cultivation solutions, but innovative new solutions are also required to solve gaps in rural growth, food security, and food security. Farms grow smarter with the help of IoT-driven gadgets and sensors, allowing for more efficient management and troop administration. Based on current historical data, machine learning will assist in carrying out the study particular to planting time and the finest agricultural items to cultivate. The solutions, which are based on cloud technology, would allow diverse stakeholders to interact and exchange data, modernizing the supply chain and farmers’ market access. The integration of IoT, Amazon Web Services, and machine intelligence heralds the start of an information-based farming era that will transform the sector. Smart farming not only improves output and sustainability, but it also addresses fundamental issues, resulting in a more stable and potent agricultural environment.

title: Optimizing fertilizer recommendations through fuzzy logic and soil nutrient analysis for advancing precision agriculture
abstract: This research concentrates on how fuzzy logic used in the realm of precision agriculture can make information more available to farmers, with emphasis on plant nutrition and fertilization. Our focus, in this regard, has been on fertilizer recommendations based upon background soil nitrogen levels for optimal fertilizer applications. The utility of different models (IT2ANFIS, CNN, LSTM, and SVM) in predicting appropriate fertilizers for different soil types was investigated. Real-time data consisting of soil nutrient levels and fertilizer recommendations are used to train and evaluate these models. The IT2ANFIS model, it turns out, has the highest accuracy in recommending fertilizer followed by CNN, LSTM, and SVM. This implies a future of using advanced machine learning to better meet crop demands. This research both strengthens precision agriculture and pushes the frontier further by providing insights into various machine learning models for soil fertility management. For their practical implementation in agricultural settings, these models should be further developed and validated. This will also support sustainable farming practices and fulfill our commitment to global food security.

title: Multidimensional Aspects of Zero Hunger in Sub-Saharan Africa
abstract: This article explores the multifaceted challenges and strategies for achieving Sustainable Development Goal 2 (SDG 2)—zero hunger—in Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA). Despite global efforts, hunger has worsened since 2015 due to Covid-19, regional conflicts, and climate change, significantly impacting SSA. We discuss the current state of hunger, undernourishment and food insecurity in SSA, highlighting regional disparities and exacerbating factors like climate variability, conflict, economic instability, and health issues. A detailed examination of East, West, and Southern African countries reveals fluctuations in agricultural orientation indices, stored genetic resources, and food price anomalies, underscoring the need for strategic investments and robust policies. We emphasize integrating food security, nutrition, sustainable agriculture, social equity, economic development, and environmental conservation. Key strategies include investments in agriculture, social protection programs, climate adaptation, nutrition interventions, market access, capacity building, and women&s;s empowerment. The transformative potential of smart technologies offers innovative solutions to improve agricultural productivity, sustainability, and resilience including precision agriculture, climate-smart practices, blockchain for market access, mobile applications for nutrition, and early warning systems. In conclusion, addressing hunger and food insecurity in SSA require national, regional, and international coordinated actions, sustained commitments, strategic investments, and leveraging smart technologies to achieving zero hunger in SSA.

title: Harmony in Harvest: Machine Learning's Symphony for Sustainable Agriculture
abstract: Global population increase and food scarcity are the two biggest obstacles to sustainable development. machine learning revolutionises agriculture by predicting optimal crop types. Utilizing a dataset of 2200 observations on agricultural parameters, including soil nutrients and environmental factors, four machine learning models were evaluated. Results show Random Forest (91.23%), Light Gradient Boosting Machine (92%), and Naive Bayes (96.2%) as top performers, highlighting their ability to comprehend complex relationships. In contrast, Decision Stump exhibited lower accuracy (36.36%). This underscores the efficacy of ensemble methods in predicting crop suitability. By leveraging machine learning, farmers can optimise productivity and resource management, ensuring sustainable agricultural practices for enhanced profitability and food security.

title: Integrated crop recommendation
abstract: A trend called “smart agriculture” places a focus on using information technology in farming. India&s;s population is largely dependent on agriculture. This circumstance is one of the factors concerning the nation&s;s development. When farmers attain a better yield from their crop, but the commodity&s;s market price is lower, they incur losses for their products. While growing novel crops, farmers are especially vulnerable to production problems and market price volatility. One way to address these problems is by utilizing machine learning technologies. Using machine learning technology, these issues are solved. Data mining&s;s branch of predictive analysis foresees probability and trends in the future. Farmers will be able to determine which crop is most suited for a specific rainfall and crop price range thanks to the forecast. This method aims to increase the crop&s;s net yield rate in response to rainfall. XG Boost, Decision Tree, AdaBoost, Support Vector Machine, and Random Forest are the 5 algorithms employed in this article. Apart from these algorithms, Decision Tree algorithms outperform the others in terms of accuracy.

title: Predictive analytics for crop yield optimization
abstract: Predictive analytics, driven by artificial intelligence (AI), is revolutionizing modern agriculture by providing actionable insights to optimize crop yield. This chapter explores how AI technologies, including machine learning and deep learning models, analyze data from diverse sources such as Internet of Things (IoT) sensors, satellite imagery, and historical weather patterns to forecast crop performance and maximize agricultural productivity. By integrating predictive models with precision farming practices, farmers can make informed decisions about resource allocation, pest management, and irrigation scheduling. This chapter also discusses the challenges of data quality, model interpret ability, and technological adoption, while highlighting real-world case studies that demonstrate successful implementations. Through predictive analytics, agriculture is transitioning into a data-driven industry, enabling sustainable practices and ensuring global food security.

title: In Silico Approaches for Green Agriculture
abstract: As the world faces mounting environmental challenges, the need for sustainable and eco-friendly agricultural practices has become increasingly urgent. In this context, in silico approaches have emerged as powerful tools for advancing green agriculture. The applications and benefits of in silico approaches in pursuing sustainable agricultural solutions are diverse. In silico approaches encompass a range of computational and modelling techniques that enable researchers to simulate and analyze complex biological systems. These approaches have been instrumental in green agriculture’s crop improvement, pest management, and resource optimization. By leveraging large-scale datasets, bioinformatics, and machine learning algorithms, in silico approaches facilitate the identification of novel plant traits, develop stress-tolerant varieties, and optimise crop yields. Furthermore, in silico modelling allows for exploring diverse scenarios and predicting outcomes, 284 enabling farmers and policymakers to make informed decisions. It aids in designing and evaluating sustainable farming practices, such as precision agriculture, where resources such as fertilizers, pesticides and water are utilized efficiently, minimizing environmental impact. By integrating in silico approaches into green agriculture, we can harness the power of technology to address the urgent challenges of climate change, food security, and environmental sustainability. This abstract highlights the potential of in silico approaches to revolutionize agricultural practices, leading to a greener and more resilient future.

title: A comparative investigation of machine learning algorithms for crop yield forecast and agricultural optimization
abstract: In this study, crop yield forecast is studied by machine-learning methods with respect to accuracy and reliability. Using algorithms like Decision Trees, Random Forests, Support Vector Machines (SVM), Neural Networks, XGBoost, and LightGBM the research scatters environmental elements, for instance rainfall, temperature, type of soil, and agriculture, for example fertilizer and irrigation utilization. With highest performance of key metrics like accurateness, exactness, recall and F1 score, Random Forest model made itself the best model capable of doing complex, nonlinear data relationship. The rainfall and irrigation frequency were found to be the two factors that affect the crop yield significantly using statistical tests such as ANOVA and Chi Square. This suggests that machine learning is a viable means towards improving the productivity of the agricultural resource. The inputs from the study can serve to guide farmers, agricultural policymakers and stakeholders in implementing data based sustainable farming strategies for better food security.

title: Yield prediction of corn crops using machine learning techniques
abstract: Precise prediction of crop yield is critical for food security, optimize allocation of resources, and enhancing agricultural decision-making. However, predicting crop yields in agricultural environments is complex challenge due to change in climate, biodiversity of soil, and farming routines. We present an machine learning approach to improve the accuracy & robustness of crop yield predictions. The implementation of the ML models is evaluated using key metrics such as CCI, Mean absolute error, RMS (Root mean square) error and Kappa statistics. This study highlights the potential use of machine learning techniques as a powerful tool for precision agriculture. ML models can provide useful information for farmers and policymakers in managing crop production under complex and dynamic conditions.

title: Challenges with Practical Solutions and Case Studies
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) accelerates the traditional way of farming by implementing modern approaches that enhance production, minimise resources, and improve predictive decision-making ability in the domain of agriculture. It also enables better solutions for various environmental problems. Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is an advanced subset of artificial intelligence that enables emerging technologies that support sustainable crop management, effective biodiversity conservation, contributing to economic development by utilising a range of predictive models, including Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), Autoencoders, Transformers, Diffusion Models, and Autoregressive models, as well as the real-time object detection algorithm YOLO (You Only Look Once), GenAI transforming crop management by enabling predictions of crop yields, facilitating weed control, diagnosing diseases, and supporting precision farming. Integration of GenAI, machine learning (ML), and deep learning (DL) with IoT (Internet of Things) devices opens up a new avenue in the sector of digital agriculture to facilitate real-time decision-making. Traditional farming is no longer adequate to satisfy consumer demand, and crop management can often be complicated and laborious; therefore, it is necessary to integrate traditional agriculture with modern computerised technologies such as GenAI to increase crop management efficiency and stimulate changes in the agribusiness sectors—even among rural farming communities. This chapter has demonstrated the need for GenAI tools in solving environmental issues, including agriculture, providing an overview of the processes, current applications, further potential applications, and limitations of GenAI tools in agriculture and other problems related to the environment. GenAI could potentially be a revolutionary force, enhancing human resilience and managing food security.

title: Economic efficiency through livestock production monitoring and prediction in smart agriculture
abstract: Livestock constitutes a critical component of agricultural systems, contributing significantly to the global economy and food security. In 2023, the livestock sector accounted for approximately 40% of the global agricultural output, underscoring its economic significance. The integration of smart agriculture technologies, particularly the Internet of Things (IoT) and advanced sensor technologies, has revolutionized livestock farming. Real-time data collection through these technologies facilitates precise monitoring and management of livestock health, reproduction, and productivity. Incorporating data analytics and predictive modelling into livestock farming enables the identification of patterns and trends that enhance decision-making processes. For instance, precision livestock farming (PLF) utilizes data to optimize resource management, improve reproductive efficiency, and ensure better disease prevention and control. Studies indicate that the application of machine learning algorithms can predict livestock diseases with an accuracy rate of over 90%, significantly reducing mortality rates and improving overall herd health. Moreover, the deployment of IoT devices has led to a 20% increase in productivity and a 15% reduction in operational costs, highlighting the economic benefits of technology adoption in livestock farming. However, challenges such as data privacy concerns, technical implementation difficulties, and economic barriers persist. Addressing these challenges requires robust data security measures, infrastructure development, and supportive policies. Future trends point towards the increased use of blockchain for traceability, artificial intelligence for enhanced predictive analytics, and sustainable practices to mitigate environmental impact, ensuring a resilient and efficient livestock farming sector.

title: A Hybrid Machine Learning Approach for Accurate Crop Yield Forecasting
abstract: Accurate crop yield forecasting is essential for enhancing farm productivity, ensuring food security, and supporting informed agricultural decision-making. Traditional prediction methods, often based solely on historical trends or limited environmental variables, struggle to capture the complex interactions in modern farming systems. This study proposes a hybrid machine learning framework that integrates historical crop yield records, soil health data, and climatic patterns with real-time inputs from high-resolution satellite imagery, drone-based sensing, and IoT-enabled soil sensors. Multiple models, including Linear Regression, Support Vector Machines (SVM), K-Nearest Neighbors (KNNs), Decision Tree, Random Forest, and XGBoost-based ensemble learning, were trained and validated using publicly available Kaggle datasets covering multiple crops and regions. The proposed approach consistently outperformed traditional statistical methods, reducing prediction errors by 18%–32% and achieving the highest accuracy with the ensemble model (R² = 0.93). The findings demonstrate the effectiveness of combining multimodal datasets with advanced machine learning techniques to improve yield prediction, enabling proactive interventions such as optimized input application, risk management, and targeted pest control. This work highlights the potential of hybrid, data-driven systems to advance precision agriculture and enhance resilience in the face of climate variability.

title: Soyabean leaf detection dataset using machine learning
abstract: The worldwide food security stands threatened by soybean leaf diseases which cause critical crop deficiencies when quick disease detection and management fail to occur. The detection of diseases at an early stage, combined with precise disease types identification remains key to protecting farm yield and implementing effective disease response strategies. The research evaluates disease recognition and classification of soybean leaf diseases through Random Forest classifier applications. Leaves with different size distributions and water levels and varying disease indications enable the model to categorize diverse foliar diseases. The system utilizes a public soybean disease dataset through several preprocessing operations where it removes unnecessary columns before applying categorical data transformation alongside missing values treatment. The cleaned dataset enables the Random Forest classifier to perform its training process before the predictive performance of the model gets evaluated. The analysis employs bar plots and box plots together with scatter plots to show distributions and correlations in the data thus improving model interpretability. This approach delivers a systematic and expandable method which enables agronomists along with researchers and farmers to identify soybean diseases accurately so they can immediately respond and reduce crop yield loss potential. The integration of machine learning in agricultural disease detection by this study assists in exact farming advancement through data-driven crop health management approaches allowing better food security.

title: Combating food insecurity through remote sensing and machine learning for enhanced crop yield prediction
abstract: This work introduces a fresh strategy for combating food insecurity by combining agricultural yield prediction based on machine learning with remote sensing technology. Improving agricultural production and resource management rely heavily on reliable yield predictions, according to the study. The suggested approach accurately predicts crop yields by analyzing environmental variables using powerful machine learning techniques and a large dataset gathered from different agricultural regions. The study shows how various models perform in terms of various performance measures. These models include random forest (RF), support vector machines (SVM), and K-nearest neighbors (K-NN). This study’s ensemble learning method achieves better prediction accuracy of 92.1% which is better than conventional models and offers policymakers and farmers practical insights. The findings aim to improve decision-making, optimize resource allocation, and contribute to food security initiatives by harnessing these advanced technologies.

title: Leveraging Artificial Intelligence for the Detection, Monitoring, and Forecasting of Plant Diseases
abstract: Plant diseases significantly impact agricultural yield, food security, and economic stability. Traditional disease detection methods are slow, laborious, and prone to errors, demanding automated solutions. The introduction of Artificial Intelligence (AI), particularly deep learning (DL) and machine learning (ML) over the last decade, has transformed identification, tracking, and forecasting of plant diseases. AI models, such as convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and transfer learning techniques, improve classification accuracy while addressing challenges like data insufficiency, environmental variability, and overfitting. Hyperspectral imaging and image processing enhance disease recognition, allowing early interventions. This chapter explores AI-driven approaches for detecting major plant diseases along with key AI applications, including mobile-based disease classification, IoT-integrated precision agriculture, and real-time disease forecasting. Additionally, the detailed information about evaluation metrics, including accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score, that determine model reliability has been discussed. The information about available open-source plant disease detection datasets has been tabulated in the chapter. Moreover, the methods and results of the studies that developed successful AI models for various plant disease detection have been outlined. In conclusion, AI-driven plant disease detection offers promising benefits for sustainable farming, helping mitigate yield losses and strengthen global food security.

title: AI Models for Advancing Plant Nanotechnology
abstract: With plant nanotechnology advances, artificial intelligence (AI) models are becoming more and more important, especially when it comes to optimizing nanomaterials for use in agriculture and enabling advancements in precision agriculture, plant biology, and sustainable food production. With an emphasis on the design, delivery, and safety profiles of nanomaterials, this abstract explores the incorporation of AI-driven methodologies to improve their effectiveness in plant systems. Researchers can improve nutrient delivery systems, optimize nanoparticle synthesis, and forecast interactions between nanoparticles and plant tissues by utilizing machine learning algorithms. In the face of global challenges, this synergistic relationship between AI and nanotechnology promises to produce creative solutions for crop improvement, pest resistance, and sustainable agricultural practices, ultimately enhancing food security. AI models are being used to optimize nanomaterials for plant growth, disease resistance, and environmental adaptation.

title: AI Models for Advancing Plant Abiotic Stress Research
abstract: Abiotic stresses such as drought, salinity, temperature extremes, and nutrient deficiencies impose severe constraints on plant growth, productivity, and global food security. Understanding and mitigating these stresses require the analysis of highly complex and dynamic interactions among molecular, physiological, and environmental factors. Artificial intelligence (AI) provides a transformative framework to address this challenge by enabling the integration, analysis, and interpretation of large, heterogeneous datasets. Through the combination of high-throughput phenotyping technologies – such as RGB, hyperspectral, thermal, and LiDAR imaging – with multi-omics data encompassing genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, and metabolomics, AI facilitates the identification of key biomarkers, regulatory networks, and adaptive mechanisms that underlie plant stress resilience. The inclusion of environmental, soil, and meteorological data further contextualizes plant responses and enhances model accuracy. Traditional machine learning algorithms, including Random Forests, Support Vector Machines, and Gradient Boosting models, have been successfully applied to stress classification, yield prediction, and trait selection. In contrast, advanced deep learning and transformer-based architectures exhibit superior performance in extracting hierarchical and temporal features from multimodal datasets, enabling early stress detection, precise phenotypic characterization, and real-time decision-making in precision agriculture. The integration of hybrid and multimodal AI models further enhances interpretability and predictive reliability, bridging the gap between data-driven insights and physiological understanding. Future perspectives emphasize the convergence of AI with systems biology, eco-physiological modeling, and sustainable breeding strategies to enhance predictive capacity, accelerate the development of stress-resilient cultivars, and support adaptive management in the face of climate variability.

title: AI Models for Plant Systems Biology
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has revolutionized plant systems biology via the possible combination of multi-omics data, higher-order modeling, and autonomous hypothesis construction. Through deep learning, machine learning, and hybrid models, AI interprets complex genotype–phenotype connections and aids predictive modeling of plant growth and development, metabolism, and environmental acclimatization. Multiscale and multi-omics merged models provide deeper insights into gene regulation, signaling, and metabolism, and generative and graph-based models provide dynamical and causal inference. Autonomous phenotyping based on AI, digital twin plants, and CRISPR genome editing optimizes crop improvement, environmental tolerance, and resource-efficient agriculture. Although data standardization, interpretation, and ethical regulation are issues, AI’s significance endures based on the improvement of precision agriculture, sustainability, and global food security. AI, IoT, and quantum computing intersection point offers a brilliant future of integrative, data-driven, and ethically responsible plant biology.

title: AI-Driven Agricultural Intelligence: Integrating Machine Learning, Computer Vision, and IoT for Smart Farming Systems
abstract: Technological advancements in Artificial Intelligence (AI) give rise to innovative perspectives on the persistent challenges of global food security, and compel us to find solutions despite simultaneous threats from climate change, disrupted supply chains, and population rise. This paper merges HCI’s technological answers and futurist perspectives on AI, and shows that AI-enabled technologies such as machine learning, computer vision, and predictive analytics have the ability to improve the agricultural sector on several fronts. Firstly, AI can improve precision agriculture; as well as its use to optimize resource inputs throughout agricultural processes; and enhance supply chains. In our research, we examine both academic research and practitioner applications, as we promote the opportunities and threats facing AI applications in agriculture, particularly in the developing world. More specifically, we highlight improvements in productivity, reductions in resource inputs, and the ability to identify early disease occurrences using AI applications, because scalability, affordability and equity are important here. We conclude on the awareness that data-driven and interdisciplinary model approaches will be imperative for agriculture in the future, to develop sustainability and resiliency.

title: Hybrid machine learning models for the prediction and recommendation of different types of crops disease: A review
abstract: Food security across the globe and economic stability ,agriculture has an indispensable role.With artificial intelligence,the role of predictive analytics has transformed crop selection, yield prediction, and recommendation systems to a higher level. Consequently, hybrid models integrating more than one machine learning and deep learning algorithms have surfaced as a successful way to increase prediction accuracy and adaptability. The paper discusses several hybrid methods used in crop prediction and recommendation systems. It discusses the integration of several ML models, such as decision trees, support vector machines, and neural networks with advanced ensemble methods and deep learning methods. It also gives a brief account of the role of feature selection, data preprocessing, and optimization techniques in enhancing model performance. Other than major issues pertaining to data availability, interpretability of models, and computational complexity, some solutions for future studies are also recommended. The paper assesses the performance of hybrid learning models for agricultural decision-making in light of current advancements, providing contributions toward precision farming and sustaining agricultural practices. Keywords: Agriculture, Crop prediction, Machine learning, Deep learning, Hybrid model, Feature extraction.

title: The digital field: Integrating IoT and deep learning for agricultural excellence
abstract: In modern agriculture, the effective utilization of resources and accurate forecasting of crop yield have become paramount concerns. Emerging technologies, such as the Internet of Things and deep learning, offer promising solutions to address these challenges. The integration of these two technologies is transforming agriculture in to smart agriculture due to improved decision making automated system as well as optimized resource utilization. This research paper presents transformative effect on agriculture due to integration of these technologies. This work emphasize the use of IoT for water management and automated system as well as use of deep learning in yield prediction and fertilizers recommendation. The synergy between IoT and DL provides scalable and intelligent solutions, promoting sustainable farming practices and supporting global food security. Furthermore, the paper discusses challenges such as network connectivity, data security, and the high initial cost of IoT infrastructure, suggesting potential solutions for these issues. This research highlights the significant advancements and future potential of IoT and DL in addressing the evolving needs of the agricultural sector.

title: Predictive efficacy assessment of deep learning models for apple leaf disease detection and classification
abstract: Plant diseases significantly impact agricultural productivity and food security. As such, the automation of disease detection using advanced technologies such as deep learning is important and crucial to timely intervene and minimise crop losses. In this study, the Kaggle apple dataset was used with the aim of analysing using deep learning models and different approaches for colour representation. The pre-processing methods include Histogram, Contrast Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization (CLAHE), and Hue-SaturationValue (HSV). Various combinations are recorded for several assessment metrics, including accuracy, precision, loss, and recall, and they are compared. The results show that the accuracy of disease detection is always higher if we employ HSV technique on the apple dataset, providing evidence in favour of the effectiveness of HSV for disease detection. In particular, MobileNet and ResNet50 were noted to have high accuracy, and MobileNet even manages to top the automated disease detection in apple leaves. In addition, this study also provides the effectiveness of colour representation techniques in improving deep learning models for disease detection in apple orchards.

title: Leveraging Machine Learning for Weather Condition Prediction and Enhanced Crop Production in Agriculture
abstract: Machine learning techniques have revolutionized the agricultural sector by enabling the understanding, prediction, and adaptation of weather conditions. Traditional methods of weather forecasting often fail to provide timely and accurate predictions, leading to the development of predictive models that can anticipate weather fluctuations with unprecedented accuracy. This allows farmers to make informed decisions, such as selecting optimal planting times and crop varieties and managing irrigation and pest control strategies. Personalized weather forecasting systems provide localized predictions tailored to specific agricultural plots, accounting for microclimates and regional variations. This precision empowers farmers to adopt site-specific strategies, mitigating risks and optimizing resource utilization. The integration of machine learning with agricultural practices extends beyond weather prediction, enhancing crop production through smart farming techniques. This results in a more sustainable and efficient approach to agriculture, ensuring food security and promoting environmental stewardship. This chapter explores machine learning-driven weather prediction methodologies, challenges, and success stories in agriculture, analyzing real-world case studies and advanced research to understand its potential to revolutionize weather forecasting and crop production.

title: Transforming agriculture and environmental monitoring with artificial intelligence
abstract: By facilitating data-driven decision-making and sustainable resource management, artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming environmental monitoring and agriculture. AI-powered solutions in agriculture improve crop monitoring, soil analysis, pest identification, and precision farming by utilizing machine learning, computer vision, and Internet of Things sensors. Increased crop yields, lower resource consumption, and less environmental impact are the results of these technologies’ optimization of irrigation, fertilization, and harvesting processes. AI systems use data from drones and satellite photography to evaluate soil nutrient levels, forecast illnesses, and track crop health in real time. AI makes it easier to analyze vast amounts of data for environmental monitoring, including deforestation, air and water quality, and climate change. Early warning systems and catastrophe risk reduction are made possible by sophisticated algorithms that analyze sensor data to forecast natural disasters. Furthermore, AI-powered drones and remote sensing tools offer ongoing environmental monitoring, supporting pollution prevention and biodiversity preservation. Climate-smart agriculture and environmental resilience are supported when AI is integrated with sustainable practices. AI has the potential to revolutionize global food security and environmental sustainability, notwithstanding obstacles in data privacy, model interpretability, and infrastructure. In order to promote innovation in sustainable agriculture and ecosystem management, ongoing research aims to increase the accuracy, scalability, and adaptation of AI models to a variety of ecosystems.

title: Data Sources and Sensors in Agriculture and Food Systems
abstract: The sudden and fast-paced digitalization of the agriculture and food system has made data sources and sensor technologies a key to sustainable, efficient, and resilient food production. The chapter gives an overall picture of how artificial intelligence (AI) can be used to harness the different sources of agricultural data and sensor networks to ensure data-driven decision-making throughout the agri-food value chain. It analyzes field-level, farm-to-fork, and supply chain information, including structured, semi-structured, and unstructured information that is produced by Internet of Things (IoT) devices, wireless sensor networks, remote sensing platforms, imaging systems, and wearable livestock sensors. This combination of heterogeneous data streams with AI methods, such as machine learning, deep learning, and multimodal data fusion, will allow real-time measurements of soil, crop, environmental, and animal health indicators, which will increase precision farming, post-harvest quality measurement, food safety, and livestock management. The chapter also explains the enabling infrastructures, which include IoT architectures, edge and cloud computing, communication protocols, and geospatial analytics that facilitate scalable and low-latency data processing. The major issues surrounding sensor reliability, calibration, data quality, interoperability, cybersecurity, cost, and adoption barriers are critically explored with a focus on their applicability to the smallholder and resource-restricted farming systems. The ethical, environmental, and governance issues of ownership of data, privacy, and sustainability are also discussed. Lastly, the future developments in the form of smart self-learning sensors, digital twins, and predictive food systems are featured as the progressive avenues to the improvement of climate resilience and policy-based sustainability in the agricultural sector. Generally, the chapter highlights the importance of successful intersections between AI, data sources, and sensor technologies as the key to creating intelligent, inclusive, and sustainable agriculture and food systems that will be able to sustain the global food security issues in the future.

title: Pest and Disease Forecasting with Time-Series Deep Models
abstract: Global agriculture faces escalating challenges from fluctuating pest and disease outbreaks, necessitating a shift from reactive to proactive control. Traditional predictive methods, often linear and limited in data integration, fail to capture the complexity, multimodality, spatiotemporal dynamics, and uncertainties of agroecological systems. This chapter presents a novel framework for pest and disease forecasting using explainable time-series deep learning models. Beyond conventional recurrent neural networks (RNNs) and long short-term memory (LSTM) models, we explore advanced architectures, such as causal Transformer networks and Graph Neural Networks (GNNs), to process heterogeneous data streams, including high-resolution satellite imagery, IoT sensor networks, genomic markers, and real-time microclimatic data. Emphasizing model interpretability and causal inference, this framework moves beyond black-box predictions to uncover outbreak drivers, fostering trust, rapid responses, and actionable insights. It incorporates advanced data fusion, agile feature learning from sparse and noisy farm data, and dynamic, self-correcting deep learning workflows for real-time adaptation. Through case studies, we demonstrate improved pre-emergence outbreak detection accuracy, optimized resource allocation for precision interventions, and robust predictive modelling across diverse environmental scenarios. This approach advances agricultural AI, promoting climate-resilient farming, minimizing environmental impact, and supporting sustainable practices to safeguard global food security through transparent, intelligent predictive analytics.

title: Interpretable Crop Yield Forecasting Under Climate Change Using Temporal Fusion Transformers
abstract: Reliable prediction of crop yields plays a vital role in ensuring food security and guiding sustainable agricultural strategies.
