title: IOT-BASED SMART AGRICULTURE SYSTEM FOR CROP MONITORING AND IRRIGATION MANAGEMENT
abstract: Agriculture remains the backbone of the Indian economy and supports millions of livelihoods. However, traditional farming practices face challenges such as water scarcity, climate variability, rising production costs, and inefficient irrigation methods. The Internet of Things (IoT) has emerged as a transformative technology that enables real-time monitoring and automation in agricultural environments. The application of IoT in agriculture will not only contribute to agriculture farming but also and enhances higher crop productivity, water conservation, food security and sustainable development. This paper presents an IoT-based smart agriculture system for crop monitoring and irrigation management. The proposed system integrates soil moisture, temperature, and humidity sensors with a microcontroller and cloud platform to monitor field conditions continuously. Based on sensor readings, irrigation is automatically controlled to ensure optimal water utilization. Farmers can remotely access field data through mobile or web applications, enabling informed decision-making. The system aims to reduce water wastage, improve crop productivity, lower labor requirements, and promote sustainable agricultural practices. The study highlights the significance of IoT in precision farming and discusses future opportunities involving artificial intelligence, machine learning, and predictive analytics.

title: CLIMATE-RESILIENT PEST AND DISEASE MANAGEMENT IN HORTICULTURAL CROPS PRODUCTION
abstract: Climate change has emerged as one of the most significant challenges affecting global agricultural sustainability by altering pest dynamics, pathogen evolution, crop microbe interactions and ecosystem stability. Increasing temperatures, changing precipitation patterns, elevated atmospheric carbon dioxide concentrations and frequent extreme weather events have modified the geographical distribution, survival, reproduction and outbreak potential of insect pests and plant pathogens. Conventional crop protection strategies based mainly on synthetic pesticides are becoming increasingly inadequate due to accelerated pesticide resistance, environmental concerns and unpredictable climatic conditions. Climate-resilient pest and disease management provides a sustainable framework by integrating ecological approaches, advanced biotechnology, digital innovations and precision crop protection strategies. Integrated Pest Management (IPM), biological control, microbial-based disease suppression, host plant resistance, molecular breeding, genome editing, nanotechnology, RNA interference (RNAi) and artificial intelligence-driven monitoring systems represent important components of climate-smart crop protection. Beneficial microorganisms, including plant growth-promoting rhizobacteria (PGPR), endophytes and mycorrhizal fungi, enhance plant defense mechanisms and improve tolerance against combined biotic and abiotic stresses. Advances in marker-assisted selection, genome-wide association studies, genomic selection and CRISPR/Cas-based technologies accelerate the development of crop varieties with durable resistance against emerging pest and disease threats. Furthermore, digital agriculture tools such as remote sensing, drones, Internet of Things (IoT) and machine learning-based decision support systems enable early detection and site-specific management of pest and disease outbreaks. Nano-enabled pesticides and RNAi-based approaches provide highly targeted and environmentally safer alternatives to conventional chemical control. Future crop protection systems must adopt an integrated and adaptive approach combining ecological knowledge, predictive modelling, genetic improvement and sustainable technologies. Climate-resilient pest and disease management will play a crucial role in maintaining horticultural productivity, reducing environmental risks and ensuring global food security under future climate uncertainties.

title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE FOR SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT: EMERGING TECHNOLOGIES AND FUTURE DIRECTIONS
abstract: Book Title: Artificial Intelligence for Sustainable Development: New Technologies and Future Trends The rapid advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) technologies has brought about a new wave of innovation, revolutionising industries and changing the landscape of how to tackle complex world problems. Over the past few years, the intersection of sustainable development aspirations with smart technologies has created opportunities for sustainable growth and development, resource efficiency, and a better quality of life. This title, Artificial Intelligence for Sustainable Development: Emerging Technologies and Future Directions, is a welcome addition to this discussion. The book offers a rich tapestry of chapters that capture the multidisciplinary aspect of AI and its uses. The book dedicates several chapters to healthcare applications, highlighting the transformative impact of AI on disease diagnosis, early detection and treatment. Chapters focusing on diabetes, Alzheimer's disease, autism, breast cancer, and smart medical imaging showcase the indispensable role of AI for sustainable and accessible healthcare. The book also explores the fields of agriculture and food security, where AI models are used for crop forecasting and precision agriculture. These are designed to increase efficiency and sustainability. The book also features research on federated learning and IoMT (Internet of Medical Things), which highlights the significance of privacy and security in intelligent systems. Contributions on intelligent software systems and automation, such as agentic AI, self-generating software tests, and AI-driven platforms for education and hiring, also feature in this book. These advancements delve into the role of AI in software engineering and enhancing the efficiency of digital ecosystems. Contributions in new areas such as human-computer interaction, gesture recognition, and natural language processing (such as demographic prediction from text and Bangla handwritten text recognition), further add value to this book. Furthermore, novel models for disaster prediction and virtual caregivers demonstrate AI's contribution to creating responsive systems for the betterment of society. This book is designed for academicians, researchers, students, and professionals from industry who are interested in the state of the art of AI and its role in sustainable development. The chapters offer insights into challenges, progress and future research directions.

title: CNN-BASED FORECASTING OF PLANT GROWTH PATTERNS FROM MULTIVARIATE WEATHER DATA
abstract: Weather has dominant impact on the growth and development of crops. The chapter is a re-articulated framework, which takes advantage of the Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) to predict plant growth behavior in response to changing meteorological conditions. The proposed methodology could include the intricate, nonlinear interactions between environmental drivers and vegetation dynamics by combining spatial-temporal weather inputs (including temperature, precipitation, humidity, solar radiation, wind and soil moisture). The model is effective in forecasting significant agronomic variables such as the height of the plant, accumulation of biomass, and yield. Naturally trained and fine-tuned models on historical observations exhibit better performance than traditional machine learning and rule-based methods, especially on spatial heterogeneity and multidimensional dependencies. The results assist with decision making based on data when it comes to smart farming, permitting to make an early warning, to optimize the use of resources and to do adaptive crop management. The framework is consistent with global sustainability goals through improving climate resilient agriculture and sharing in food security and climate action.

title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN AGRICULTURAL BIOTECHNOLOGY AND ENVIRONMENTAL BIOLOGY
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has emerged as a transformative technology with significant implications for agricultural biotechnology and environmental biology. This chapter explores the integration of AI with biological sciences to address global challenges such as food security, climate change, and environmental sustainability. AI-driven techniques, including machine learning, deep learning, computer vision, and natural language processing, enable efficient analysis of complex biological datasets generated through high-throughput technologies. In agricultural biotechnology, AI supports precision farming, crop improvement, disease detection, and smart irrigation systems, leading to enhanced productivity and resource efficiency. In environmental biology, AI facilitates ecosystem monitoring, biodiversity conservation, pollution detection, and climate change modeling through predictive analytics and data-driven insights. Furthermore, the chapter highlights the role of AI in genomics, proteomics, and bioinformatics, emphasizing its contribution to accelerating scientific discovery and innovation. Despite its advantages, the adoption of AI is challenged by issues such as data availability, high implementation costs, ethical concerns, and the need for regulatory frameworks. The chapter concludes by discussing future perspectives, including autonomous farming, climate-smart agriculture, and sustainable environmental management. Overall, the integration of AI with biotechnology represents a promising approach toward achieving sustainable development and addressing pressing global environmental and agricultural challenges.

title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE-DRIVEN INNOVATIONS FOR SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURAL DEVELOPMENT
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is playing a vital role in promoting sustainable agriculture by improving productivity, reducing resource waste, and supporting environmentally friendly farming practices. With increasing challenges such as climate change, soil degradation, water scarcity, and rising food demand, AI-based technologies provide innovative solutions for efficient agricultural management.AI applications in agriculture include precision farming, smart irrigation, crop monitoring, pest and disease detection, yield prediction, and supply-chain optimization. Technologies such as machine learning, deep learning, computer vision, drones, and IoT sensors enable farmers to collect and analyze real-time data on soil conditions, weather patterns, crop health, and resource usage. This helps optimize the use of water, fertilizers, and pesticides while minimizing environmental impact. Advanced predictive models, including Random Forest, Support Vector Machines, and neural networks, improve decision-making by forecasting crop yields and identifying potential risks. AI-powered automation also reduces labor requirements and increases operational efficiency. Studies show that AI-driven systems can significantly improve crop productivity while conserving natural resources. Overall, AI is transforming agriculture into a smarter, more sustainable sector capable of meeting future food security needs while protecting ecosystems and supporting long-term environmental sustainability.

title: DEEP LEARNING–BASED FRAMEWORK FOR AGRICULTURAL YIELD PREDICTION
abstract: Agriculture is a cornerstone of the global economy, and accurate crop yield prediction is essential for food security and efficient resource utilization. Conventional statistical and machine learning approaches often struggle to model complex, nonlinear relationships present in agricultural data. Recent advancements in Deep Learning (DL) have enabled the development of highly accurate predictive models capable of learning intricate spatial and temporal patterns from large-scale datasets. This chapter presents a deep learning–based framework for agricultural yield prediction using environmental, soil, and crop management parameters. The proposed system integrates time-series weather data with multi-dimensional agricultural features and employs advanced deep learning architectures such as Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks. Experimental results across multiple crops and climatic regions in India demonstrate improved prediction accuracy and robustness compared to traditional machine learning methods, supporting intelligent decision-making in smart agriculture.

title: DIGITAL ADVISORY SYSTEM AND TOOLS FOR ECO-EFFICIENT AGRICULTURE
abstract: The agricultural sector of the world is standing at a cross road, where this industry is faced with the challenge to produce enough food to keep up with the increasing demand of foodstuffs and at the same time managing the available natural resources in the most sustainable manner. Reduced productivity due to poor planning, climate change, soil erosion, overuse of chemicals, and poor management of resources poses a threat to food security in the long run. Eco-efficient farming where the optimal use of water, fertilizers, energy and other inputs are considered, and the environmental impacts limited have come out as a strategic solution. In this regard, digital Agriculture Advisory Systems (DAS) and smart farming technologies are changing the traditional methods of agriculture as an intuitive practice to a data-driven decision-making system. Digital agriculture uses a combination of artificial intelligence, machine learning, Big Data analytics, IoT, satellite imagery, cloud computing, GIS, GPS, drone, and mobile-based solutions to increase precision in input application, crop monitoring, hazard forecasting, and resource optimization throughout the agricultural value chain. The Digital Agriculture Advisory Systems (DAAS) are an innovative solution to the development of eco-friendly and sustainable agriculture based on the use of data, its accuracy, and contextuality in decision-making. Through the combination of sophisticated digital technologies, such as artificial intelligence, Internet of Things (IoT), remote sensing, decision support systems, and mobile-based advisory platforms, the so-called DAAS allow optimizing water, nutrients, energy, and pesticide usage as important agricultural inputs. This optimization is more productive, as well as ecological, and promotes sustainability of the environment as well as the sustainability of the economy. Good delivery systems, such as mobile applications, SMS and voice-based services, web portals, and smart devices, extend reach and facilitate inclusiveness especially among smallholder farmers. Although adoption and impact may be limited due to issues associated with infrastructure constraints, digital literacy levels, the high cost of starting up, and data governance, policy facilitation and focus capacity-building efforts can greatly increase adoption and impact. Altogether, DAAS represent a strategic direction of development of resilient, resource-saving, and sustainable agro-systems.

title: DESIGN AND DEVELOPMENT OF SOIL TESTING AND FEEDBACK SYSTEM FOR AGRICULTURE USING IOT AND ML
abstract: Agriculture plays a crucial role in global food security and economic development; however, modern farming faces challenges such as soil degradation, inefficient resource utilization, climate variability, and declining agricultural productivity. Accurate and timely soil analysis is essential for improving crop yield and ensuring sustainable farming practices. Conventional soil testing methods are often laboratory-dependent, time-consuming, costly, and inaccessible to farmers in rural areas. To address these limitations, this study proposes an Internet of Things (IoT) and Machine Learning (ML)-based soil testing and feedback system for real-time soil health monitoring and intelligent agricultural decision support.The proposed system integrates multiple soil sensors with a microcontroller-based IoT architecture to continuously monitor critical soil parameters such as soil moisture, pH, temperature, humidity, and nutrient levels including Nitrogen (N), Phosphorus (P), and Potassium (K). The collected sensor data is transmitted wirelessly through Wi-Fi communication to a cloud-based platform for storage and processing. Machine Learning algorithms are utilized to analyze real-time and historical soil data, identify soil health patterns, predict nutrient deficiencies, and generate actionable recommendations regarding irrigation scheduling, fertilizer application, and crop suitability.The system also includes a user-friendly mobile interface for real-time visualization of soil parameters and automated feedback alerts. Experimental testing was conducted under laboratory and field conditions to evaluate the accuracy, reliability, and responsiveness of the system. The results demonstrated high accuracy in detecting soil conditions, stable wireless communication, and effective real-time monitoring capabilities. The integration of IoT and ML technologies enables data-driven decision-making, reduces excessive use of water and fertilizers, minimizes operational costs, and enhances crop productivity.

title: GEOINFORMATICS IN PRECISION FARMING FOR ENHANCING AGRICULTURAL SUSTAINABILITY PRODUCTIVITY AND CLIMATE RESILIENCE
abstract: Agriculture is experiencing a paradigm shift from conventional practices to data-driven, knowledge-intensive systems in response to growing demands for food, fiber, and bioenergy amid climate change, land degradation, and resource constraints. Precision farming, powered by geoinformatics, has emerged as a transformative approach to enhance productivity while ensuring environmental sustainability. Geoinformatics integrates Geographic Information Systems (GIS), Remote Sensing (RS), and Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS/GPS) with advanced spatial modeling to generate spatio-temporal insights into soil variability, crop growth, hydrological regimes, and pest–disease dynamics. These technologies enable site-specific crop management (SSCM) by combining multispectral and hyperspectral imagery, soil and meteorological datasets, and digital elevation models with machine learning techniques. Applications of geoinformatics-based precision farming include variable-rate fertilizer application, irrigation scheduling, yield forecasting, and real-time monitoring of crop stress using vegetation indices such as NDVI, SAVI, and EVI. Such practices reduce input overuse, conserve water, lower greenhouse gas emissions, and maintain soil fertility, thereby aligning with climate-smart agricultural strategies. Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and satellite constellations like Sentinel and Landsat further enhance decision support by providing high-resolution, near-real-time data for farm-level management. Beyond boosting productivity, geoinformatics strengthens resilience by offering early-warning systems for droughts, floods, and pest outbreaks. Socio-economic benefits include reduced input costs, improved profitability, and enhanced livelihood security, while broader impacts encompass food security and contributions to Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Despite these advantages, challenges remain, including high initial investment, limited technical expertise, poor data interoperability, and inadequate institutional support in developing economies. Present research consolidates current advances in geoinformatics applications for precision farming, highlights their role in sustainable and resilient agriculture, and identifies research gaps for integration with emerging tools such as Artificial Intelligence (AI), Internet of Things (IoT), and big data analytics.

title: AI-APPLICATIONS IN APPLIED ENTOMOLOGY
abstract: Insect pests are responsible for the loss of an estimated 20-40% of global crop production annually, with projections indicating that warming climates will further exacerbate these losses in coming decades. Simultaneously, the formal description of the world's estimated 5.5 million insect species remains incomplete, with fewer than one million currently catalogued, a taxonomic deficit that conventional morphology-based methods are ill-equipped to resolve at scale. Against this backdrop, artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a transformative computational paradigm in applied entomology, offering high-throughput, automated, and scalable solutions to longstanding challenges in pest management, species identification, biodiversity monitoring, and food safety. Conventional entomological practices, which depend predominantly on manual field inspection and expert morphological assessment, are inherently labour-intensive, geographically constrained, and limited in their capacity for real-time decision-making. AI addresses these constraints by integrating machine learning, deep learning, computer vision, and big data analytics to process complex biological and environmental datasets with high efficiency and reproducibility. Among these techniques, convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have demonstrated classification accuracies exceeding 95% in controlled insect identification tasks, substantially reducing dependence on specialist taxonomic expertise. The integration of AI with Internet of Things (IoT) devices, smart traps, hyperspectral sensors, and unmanned aerial vehicles further enables continuous, field-scale pest monitoring and early detection of infestations. These capabilities contribute to optimized pesticide application, reduced environmental contamination, and improved food safety across the production-to-storage continuum. Within Integrated Pest Management (IPM) frameworks, AI-powered decision support systems facilitate predictive modelling of pest population dynamics using climatic, phenological, and remote sensing data, enabling proactive rather than reactive management interventions. Additionally, AI enhances biological control programmes through optimization of mass rearing conditions and release strategies for natural enemies. Despite these advances, critical challenges persist, including the scarcity of high-quality annotated datasets, limited model generalisability across agroecological zones, inadequate infrastructure in developing agricultural regions, and unresolved ethical and regulatory concerns. This chapter provides a comprehensive review of AI applications across the spectrum of applied entomology, critically assessing current achievements, technological limitations, and future directions toward sustainable pest management and global food security.

It discusses the physiological and spectral basis of crop stress detection and explains how biotic stress alters chlorophyll concentration, canopy structure, moisture balance, photosynthetic activity and thermal behavior, thereby modifying spectral reflectance patterns. Hyperspectral and multispectral sensing systems demonstrated that diseases produce distinct detectable spectral signatures. Recent developments in Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), transfer learning, ensemble learning and Vision Transformers (ViTs) have substantially improved automated disease diagnosis and pest classification under complex field conditions. UAV-assisted AI systems and IoT-integrated agricultural monitoring platforms demonstrate the growing convergence of autonomous sensing, robotics and intelligent decision-support systems. The chapter also examines the role of GIS and remote sensing in ecological pest- disease forecasting and habitat suitability assessment. Major challenges including environmental variability, spectral similarity between stress conditions, limited annotated datasets, computational complexity and operational scalability are critically discussed. The chapter highlights the evolution of agricultural image processing from conventional statistical approaches to advanced AI-driven analytical frameworks also remote sensing integrated with AI is expected to play a vital role in climate-resilient agriculture, sustainable crop protection, reduced pesticide dependency and next-generation smart farming systems.

title: SMART PEST SURVEILLANCE: AN AI AND IOT ENABLED INTEGRATED MONITORING SYSTEM
abstract: Insect pests cause major yield losses and pose a serious threat to global food security. Insect pests cause enormous yield loss and threaten global food security. Conventional methods for pest surveillance involve manual scouting coupled with expert identification, which is cumbersome, very labor intensive, and often falls short of real-time monitoring. Now, with recent advances in artificial intelligence and IoT, smart, automated data-driven integrated pest management systems can be built that integrate smart sensors, automated insect traps, computer vision, machine learning algorithms, and decision support systems that allow continuous monitoring of pest populations. AI-IoT based systems will provide accurate and early detection and identification, population estimation, hot spot mapping, and early warning alerts based on economic threshold levels. Integration of weather and crop-related data will enhance pest forecasting and risk assessment. Site-specific and need based interventions reduce pesticide overuse, support IPM, and promote environmental sustainability. Global case studies demonstrate that AI and IoT enabled approaches improve the accuracy of pest identification, strengthen data-driven decision making, and improve farmer advisory services. Overall, AI-IoT offers a promising and sustainable solution for modern pest surveillance and crop protection.

title: HOW DIGITAL TOOLS AND AI SUPPORT ACHIEVING SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURE AND FOOD SECURITY (SDG 2)
abstract: The urgency of achieving Sustainable Development Goal 2 (SDG 2): Zero Hunger has increased due to the world's population expansion, growing climate variability, and declining agricultural resources. The increasing demand for food cannot be met by traditional agricultural methods alone. Artificial intelligence (AI) and digital tools have become revolutionary technologies in the last ten years that can increase output, reduce hazards, and support resource-efficient agriculture. Predictive analytics, machine learning-based crop monitoring, precision irrigation, drones, and digital advisory platforms are examples of AI-driven technologies that help farmers make well-informed decisions while protecting soil, water, and biodiversity. This paper offers a thorough summary of how AI and digital technology support food security and sustainable agriculture. It looks at big data applications, AI-based decision-support systems, precision farming equipment, and breakthroughs in digital agriculture. The article also discusses implementation issues, such as skill gaps, high initial costs, data privacy, and digital inequalities, particularly in developing nations. In general, improving productivity, resilience, and sustainability while achieving SDG 2 goals requires the integration of AI and digital technologies.

title: INFLATION, GDP, AND FORECASTING: A REVIEW OF MIXED-FREQUENCY APPROACHES
abstract: This review study thoroughly investigates the relationship between inflation and economic growth, utilizing new work that integrates advanced econometric techniques, namely the use of mixed-frequency data for forecasting. This article examines the impact of inflation on GDP in many economic settings, including emerging countries and certain economic sectors like food prices. It does this by combining important empirical studies with theoretical viewpoints. The findings emphasize the importance of the inflation-GDP relationship to SDG 8: Decent Work and Economic Growth, and how complex, dynamic, and context-dependent it is. This study investigates novel methods for the sake of economic forecasting that may increase the accuracy of GDP and inflation projections, which is important for stable economic management, through the use of mixed-frequency data. Inflation's consequences are able to be seen. Inflation in food prices stands out. In this analysis, policies that are well-calibrated and established are shown to be important. Flexible for managing inflation along with promoting development that is sustainable and inclusive. Goals 2: We can better understand Zero Hunger, SDG 10: Reduced Inequalities, and SDG 1 overall. This understanding involves an end to No Poverty.

title: POTENTIAL OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE TO COMBAT CHALLENGES IN TRANSFORMING AGRICULTURE
abstract: The agricultural industry has many difficulties in the twenty-first century, such as issues with food security, sustainability and rising demand brought on by population increase. To tackle these issues, artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a game-changing tool with enormous potential. This essay examines how artificial intelligence (AI) could revolutionize agriculture by improving production, resource management and decision-making. Precision farming, which uses AI-powered sensors, drones and machine learning algorithms to assist farmers in enhancing crop yields, minimizing waste and optimizing resource use, is a significant component of AI’s impact on agriculture. AI also helps with disease outbreak prediction, task automation and monitoring soil conditions, all of which increase productivity and lower labour costs. AI-driven data analytics also promote sustainable practices and guarantee food security by enabling better-informed decisions, from crop selection to market forecasts.

title: APPLICATION OF MACHINE LEARNING FOR CROP YIELD PREDICTION CHALLENGES AND FUTURE DIRECTIONS
abstract: In recent years, the global agricultural landscape has witnessed a transformative shift, driven by technological advancements that aim to address the pressing challenges of food security and sustainability. It is critical aspect of precision agriculture and plays a pivotal role in optimizing agricultural practices, resource allocation, and decision-making for farmers, policymakers, and stakeholders alike. Accurate crop yield prediction empowers the agricultural community to anticipate potential fluctuations in productivity, optimize resource utilization, and mitigate risks associated with climate variability, pest outbreaks, and market fluctuations. Traditionally, crop yield prediction relied on empirical methods, historical data analysis, and localized expertise. However, these conventional approaches often suffer from limited accuracy and generalizability, making them less suitable for addressing the complexities of modern agriculture. In recent years, deep learning made revolution in by harnessing the power of neural networks to learn intricate patterns and relationships from vast and diverse datasets. The ability of deep learning models to process multimodal information, such as remote sensing data, climate records, and historical yield statistics, has opened new horizons in predicting crop yields at both regional and global scales. The objective of this chapter is to offer a thorough exploration of the utilization of deep learning methodologies. The emphasis is placed on addressing the obstacles encountered in this evolving domain and outlining potential paths for future advancements.

title: Commodity Prices Volatility and Inflation in Ethiopia: Using Machine Learning Techniques
abstract: Commodity price fluctuations have significantly impacted global and national economic stability, particularly during the COVID-19 pandemic and ongoing geopolitical tensions. High inflation, one of Ethiopia's most pressing economic challenges, has persisted above 30% annually. This study investigates the impact of commodity price volatility on inflation in Ethiopia using time series data from 1992 to 2022. The research employs various machine learning models, including XGBoost, Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, and an Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) regression model to analyze both global and domestic shocks influencing inflation. The findings indicate that oil price growth and lagged domestic and global inflation are the most significant predictors of domestic inflation, emphasizing Ethiopia's vulnerability to global commodity price changes and the persistence of inflationary trends. The Gradient Boosting model demonstrated superior predictive accuracy, explaining over 64% of the variation in inflation. The results suggest that effective policy measures focusing on macroeconomic stability and managing external shocks are crucial for mitigating inflationary pressures in Ethiopia. Lastly, this research provides a novel approach by incorporating machine learning techniques to enhance the understanding of inflation dynamics in developing economies, thereby offering valuable insights for policymakers.

title: Forecasting Nigeria Inflation Rate Using Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (ARIMA) Model
abstract: This study focuses on forecasting Nigeria's inflation rate using the Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (ARIMA) model. The research utilizes monthly inflation data from January 2010 to December 2024, obtained from the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN). The primary objective is to model and forecast inflation trends in Nigeria, which has been experiencing significant inflationary pressures in recent years. The study employs the Augmented Dickey-Fuller (ADF) and Phillips-Perron (PP) tests to check for stationarity, revealing that the inflation series becomes stationary after a second differencing (I (2)). The ARIMA (2,2,1) model is identified as the best fit based on the Akaike Information Criterion (AIC) and Bayesian Information Criterion (BIC), providing a balance between model complexity and predictive accuracy. The model reveals strong autoregressive and moving average dynamics, with significant coefficients for AR (1), AR (2), and MA (1) terms. The forecasted inflation rates for 2025 indicate a steady upward trend, with inflation expected to rise from 35.26% in January to 38.93% by December 2025. The findings highlight the persistent inflationary pressures in Nigeria, driven by factors such as currency depreciation, rising food prices, and energy costs. The study concludes that the ARIMA (2,2,1) model is effective for forecasting Nigeria's inflation rate and recommends that policymakers implement measures to stabilize the economy, including tighter monetary policies, fiscal discipline, and investments in domestic production to mitigate inflationary pressures. Continuous monitoring and timely adjustments to economic policies are also emphasized to address the ongoing challenges posed by inflation. Additionally, the study recommends diversifying the economy to reduce dependence on oil exports, improving agricultural productivity to curb food price volatility, and enhancing data collection methods for more accurate inflation forecasting.

title: A Novel Hybrid Method for Predicting Specific Crop Yield
abstract: Predicting crop yields is crucial for economic planning, food security, and agricultural management. Conventional approaches frequently need accurate results regarding the complex interaction between environmental conditions and crop-specific traits. By combining the best features of machine learning algorithms with expert-level domain knowledge, we provide a new hybrid approach to predicting crop yields that is both state- and crop-specific. Our approach integrates historical yield data, satellite imagery, meteorological data, soil properties, and crop-specific information to build robust predictive models. Specifically, we employ ensemble learning techniques, including random forest and gradient boosting, to capture complex nonlinear relationships and improve prediction accuracy. Additionally, we incorporate domain knowledge through feature engineering and selection to enhance model interpretability and generalization. We validate our method using real-world datasets from diverse geographical regions and crops, demonstrating its superior performance compared to traditional approaches. Our proposed hybrid method offers a promising solution for accurate and reliable crop yield prediction, facilitating informed agricultural decision-making.

title: The evolving sphere of food security
abstract: Hundreds of millions of people still suffer from chronic hunger and food insecurity despite sufficient levels of global food production. The poor's inability to afford adequate diets remains the biggest constraint to solving hunger, but the dynamics of global food insecurity are complex and demand analysis that extends beyond the traditional domains of economics and agriculture. How do the policies used to promote food security in one country affect nutrition, food access, natural resources, and national security in other countries? How do the priorities and challenges of achieving food security change over time as countries develop economically? The Evolving Sphere of Food Security seeks to answer these two important questions and others by exploring the interconnections of food security to security of many kinds: energy, water, health, climate, the environment, and national security. Through personal stories of research in the field and policy advising at local and global scales, a multidisciplinary group of scholars provide readers with a real-world sense of the opportunities and challenges involved in alleviating food insecurity. In sub-Saharan Africa, for example, management of HIV/AIDS, the establishment of an equitable system of land property rights, and investment in solar-powered irrigation play an important role in improving food security---particularly in the face of global climate change. Meanwhile, food price spikes associated with the United States' biofuels policy continue to have spillover effects on the world's rural poor with implications for stability and national security. The Evolving Sphere of Food Security traces four key areas of the food security field: 1) the political economy of food and agriculture; 2) challenges for the poorest billion; 3) agriculture's dependence on resources and the environment; and 4) food in a national and international security context. This book connects these areas in a way that tells an integrated story about human lives, resource use, and the policy process.
